Whatever is missed from livelihood today may be hoped for tomorrow with increase, but whatever is lost from one’s lifetime yesterday, its return cannot be hoped for today.
Every person is seeking his aspirations while [concurrently] being sought by his death.
How many a person is deluded by hopes, [and] ends up wasting his actions!
Hope is sufficient as a deception.
Increased aspirations stem from corruption of the intellect.
For every hope there is a delusion.
Hopes never end.
Hope causes death to be forgotten.
Aspirations are incentives for men.
Hope is the veil of death.
There is no end to hope.
Hope is an intimate companion.
Hope is a cheater, deceiver, and harmer.
Hope corrupts [one’s] actions and wastes [one’s] lifetime.
Aspirations blind the eyes of insight.
Aspirations beguile you, and in the presence of reality, they abandon you.
Verily I am fighting against my hopes and waiting for my death.
Verily you will not reach what you hope for and will never surpass death, so be conscious of Allah and be moderate in your desires.
If you are deceived by hopes, you will surely be annihilated by the fast approaching death and will have lost [the opportunity to perform] good deeds.
The bane of hopes is the coming of death.
The bane of hope is death.
With the realization of hopes, it becomes easier to overcome [one’s] fears.
The worst habit is hoping [for too much] as it wastes one’s lifetime and causes one to lose [the opportunity to perform good] deeds.
Keep away from vain hopes, for they take away the delight of the blessings of Allah from you and make them seem small and insignificant, thereby increasing your lack of gratitude.
The fruit of hope is corruption of deeds.
The product of aspirations is regret (and its fruit is loss).
How close death is to hope!
How corrupting is hope for deeds!
How severing is death for hope!
No one lengthens his hopes except that he [also] curtails his actions.
What is the matter with you? You hope for that which you do not achieve, amass wealth which you do not use and build houses which you do not occupy!
No one lengthens his hopes except that he forgets death and performs evil actions.
The best assistance for action is curtailing hopes.
Let aspirations and ploys not deceive you, for this suffices as ineptness.
No deception is more misleading than hope.
Nothing is more untrue than hope.
Aspirations are not loyal to those who rely on them.
The smallest of hopes leads to corruption of actions.
Be wary of [false] aspirations, for verily they are certain [causes of] deaths.
Be cautious not to depend on hopes, for they are the wares of the unintelligent.
The most beneficial cure is abandoning [false] aspirations.
Aspirations are scattered [and dispersed].
Aspirations delude.
False aspiration is the trait of fools.
Submission to hope corrupts [one’s] actions.
It is when death comes that the failure of hopes becomes apparent.
I wonder at the one who has no control over his death, how can he lengthen his hopes?
The end of hope is death.
The farthest thing is hope.
Those who have the most [false] hopes are the ones who remember death the least.
Those who have the longest hopes are the ones whose deeds are the worst.
Verily Allah, the Glorified, hates the one who has long hopes and performs evil actions.
Indeed man reaches near [the realization of] his hopes, when the [sudden] approach of his death cuts them short, then - Glory be to Allah! - Neither is the hope realized nor is the hoper spared.

Be cautious not to lengthen [your] hope, for many a deceived person has been enticed by his long hope and corrupted his deeds and cut [short] his lifetime, then neither was his hope realized nor was that which he lost regained.
Where will the falsehoods of hopes mislead you to?!
Where will the mirage of hopes misguide you to?!
The most delusive thing is hope.

The one who is worst in bargaining and most unsuccessful in striving is he who exerts himself in seeking the realization of his hopes while fate does not help him in his aims, and [as a result] he leaves this world in a sorrowful state and proceeds to the next world where he faces the consequences.
Hope is treacherous.
Hope deceives and lifetime passes.
Hope misleads and transgression strikes down.
One who is deceived by hopes is misled.
Aspirations are the wares of the unintelligent.
Hopes are the delusions of the foolish.
Hopes bring death closer.
One whose aspirations increase, his satisfaction decreases.
One whose hopes lengthen, his actions become worse.
One who is deceived by hope is misled by it.
One who is deceived by aspirations is belied by death.
One who reaches the end of his hopes should expect the arrival of his death.
One who follows his aspirations faces increased hardship.
One who proceeds on the path of his hopes, stumbles upon his death.
One whose aspirations increase, his hardship increases.
One who hopes for that which is not possible, his anticipation becomes long.
One whose hope is [to reach] Allah, shall realize the fulfilment of his hope and aspiration.
Whoever regards his remaining lifetime to be fleeting, his hopes and aspirations become short.
One who proceeds on the course of his hopes, stumbles upon his death.
One who hopes for anything other than Allah, the Glorified, has given lie to his hopes.
One who seeks support from his aspirations becomes penniless.
It is foolishness to depending on [one’s] hope.
The humiliation of men is in the dashing of hopes.
May Allah have mercy on the man who shortens his hopes, anticipates death, makes good use of his time and takes with him the provisions of [good] deeds.
Many an aspiration may lie beneath death.
Take away from your long hopes and increase your short lifetime, and do not be deceived by your good physical health and yesterday’s wellbeing, for life is short and good health is prone to change.
The worst poverty is [false] aspiration.
Lifetimes are wasted between hope and aspiration.
Blessed is he who shortens his hopes and makes good use of his time.
Blessed is he who belies his aspirations and sacrifices his world in order to build his Hereafter.
One who relies on his aspirations dies without [realizing] his hopes.
One who trusts his aspirations will have them severed by death.
Whoever shortens his hopes, beautifies his actions.
Whoever lengthens his hopes, corrupts his actions.
A just leader is better [and more beneficial] than heavy rainfall.
One who obeys his Imām has obeyed his Lord.
A leader needs a wise mind, an eloquent tongue and a heart that is steadfast in the establishment of truth.
Leadership (imāmah) is a social order.
Leadership is an organizational structure for the society
Whoever gives refuge to the one who seeks his help, Allah will grant him refuge from His punishment.
One who protects a fearful person from what he fears, Allah, the Glorified, will protect him from His chastisement.
Many a person who is secure gets frightened.
Nothing brings greater security than [having] faith and [performing] good deeds.
By Allah, no one hinders the security of the peaceful or takes away the rights of the people except the disbelieving infidel and the duplicitous apostate.
Do not be deceived by [a false sense of] security, for you will surely be taken from your sanctuary.
It is not appropriate for an intelligent person to live in fear when he has found a way to [attain] security.
There is no blessing better than security.
Security is [a cause of] deception; fear is [a means of] precaution.
The sweetness of security is spoilt by the bitterness of fear and panic.
Many a security turns into fear.
The comfort of life is in security.
One who feels secure from the scheme of Allah, his sense of security is futile (or his faith is nullified).
He from whose evil people are not safe, is not secure from the punishment of Allah.
How few are the reliable, trustworthy people, and how many are the treacherous!
Trustworthiness leads to truthfulness.
Trustworthiness and loyalty are sincere actions, lying and fabrication are perfidious utterances.
Return the trust to the one who has entrusted it to you, and do not act treacherously with the one who betrayed your trust.
Return the trust when it is entrusted to you, and do not accuse anyone when you entrust something to him, for surely one who is not trustworthy has no faith.
The best [form of] trustworthiness is keeping one’s promise.
Trustworthiness is [a sign of] faith; cheerfulness is [a form of] kindness.
Trustworthiness is preservation [and safeguarding of what has been entrusted].
Trustworthiness is a success for the one who observes it.
Trustworthiness is a merit for the one who executes it.
The bane of trustworthiness is treachery.
When you are entrusted with something, then do not betray [the trust].
When you entrust anyone [with something], then do not accuse them of treachery.
When trustworthiness becomes stronger, truthfulness increases.
The cornerstone of faith is trustworthiness.
Sound trustworthiness is a symbol of good conviction.
Espouse trustworthiness for it is the best [form of] religiosity.
Corruption of trustworthiness is submission to treachery.
Successful is the one who clothes himself with loyalty and arms himself with trustworthiness.
Everything that is not fit to be disclosed is a trust, even if its confidentiality is not specifically sought.
One who has no trustworthiness has no faith.
One who takes [the] keeping [of] trust lightly will fall into treachery.
One who acts with trustworthiness has perfected his religion.
The best trust that can be kept is fulfilling [one’s] obligations.
There is no faith in one who is not trustworthy.
There is no trustworthiness in one who has no religion.
Faith is the better of the two trusts (or securities).
Faith is acknowledging with the tongue and acting with the limbs.
Faith and modesty are linked in one linkage and they do not separate.
Faith and knowledge (or action) are twin brothers and companions who do not part ways.
Faith is a tree, its root is certitude, its branch is piety, its sunlight is modesty and its fruit is generosity.
Faith, sincerity, certitude and piety are [encapsulated in] patience and acceptance of what has been decreed [by Allah].
Faith and action are twin brothers and companions who do not part ways; Allah does not accept one without its counterpart.
The best [sign of] faith is trustworthiness.
The best faith is [based on] complete certitude.
The people who are strongest in faith are those who rely the most on Allah, the Glorified.
The closest people to Allah, the Glorified, are the ones with the greatest faith.
The best faith is [accompanied with] sincerity and good deeds, and the worst traits are cruelty and aggression.
The best faith is [based on] complete certitude, and the greatest honour is [in] doing good deeds.
Verily the best faith is for a man to act justly with others.
Indeed the place of faith is the heart, and the path to it is [through] the ears.
Faith is security.
Faith is the path with manifest inner secrets.
Faith is an effective intercessor.
Faith is free of jealousy.
Faith is the loftiest goal.
Disbelief is wiped out by faith.
Faith is sincerity in action.
Salvation comes with faith.
Faith is a flame that cannot be extinguished.
Faith is free of hypocrisy.
Faith is patience in tribulation and gratitude in ease.
If you have faith in Allah, your place of return will be secure.
It is through faith that salvation is attained.
It is through faith that one is guided towards virtuous actions.
It is through faith that one reaches the pinnacle of felicity and the zenith of happiness.
Faith is salvation.
The fruit of faith is success with Allah.
The fruit of faith is desire for the Eternal Abode.
Three things, if possessed, complete one’s faith: intellect, forbearance and knowledge.

Three things, if possessed, perfect one’s faith: that when one is pleased, his pleasure does not lead him towards vice; and when he gets angry, his anger does not draw him away from the truth; and when he is in a position of power, he never takes that which is not his.
Three things, if possessed, perfect one’s faith: justice in anger and contentment, moderation in poverty and wealth, and maintaining a balance between fear and hope.
Three things are from the treasures of faith: concealing misfortune, charity and sickness.
Virtuous chastity and contentment with what suffices are from the pillars of faith.
Lowering your voice, casting down your gaze and walking with modesty are from the signs of faith and religiousness.
Contently remaining obedient [to Allah], performing good deeds and hastening towards noble traits are from the perfections of faith and the best virtues.
The embellishment of faith is piety.

He (‘a) said about faith: It is nearness [to Allah] for the one who guards [against evil], confidence for the one who trusts [in Allah], comfort for the one who entrusts [his affairs to Allah] and a shield for the one who endures patiently.
The embellishment of faith is [in] purity of one’s innermost thoughts [and secrets] and [performing] good deeds in the open.
Ask Allah for [strong] faith and act upon the ordinances of the Qur’an.
The worst faith is that in which doubt enters.
The uprightness of faith is [in] piety and its corruption is [in] greed.
True faith and good deeds are the best provisions.
Protect your faith from doubt, for doubt spoils faith the same way salt spoils honey.
Make your faith sincere, for this is the path to Paradise and safety from hellfire.
It is on truth and trust that faith is based.
The pinnacle of faith is certitude.

The highest degree of faith is befriending for the sake of Allah, having enmity for the sake of Allah, spending on each other for the sake of Allah and establishing ties with each other for the sake of Allah, the Glorified.
One type of faith is that which is firmly fixed in the hearts and another is that which shifts between the hearts and breasts [without being firmly fixed in the hearts].
Allah, the Glorified, has prescribed faith as a purification from doubt.
Faith has made it incumbent on its possessor to establish the traditions of Islam and its ordinances.
Strengthen your faith with certitude, for this is the best religion.
How can he who resents the truth taste the sweetness of faith?
Acquiring faith is [through] adhering to the truth and being sincere with the creatures.
He who claims to have faith yet is infatuated by misleading aspirations and false amusements of this world, has lied.
The conception of faith is [achieved through] the recitation of the Qur’an.
One who entertains doubt in his faith [in one God] becomes a polytheist.
One who has no faith has no trustworthiness.
One who likes his faith to become perfect should ensure that his love, hate, pleasure and displeasure are [all] for the sake of Allah.
One who gives for the sake of Allah, withholds for the sake of Allah, loves for the sake of Allah and hates for the sake of Allah, has perfected [his] faith.
The basis of faith is unwavering certitude.
One whose faith is true is saved, and one whose submission is complete is guided.
There is no honour higher than faith.
There is no medium more successful than faith.
There is no faith like modesty and generosity.
Faith without piety is of no benefit.
A servant’s faith is not complete until he loves whom Allah, the Glorified, loves and hates the one whom Allah, the Glorified, hates.
The faith of a servant is not true until he is more confident of what is in the Hand of Allah, the Glorified, than what is in his own hand.
Nothing that is preserved by human beings is like faith in Allah and good deeds.
The faith of a man is deduced by his submission and obedience [to Allah].
The faith [of a person] is deduced by increased fear [of Allah], controlling lust and overcoming lowly desires.
Faith requires certitude.
Faith requires sincerity.
One who believes in Allah [and attests to His oneness] is saved.
The foundation of faith is total submission to the will of Allah.
Have faith and you will be safe.
A believer is very truthful in [his] speech and generous in [his] benevolence.
A believer is [always] alert, waiting for one of the two boons [of this world or the Hereafter].
A believer is chaste, contented, free from sin and pious.
A believer is one whose love is for [the sake of] Allah, whose hate is for Allah, whose taking is for Allah and whose leaving is for Allah.
A believer is thankful in [times of] comfort, patient in tribulation and fearful in affluence.
A believer is moderate in [times of] affluence, [and] keeps away from the [pleasures of this] world.
A believer is [always] between blessing and wrongdoing, [and] nothing reforms these two except thankfulness and repentance.
A believer is dignified, honourable, self-reliant, cautious and sorrowful.
A believer constantly remembers [Allah], frequently contemplates, is thankful for blessings and patient in the face of tribulation.
A believer is modest, independent, certain and pious.
When a believer is asked [for help], he helps, and when he asks [other for help], he is lenient [and does not overburden them].
A believer is wary of his sins, always fearing chastisement and hoping for the mercy of his Lord.
To a believer, this world is his arena, action is his endeavour, death is his gift and Paradise is his prize.
A believer is one who has purified his heart of vileness.
A believer is one whose affair is near, whose sorrow is distant, whose silence is much and whose actions are sincere.
A believer is eager in [his] obedience [to Allah] and refrains from what is forbidden.
The soul of a believer is firmer than a hard rock while he is [himself] humbler than a slave.

When a believer observes, he takes lesson; and when he is quiet, he contemplates; and when he speaks, he remembers [Allah]; and when he is given, he is grateful; and when he undergoes hardship, he is patient.

When a believer is admonished, he restrains himself; and when he is warned, he becomes cautious; and when he is shown an example, he learns [from it]; and when he is reminded, he remembers; and when he is oppressed, he forgives.

The persistence of a believer is [in] his renunciation [of worldly pleasures], his interest is [in] his religiosity, his dignity is [in] his contentment and his striving is for his Hereafter. His good deeds are many, his status is elevated and he has managed [to gain] his freedom and salvation.
A believer looks at this world with eyes that derive lesson, and consumes from it only what is necessary, and hears in it with ears of hatred and enmity [towards it].
The believers blame themselves and are fearful of their past mistakes; they detest this world, eagerly yearn for the Hereafter and hasten towards [acts of] obedience.
A believer is one who bears with the harm that people inflict [on him] but nobody is ever harmed by him.
The believer is one who safeguards his Hereafter by [sacrificing] his world, while the vicious is one who safeguards his world by [sacrificing] his Hereafter.
A believer is faithful to himself and struggles against his vain desires and feelings.
Be careful of the opinions of believers, for Allah, the Glorified, effectuates the truth through their tongues.
The most honourable of believers is the most sagacious of them.
The best of believers in terms of belief is the one whose taking, giving, anger and pleasure are all for [the sake of] Allah.
Believers are indeed compassionate.1
Verily believers are afraid [of displeasing Allah].
Indeed the cheerfulness of a believer is in his face, his strength is in his religion and his sorrow is in his heart.
Verily a believer feels ashamed if an act which goes against his faith is committed by him.
The goal of a believer is Paradise.
The needlessness of a believer is through [his reliance on] Allah, the Glorified.
He (the believer) has enlivened his intellect, killed his lust, obeyed his Lord and disobeyed his lower- self.
How many a believer has succeeded through patience and thinking positively.
Be a pious, contented and modest believer.
A believer has a perfect intellect, a pleasing leniency, an inclination towards good deeds and an aversion towards bad deeds.

A believer has three times: a time for whispering to his Lord, a time for assessing himself (or in another narration: a time for making arrangements for his livelihood) and a time when he freely enjoys himself with what is lawful and pleasant.
The faith of a believer is not perfected until he deems comfort to be a trial and affliction to be a blessing.
A believer is never found to be envious, malevolent or miserly.
A believer is never anything other than forbearing and merciful.
It behoves a believer to feel ashamed if the thought of disobedience crosses his mind.
It behoves a believer to remain obedient and to cover himself with piety and contentment.
A believer is tested with affliction just like the purity of gold and silver is tested with fire.
There are three signs of a believer: truthfulness, certitude and [having] short hopes.
A believer is never found to be anything but content.
He who is not concerned about improving his Hereafter is not a believer.
If I were to strike the nose of a believer to make him hate me he would still not hate me, and if I were to bestow the whole world to a hypocrite to make him love me he would still not love me.
One who believes is safe.
One who believes increases his certitude.
One who believes in Allah seeks [help and] protection from Him.
A believer has not [truly] believed until he comprehends.
The example of a believer is like that of citronella, both its taste and its fragrance are pleasant.
One who purifies his faith is guided.
The concern of a believer is for his Hereafter, and all his efforts are for his place of [final] return.
A believer is never satiated while his brother is hungry.
A believer never falls short of forbearance and never gets anxious when faced with difficulty.
A man does not become a [true] believer until he is no longer concerned about what [food] will end his pangs of hunger and which of his two attires he will wear.

The cheerfulness of a believer is in his face and his sorrow is in his heart. He has the broadest chest (i.e. has great patience, knowledge and virtue) and is most humble in spirit. He hates high position and dislikes renown. His grief is long, his sorrow is distant, his silence is much and his time is occupied. He is grateful and patient, submerged in his thoughts [about the Hereafter], sparing in his friendship, easy going and of soft temperament. He is firmer than a hard rock but humbler than a slave.
The beauty of a believer’s face is from the special favour of Allah on him.
Verily the certitude of a believer is seen in his actions and the doubt of a hypocrite is seen in his actions.
A believer is sagacious and intelligent.
A believer is free from perversion and dissension.
A believer is penitent, repentant and remorseful.
The nature of a believer is [being] sincere and his trait is suppressing anger.
The believers are such that their good deeds are expected and people are safe from their evil.
The fear of a believer is in his heart and his repentance is in his admission.
Three things are adornments for believers: fear of Allah, truthful speech and returning trusts [to their rightful owners].
The beauty of a believer is his piety.
The joy of a believer is in the obedience of his Lord, and his sorrow is due to his sin.
The integrity of a believer is in his keeping away from what is forbidden and hastening towards virtues.
A believer is easy going, polite, approachable and reliable.
A believer makes few mistakes and does plenty of work.
The demeanour of a believer is characterized by moderation and his conduct is upright.
A believer loathes idle play and likes to work hard.
When the soul of a believer ascends to the heavens, the angels are amazed and say: It is incredible how he was saved from a place where the best of us2 got corrupted.
A believer is sorrowful in his thoughts [about himself], sparing in his friendship.
A believer has a mild disposition and is easy going.
A believer does not oppress [anyone] and eschews sin.
A believer is fair to the one who is unfair to him.
A believer is affectionate, endearing and compassionate.
Indeed believers are approachable and soft-hearted.
Believers are indeed virtuous.
Indeed believers are fearful [of Allah].
A believer is [gauged] by his actions.
Believers possess more intelligence [than others]. apprehensive [of the punishment of Allah].
The human being is [distinguished] by his intellect.
The uprightness of a human being is in controlling the tongue and doing good deeds.

He (‘a) said about the one whom he censured: He does not anticipate any misfortune and does not humble himself in piety. He does not know the door of guidance so as to go towards it, nor [does he know] the door of perdition so as to turn away from it.
The fruit of intimacy with Allah is keeping aloof from the people.
How can one become intimate with Allah when he has not separated himself from the creation?
One who is intimate with Allah keeps aloof from the people.
One who keeps aloof from the people, becomes intimate with Allah, the Glorified.
The comfort of security is removed by the anxiety of loneliness and the apprehension of fear disturbs the familiarity of society.
Intimacy is in three [people]: A compatible wife, a righteous child and an agreeable brother.
The most deserving of intimacy among the people is the close friend.
Acting slowly is praiseworthy in everything except in opportunities for [doing] good.
Taking time [to ascertain] is better than making haste, except in opportunities for [doing] good.
Deliberateness is judiciousness.
Deliberateness brings about assurance.
Deliberateness in action protects against errancy.
Through deliberateness, matters become easy.
Confidence in speech protects from slips and mistakes.
Through deliberateness, means become easy.
Slowly! Darkness is disappearing; as though those who had departed have arrived [at their final destination] and those who hasten will soon join.

Bind your haste with your deliberateness, your domination with your friendliness and your evil [traits] with your good [ones]. Help the intellect overcome vain desires and you will possess understanding.
You must adopt deliberateness, for indeed one who acts unhurriedly is deserving of success.
In deliberateness there is [precaution and] assurance.
In deliberateness there is safety.
One who acts without haste is saved from mistakes.
There is no success for one who has no deliberateness.
Deliberateness is a virtue.
Deliberateness is success.
One who acts unhurriedly is deserving of success.
The one who acts with deliberateness is successful even if he perishes.
The one who acts without haste is either successful or close to success.
Strengthening oneself is [a sign of] judiciousness.
How close is misery to felicity, and death to life.
Stinginess is one of the two forms of poverty.
Stinginess earns dishonor and makes one enter hellfire.
Stinginess in spending from one’s wealth that which Allah, the Glorified, has made obligatory, is the worst type of stinginess.

Protect yourselves from vehement miserliness, malice, anger and jealousy and prepare for each of these things a contrivance which you can fight it with, like thinking about the consequence, refraining [from] vice, seeking virtue, improving your Hereafter and espousing forbearance.
Be wary of stinginess, for it is ignobility and [leads to] vilification.
Be wary of avarice, for verily it brings hate, tarnishes [one’s] good qualities and exposes [one’s] faults.
I bid you not to adorn yourself with stinginess, for it will disparage you near those who are close to you and will make your hated by your relatives.
I bid you to refrain from avarice, for it is the garment of indigence and the bridle that is used to drive one towards every [type of] vileness.
I bid you to refrain from stinginess, for the miser is hated by strangers and shunned by those who are close to him.
The worst stinginess is withholding money from those who deserve it.
Stinginess is [a form of] poverty.
Avarice leads to vilification.
Making too many excuses is a sign of stinginess.
Avarice earns vilification.
Stinginess degrades its possessor.
Stinginess earns condemnation.
Stinginess gives rise to hatred.
Stinginess with what is available [in one’s possession] is thinking negatively of God.
Stinginess humiliates its possessor and elevates the one who turns away from it.
Through stinginess, vilification increases.
The worst trait is stinginess.
Excessive avarice sullies chivalry and spoils brotherhood.
In avarice there is vilification (and dishonour).
Excessive avarice leads to vilification.
If you were to see stinginess in the form of a man, you would have surely seen an ugly, disfigured person.
If you were to see stinginess in the form of a man, you would have surely seen a disfigured person, from whom every eye would look away and every heart would turn away.
One who persists in avarice is deprived of [sincere] advisers.
Avarice is one of the most revolting traits.
How revolting is stinginess with affluence!
How revolting is stinginess by those who possess nobility.
Nothing brings down the wrath of Allah like stinginess.
The honourable do not flee from death the way they flee from stinginess and the company of the wicked.
There is no vilification like avarice.
There is no alienation like avarice.
There is no magnanimity with avarice.
There is no evil trait worse than avarice.
There is no evil trait worse than stinginess
A miser is stingy towards himself with little of his worldly possessions and leaves all the rest for his heirs.
A miser gives up of more of his honour than what he holds of his possessions and loses multiple times more of his religion than what he saves of his property.
The farthest of creatures from Allah, the Exalted, is the wealthy miser.
The most miserly with his possessions is the most generous with his honour.
The most miserly of all people is the one who is stingy to himself with his wealth, and [eventually] leaves it behind for his heirs.
The miser is dispraised, the envious is disheartened.
The miser is a treasurer for his heirs.
A miser hastens poverty.
A miser is always disgraced.
A miser always comes up with excuses and pretexts.
A miser is abased among those who are dear to him.

I am amazed at the wretched miser who rushes towards the poverty that is fleeing him and loses the wealth that is seeking him; he lives a life of poverty in this world and is called to account with the reckoning of the wealthy in the Hereafter.
The avaricious has no friend.
The miser has no close friend.
He who is stingy to himself with his wealth is not successful and leaves behind his possessions for others.
One who withholds his hand out of fear of poverty has [actually] hastened poverty.
One who is stingy with his wealth is abased.
One who is miserly with that which he does not [even] possess, has exceeded in meanness.
One who withholds his hand from [spending on] his family has only held back one hand from them but caused many hands to be withheld by them [against him].
One who is stingy with his wealth towards himself, is generous with it to his wife’s [next] husband.
He who is stingy to the one who needs what he possesses, Allah’s wrath upon him increases.
He who is stingy with his favours has not fastened his faith [and made it firm].
He who is stingy with his favours is not intelligent.
While passing by some filth in a cesspit, he (‘a) said: This is what you were competing for yesterday. And in another narration, he said: This is what the misers were stingy with.
Woe to the miser who hastens towards the poverty which has fled from him and abandons the wealth that has sought him.
Do not be stingy by acting tightfistedly; and do not waste by acting extravagantly.
There is no magnanimity in a miser.
Nothing holds back wealth except stinginess, and a miser is blameworthy and liable for punishment.
A miser is rebuked in this world, and punished and chastised in the Hereafter.
Take the initiative to act, belie [false] hope and recall death.
Take the initiative to act and fear the suddenness of death, [then] you will realize the greatest hope.
Hasten towards [virtuous] actions before old age disables you.
Hasten towards [virtuous] actions before debilitating illness or sudden death [overtakes you].
Hasten towards virtue, for verily virtuous deeds are an opportunity [to secure your Hereafter].
Take the initiative to perform good deeds [now] while the neck is free from the noose and the spirit is unfettered.
Take the initiative in your youth before your old age and in your health before your illness.
Take the initiative in your affluence before your poverty and while you are alive before your death.
Take the initiative while the rest of your life is before you, and you have the ability to act by volition1, and have the opportunity of repentance, and the possibility of abrogating your misdeeds.
Hasten to act while the bodies are healthy, the tongues are untied, the [cry of] repentance is heard and the deeds are accepted.
Hasten to act before [you are seized with] the seizing of the all-Powerful, the Omnipotent.
Hasten to act before the narrowness and constriction [of the grave].
Hasten to act before the terror [of death] and the departure of your soul [from your body].
Hasten towards good deeds before your deaths, and purchase what will remain for you [in the Hereafter] with what will depart from you [of this world].
Hasten [to do good] with your wealth before your deaths come upon you, so that it may purify you, set you aright and bring you closer [to Allah].
Hasten towards obedience [to Allah] and you will be felicitous.
Hasten towards good and you will be guided.
Hasten [to do good] before the coming of the hidden awaited one.
Anticipate death and its throes, prepare for it before its arrival and get ready for it before it descends.
Hasten [to act] in the period of guidance and repose of the bodies, and in your remaining lifetime, and while you have the ability to act by volition.

Hasten in performing your good deeds and compete with your deaths, for you will be compensated for what you sent forward, rewarded for what you did beforehand and held accountable for what you left behind.
Surpass your hope and anticipate the assault of death, for people are on the verge of having their hopes cut short and being surprised by death.
Hurry to take advantage of opportunity before it becomes [a cause of] distress.
Blessed is the one who hastens to perform good deeds before his means are cut short.
Blessed is he who anticipates death, takes advantage of respite and prepares the provision of good deeds [for the Hereafter].
Be cautious of the cold [of winter] at its onset and embrace it towards its ending, for it acts upon the bodies as it acts upon the branches its beginning scorches and its end causes leaves to grow.

topic: Righteousness and Those Who prevent it
text: The righteous act is an action that reforms.

topic: Righteousness and Those Who prevent it
text: The righteous act is a good deed.

topic: Righteousness and Those Who prevent it
text: Righteousness is the prize of the judicious.

topic: Righteousness and Those Who prevent it
text: Righteousness is the quickest in acquiring reward.

topic: Righteousness and Those Who prevent it
text: Through righteousness the free man is owned.

topic: Righteousness and Those Who prevent it
text: Hastening to perform righteous acts increases [one’s] righteousness.

topic: Righteousness and Those Who prevent it
text: The best benefaction is that which reaches the free.

topic: Righteousness and Those Who prevent it
text: The best righteous act is that which reaches the needy.

topic: Righteousness and Those Who prevent it
text: In every righteous act there is gratitude.

topic: Righteousness and Those Who prevent it
text: One who prevents righteousness is deprived of gratitude.

topic: Righteousness and Those Who prevent it
text: Whoever extends his righteousness, his renown spreads.

topic: Righteousness and Those Who prevent it
text: One whose righteousness is close [at hand], his reputation goes far [and wide].

topic: Righteousness and Those Who prevent it
text: One who follows up one good act with another good act and bears the offences of his brothers and neighbours has perfected [his] virtue.

topic: Righteousness and Those Who prevent it
text: One who is miserly towards you with his cheerfulness will not be generous with his righteousness.

topic: Righteousness and Those Who prevent it
text: One of the best righteous acts is being kind to the orphans.

topic: Righteousness and Those Who prevent it
text: With righteousness, mercy flows forth abundantly.

topic: Righteousness and Those Who prevent it
text: The righteous tongue rejects the foolishness of the ignorant.

topic: Righteousness and Those Who prevent it
text: One whose righteousness increases is praised.

topic: Righteousness and Those Who prevent it
text: Urging the self towards altruism is from the qualities of the righteous.
One who insists [too much] makes others fed up of him.
The innocent one is healthy, the suspicious one is sick.
The innocent one is fearless.
How courageous the innocent one is and how timid is the suspicious one!
No one is more courageous than an innocent person.
Every innocent one is well.
Cheerfulness is one of the two forms of hospitality.
Cheerfulness is [a form of] kindness.
Cheerfulness is a trap for [ensnaring] affection.
Adopt cheerfulness for it is indeed a trap for [ensnaring] affection.
There is no cheerfulness with annoyance.
Cheerfulness cools down the fire of opposition.
Cheerfulness is the first gift [that can be given].
Cheerfulness is the trait of the free.
Cheerfulness makes companions affable.
Cheerfulness renders goodness without any expense.
By cheerfulness and keeping a smiling face, the act of giving becomes virtuous.
Your cheerfulness is your first righteous act and your promise is your first gift.
Your cheerfulness shows the nobility of your soul and your humility points to your righteous character.
Being cheerful is the first gift and the easiest [form of] generosity.
Cheerfulness is one of the two glad tidings.
Cheerfulness is the disposition of all those who are [truly] free.
Being cheerful is one of the signs of success.
The cause of affection is cheerfulness.
Smiling with cheerfulness, [practicing] benevolence, [performing] righteous actions and bestowing greetings invites the love of the people.
Increased cheerfulness is a sign of benevolence.
A cheerful face is better than a serious, frowning face.
Cheerfulness is one of the two gifts.
Cheerfulness is a delightful countenance and a radiant disposition.
Cheerfulness is kindness, frowning is meanness.
Cheerfulness is the beginning of righteousness.
Keeping a cheerful face is a trait of the free.
Cheerfulness is the first gift.
Where are the eyes that glance at the [illuminated] signposts of piety?
The most observant person is one who sees his own faults and refrains from his sins.

[It is narrated that at one time some people looked at a passing woman with lust, at which point the Imam (‘a) said:] Verily the eyes of these virile males are covetous and this glancing is the cause of their lust. Whenever any of you sees a woman whom he finds attractive, he should go to his wife, because she [too] is a woman like her.
Indeed the perceptive person is one who listens and then ponders, sees then reflects, and derives benefit from examples.
It is through observation [and reflection] that lessons are learned.
The loss of eyesight is better than the blinding of insight.
Loss of vision is better than looking at something that causes temptation.
Sometimes the one who can see [also] loses his way.
Loss of eyesight is easier than loss of insight.
One who has lost his sight makes wrong judgments.
Indeed the secrets have been revealed for people of insight.
You are shown if you observe, made to hear if you listen, and guided if you seek guidance.
Whoever reflects with astuteness, wisdom gets established for him and he understands the lesson [of the past].
Eyesight is of no benefit if insight is blinded.
One who does not ponder has no insight.
The glance is a pathfinder of infatuations.
Many a passion is aroused by a [single] glance.
The blinding of sight is better than a lot of gazing [at what is forbidden].
How many a passion has been aroused from a [single] glance!
How many gazes have led to regret!
A person’s glance is the scout of his heart.
One who glances [everywhere] freely, his regret increases.
Vision is not attained by sight [alone], for sight can fool its possessor.
Wantonness takes away blessings and brings chastisement.

One who is pleased with the action of a group is like one who participates in it with them, and for everyone who participates in falsehood there are two sins: the sin of being pleased with it and the sin of acting upon it.
Falsehood is the opposer of truth.
Falsehood is a deceptive beguiler.
Falsehood is the weakest supporter.
Falsehood [is like a mount that] makes its rider stumble.
Falsehoods hurl one into deviations.
Collaborating in support of falsehood is vileness and treachery.
Oppose the one who opposes the truth for falsehood; and leave him and that which he has chosen for himself.
Seeking assistance in support of falsehood is a serious offence and an act of treachery.
One who helps falsehood has oppressed the truth.
How can one separate from falsehood when he has not attached [himself] to the truth?
Falsehood has a [fixed] circuit.
There is no joy in a flash of lightening for one who is immersed in darkness.
One who embarks on falsehood, regrets.
One whose falsehood increases, his truth will never be accepted.
One who rides on falsehood, his mount will destroy him.
One who embarks on falsehood, his feet will slip.
One whose goal is falsehood will not perceive the truth even if it is more manifest than the sun.
One who supports falsehood, regrets.
How ugly falsehood is!
The one who employs falsehood is chastised and condemned.
One who resorts to falsehood does not become powerful.
The aim of the falsifier is [to cause] corruption.

topic: The Stomach and the Private Parts
text: Protect your stomach and your private parts from what is forbidden.

topic: The Stomach and the Private Parts
text: Protect your stomach and your private parts, for in these two lie your trials [and afflictions].

topic: The Stomach and the Private Parts
text: A man’s stomach is his enemy.

topic: The Stomach and the Private Parts
text: How far is goodness from the one whose efforts are [solely] for his stomach and private parts!

topic: The Stomach and the Private Parts
text: The most detested servant in the sight of Allah, the Glorified, is the one whose concern (and effort) is [solely] for his stomach and his private parts.
Wake up early [in the morning] for there is blessing in early rising; and consult each other, for success is in consultation.
Weeping out of fear of Allah, because of being far from Allah, is the worship of the cognizant.
Weeping out of the fear of Allah illuminates the heart and protects [one] from repetition of sin.
Weeping out of the fear of Allah is the key to [divine] mercy.
Weeping is the trait of the soft-hearted [and those who fear Allah].
By weeping out of the fear of Allah, sins get purified.
The weeping of a servant out of the fear of Allah clears away his sins.
Blessed is the one who is granted success in his worship and weeps because of his sins.
The worst of countries is the country in which there is neither peace nor productivity.
The worst homelands are those in which the inhabitants are not safe.
There is no country (or city) that has a greater right over you than another; the best country is the one that bears you.
Eloquence is that which is easy on speech and light on reasoning.1
Eloquence is to reply without hesitation and [to speak] correctly, without making mistakes.
Conciseness can be enough of an eloquence.
One who undertakes the rending and mending of speech has attained eloquence.
The tools of rhetoric are: an intelligent mind and an eloquent tongue.
Sometimes even the eloquent one is left speechless.
One whose attention reduces is [taken unawares and] thrown down.
While recalling the [rule of the] Umayyads (he said): It is the spittle from the deliciousness of [this temporary] life; they [shall] taste it for a short while and then spit it all out.
Verily the [only] concern of quadrupeds (i.e. animals with four legs) is their stomachs.
Indeed the [only] concern of predators is attacking other animals.
There is no shamelessness like fabricating lies.
Visiting the House of Allah is a safeguard against the torment of hellfire.

Verily this wealth is not for me or you, rather it belongs to the Muslims and [is] for obtaining their weapons [of defence]; so if you participate in their war [with them] then you are a partner in it, otherwise that which their hands have acquired cannot be for other than their [own] consumption.
Do business with Allah and you will profit.
Whoever does business with Allah, profits.
One who carries out transactions without knowledge, falls into usury.
The merchant puts himself at risk [of doing something that is forbidden].
What a good purifier earth is!

topic: Abandoning for the Sake of Allah
text: One who abandons something for the sake of Allah, the Glorified, is granted something better than it by Allah.
Repentance is heartfelt regret, seeking forgiveness with the tongue, abandoning [the sin] with the limbs and a determination never to repeat it again.
Be careful not to make haste in sinning and to delay repentance, thereby making your punishment greater.
Is there no one who is repentant for his sins before his death comes?
Repentance is an eraser [of bad deeds].
One who confesses his sins [and feels regret] is repentant.
Repentance causes [divine] mercy to descend.
Sincere repentance cancels [one’s] sins.
Repentance purifies the hearts and washes away sins.
Through repentance, sins are purged.
Through repentance, sins are expiated.
The fruit of repentance is correcting the excesses of the self.
Sincere repentance erases misdeeds.
One who repents [with sincerity] has indeed returned [to Allah].
One who is granted repentance will not be deprived of its acceptance.
How devastating repentance is for the great crimes [one commits]!

There is no good in this world except for two [types of] people: the person who makes amends for the sins that he commits, through repentance, and the person who struggles against his lower-self in obedience to Allah, the Glorified.
The smallest [amount of] repentance and seeking forgiveness purges sins and repeated misdeeds.
It is by returning [to Allah] that forgiveness is gained.
The foundation of contentment is complete reliance on Allah.
Relying on Allah is the strongest hope.
Acquiring [divine] reward is the best achievement and coming close to Allah is the pinnacle of success.
Reward is gained in proportion to the difficulty endured.
There is no gain like divine reward.
There is no provision [for the Hereafter] like reward [for good deeds].
Raise your garment (i.e. do not let it be too long) for that is purer for you, safer for your heart and more long-lasting on you.
Wear that which neither makes you famous nor degrades you.
Be wary of cowardice for it is indeed disgraceful and [is] a deficiency.
Cowardice is an affliction and impuissance is feeble-mindedness.
Extreme cowardice stems from impuissance of the self and weakness of conviction.
The best striving is that which is accompanied by [divinely granted] success.
You must be diligent even if you are not assisted by [good] fortune.
One who is diligent becomes fortunate.
Striving has been linked to achievement.
One whose diligence becomes weaker, his opponent gets stronger.
Whoever embarks upon [any action with] diligence, overpowers his opponent.
One who employs diligence arrives at his goal.
One who strives with all his effort arrives at the core of his desired objective.
Striving is useless without accomplishment.
Striving is useless without [divinely given] success.
Experiences don’t end.
Experiences are beneficial knowledge.
Experience bears the fruit of learning.
The fruit of experience is making the right choice.
Preservation of experiences is the pinnacle of intelligence.
The best of what you have experienced is that which taught you a lesson.
In every experience there is an admonition.
Experiences suffice as educators.
One who experiences, increases in judiciousness.
One whose experiences increase, his negligence decreases.
One who consolidates the experiences [he has had] will be safe from danger.
One who discards experiences becomes blind to the consequences [of his actions].
Whoever preserves [and learns from his] experiences, his actions become correct.
One who lacks experience is [easily] deceived.
The experienced person is more proficient than a doctor [who is inexperienced].
Anxiety during hardship completes [and enhances] the calamity.
Anxiety during adversity is severer than the adversity itself.
The adversity is one, but if you become anxious it becomes twofold.
Adversity [endured] with patience is the better of the two adversities.
Anxiety does not ward off destiny, rather it blocks recompense.
Anxiety during adversity increases it whereas patience ends it.
Overcome anxiety with patience, for anxiety voids recompense and magnifies the calamity.
Anxiety is [a cause of] destruction.
Anxiety is one of the assistants of the [difficult] time.
Anxiety magnifies the calamity.
Anxiety is more exhausting than patience.
If you are [one who gets] anxious about all that has escaped from your hands, then be anxious about what has not reached you.
With excessive anxiety, the calamity is magnified.
Counter anxiety with patience.
There is no recompense with anxiety.
Whoever becomes anxious, his adversity increases.
One who is overcome by anxiety is deprived of the merit of patience.
One who becomes anxious has tormented himself, neglected the command of Allah, the Glorified, and sold off his reward.
Do not get anxious in the [face of] little that you dislike for it will put you in a lot of what you dislike.
Patience and anxiety do not go together.
One who believes in [divine] requital does not choose [to do] anything but good.
One who is certain about requital does not choose [to do] anything but good.
The reward is proportionate to the tribulation [endured].
The grant [of reward] from Allah is proportionate to the [sincerity of] intention.
One who is not certain of the recompense [for actions], doubt has corrupted his certitude.

Never make haste in reacting harshly and never be quick to punish when there is an alternative, for this causes depletion of the faith and brings closer the transformations [of blessing into calamity].
The quickest punishment is the punishment for transgression.
Verily Allah, the Glorified, has ordained punishment for committing sins against Him in order to save His servants from His chastisement.
The punishment of noble ones is better than the forgiveness of the vile ones.
The punishment of the hot tempered, spiteful and jealous people starts from [within] themselves.
The punishment of the intelligent is [in the form of] insinuation.
The punishment of the ignorant is [in the form of open] declaration.
There is no protector for one who is sought by Allah [for punishment].
Whoever punishes the one who is apologetic has committed a grave injustice.
One who punishes [a person] for [having committed] an offence has no merit.1
Not every sinner deserves to be punished.
How repulsive is punishment [that is meted out] despite apology.
Serving the body is granting it whatever it seeks of pleasures and desires and what it covets, but in [all] this is the destruction of the soul.
Physical health is one of the most wholesome bounties.
How can one be deceived by the health of a body that is prone to malady?
Beware of antipathy, for it corrupts brotherhood and makes one despised by Allah and the people.
Antipathy is a disgrace and sinning is [a cause of] destruction.
Antipathy spoils brotherhood.
When acts of kindness increase and forbearance becomes strong, loftiness is attained.

He (‘a) was asked about intercourse, so he said: [It is] shame that is lifted, loins that are joined and the closest thing to insanity. Persistence in it makes one senile and revival from it brings regret. When lawful, its fruit is a son who, if he lives, subjects [one] to trial and if he dies, causes sadness.
External beauty is [in possessing] good looks.
Internal beauty is [in possessing] a good heart.
The beauty of a man is his clemency.
The beauty of a man is dignity.
Beauty of the freeman is [in] keeping away from dishonour.
The purity of beauty is [in] chastity.
One whose beautiful actions increase, the people unite in elevating him.
Grooming oneself is an apparent [form of] magnanimity.
Self-grooming is a characteristic of the believers.
Not everyone who is moderate in seeking [his livelihood] is deprived.1

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: Paradise is the best place of return and hellfire is the worst place of residence.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: Indeed, I have not seen any place whose seeker is in slumber like Paradise and any place whose fleer is in slumber like hellfire.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: Verily the people of Paradise constitute all the believers who are easygoing and gentle.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: Verily Allah, the Exalted, makes whomever He wishes, from those of his servants who posses sincere intentions and righteous hearts, enter Paradise.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: Paradise is the abode of peace.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: If you must be desirous of something, then be desirous of a Paradise, the span of which covers the heavens and the earth.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: Paradise is the reward of the obedient.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: Paradise is the abode of the pious.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: Paradise is the goal of the foremost [in righteousness].

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: Paradise is the most excellent goal.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: Paradise is the returning place of the victorious.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: Paradise is the reward of every righteous believer.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: Paradise is attained through keeping away from sins.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: Verily you will not enter Paradise until you restrain yourself from misdeeds and stop [committing them]; and deter yourself from sins and desist [from them].

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: If you believe in Allah and abstain from what He has forbidden, He will put you in the Abode of Peace, and if you please Him, He will cover you with [divine] favour.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: The price of Paradise is good deeds.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: The price of Paradise is renunciation of the [pleasures of this] world.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: The chiefs of the people of Paradise are the generous and the pious.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: The chiefs of the people of Paradise are the sincere ones.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: The chiefs of the people of Paradise are the God-fearing and the virtuous.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: Seeking Paradise without good deeds is foolishness.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: Paradise is not achieved [simply] by wishing for it.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: Neither a swindler nor one who put others under obligation, will enter Paradise.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: None will be victorious in attaining Paradise except one whose heart is good and intention sincere.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: Every bliss other than Paradise is derisory.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: None will be victorious in attaining Paradise except the one who works hard for it.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: None shall attain Paradise except the one who struggles against his [lower] self.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: One who yearns for Paradise forgets his [worldly] desires.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: Paradise is attained through abstaining from sins.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: One who shuns what is forbidden shall attain Paradise.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: How impossible! Allah cannot be cheated of His Paradise, and none can attain what is with Him except by His pleasure.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: The delegation that enters Paradise is constantly showered with blessings.

topic: Paradise and the People of Paradise
text: Those who enter Paradise are in perpetual bliss.
Generosity for the sake of Allah is the worship of those who are close [to Allah].
Generosity without fear or hope of recompense is true generosity.
Give generously and you will be honoured.
The most generous of you is the one who will gain the most.
The most excellent of noble traits is generosity.
The best generosity is to forgive after gaining the upper hand.
The greatest generosity is being open-handed with whatever is available.
The greatest generosity is delivering the rights to their [rightful] owners.
The greatest generosity is giving despite [facing] hard times.
Generosity is [true] leadership, sovereignty is [only] administration.
Generosity is a present honour.
Generosity is the protector of honour.
The bane of generosity is poverty.
The bane of generosity is wastefulness.
Through generosity, authority is acquired.
Generosity stems from nobility of character.
Through generosity, men gain authority.
Through generosity, distinction is established and praise is acquired.
Be generous with whatever you have, [and] you will be praised.
Be generous and you will gain authority; be patient and you will be triumphant.
The generosity of the poor is the best generosity.
Be generous with what is available, fulfil your promises and be loyal with the trusts [that have been entrusted to you].
The generosity of a poor person dignifies him and the stinginess of a rich person debases him.
Be generous with that which perishes and you will be compensated for it with that which lasts.
Be generous for the sake of Allah and struggle against your selves in obedience to Him, He will [in return] magnify your reward and increase His favour upon you.
Generosity is the practice of the honourable.
The highest extent of generosity is giving [from] whatever is available.
One who is open-handed does good to others.
One who is generous gains authority.
One who does not show generosity is not praised.
How excellent is generosity when in straitened circumstances!
One who does not give generously while he is praised has to give away while he is dispraised.
One who does not give generously does not gain authority.
The generosity of a man endears him to his rivals and his stinginess makes him hated by his [own] children.
The generous person is loved and praised, even if nothing of his generosity reaches his praiser, and the stingy person is the opposite of this.
The one who is generous is praised in this world and felicitous in the Hereafter.
Verily the masters of the people of this world (and the Hereafter) are the generous.
Be generous with the truth and miserly with falsehood.
Be [either] selflessly generous or moderate in giving but do not be from the third kind (i.e. the misers).
One who is close to Allah is safe, while [one who is] His enemy is frightened.
Proximity to Allah is granted to those who obey Him and keep away from disobedience to Him.
The worst of neighbours is the wicked neighbour.
A wicked neighbour is the greatest adversity and the most serious tribulation.
Be a neighbour to one from whose evil you are safe and whose goodness does not turn away from you.
Ask about the neighbour before the house.
Being a bad neighbour and offending the virtuous are the worst forms of vileness.
One who is neighbourly gets many neighbours.
One who is good to his neighbours gets many helpers.
Taking care of one’s neighbour is an act of magnanimity.
Hunger is better than the humiliation of subjugation.
Keeping oneself hungry is the most beneficial cure, whereas eating to one’s fill increases maladies.
Hunger is better than subjugation.
Complement your food with hunger and discipline yourself with contentment.
The best condiment is hunger.
How good an assistant of piety hunger is!
How good an assistant in cutting down the [desires of the carnal] self and breaking its [bad] habits hunger is!
The alms-tax of high rank [and power] is benefitting others with it.
One of the obligations of a person who possesses a high rank is to use it to grant the [needs of] one who seeks from him.
One who benefits others with his high rank makes himself praiseworthy.
Whoever makes an effort to strive in obedience to Allah and His messenger, his soul shall be safe and sound [from the torments of the Hereafter] and his transaction will be profitable and gainful.

The first thing which you overcome through Jihād is through striving with your hands, then [if this is not possible] by your tongue, then [if this is not possible] with your hearts; and the one who neither supports good with his heart nor censures evil, is turned upside down (i.e. will face the wrath of Allah).
Struggling [in the way of Allah] is the pillar of faith and the path of the felicitous.
The doors of the heavens are opened for those who strive [in the way of Allah].

If the people who came before me complained about the injustice of their rulers, then today I complain about the injustice of my people; it is as if I am led and they are the leaders, [and] I am restrained and they are the restrainers.
The reward for striving [in the way of Allah] is the greatest reward.
And [Allah has prescribed] Jihād as [a means of preserving the] honour of Islam.
Strong determination and lavishness do not go together.
The purification of the body is [in] striving and fasting.
Indeed Jihād is the price of Paradise, so the one who struggles against his self will acquire it, and this is the greatest reward of Allah for the one who is cognizant of it.
The best Jihād is the struggle of a man against his [carnal] soul.
The best Jihād is the struggle of the self against lustful desires, and its weaning away from the pleasures of this world.
The first thing that you disavow from Jihād is struggling against your selves.
The last things that you [should] lose are: the struggling against your selves and obedience to those who have authority among you.
Indeed the best Jihād is the struggle of a man against his [carnal] soul.
Verily struggling against the self restrains it from sins and protects it from destruction.
Verily the one who struggles with his [lower] self, in obedience to Allah and against disobedience to Him, has the status of a virtuous martyr in the sight of Allah.

Indeed the one who struggles against his [lower] self, overcomes his anger and is careful in obeying [the commandments of] Allah, is raised by Allah, the Glorified, to the status of the one who fasts by day and stands in prayer by night, and is granted the rank of the patient soldier [who fights in His way].
Verily if you struggle against your [lower] self you will obtain the pleasure of Allah.
The fruit of struggle [against the self] is overpowering the self.
Struggling against the self is the dowry for Paradise.
Struggling against vain desires is the price of Paradise.
Struggling against the self is the best Jihad.
Struggle against your [lower] self and seek repentance, you will be successful in the obedience of your Lord.

Struggle against your vain desires, overcome your anger and resist your bad habits, [by this] your soul will become pure, your intellect will become perfect and the reward of your Lord will be complete.

Fight against your [lower] self in obedience to Allah the way an enemy would fight his enemy, and overpower it the way a rival would overpower his opponent, for indeed the strongest person is the one who subdues his self.

Struggle against your [lower] self and call it to account the way a partner would hold his partner accountable, and demand from it the right of Allah the way an adversary would demand from his foe, for verily the most felicitous of people is the one who undertakes to hold his self to account.
Struggling against the [lower] self is the price of Paradise, so the one who struggles against it will acquire it, and this is the greatest reward of Allah for the one who is cognizant of it.
Struggling against the self with knowledge is a symbol of intelligence.
Fighting anger with forbearance is evidence of nobility.
The most excellent Jihād is struggling against the self.
The highest form of struggle is for a man to struggle against his self.
It is sufficient for you, in your struggle against your [lower] self, that you always prevail over it and fight its vain desires.
One who fights his [lower] self perfects his piety.
One who knows his self struggles against it.
One who does not struggle against his self will not achieve victory.
There is no struggle more worthy than struggling against the self.
Struggling against the self is a trait of the noble ones.
Struggling against the self is a symbol of nobility.
Struggling against the self is the best Jihād.
There is no Jihād like struggle against the self.
Ignorance and miserliness are bad and harmful.
Ignorance in a human being is more harmful than gangrene [is] to the body.
Ignorance is a balky mount; whoever rides it stumbles and whoever accompanies it is led astray.
Ignorance of merits is one of the grossest demerits.
The greatest calamity is ignorance.
The worst ailment is ignorance.
The greatest ignorance is the ignorance of a person about himself.
The greatest ignorance is making enmity with the powerful, befriending the immoral and trusting the traitor.
Ignorance is a curse.
Ignorance is [a form of] death.
People are enemies of that which they are ignorant of.
Ignorance is the most harmful foe.
Ignorance makes one stumble.
Ignorance spoils the Hereafter.
Ignorance is the [primary] source of evil.
Ignorance is an ailment and a chronic disease.
Ignorance attracts peril.
Ignorance is the root of all evil.
Ignorance is the worst disease.
Ignorance corrupts all matters.
Ignorance makes one stumble and brings regret.
Ignorance causes the living to die and perpetuates misery.
Verily you will not attain any goal by ignorance, nor will you achieve any goodness by means of it, nor will you realize any of your wishes in the Hereafter through it.
It is through ignorance that every evil is instigated.
Many an ignorance is better than forbearance (or knowledge).
Ward off ignorance with knowledge.
Too much ignorance is destructive.
The worst affliction is ignorance.
Counter ignorance with knowledge.
The outcome of ignorance is loss; and the joy of the envious does not last.
The pinnacle of ignorance is for a person to brag about his ignorance.
Many a revered person has been humiliated by his ignorance.
Ignorance suffices as ignobility.
It suffices as ignorance for a person to be ignorant about himself.
It suffices as ignorance for a person to be pleased with himself.
It suffices as ignorance for a person to laugh without [a reason for] amusement.
It suffices as ignorance for a person to be ignorant of his limits [and standing in society].
It suffices as ignorance for a person to be ignorant of his flaw.
It suffices as ignorance for a person to be ignorant about his own faults and to malign people for that which he [himself] cannot turn away from.
It suffices as ignorance for a person to forbid people from that which he performs himself.
The language of ignorance is impoliteness.
One who gets uplifted by ignorance has opposed the intellect.
One who fights his ignorance with his knowledge succeeds with the most felicitous victory.
Being overcome by ignorance is one of the severest afflictions.
There is no poverty like ignorance.
With ignorance, no path is purified.
There is no poverty more severe than ignorance.
There is no abomination more disgraceful than ignorance.
There is no adversity more severe than ignorance.
The cornerstone of ignorance is animosity towards people.
An ignorant person is never found to be anything but falling short or excessive.
Neither does an ignorant restrain himself [from wrongdoing] nor does he benefit from good advice.
An ignorant person is one who obeys his vain desires in disobedience to his Lord.
The ignorant person feels aversion towards that which the wise person feels at ease with.
The ignorant person does not understand the learned because he [himself] was never learned before.
An ignorant person does not recognize his failure and does not accept the [good] advice given to him.
An ignorant person relies on his hopes and is negligent in his actions.
The ignorant person is like a rock through which water does not gush forth, and a tree, the branches of which do not become green, and a ground upon which foliage is not found.
An ignorant person is [like the] dead among the living.
The most wretched of all people is the ignorant one.
An unremorseful sinner is the most ignorant person.
The most ignorant person is one who is deceived by the praise of a flatterer who makes the ugly look appealing to him and makes him hate the [sincere] adviser.
The most hated creature in the sight of Allah is the ignorant person, because He deprived him of what He bestowed on His creation, and that is intellect.
Verily the ignorant is one whose ignorance leads astray and whose vain desires entice [towards evil]; so his speech is unhealthy and his action is blameworthy.
The ignorant one is perplexed.
The ignorant person inclines towards the one who is like him.
Man is an enemy of that which he is ignorant of.
The ignorant one does not restrain himself [from evil].
An ignorant person is a slave to his passions.
The ignorant person does not desist [from sinning].
An ignorant person seeks to raise himself but ends up abasing himself.
The ignorant person is one who is ignorant of his own capability.
An ignorant person is dead, even when he is alive.
The correctness of an ignorant person is like the mistake of a learned person (i.e. it happens rarely).
The ignorant person is deceived by [false] claims.
The ignorant person is one who is ignorant about his [own] affair.
The ignorant person is one who is deceived by his vain desires and his arrogance.
An ignorant person is one who takes his sincere advisor to be a deceiver.
When the ignorant one becomes stingy (or denies), he obtains [wealth] and when he obtains [wealth] (or professes belief in one God), he apostatizes.
Indeed the ignorant person is one who is enslaved by [worldly] pursuits.
When an ignorant person grows older, his ignorance rises.
The wealth of an ignorant person is in his worldly possessions and his hopes.
The reign of an ignorant person is like a stranger who [soon] moves to another place.
Many an ignorant person is saved by his ignorance.
The slip-ups of an ignorant person are excusable.
An ignorant king exposes his [own] flaws.
The worst person you can accompany is an ignorant one.
The correct [action] of an ignorant person is like the slip-up of an intelligent person.
The lost item of the ignorant person cannot be found.
Obedience to the foolish is a sign of ignorance.
Obedience to the foolish and being excessive [in speech or action] are two signs of ignorance.
The habit of the inexperienced [and ignorant] ones is to cut off the elements of favour.
The wealth of an ignorant person is in his worldly possessions.
The ignorant one is deceived by futile absurdities.
Every ignorant person is prone to temptation.1
For the ignorant there is loss in every situation.
One who is ignorant is disregarded [by others].
When one is ignorant, his consideration is reduced.
One who is ignorant of [a branch of] knowledge is hostile towards it.
One who does not know where he is placing his foot, trips.
One who is ignorant makes many blunders.
One who is ignorant becomes self-conceited; and his ‘today’ is worse than his ‘yesterday’.
It is from the nature of the ignorant to get angry quickly, in every situation.
No one antagonizes the learned like the ignorant [do].
Woe be to the one who persists in his ignorance and blessed is the one who realizes [his mistake] and finds the right course.
There is no independence for an ignorant person.
The ignorant one is not seen to be anything but immoderate (or excessive).
Nothing restrains the foolish except the edge of a sword.
Disobey the ignorant and you will be safe.
Hell is sufficient as a punishment.

He (‘a) said in his description of hell: [It is] a fire whose burning is intense, its roar is loud, its flames are rising, its blaze is incinerating, its groans are terrifying, its abatement is remote, its fuel is igniting, [and] its horrors are terrifying.

He (‘a) said while describing hell: Its inmate cannot leave, its prisoner cannot be released by ransom and its shackles cannot be broken. This abode has no fixed age so that it may perish, nor is there a lifespan for its inmates that they may pass away.
Verily all disbelieving schemers are inmates of the fire.
He (‘a) also said in his description of hellfire: Its pits are engulfed [with fire], its sides are pitch- dark, its vessels are scorching hot and everything about it is horrid.
None will be saved from the fire of hell except the one who abandons its actions (i.e. the actions that lead to it).
This tender skin does not have the tolerance to withstand the fire [of hell].
One who is afraid of hellfire keeps away from that which has been forbidden.
The inmates of hell are eternally tormented.
The one who enters hellfire is forever wretched.
The fuel of hellfire on the Day of Judgment will comprise of every rich person who was miserly towards the poor with his wealth and every learned scholar who sold his Hereafter for the world.
Be wary of the fire whose heat is intense, whose pit is deep and whose ornaments are made of [molten] iron.
Be wary of the fire whose tumultuous blaze is ready, its flames are intense and its torment is forever renewed.
Hellfire is the final end of the extremists.
Whoever loves us with his heart, supports us with his speech and fights our enemies with his sword, then he will be with us in Paradise at our stage.
Whoever loves us with his heart and supports us with his speech but does not fight alongside us with his hand, then he will be in Paradise but not at our stage.
Whoever loves us with his heart but pretends to hate us with his tongue will go to Paradise.
He who loves us should emulate our actions and clothe himself with piety.
One who loves us should prepare to be covered with afflictions.
One who befriends us should have a thick skin for tribulations [that will befall him].
Two types of people are destroyed because of me: the fanatic lover and the extreme hater.
If a mountain loved me, it would crumble.
Losing a loved one leads to forlornness.
One who loves you forbids you [from evil].
One who loves something speaks about it constantly.
Indeed only he who does not flatter you loves you, and only he who does not let you hear [his praise] praises you.
Let the most beloved person to you and the one who has the greatest status in your eyes be the one who strives hardest in benefiting people.
Let the most beloved person to you be the compassionate adviser.
The strength of the authority of evidence is stronger than the strength of the authority of force.
Allah, the Glorified, never leaves His servants without a necessary proof or an established, clear path.
Allah, the Glorified, does not leave His creation unheeded, nor does He neglect their affairs.
Allah, the Glorified, never lets His servants remain without a divinely appointed Prophet or a revealed book [to guide them].
One who is disproved has no right.

topic: The One who Presnts an Argument
text: The one who presents a strong argument may get support.

topic: The One who Presnts an Argument
text: One who argues by truth, succeeds.
The Hajj is a means of strengthening the religion.
Rage is a bout of insanity because its possessor regrets [afterwards], but if he does not feel regret, then his insanity is firmly established.
Repel [your] rage, think about the proof and protect yourself from nonsense - you will be safe from slip-ups.
One who is overly cautious may be destroyed.
Harm comes to the cautious one from his [own] place of security.
One who warns you is like the one who brings you glad tidings.
Soldiers [who fight for Islam] are the glory of religion and the bastions of [its] leaders.
Fleeing at the right moment is equivalent to victory in its time.
Soldiers are defenders of the people.
The bane of an army is opposing its commanders.
One who abandons his army has helped his adversaries.
Cast down your gaze in battles, for this will make you calmer and cause your hearts to be more tranquil.
Put the armoured man forward and the unarmoured one behind, and grit your teeth because this will make the swords skip off the skulls.
He who is frightened by what is in front of him retreats [and flees].
Defend [yourselves] with the edge of blades, charge forward [against the enemy] with your swords, give up your lives [for the sake of Allah] and walk towards death with calm.

By the one who splits the seed and creates the human being! They did not accept Islam, rather they succumbed to it [to remain safe] and hid their disbelief; and when they found supporters for it, they brought forth in the open that which they had hidden and made manifest that which they had concealed.

I swear by Allah! Even if you run away from the sword of this transitory world you will not be safe from the swords of the Hereafter. You are the foremost among the Arabs and the greatest figures [of the community], so be ashamed of fleeing [from the battlefield], for certainly in it is a covering of disgrace and [a cause of] entry into hellfire.
Do not fight against the one who seeks refuge in religion, for one who combats religion is ruined.
Do not combat the one who seeks the support of truth, for the one who fights the truth is [always] defeated.
Never seek to challenge anyone in combat, but if you are challenged, then respond; for the one who seeks it is an aggressor, and the aggressor is struck down.
Do not let the fleeing which is followed by return and the retreat that is followed by attack bear down

topic: on you. Give the swords their due right and prepare a place for the fallen [soldiers]
text: Embolden yourselves to charge with intensity and strike with full force, and silence the voices, as this dispels cowardice.

topic: on you. Give the swords their due right and prepare a place for the fallen [soldiers]
text: Keep on enduring and remain firm, until the pillar of truth illuminates upon you while you have the upper hand, and Allah is with you, and never will He stint [the reward of] your deeds.

topic: on you. Give the swords their due right and prepare a place for the fallen [soldiers]
text: Defend your religion with the edge of blades, charge forward [against the enemy] with your swords and seek the help of Allah you will gain victory and [His] assistance.

topic: on you. Give the swords their due right and prepare a place for the fallen [soldiers]
