Verily I have divorced this world thrice uncompromisingly, [such that] there is no return to it for me, and I have released it completely.
Indeed, if you approach this world you have turned your back [from the Hereafter].5
Indeed, when you turn your back on this world, you have approached [the Hereafter].6
Verily you have not been created for this world, so renounce it and turn away from it.
If you work for this world, your transaction will have made a loss.
Verily you will never meet Allah, the Glorified, with an action more harmful to you than love for this world.
Indeed, if you crave after this world, you will waste your lives for that which you will not remain for and that which will not remain for you.
Indeed, this world is only a trap into which those who do not recognize it fall.
This world is only [a place of] varying circumstances, changing situations and marked targets.
This world is only a corpse and those who establish bonds of brotherhood for [acquiring] it are similar to dogs, such that their brotherhood does not prevent them from harming each other for it.

The people [who seek] of this world are just like howling dogs or starving predators growling at each other. The mighty among them eat the meek and the big among them crush the small. Some are like tied cattle and some are like untied cattle that have lost their wits and are running in every direction.
You are only like the standing [and ready] riders who do not know when they will be ordered to march.
This world is only an enjoyment for a few days, then it will disappear like the mirage disappears and pass by like the clouds pass by.
Indeed, the only share of the earth for every one of you is the length and breadth of his own stature, [of the grave] wherein he would lie on his cheeks covered with dust.

Indeed this world is only the abode of passage and the Hereafter is the abode of [permanent] residence. So take [provisions] from the abode of passage for the abode of residence and do not tear your veils in front of the one who knows your secrets.

The example of those who have known this world is like a group of travellers who abandon a drought-stricken place and set off for a fruitful and fertile place. Then they endure the difficulties of the path, the hardships of the journey and the coarseness of the food in order to reach their fields of plenty and the place of their [permanent] residence.
Indeed man (in this world) is only a target that is struck by [the arrows of] death and a booty that is rushed towards by tribulations and calamities.
The bane of the soul is being infatuated with this world.
When this world comes towards a servant, it covers him with the merits of others and when it turns its back from him it snatches away his [own] merits.
When something of this world slips away from you then do not despair, and when you do good, do not put others under obligation.
This world ends with annihilation.
By preferring the love of this transient world, one ends up in an unpleasant state in the Hereafter.
How bad an abode this world is!
The worst choice is exchanging the everlasting with the transient.
Your remaining [in this world] is towards annihilation and your annihilation [from this world] is towards eternity.
Sell that which perishes for that which remains and exchange the wretchedness of this world for the abundant bounties of the Hereafter.
When you are deprived of something in this world, take comfort in the fact that it would have been with you [only] for a little while.
The fruit of infatuation with this world is great tribulation.
The one who seeks refuge in this world is ruined and the one who takes his fill from it is destroyed.
The bounty of this world is transient, its comfort is [marred by] trouble, its soundness is destruction and its gifts are taken away.
Love of this world is the source of every misdeed.
Love of this world is the source of trials and the root of tribulations.
Love of this world gives rise to avarice.
Love of this world corrupts the intellect, preoccupies the heart from listening to [words of] wisdom and leads to a painful chastisement [in the Hereafter].
The sweetness of this world leads to the bitterness of the Hereafter and an unpleasant ending.
The sweets of this world are like myrrh, its foods are poisons and its means are worn-out [and weak] ropes.
The living of this world are prone to death and its healthy are prone to sicknesses and the target of [the arrow of] death.
Wretchedness, annihilation, destruction and ruin have been decreed for the people of this world.
This world has been surrounded with lustful desires, liked for its immediate enjoyments, embellished with deceptions and sweetened with aspirations.
Wage war against yourselves for [keeping away from] this world and turn yourselves away from it, for it vanishes quickly, quakes frequently and transfers soon.
Neediness has been decreed for those from among the people of this world who seek to increase their wealth while those who get along without it have been assisted with comfort.
The good of this world is [a cause of] sorrow and its evil is [a cause of] regret.
The good of this world is insignificant and its evil is ready at hand.
Take from that which will not last for you for that which will last for you and will not separate from you.
Take from the little of this world that which suffices you and leave from its abundance that which makes you transgress.
Take from this world that which comes to you and turn away from that which turns away from you, but if you don’t do this then [at least] be moderate in what you seek.
Mingling with those who are attached to this world is the primary cause of affliction and corruption of piety.
Mingling with those who are attached to this world tarnishes religion and weakens certitude.
The significance of this world is little, its product is inferior, its delight is false and its bounties are illusory.
The aspiration and pursuit of one whose hope and desire is [acquiring felicity in] this world, is frustrated.
It is an abode which is fraught with tribulations and known for its treachery. Its circumstances do not last and its dwellers are not safe.
It is an abode which is lowly before its Lord, so its lawful has been mixed with its forbidden, its good with its evil and its sweetness with its bitterness.
It is the abode of transience, the resting place of the sinners, the residence of the wretched and the transgressors (or the repulsed and those who exceed the limits).

Allah, the Glorified, called you to the Eternal Abode and the permanent residence, and great blessings and proximity to the Prophets and the felicitous, but you sinned and turned away; whereas this world called you to an abode of wretchedness and the place of annihilation and different types of tribulations and hardships, but you obeyed it and quickly rushed [towards it].
Recalling [the pleasures of] this world is the worst of all maladies.
The humiliation of this world is the glory of the Hereafter.
Leave that which is little for that which is abundant and that which is limited for that which is vast.
The cornerstone of calamities is infatuation with this world.
Many an adviser from this world may be suspected by you.
Many a person who is truthful about this world is considered a liar by you.
Many a thing which one should be cautious of in this world is not taken into consideration by you.
You desire for the unachievable is [a sign of] ignorance.
Your being content with this world is from your bad choices and your wretched endeavours.
Increase in [one’s desire for] this world corrupts the Hereafter.
The ornaments of this world corrupt weak minds.
The cause of wretchedness is love of this world.
The cause of corruption of the mind is love of this world.
The sovereignty of this world is disgrace and its loftiness is lowness.
The joy of this world is deception and its enjoyment is destruction.
One’s seeking tranquillity in [the delights of] this world is from the greatest deceptions.
The worst of tribulations is love of this world.
The worst of afflictions is love for this world.
The health of this world is [fraught with] sicknesses and its pleasures are [fraught with] pains.
Adultery has become the key to lineage in the world (or among the people), chastity is rare and Islam is worn the wrong way up like fur.
Divorcing this world is the dowry for Paradise.
Seeking this world is the primary cause of tribulation.
The one who seeks this world through religion is chastised and condemned.
Seeking to join this world with the Hereafter is from the deceptions of the self.
The seeker of this world misses [the opportunity to work for] the Hereafter and death comes to him unexpectedly, and he does not get from this world except what has been apportioned for him.
He who turns away from the embellishments of this world gains the joy of the glad tidings [of Paradise].
I am amazed at the one who builds his transient abode and abandons his Eternal Abode.
The servant of this world faces continuous afflictions and calamities.
The end of this world is annihilation.
The deception of this world strikes [a person] down.
World, deceive the one who is ignorant of your tricks and for whom your traps of deceit are concealed.
He (‘a) said about this world: It is deceitful - that which is in it is illusory; it is perishing all that is upon it perishes.
It is deceitful, harmful, volatile, evanescent, transient and perishing.
The foods of this world are poisons and its means are worn-out [and weak] ropes.
In being averse to this world there is attainment of prosperity.
In the vicissitudes of this world there are lessons to be learnt.
In this world there is action without reckoning.
This world is what the wretched desire.
The two that are attached to each other may get detached and the two groups that are united may get separated.
Indeed, that which was sweet of this world has become bitter, and that which was clean of it has become dirty.
Indeed this world has embellished itself with its deception and it deceives [its inhabitants] with its embellishments.
Little of this world takes away a lot of the Hereafter.
The little of this world does not last and its abundance is not safe from calamities.

The mainstay of this world is by four [groups]: A scholar who acts on his knowledge, an ignorant person who is not too proud to learn, a wealthy person who is generous with his wealth to the needy and a poor person who does not sell his Hereafter for his worldly life. So when the scholar does not act on his knowledge, the ignorant one refuses to learn; and when the wealthy is miserly with his wealth, the poor one sells his Hereafter for his world.
Every gathering is [headed] towards dispersion.
Every profit of this world is a loss.
Everything that passes [away] is as if it never was.
Every ease of this world is difficulty.
Every provision of this world is trivial for the contented and the chaste.
Everything in this world [is such that it] seems greater when heard than when seen.
All the circumstances of this world change abruptly and its ownership is taken away and transferred [to others].
Every moment of this world is [taking it] towards the end and every living thing in it is [moving] towards its death and annihilation.
How many a person who relied upon this world has been made to suffer by it!
How many a person who had confidence in this world has been struck down by it!
How many a person who possesses grandeur has this world abased!
How many a person who possesses high standing has this world returned to humility!
That which has passed from this world suffices as an informer of what remains of this world.
The abundance of this world is paucity, its grandeur is humiliation, its embellishments are misguiding and its gifts are a trial.
Be in this world with your body and in the Hereafter with your heart and your actions.
Be most cautious of this world when you are most at ease with it.
Become uninterested in this world and be infatuated with the Hereafter.
Be among those who recognize the transience of this world so they renounce it and know about the eternity of the Hereafter so they work for it.
Be a community that understands that this world is not their [permanent] abode so they exchange it [for the Hereafter].
Be from the children of the Hereafter and do not be from the children of this world, for every child will cling to his mother on the Day of Resurrection.
Whenever a person becomes more preoccupied and infatuated with this world, it makes him enter paths [of danger] and fall into places of destruction.
Whatever does not benefit, harms, and this world with its sweetness, becomes bitter whereas poverty with [seeking] sufficiency through Allah, never harms.
Every time something of this world slips away from you, it is an advantage [and a blessing].
Just as the sun and the night do not come together, similarly love for Allah and love for this world do not come together.
He who claims [to have] certitude in the eternal while he is still attached to the transient, has lied.
For every abundance [in this world] there is paucity.
For everything in this world there is expiry and annihilation.
For the one who finds delight in the pleasures of this world there is distress [and regret in the Hereafter].
Indeed, this world has unveiled the cloak [of its disloyalty] and notified you all equally.
Verily this world of yours is more lowly in my view than the [dry] bone of a pig in the hand of a leper.
It is not a [good] trade to consider this world to be a price for your soul and a substitute to that which is for you with Allah.
For love of this world, listeners turn a deaf ear to [words of] wisdom and hearts become blind to the light of insight.
Nobody gains any joy from this world but that it is followed by tears [of sorrow].
Allah, the Glorified, has not cleansed this world for His friends nor has He withheld it from His enemies.
Nobody gets the comforts of this world internally but that he has to face its hardships externally.7
One whose effort was for this world did not earn any recompense [for it] nor did he fulfil any obligation.
No person in this world is covered by the light rain of ease but that the heavy rain of distress pours upon him.
If the people of the world understood [the truth about it], this world would surely be ruined.
If this world was praiseworthy in front of Allah, He would have reserved it for His friends, but He turned their hearts away from it and expunged its desires from them.
If this world was to remain with one of you, it would not have reached the one in whose hands it is [now].
One who strives for this world is eluded by it.
One who holds back from this world is sought by it.
One who wrestles this world is knocked down by it.
One who disobeys this world is obeyed by it.
One who turns away from this world is approached by it.
One who knows [the reality of] this world, renounces it.
One who thinks little of this world, it comes to him humiliated.
One who is owned by this world falls down often.
One who is delighted by the embellishments of this world is owned by [its] deceptions.
One who buys his Hereafter with his world, gains both of them.
One who sells his Hereafter for his world loses both of them.
One who seeks less of this world gains more of that which keeps him secure [in the Hereafter].
One who seeks more of this world gains more of that which will ruin him.
One who builds his world destroys his place of return [in the Hereafter].
One who is deceived by this world is deceived by [his] aspirations.
One who is pleased with this world is eluded by the Hereafter.
One who is greedy for this world is destroyed.
One who is not content with the little [he has] of this world will not be satisfied with the much that he accumulates from it.
Who is more at a disadvantage than the one who sells the eternal [Hereafter] for the transient [world]?
Who is more at a loss than the one who exchanges the Hereafter for this world?
One who seeks from this world that which pleases him, his crime (and sinfulness) increases and his transgression prolongs.
One who relies on the deceptions of this world considers himself safe from its perils.
Whoever keeps back from seeking this world, it rises towards him.
One who exceeds the limits in seeking this world dies a pauper.
Whoever turns away from this world, it comes to him belittled.
One whose heart is attached to the love of this world catches three things from it: worry that never leaves him, greed that never abandons him and hopes that are never realized by him.
Whoever is attracted by the dazzle of this world, it blinds both his eyes.
One who desires the adornments of this world is eluded by the sought after eternal bliss [of the Hereafter].
One who has been overcome by this world is blind to that which is in front of him.
One who builds his world corrupts his religion and ruins his Hereafter.
One who loves [to acquire] the prestige of [both] this world and the Hereafter must detest prestige in this world.
One who humbles himself for the children of this world takes off the garment of piety.
One who fixes his gaze on the children of this world is blinded from the path of guidance.
One who seeks something from this world is eluded by something greater from the Hereafter than what he seeks [from this world].
Whoever seeks [the profits of] this world through the work of the Hereafter, it takes him further away from that which he seeks.
One who is glad to relinquish the bounties of this world [for the sake of the Hereafter] has certainly perfected his intellect.
Whoever gains possession of something of this world loses much more of the Hereafter than what he possesses [of this world].
One who knows [the reality of] this world is not saddened by that which befalls him [in it].
One who recognizes the deceptions of this world will not be deceived by its impossible dreams.
One who triumphs in this world becomes troubled and one whom it eludes gets distressed.
One in whose eyes this world is grand and in whose heart its position is great, prefers it over Allah and devotes himself to it and becomes a slave to it.

One who becomes infatuated with this world, it fills his heart with a sadness which keeps alternating in the black part of his heart, a distress that worries him and a grief that causes him pain, until its suffocation [of death] overtakes him and he is flung in the open while both the arteries of his heart are severed. It is easy for Allah to cause him to die and he becomes too far for his comrades to meet him (or to remain with him).
One who relies on this world is indeed wretched and deprived.
Whoever serves this world, it exploits him and whoever serves Allah, the Glorified, it (this world) serves him.
One whose concern [and effort] is for this world, his wretchedness and misery will be prolonged on the Day of Resurrection.
One who does not think about the bounties of his world becomes powerful.
One of the troubles of this world is the spoiling of union by separation and happiness by distress.
It is from the lowliness of this world in front Allah is that He is not disobeyed anywhere except in it.
From the [signs of the] contemptibleness of this world in the sight of Allah is that one does not gain that which is with Him except by abandoning it.
Nothing corrupts the faith like this world.
How will the offshoot remain after the root has gone?
This world of yours which endears itself to you is not better than the Hereafter which is made to appear ugly by your negative perception [of it].
That which you send forth from this world is for your own benefit and that which you leave behind from it is for your enemy.
That which [one] increases in this world, [he] diminishes in the Hereafter.
That which [one] diminishes in this world, [he] increases in the Hereafter.
Do not be overjoyed by that which you obtain in this world and do not despair with sadness for that which eludes you from it.
What is good in a house that falls down like demolished construction and in a lifetime that expires as [its] provisions get exhausted?
What is the matter with you? You are delighted with the little of this world that you obtain while you are not saddened by the abundance of the Hereafter that you are deprived of?!
This world has not deceived you, rather through it you have been deceived.
The transient world has not beguiled you, rather through it you have been beguiled.

What is [the matter] with you that which, if you acquire it [the wealth of this world], its improvement [and seeking something better than it] preoccupies you from enjoying it, and if you enjoy it, it spoils it [the enjoyment] for you with the victory of death over you.
The deceived person who gains success in this world through its smallest portion is not like the other person who is gains success in the Hereafter by exerting his greatest effort.8
How close this world is to departure, old age is to youth, and doubt is to uncertainty!
The bitterness of this world is the sweetness of the Hereafter.
One who accompanies this world is a target of calamities and mishaps.
The similitude of this world is like your shadow, if you stop it stops and if you seek it, it moves further away.

The similitude of this world is like the snake, its feel is soft but it has deadly venom in its fangs. The inexperienced and ignorant one reaches towards it while the wise and intelligent one is cautious of it.

The wares of this world are [like] broken orts that cause epidemics, therefore keep off the grazing land which is more beneficial to migrate from than to peacefully stay in, and that of it which suffices for subsistence in it is purer [for the soul] than its riches.
Destroyed is one who finds reassurance in this world and makes his religion its dower, so he turns towards it wherever it turns, having taken it to be his [only] concern and his deity.
Take it easy, for indeed the matter is near, the companionship is short and the sojourn is brief.
It (this world) is obstructive and obdurate, deviating and swaying, deceiving and ungrateful.
Those who are pleased with this world are destroyed on the Day of Resurrection and those who are disheartened by it are saved.
Do not desire anything that perishes and goes away, for this enough of a detriment.
Do not desire this world thereby losing your Hereafter.
Do not desire that which perishes, and take from the transient for the eternal.
Do not jostle for the bounties of this world, for indeed its bounties are trifling.
Do not give your religion as dower for this world, for indeed whoever gives his religion as dowry to this world, it brings to him wretchedness, pain, hardship and tribulation.
Do not sell the Hereafter for this world and do not exchange the eternal with the transient.

Do not let this world tempt you, and do not let your vain desires overpower you, and do not consider your stay in this world to be long, and do not let your hopes deceive you, for indeed hopes are not part of religion in any way.
Let not the greatest thing that you achieve in this world be the attainment of pleasures and the quelling of rage, rather let it be the enlivening of truth and the annihilation of falsehood.
Do not be tempted by good loans [and temporary pleasures], for the loans of this world are returned and you remain with that which you have accumulated of the forbidden.
Do not let the transient world deceive you with its false amusements, for indeed its amusement ceases while the vices which you have acquired remain with you.
Let not any of you pine the way a servant girl pines, for that which has departed from him of this world.
Do not solicit this world by the work of the Hereafter and do not prefer the transient over the eternal, for this is the trait of the hypocrites and the character of the apostates.
Never be deceived by the condition of the people of vanities [and what they enjoy of this world], for indeed it is an extended shadow [which lasts] until a fixed time.
The deceptions of this world do not excite the learned.
This world does not protect the one who seeks refuge in it.
People do not abandon anything from their religion for the sake of this world but that Allah opens for them that which is more harmful for them.
The delights of this world do not continue and its joys do not last, and there is no security from its afflictions.
It behoves the one who recognizes this world to renounce its pleasures and to turn away from it.
It behoves the one who recognizes the transient abode to work for the Eternal Abode.
It behoves the one who knows how fleeting this world is, to renounce its pleasures.
It behoves a person to seek a cure from the ailments of this world just like a sick person seeks treatment, and he should avoid its lusts and pleasures just as a sick person avoids certain foods.
Little of this world corrupts the faith.
Little of this world suffices and plenty of it destroys.
Little of this world is better than plenty of it, and that of it which suffices for subsistence in it is better than that which destroys.
Slaves of desire, cut them short! For indeed, the one who leans on this world gets nothing out of it but the grating sound of hardship.

One who works for this world makes a loss. afflictions. (‘a) (Ref: Sharhe Ghurar al-Ḥikam vol. 2 pg. 656). greatest effort is not like the other who is successful in the Hereafter by gaining its smallest portion. (Saying no. 380)
Many a remedy brings about an ailment.
Many an ailment turns into a remedy.
Sometimes the remedy is [itself] an ailment.
Sometimes the ailment is [itself] a cure.
One whose ailments are many, his cure will not be known.
One who does not bear the bitterness of the remedy, his pain persists.
There is no remedy for the one who is fond of his ailment.
There is no cure for the one who hides his ailment from his doctor.
I am amazed at the one who knows the remedy of his ailment yet does not seek it, and if he finds it he does not apply it [to cure his ailment].
For every living thing there is an ailment.
For every sickness there is a remedy.
Walk with your ailment as long as you can.1
The signs of alternation of power are the creation of stratagems.
One of the signs of alternation of power is vigilance in safeguarding affairs.
The sovereignty of the honourable is one of the most beneficial gains.
From the indicators of alternation of power is decrease of negligence.
Nothing protects empires like justice.

The decline [and imminent fall] of empires is evinced by four things: neglecting the principles [and core values of justice and equity], clinging to vanities, promotion of the wicked and demotion of the virtuous.
The sovereignty of scoundrels is founded on oppression and corruption.
The sovereignty of the great (or honourable) people is one of the best of bounties.
For every empire there is a period [after which it falls].
Do not flatter each other thereby letting flattery plunge you into sin.
The worst collar is the collar of debt.
Too much debt makes a truthful person a liar and an honest person dishonest.
Debt is one of the two bondages.
Debt is bondage, repayment is freedom.
Religion is the more honourable of the two lineages.
Religion and good manners are a result of intelligence.
The foundation of religion is returning trusts [to their owners] and fulfilling pledges.
Know that the beginning of religion is submission and its end is sincere devotion.
Indeed the codes of religion are one and its ways are straight, so the one who follows it arrives [at the destination] and gains [success], and the one who stands away from it strays and regrets.
Where are the different paths taking you?
Where is the darkness misleading you and [how are] the falsehoods deceiving you?
Where are your minds straying and your souls deviating [to]? Do you seek to substitute facts for lies and exchange truth for falsehood?
The greatest felicity is [in] the uprightness of religion.
Little religion is better than plenty of worldly possession.
The most religious of all people is one whose religiosity is not corrupted by [lustful] desire.
The best religion is cutting short [false] aspirations, and the highest worship is being sincere in your action.
Verily Allah, the Glorified, grants this world to [both] the one whom He loves and the one whom He does not love, but He grants religion only to the one whom He loves.
Verily Allah, the Most High, does not give the religion except to His chosen ones and the elite from among His creation.
Indeed the best religion is loving for the sake of Allah, hating for the sake of Allah, taking for the sake of Allah and giving for the sake of Allah, the Glorified.
Indeed the religion [of Islam] is like a tree, its roots are certitude in Allah and its fruits are befriending for the sake of Allah and having enmity for the sake of Allah, the Glorified.
Verily Allah, the Glorified, has illuminated the path of truth and has clarified its ways, so [there is] either inescapable wretchedness or eternal felicity.
Religion safeguards.
Religion exalts, this world humiliates.
Religion is [the path to] joy.
Religion is light, certitude is joy.
Religion is the greatest pursuit.
Religion is the strongest pillar.
The Sharī‘ah is [for] disciplining the self.
The Sharī‘ah is for the benefit [and reformation] of mankind.
Religion is a treasure and knowledge is a guide [to it].
Religion is a tree whose roots are submission and contentment.
Religion deters [one] from the unlawful.
Religion is not reformed except by the intellect.
If you make your religion follow your worldly desires, you will have destroyed your religion and your [life in this] world, and you will be among the losers in the Hereafter.
The fruit of religion is trustworthiness.
The fruit of religion is strong conviction.
Three things are the disgrace of religion: lewdness, treachery and betrayal [of trust].
Three things are the consolidators of religion: chastity, piety and modesty.
Three things are the perfection of religion: sincerity, certitude and contentment.
The steadfastness of religion is through the strength of conviction.
The consolidation of religion is in sincerity of action, cutting short [false] aspirations, doing good to others and refraining from ugly deeds.
The beauty of religion is piety.
The excellence of [one’s adherence to] religion stems from the strength of [one’s] certitude.
Preserving the faith is the fruit of cognizance and the peak of wisdom.
Safeguard the religion through [the means of] this world and do not safeguard this world through the religion.
The best course of religion is piety.
The sign of a servant’s faith is his piety.
Defend the religious laws, protect the borders of the Muslim lands and safeguard your religion and your trust through your impartiality towards yourself and acting justly among your subjects.
The cornerstone of religion is acquiring good deeds.
The adornment of religion is intelligence.
The adornment of religion is patience and contentment.
The cause of piety is soundness of faith.
The uprightness of religion is through virtuous piety and certitude.
The safety of religion is in seclusion from the people.
The safety of [one’s] religion and worldly life is in being amicable with the people.

Six things are used to test the faith of a man: the strength of his religion, the truth of his conviction, the intensity of his piety, his overcoming vain desires, the paucity of his [worldly] inclinations and his being moderate in what he seeks.
The pinnacle of religion is patience, certitude and struggling against vain desires.

There are six fundamentals of faith: sincerity of conviction, giving advice [and guidance] to [fellow] Muslims, establishing the prayer, paying the zakāt [alms-tax], performing the Hajj [pilgrimage] and renouncing the pleasures of this world.
The rectitude of religion is [through] piety.
The rectitude of religion is through strong conviction.

Make religion the fortress of your state and [make] gratitude the protection of your blessings, for every state that is surrounded by religion will not be defeated and every blessing that is protected by gratitude will not be taken away.
Make religion the shield of your life and piety the preparation for your death.
A person’s preservation [of himself from sin] is to the extent of his religiousness.
Safeguard your religion through your worldly life and you will gain both of them, and do not safeguard your worldly life through your religion thereby losing both of them.
Safeguard the faith through [the life of] this world and it will save you, and do not safeguard [the life of] this world through the faith otherwise it will destroy you.
Blessed is he who acts upon the teachings of religion and follows the footsteps of the Prophets.
You must cling to religion, piety and certitude, for these are the best of virtues and through them the lofty stations are attained.
One’s religiousness is proportionate to his intellect.
The height of religion is faith [and conviction].
The height of religion is satisfaction [with the decree of Allah].
The height of religion is enjoining good, forbidding evil and upholding the boundaries [of Islamic law].
The one who lacks religion falls into disbelief and misguidance.
This world is the corruptor of religion.
The basis of religious law is enjoining good, forbidding evil and upholding the boundaries [of Islamic law].
Just as a body and its shadow do not separate, so too religion and success do not separate.
For every religion there is a character and the character of faith is kindness.
One who becomes religious fortifies himself.
One who is stingy with his religion [and does not give it up for the sake of this world] becomes exalted.
He who has no religion has no magnanimity.
One who becomes learned in religion increases [his prosperity].
One whose religiousness is sound, his trustworthiness is stronger.
One who corrupts his faith corrupts his Hereafter.
One who is endowed with religion is endowed with the good of this world and the Hereafter.
One who considers his religion to be precious, [the hardship of] this world becomes easy for him [to bear].
One whose faith is strong is certain about the reward [he will get for his good actions] and is satisfied with whatever has been decreed [for him by Allah].
One who has no religion has no salvation.
One whose observance of religion is thorough, his position in the Hereafter will be exalted.
One who is careless in his religion becomes lowly and one who fights with the truth, is forced to yield [to it].
Whoever takes the religion of Allah as idle sport and play, Allah, the Glorified, will put him into the fire for eternity.
One who is cautious [and concerned] about this religion is safe from destruction.
Nothing undermines religion like abandoning the upholding of Allah’s religion and neglecting the obligatory [actions].
The basis of religion is piety.
The basis of religion is opposing vain desires.
What a good companion religion is!
Keep your religions unsullied by uncertainties and safeguard yourselves from situations of destructive doubts.
The structure of religion is [based on] opposing vain desires and keeping away from [the unlawful pleasures of] this world.
The structure of religion is [based on] two qualities: your impartiality towards yourself and supporting your brethren.
Guided is the one who puts on the garment of religion.
In describing the religion of Islam [he (‘a) said]: It is the brightest of all paths, the clearest [and most illuminated] of all passages; it is an elevated land, [with] a lofty peak.
Guard your religion by seeking help from Allah.

Do not be neglectful of your religion and eager for your world by seeking more of that which will not last for you and less of that which will last for you, for this will lead you to severe chastisement [in the Hereafter].
Religion does not remain safe with avarice.
Religion does not surrender the one who takes refuge in it.
The religiousness of a man is deduced by the virtue of his God-wariness and the truth of his piety.
The best savings are good actions.
The best of (all) savings are good actions.
The best of (all) savings is knowledge that is acted upon and good that is not followed by obligation
Remembering [Allah] is the better of the two gains.
Remembering [Allah] comforts the soul, illuminates the heart and brings down the mercy [of Allah].
Remembering [Allah] is the light of intellect, the life of the souls and the polishing of the hearts.

Sitting in the masjid from after dawn up to sunrise in order to remember [and praise] Allah, the Glorified, is quicker in making sustenance [more easily] obtainable than travelling to different parts of the land [in order to earn one’s livelihood].
A beautiful remembrance is one of the two lives.1
A beautiful remembrance is one of the two lifetimes.
Remembering [Allah] is not from rituals of the tongue nor is it from the passing of thoughts rather it is first from the remembered and then from the rememberer.
Fill your solitude with the remembrance [of Allah] and accompany blessings with gratitude.
Be abundant in your remembrance of Allah, for it is the best remembrance.
Be constant in your remembrance [of Allah] for it illuminates the heart and is surely the best [form of] worship.
The most deserving to be remembered by you is the one who does not forget you.
Remember the disperser of gatherings, the dasher of hopes, the bringer of death[s] and the announcer of disunion and separation.
The basis of reformation of the heart is occupying it with the remembrance of Allah.
Verily Allah, the Glorified, has made [His] remembrance a polishing for the hearts, to see with after blindness and listen with after deafness and to become submissive with it after obduracy.

Verily there are those who hold on to the remembrance of Allah and have taken it in lieu of this world and thus neither trade nor business has preoccupied them from [His] remembrance. They spend the days of their lives with it and shout it in the ears of the negligent [in order to remind them].
Remembrance is being in the company of the beloved.
Remembering [Allah] is the key to intimacy [and nearness with Him].
The remembrance [of Allah] is a light and guidance.
The remembrance [of Allah] is the delight of the lovers.
Remembrance of Allah brings comfort [and delight].
Remembrance of Allah is the polishing of visions and illumination of the inner selves.
Remembrance [of Allah] is the guidance of the intellects and the enlightenment of the souls.
When you see that Allah is making you comfortable with His remembrance, then [know that] He loves you.
When you see that Allah is making you comfortable with His creation and isolating you from His remembrance, then (know that) He dislikes you.
It is through the remembrance of Allah that mercy descends.
Through the constant remembrance of Allah, heedlessness is dispelled.
The fruit of remembrance [of Allah] is illumination of the hearts.
The best means by which you achieve success in [all] matters is the remembrance of Allah, the Glorified.
Constant remembrance [of Allah] illuminates the heart and mind.
Remembrance of Allah is the light of faith.
Remembrance of Allah is a means of driving away Satan.
Remembrance of Allah is the practice of the Near Ones.
Remembrance of Allah is the polishing of the breasts and the tranquillity of the hearts.
The remembrance of Allah is nourishment for the souls and [being in] the company of the [most] Beloved.
Remembrance of Allah illuminates the visions and comforts the consciences.
The remembrance of Allah is what makes matters successful and inner selves illuminated.
Remembrance of Allah is the cure for the maladies of the souls.
The remembrance of Allah is a dispeller of hardships (or maladies) and misery.
Remembrance of Allah is the [principal] asset of every believer and its profit is safety against Satan.
The remembrance of Allah is the pillar of faith and a protection against Satan.
Remembering Allah [at all times] is the trait of every good-doer and the quality of every believer.
Remembrance of Allah is the joy of every God-wary person and the delight of every possessor of certitude.
The one who listens to the [remembrance and] glorification of Allah is [himself] a glorifier.
You must espouse the remembrance of Allah for it is surely the light of the heart.
In the remembrance of Allah there is life for the hearts.
Whoever remembers Allah, He remembers him.
One who remembers Allah is gains insight.
Whoever is preoccupied in remembering the people, Allah, the Glorified, cuts him off from His remembrance.
Whoever is preoccupied in the remembrance of Allah, Allah makes his remembrance good.
Whoever fills his heart with the constant remembrance of Allah, his actions become good [both] in secret and in the open.
Whoever remembers Allah, the Glorified, Allah enlivens his heart and illuminates his intellect and his mind.
One whose remembrance [of Allah] increases, his mind becomes illuminated.
Constant remembrance [of Allah] is the quality of the friends [of Allah].
The constant remembrance [of Allah] is nourishment for the souls and the key to righteousness.

Do not remember Allah, the Glorified, in a state of inattentiveness, and do not forget Him by being distracted [with the amusements of this world], and remember Him perfectly such that your heart is in agreement with your tongue and your inward is in accordance with your outward; and you will never remember Him with the befitting remembrance until you forget your ego in your remembrance and lose it in your affair [because all your attention is towards Allah].
There is no guidance like remembrance [and glorification of Allah].
The one who remembers Allah is in His Company.
The one who remembers Allah is His intimate friend.
The one who remembers Allah is from the successful ones.
One who reminds you [of Allah and the Hereafter] is has surely warned you [against evil].

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Vices are a disease, and its remedy is seeking forgiveness, and its cure is not repeating [the vices].

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Taking a sin lightly is worse than committing the sin.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Giving up sin is difficult, but giving up Paradise is [going to be] more difficult.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Things come to us that seem to be much when we amass them but which we consider to be less when we divide them.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Be careful of the sins that lead you to deep trouble the vices that bring the wrath of Allah.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Refrain from desecration of the sacred, for indeed this is the practice of the wicked and the people of depravity and vice.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Refrain from persistence [in committing vices] for it is surely the gravest of great sins and the worst of offences.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Refrain from exposing [your] sins, for this is one of the worst of offences.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Refrain from vices, for the one who sells the eternal Paradise for a vile sin from the sins of this world is indeed wretched.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Do not take the committing of vices lightly, for verily it will cover you with humiliation in this world and earn you the wrath of Allah in the Hereafter.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Verily wrongdoings are [like] wild horses that carry their riders on their backs while their bridles have been thrown off, so they take them [straight] into the fire of hell.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: The greatest misdeed is recommending the vicious.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: The worst misdeed is refusing to accept an excuse [that is valid].

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: The worst of sins in the sight of Allah is the sin upon which its doer persists.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: The gravest of sins in the sight of Allah, the Glorified, is the sin which is taken lightly by the one who commits it.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: The vice that brings the quickest retribution is oppressing the one who does not oppress you.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: The vilest of sins is cutting off ties with near relatives and impiety [with one’s parents].

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: The gravest of sins is the sin upon which the sinner persists.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Verily the vice with the worst of consequences is error [and misguidance].

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Verily Allah, the Glorified, hates the one who is insolent and bold in committing sins.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Indeed one who disobeys Allah is the enemy of Muhammad (s), even if he is the nearest of his relatives.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Verily the clemency shown by Allah, the Most High, despite [your] acts of disobedience has made you bold and has driven you to [do things that will] destroy yourself.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Persistence [in sinning] is the practice of the depraved.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Persistence [in sinning] leads one to hellfire.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: The one who openly declares his sin is an advertiser [of his disobedience to Allah].

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Disobedience [to Allah] is the negligence of the vicious (or the weak).

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Sin prevents the one’s supplication from being answered.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Persistence [in sinning] is the worst of ideas.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Persistence [in sinning] is the gravest of sins.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Persistence [in sinning] is the trait of the doomed.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Retribution is the fruit of misdeeds.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Persistence [in sinning] brings [divine] wrath.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Disobedience [to Allah] brings retribution.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Returning to sin [and repeating it] is persistence [in sinning].

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Persistence [in sinning] is the gravest sin and the quickest in [bringing] retribution.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Keeping away from vices is more important [and better] than earning good deeds.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: If you must, by all means, be pure, then purify yourselves from vices of the hearts.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: If you must, by all means, be clean, then clean yourselves from the filth of flaws and vices.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: If you purify yourselves from vices, Allah will love you.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Verily if you keep away from vices you will attain elevated ranks.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: The bane of obedience is insubordination.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: When you commit a sin then be remorseful for it.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: It is through disobedience [to Allah] that wretchedness comes about.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Through disobedience [to Allah] the [gate of] hellfire is closed for the aberrant [and they are unable to escape it].

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: How evil an action disobedience [to Allah] is!

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Avoid disobeying Allah and you will be successful.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Guard yourself against sins and restrain yourselves from them, for indeed, wretched is the one who gives them free rein.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Exalted is Allah, the Mighty, [yet] how lenient is He! And you are lowly and weak yet how bold you are in your disobedience to Him!

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: The sweetness of sin is spoilt by the pain of retribution.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: The outcome of sins is loss [and destruction].

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Many a great sin of yours is deemed by you as [being] small.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: The one who embarks upon sin, his [final] abode is hellfire.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Submission to sin is the trait of the doomed.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: I am amazed at the person who knows the severity of Allah’s retribution and [yet] he still continues being persistent [in sinning].

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: The companion of vices is the hostage of [his] misdeeds.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: For every evil act there is punishment.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: For the one who is bold in [committing] sins there are retributions from the chastisement of Allah, the Glorified.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: If Allah, the Glorified, had not forbidden that which He has ordained as unlawful, it would have [still] been mandatory for the intelligent one to keep away from it.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Rejoicing in vices is uglier than committing them.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Is there any place of protection or shelter, or any sanctuary or asylum, or any place to flee or return back to?

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Do not persist in that which is followed by sin.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Do not tear your veils [of innocence] in front of the One who knows your secrets.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Do not undertake acts of disobedience to Allah, the Glorified, and act with obedience to Him, as this will be a provision for you [in the Hereafter].

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Never belittle the small sins, for they are indeed dangerous [and destructive]; and one who is surrounded by his belittled [sins] is destroyed by them.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Those who remain behind [in this world after others have passed away before them] do not stop from committing sins.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: There is no vice greater than persistence [in sinning].

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: There is no vice greater than rejoicing in acts of depravity.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: One who is persistent in his sin shows audacity in front of the wrath of his Lord.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Whoever takes pleasure in the disobedience of Allah is made to suffer utter humiliation by Allah.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: One whose sins increase, his disparagement becomes necessary.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Neither are blessings taken away from you nor are you deprived of any comforts of life but because of the sins that you commit, and Allah is not unjust to the Servants.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: None of the acts of disobedience to Allah, the Glorified, come about except in [the garb of] desire.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Constant sinning cuts [one’s] sustenance.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Openly [and boldly] sinning in front of Allah [without any shame] hastens [divine] retributions.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: We seek refuge with Allah from the evils of the intellect (or from evil actions) and the ugliness of errors, and from Him do we seek assistance [against all this].

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Far be it! You have not feigned ignorance except because of what has passed before you of mistakes and sins.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Every disobedient one is a sinner.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Whoever disobeys Allah, his status gets lowered.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Woe be to the sinner, how ignorant he is and how much of his share he has relinquished!

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Woe to the one who is afflicted with disobedience, deprivation and abandonment.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Rushing into vices causes [one to face] the chastisement of hellfire.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: When committing sins, recall how the pleasures will [soon] end and the consequences that follow will remain.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Be wary of the sins done in seclusion, for indeed the Witness (to it) is the Judge.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Caution, caution O listener! Strive, strive O intelligent one! None can inform you like the One who is all-aware.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: I am amazed at the one who avoids the food that could harm him, how does he not avoid the sin that would bring painful chastisement?!

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Vice is the endeavour of the filthy.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: How bad a leash is the leash of vices!

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: In every evil act there is retribution.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: The one who sins knowingly does not deserve pardon.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Denial [of sin] is persistence [in it].

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: The one who sins without knowing is free from sin.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: The weapon of the sinner is repentance.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: A sinner who confesses his sin is better than the obedient one who is proud of his action.

topic: Vices and Those who commit them
text: Do not dishearten a sinner, for how many a person who is occupied with his sin ends up being forgiven, and how many a person has embarked on a virtuous action which he corrupts at the end of his life and winds up in the fire of hell.
Divulgence [of secrets] is [and act of] disloyalty
Divulgence [of secrets] is the practice of the others [and not of the believers].
What an excellent person the compassionate one is!
Restrict your opinion to that which is necessary and you will be safe; avoid entering into that which does not concern you and you will be honoured.
Churn the opinion [like] the churning of a water-skin, and the outcome will be the most pertinent of opinions.
The closest of opinions to reason will be the furthest of them from vain desire.
The ones who possess most pertinent opinions are those who have experience.
The person with the best opinion is he who does not consider himself needless of the counsel of an advisor.
The best opinion is one which neither causes opportunities to be wasted nor brings about distress.
Indeed your opinion cannot encompass everything, so leave it for the important [issues].
The [right] opinion is [acquired] by protecting secrets.
Through correct opinion (or prudence), ones judiciousness is strengthened.
The best of opinions is the furthest of them from vain desire and the closest of them to pertinence.
Hidden opinions are revealed through consultation.
The opinion of an elderly person is more beloved to me than the fortitude [and bravery] of a youth.
A person’s opinion is the gauge of his intelligence.
The opinion of an intelligent person saves.
The opinion of an ignorant person destroys.
The opinion of a person is in accordance with his experience.
Erroneous opinion annihilates the kingdom and heralds destruction.
The most evil of opinions is that which goes against the laws of Islam.
The validity of an opinion is [measured] by the sincerity of the adviser.
Correct opinion saves [one] from errors.
Correct opinion [and decision] comes with [the coming of] power and it vanishes with its disappearance.
Correct opinion is [derived] through careful consideration.
Misguided opinion corrupts the goals.
Determination [and resolve] is proportionate to the strength of one’s opinion.
Indeed the lone opinion [without any consultation] may be erroneous.
Indeed one who thinks his opinion is sufficient [and does not seek advice] has taken a [huge] risk.
One who is ignorant of the different opinions is incapacitated by ruses [and is unable to decide on the correct course].
One who fails to apply the [correct] opinion becomes disconcerted.
One who acts on the [correct] opinion, benefits [from it].
One whose opinions are weak, his enemies become stronger.
One who is impressed by his [own] opinions is defeated by his enemies.
One who admires his [own] opinion is overwhelmed (or destroyed) by incompetence.
Do not become opinionated [and headstrong], for the one who is opinionated is destroyed.
Do not use opinion [and conjecture] in that which is neither perceived by sight nor penetrated by thought.
One who is not obeyed has no opinion.
One who is content with his [own] opinion is indeed doomed.
When one is opinionated, it becomes easy for his enemies to defeat him.
One who takes the different opinions into consideration recognizes the points of error.
One who is opinionated has endangered and imperilled [himself].
The opinionated one falls into error and blunder.
Indeed the opinionated one has made an error [by not considering the other opinions].
One who is opinionated [and headstrong] slips.
Being opinionated will make you slip and will cause you to fall into an abyss.
How bad a disposition opinionatedness [and arbitrariness] is!
The outside of the one who shows off is beautiful but his inside is sickly.
Work without seeking to show off or for the sake of renown, for indeed the one who works for other than Allah is left by Allah to the one whom he worked for.
Showing off is [a form of] ascribing partners [to Allah].
The bane of worship is showing off.
The smallest amount of showing off is polytheism.
The words of the one who shows off are beautiful, but in his heart there is an internal disease.
Many a profit turns back into loss.
The gainer is one who has sold this world for the Hereafter and has exchanged the transient for the eternal.

topic: Hope in [The Mecy of] Allah and [in] others
text: Keep all your hope for Allah, the Glorified, and do not have hope [in] anyone other than Him, for indeed no one has hoped in other than Allah, the Exalted, but that he has been disappointed.

topic: Hope in [The Mecy of] Allah and [in] others
text: The greatest affliction is the severance of hope.

topic: Hope in [The Mecy of] Allah and [in] others
text: Hope in the mercy of Allah brings more success.

topic: Hope in [The Mecy of] Allah and [in] others
text: Verily, if you have hope in Allah you will attain your hopes, but if you have hope in other than Allah then your hopes and aspirations will be frustrated.

topic: Hope in [The Mecy of] Allah and [in] others
text: Many a hope leads to deprivation.

topic: Hope in [The Mecy of] Allah and [in] others
text: Many a frustrated hope is brought about by a false aspiration.

topic: Hope in [The Mecy of] Allah and [in] others
text: Be closer to that which you do not hope for than [you are to] that which you hope for.

topic: Hope in [The Mecy of] Allah and [in] others
text: For every absence, there is a return.

topic: Hope in [The Mecy of] Allah and [in] others
text: At times the distant may come close and the close may become distant.

topic: Hope in [The Mecy of] Allah and [in] others
text: When one has hope in you, [then] do not disappoint his hope.

topic: Hope in [The Mecy of] Allah and [in] others
text: When one is not known to have a generous nature, [then] do not have hope in him.

topic: Hope in [The Mecy of] Allah and [in] others
text: Who would have hope in your kindness when you have cut off ties with your near relatives?!

topic: Hope in [The Mecy of] Allah and [in] others
text: Whoever makes Allah, the Glorified, the refuge of his hopes, He will suffice him in his religious and worldly affairs.

topic: Hope in [The Mecy of] Allah and [in] others
text: When one takes himself to be lowly, [then] do not expect [or hope] for any good from him.

topic: Hope in [The Mecy of] Allah and [in] others
text: One who does no evil to others, [then] expect good from him.

topic: Hope in [The Mecy of] Allah and [in] others
text: Do not have hope [or expectation] except from your Lord.

topic: Hope in [The Mecy of] Allah and [in] others
text: Do not hope in that which will cause you to receive rebuke for your hope.

topic: Hope in [The Mecy of] Allah and [in] others
text: Do not risk anything with the hope of getting more than it.

topic: Hope in [The Mecy of] Allah and [in] others
text: Never have hope in the favour of one who makes you feel obliged, and do not rely upon the fool and the traitor.

topic: Hope in [The Mecy of] Allah and [in] others
text: Aba Dharr! Indeed you got angry for the sake of Allah so have hope in the One whom you got angry for. Indeed the people feared you in the matter of their world while you feared them for your faith. Then leave to them that for which they are afraid of you and get away from them with that which you feared them for. How needy they are for that which you dissuade them from and how needless you are of that which they deny you. Even if the skies and the earth were closed to an individual and [then] he feared Allah, Allah would most certainly open a way for him in them. So let nothing give you comfort but the truth and let nothing distress you except falsehood. If you would have accepted their world [and its attractions] they would have loved you, and if you had shared in it they would have given you asylum.
By showing compassion, [divine] mercy descends.
Being compassionate to the weak brings down [divine] mercy.
Showing compassion to one who does not show compassion [to others] prevents [divine] mercy, and sparing one who does not spare others destroys the nation.
I am amazed at the one who hopes for the mercy of one who is above him, how can he not show compassion to the one who is below him?!
Make your heart feel compassion for all people and [show] kindness towards them, [and] do not oppress them or terrorize them.
The most deserving of [showing] mercy among the people is the one who is most in need of it [himself].
The best thing that draws forth mercy is having compassion for all people [in your heart].
When you are incapable of helping the weak [and needy] then let your compassion encompass them.
Just as you show mercy, mercy will be shown to you.
One who shows no mercy will be shown no mercy.
One who shows no mercy to the people, Allah will withhold His mercy from him.
One in whose heart there exists no mercy, meets less of it (mercy) when he needs it.
One who shows mercy is shown mercy.
It is by the honourable that mercy is shown.
One of the surest means of intelligence is showing mercy to the ignorant.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: By keeping ties with near relatives, blessings flow forth [abundantly].

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: By cutting off ties with near relatives, [divine] retributions are brought down.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: The kindness of a person towards his near relatives is a [form of] charity.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: The protection of blessings is in keeping ties with near relatives.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: The descending of [divine] retributions is in cutting off ties with near relatives.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: Many a near relative is farther away than one who is distant [or unrelated].

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: Many ties are better to cut off than to keep.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: Sometimes [certain] ties may result in heavy burdens [and obligations].

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: Keeping ties with near relatives makes blessings flow forth and repels calamities.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: Keeping ties with near relatives is one of the best practices.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: Keeping ties with near relatives makes the numbers grow and multiplies the blessings.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: Keeping ties with near relatives hurts the enemy and protects one from falling into evil places of destruction.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: Keeping ties with near relatives produces wealth and delays death.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: Keeping ties with near relatives brings about love and restrains the enemy.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: Keeping ties with near relatives increases [one’s] lifespan and makes wealth grow [and multiply].

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: Keeping ties with near relatives is a means of increasing wealth and a raiser of [good] deeds.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: Keeping ties with near relatives is from the best practices of the honourable ones.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: Keeping ties with near relatives makes blessings flourish and repels [divine] retributions.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: Keeping ties with near relatives makes the numbers grow and results in eminence.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: One who is neglected by the near one is [made dear to and] supported by the distant [unrelated] one.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: One who wrongs his near relative has indeed disgraced his honour.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: Part of honour is keeping ties with near relatives.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: In keeping ties with near relatives there is the safeguarding of blessings.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: In cutting off ties with near relatives there is the coming down of [divine] retributions.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: Keeping ties with near relatives is a means of growing the numbers.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: Cutting off ties with near relatives brings [divine] retributions.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: Cutting off ties with near relatives is one of the ugliest practices.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: Cutting off ties with near relatives causes the cessation of blessings.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: There is no increase [in wealth] with cutting off ties with near relatives.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: No one is considered close by the one who cuts off ties with his near relatives.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: It is not part of honour to cut off ties with near relatives.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: Honour your family, for indeed they are your wings by which you fly, and your origin to which you return, and your hand by which you attack [the enemy].

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: Honour your near relatives, revere the forbearing from among them, be patient with the foolish among them and lighten the burden for the poor among them, for verily they are the best means of support [and assistance] in times of difficulty and ease.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: The best practice is keeping ties with near relatives.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: Indeed when near relatives are in contact, they become kind to each other.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: Verily keeping ties with near relatives is from the obligatory acts of Islam, and Allah, the Glorified, has commanded that they should be honoured, and He, the Most High, keeps ties with the one who keeps ties with them and cuts off ties with the one who cuts off ties with them and honours the one who honours them.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: Making false accusations is the first step in cutting off ties.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: Beware! None of you should ever abandon [any of] his near relatives whom he finds in [a state of] poverty and [neither should he] desist in helping them with that which will not increase if he withholds it nor will it decrease if he spends it.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: False accusation is the messenger of severance of ties.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: He who cuts off ties [with near relatives] does not believe in Allah.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: How ugly is cutting off ties after establishing them, and alienation after brotherhood, and enmity after goodwill, and the disappearance of affinity after it had been strengthened.

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: Who will ever trust you when you are disloyal to your near relatives?

topic: Near Relatives and Keeping or Cutting off Ties with Them
text: Many a distant one is closer than every near one.
When the circle of affliction tightens, ease follows.
The excellence of gratitude is in times of ease.
One who does not restrain himself [from evils and excesses] is ignorant.
By keeping away from depravities, you are saved from disgrace.
Do not make yourself needless through depravities such that your value is dropped.
He who delights in depravities will never succeed.
It is sufficient of a depravity for one to be pleased [and impressed] with himself.
Decline into depravities easily destroys.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: Make sustenance come down by [giving] charity.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: Verily Allah, the Glorified, dislikes to put the sustenance of his believing servants except [in places] from where they least expect it.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: Assistance comes down from Allah to the extent of the provisions [that are required for sustenance].

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: Your sustenance is seeking you, so spare yourself the trouble of seeking it.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: He who seeks sustenance from the wicked has accepted deprivation.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: The sustenance of every person is preordained just as the end of his life is predetermined.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: The sustenance of a person is proportionate to his intention.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: That which has been decreed for you will come to you, so take it easy in your earning.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: All of you are the dependants of Allah, and Allah, the Glorified, takes care of His dependants.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: For every sustenance there is a means, so be moderate in your seeking [it].

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: No [other] seeker will ever overtake you in [acquiring] your sustenance.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: Nobody will ever overcome you in getting that which has been decreed for you.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: That which has been apportioned for you will never escape you so be moderate in what you seek.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: That sustenance which has been decreed for a soul shall not escape it.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: If sustenance was bestowed based on understanding and intellect, the animals and foolish ones would not live.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: One who is [too] concerned about his next day’s sustenance will never be successful.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: One of the most pleasant blessings is abundant sustenance.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: What a good blessing abundant sustenance is!

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: Do not let seeking that which is guaranteed for you be more important to you than the action which has been made obligatory upon you to perform.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: Do not let the worry of the day which has not come upon you bear on the day which has [already] come upon you, for indeed if it will be from your lifetime, [then] Allah, the Glorified, will grant your sustenance in it and if it is not from your lifetime then what worry do you have for that which is not for you?!

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: Sustenance is not acquired by toiling [for it].1

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: No one possesses the ability to withhold sustenance or to bestow it except the Sustainer.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: Your sustenance seeks you with more intensity than you seek it, so be moderate in what you seek.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: Be moderate in what you seek, for how many greedy people have been disappointed and how many who are moderate have not been unsuccessful!

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: Sustenance seeks the one who does not seek it.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: Sustenance is not acquired by greed or by being sought after.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: Indeed I will complete my sustenance, and struggle with my [lower] self and will end with my [allotted] portion.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: Verily you will acquire your share - your sustenance is guaranteed and that which has been decreed for you will be fulfilled, so spare yourself the trouble of the wretchedness of greed and the humiliation of seeking [from others]; trust in Allah and take it easy in your earning.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: Be satisfied and you will be relaxed.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: Be satisfied with that which has been apportioned for you and you will be a [true] believer.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: Be satisfied with the sustenance that has been apportioned for you and you will live a life of prosperity.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: The sustenance has been apportioned; the greedy has been deprived [of what he seeks beyond his share].

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: One who seeks more [than what has been apportioned for him], falls into loss.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: The deprived may [also] be granted sustenance.

topic: Sustenance and One Who Seeks It
text: Neither you overtake your death nor will you get the sustenance that is not [decreed] for you, so why are you making yourself miserable O wretched one?!
One who confides less in others is safe.
One who confides a lot in others regrets.
Confiding less in people [and not telling them your secrets] is more judicious.
By the intelligence of the messenger and his etiquette, the intelligence of the sender [of the message] is gauged.
A person’s messenger is the interpreter of his reason, and his written message is more conveying than his speech.
You messenger is the interpreter of your intellect, and your tolerance is an indication of your forbearance.
Your messenger is the gauge of your nobility, and your pen is the most eloquent thing that speaks on your behalf.
Indeed the intelligent one who is heedless strays from the path of right guidance and the one who strives with seriousness [to find it] gets it.
You will never know rectitude until you know the one who has abandoned it.
One who seeks right guidance becomes knowledgeable [about it].
One who seeks right guidance from the deviated, goes astray.
One who opposes his reason follows his desires.
The best of paths is [the path of] right guidance.
It is possible for the seeker of right guidance to attain it.
One who is truthful to you about yourself has indeed guided you aright.
There is no going astray with right guidance.
One who is successful in his [attaining] rectitude acquires provisions for his Hereafter.
One who is pleased with the decree [of Allah] is at ease.
The thing which is most befitting of true faith is being satisfied [with what has been decrees] and total submission [to Allah].
Satisfaction is abundance while disappointment is agony.
Satisfaction dispels sadness.
Satisfaction [with the decree of Allah] is the fruit of certitude.
Satisfaction with the decree of Allah makes great calamities easy [to bear].

If you have made a covenant [to believe in Allah] then be satisfied with that which has been decreed against you and for you, and do not have hope in anyone other than Allah, the Glorified, and await that which is brought to you by [divine] decree.
Indeed if you are pleased with the decree [of Allah], your lives will become enjoyable and you will attain prosperity.
When what you want does not happen, then do not fret about how you were [and be satisfied with the decree of Allah].
By satisfaction with the decree of Allah, the strength of [one’s] certitude is evinced.
Seek the pleasure of Allah and fear His displeasure, and let your heart become unsettled by [your] fear of Him.
Seek the pleasure of Allah by being satisfied with His decree.

Seek the pleasure of Allah, and keep away from His displeasure, for indeed there is none who can save you from His retribution and there is nothing that can make you needless of His forgiveness, and there is no refuge for you from Him except with Him.
The fruit of satisfaction is prosperity.
The pinnacle of worship is satisfaction [with the decree of Allah].
The cornerstone of contentment is satisfaction [with the decree of Allah].
Remain satisfied in times of difficulty and ease.
Whoever is pleased with [Allah’s] decree, his life becomes pleasant.
One who is satisfied with the decree [of Allah] takes the changing circumstances [of his life] lightly.
Whoever is satisfied with what has been decreed, his certitude is strengthened.
One whose satisfaction with what is decreed is good, his patience in [times of] tribulation will be good.
One who is pleased with the share allotted to him by Allah does not grieve for that which escapes him.
One who is satisfied with what Allah has allotted for him does not become sad about what others possess.
Whoever is not satisfied with the decree [of Allah], disbelief seeps into his religion.
From the most excellent faith is being pleased with whatever [divine] decree brings.
Allah, the Glorified, does not pass any decree for the servant who is satisfied with it but that there is benefit in it for him.

Allah, the Glorified, does not repel any of the afflictions of this world and chastisements of the Hereafter from the believer except because of his satisfaction with His decree and his good patience in the face of His trials.
What a good companion of faith satisfaction is!
What a good expeller of sadness satisfaction with [divine] decree is!
He who is satisfied with the decree [of Allah] has acquired abundance.
There is no submission like satisfaction [with what has been decreed].
Nothing takes away poverty like satisfaction and contentment.
