It behoves one who is pleased with the decree of Allah, the Glorified, to rely upon Him.
The pleasure of Allah, the Glorified, is the nearest goal that can be achieved.
The pleasure of Allah, the Glorified, is linked to His obedience.
The sign that Allah, the Glorified, is pleased with His servant is his (the servant’s) satisfaction with that which He, the Glorified, has decreed for or against him.
The highest goal is in [attaining] the pleasure of Allah.
How can the heart that is inclined to this world be capable of being satisfied [with what has been decreed]?!
Satisfaction suffices as abundance.
Whoever prefers the pleasure of the All-Powerful Lord, then let him speak with words of justice in the presence of the tyrannical ruler.
Whoever seeks the pleasure of Allah at the expense of displeasing the people, Allah will turn his dispraiser among the people into his praiser.
One who hastens towards the actions that please Allah, the Glorified, and delays acts of disobedience to Him has indeed perfected [his] obedience.
Allah! Grant us your pleasure and make us needless of having to stretch out our hands to other than you.
Whoever seeks the pleasure of people by displeasing Allah, Allah will turn the one who praises him among the people into one who dispraises him.
How great is the wrongdoing of the one who seeks the pleasure of the creation by angering the Creator.
One who is pleased with what has been decreed becomes content with little.
One who is satisfied with his portion will not be angered by anyone.
One who is pleased with his state will not be affected by jealousy.

The one who is pleased with the action of a group is like one who participates in it with them, and for everyone who participates in falsehood there are two sins: the sin of being pleased with it and the sin of acting upon it.
Every satisfied one is at ease.
Be pleased [with Allah’s decree] and He will be pleased with you.
Always be pleased with what is brought by [divine] decree.
One who is satisfied with his [allotted] portion is at ease.
Desire is the key to difficulty [and hardship].
The fruit of desire is hardship.
Your longing for the one who has no interest in you is a humiliation.
One who desires your company when you advance [in rank] wishes to keep away from you when you fall.
One who desires that you remain alive has clutched on to your cord.1
One who desires that which is with Allah, his prostrations and bowings increase.
One who desires that which is with Allah makes his actions sincere.
One who desires that which is with Allah attains his hopes.
Indeed if you desire [closeness to] Allah, you will become prosperous and will be saved, whereas if you desire the [attainment of this] world, you will be at a loss and will be destroyed. person.
Leniency is the key to rightness and the trait of the people of understanding.
Leniency makes difficulties bearable and eases the harshness of situations.
Leniency is the infusion of goodness and the symbol of success.
Be lenient and you shall gain success.
The best thing is gentleness.
The greatest [form of] piety is gentleness.
Leniency is the key to success.
Leniency is the key to rightness.
Gentleness blunts the edge of opposition.
Leniency is the symbol of nobility.
Leniency is the symbol of aptness.
With leniency there is auspiciousness.
Leniency leads to peace.
Gentleness is the brother of a believer.1
Being lenient with one’s subjects [and dependents] stems from an honourable disposition.
When you punish, be lenient.
When leniency is unsuitable, then harshness is lenience.
Through leniency, magnanimity is completed.
Through gentleness, goals are achieved.
Through gentleness, difficulties become easy [to bear].
Through gentleness, companionship lasts longer.
The pinnacle of knowledge is leniency [and compassion].
The cornerstone of politics is employing leniency.
The gentleness of a person and his generosity endear him to his enemies.
Adopt leniency, for indeed it is the key to rightness and the quality of the people of understanding.
Adopt gentleness, for whoever is gentle in his actions, his matters will be [successfully] completed.
How many difficulties are made easy with gentleness.
Let the most favoured of people in your sight be the one who is the most lenient in his actions.
Be gentle with the one who is harsh with you, for he will soon become gentle with you.
One who acts with leniency, prospers.
One who treats others with gentleness, gains success.
One who employs leniency, prospers.
Whoever employs gentleness, the hard becomes soft for him.
One who proceeds with leniency in his matters, acquires his objectives from them.
One who employs leniency causes sustenance to flow [in abundance].
Gentleness does not exist in anything but that it beautifies it.
What a good companion leniency is!
The best quality is employing leniency.
The best policy is leniency.
There is no regret for the one who is very lenient.
Violence and gentleness do not go together.
There is no quality more honourable than leniency.
May Allah have mercy on the servant who scrutinizes his sins and fears his Lord.
A comfortable mode of transport is one of the two comforts.

[In the Hereafter] the souls are held at ransom by the weight of their sins and have become certain of their unseen fates. Neither can good acts be added [to their record] nor are they given warning about their evil deeds [rather, the harsh punishment of hell awaits them].
Peace of mind is in abstinence from worldly pleasures.
How close is peace of mind to hardship [and discomfort]!
Sometimes the intended objective may be acquired.
That which infuses discipline is the study of wisdom and overcoming [bad] habits.
Discipline is not beneficial except in a woken soul.
He who has no desistance has no restraint.
Fortify [and protect] your wealth by [giving] charity.
And charity [was prescribed as] a means of sustenance.
One who pays his zakāt is protected from the greediness of his soul.
Whoever looks at his own lapses, the faults of others seem trivial to him.
Whoever is blind to his own lapses, the errors of others seem great to him.
Lapses are a cause of regret.
The lapse of one who is [evidently] pious is the worst of lapses and the sickness of ignobility is the most repulsive of sicknesses.
The slip of the foot is the easiest to recover from [unlike other lapses].
The most despised of creatures in the sight of Allah is the old adulterer.
The abandoning of adultery is [prescribed] for safeguarding the descendants and the renouncing of homosexuality is a means of increasing the progeny.
A dignified person would never commit adultery.
A chaste person does not commit adultery.
A righteous wife is one of the two [lofty] acquisitions.
An agreeable wife is one of the two comforts.
The worst of wives is the one who does not comply [with her husband’s wishes].
The death of one’s wife is the sadness of the hour.
Indeed, you have been commanded to decamp and have been shown your provision [for the journey], so take from this world the provisions that you can hold on to (or that will protect you) tomorrow.
Verily the wasting of provisions is from corruption.
Take provisions from the days of transience for the everlasting [abode], for you have been shown your provision and commanded to decamp and [have been] driven upon the course.
Take from this world the provisions that you can hold on to (or that will protect you) tomorrow and take from the transient for the everlasting.
The provision of a person for the Hereafter is piety and God-wariness.
You must be well prepared and ready, and increase in your provision [for the Hereafter].
I am amazed at the one who knows that he will surely be moving away from his world, how can he not acquire a goodly provision for his Hereafter?!
Every person is approaching that which he has sent forward and will be recompensed for his actions.
As you send forth, so you shall find [waiting for you in the Hereafter].
As you sow, so shall you reap.
Let your provision be God-wariness.
Wasting of provision is from corruption.
That which you send forth today is what you shall come upon tomorrow, so make arrangements for your arrival and send forth [provisions] for your day.
Renunciation of worldly pleasures is the better of the two comforts.
Renunciation of worldly pleasures is the attribute of the God-wary and the quality of the repentant.
Renunciation of worldly pleasures means cutting short [one’s] aspirations and performing actions with sincerity.
Renunciation of worldly pleasures is rarely found [among the people] and is the loftiest thing that is observed; it is praised by everyone but left [unpractised] by the majority of people.
Renounce the pleasures of this world and [divine] mercy will descend upon you.
Turn away from your [vain desires in this] world and you will be happy with your place of return [in the Hereafter] and will reform your [final] abode.
Renounce [vain] pleasures in this world and Allah will show you its flaws, and do not be negligent, for you are not neglected.
The best act of worship is renouncing worldly pleasures.
The first step of asceticism is renouncing worldly pleasures.
The best [form of] renunciation of worldly pleasures is concealing [one’s] asceticism.
The best garment (or better than wearing the garment) of this world is renouncing it.
The one who is most deserving of renouncing worldly pleasures is he who knows the flaws of this world.
Verily the renunciation of ignorance is proportionate to the desire for [knowledge and] intelligence.
Verily the renunciation of a tyrant’s reign is to the extent of the desire for the reign of a just ruler.

Verily, renunciation of worldly pleasures means shortening aspirations, being grateful for blessings and keeping away from that which is forbidden; and if this [practice] leaves you then let not the forbidden overcome your patience and do not forget to be thankful for your blessings, for Allah, the Glorified, has left no room for excuse through manifest and clear proofs and books that are open and unambiguous.
Renunciation of worldly pleasures is affluence.
The root of renunciation of worldly pleasures is the desire for that which is with Allah.
Renunciation of worldly pleasures is the fruit of religion.
Renunciation of worldly pleasures is the fruit of certitude.
Renunciation of worldly pleasures is the root of religion.
Renunciation of worldly pleasures is the foundation of certitude.
Renunciation of worldly pleasures is a profitable trade.
Renunciation of worldly pleasures is a quality of the sincere.
Renunciation of worldly pleasures is the key to goodness.
Renunciation of worldly pleasures means shortening aspirations.
Renunciation of worldly pleasures leads to asceticism.
Renunciation of worldly pleasures means not seeking that which is absent until that which is present [and available] perishes.
Renunciation of worldly pleasures is the greatest comfort.
If you desire the eternal, then renounce the pleasures of the evanescent world.
If you renounce worldly pleasures, you will be free from the wretchedness of this world and prosperous in the everlasting abode.
Through renunciation of worldly pleasures, wisdom is brought forth.
The fruit of renouncing worldly pleasures is repose.
Complete renunciation of worldly pleasures is from the best [act of] faith while desire for this world corrupts conviction.
The foundation of generosity is renunciation of worldly pleasures.
Your renunciation of this world will save you and your desire for it will cause you to fall into destruction.
A person’s renunciation of that which perishes is proportionate to his certainty about that which is everlasting.
Restraining the soul from the pleasures of this world is the praiseworthy asceticism.
Espouse the renunciation of worldly pleasures, for indeed it helps the religion.
How can one who does not know the value of the Hereafter renounce worldly pleasures?!
How can one who has not killed off his lustful desires reach the essence of asceticism?!
Let your renunciation be of that thing which perishes and disappears, for indeed neither will it remain for you nor will you remain for it.
He who renounces worldly pleasures will never become poor.
Whoever renounces worldly pleasures, tribulations become easy for him [to bear].
One who renounces pleasures in this world fortifies [and protects] his religion.
Whoever renounces this world, it will not elude him.
By renouncing worldly pleasures, the fruit of wisdom comes forth.
Never renounce anything until you know what it is.
There is no asceticism like refraining from that which is forbidden.
There is no benefit in the asceticism of one who does not renounce avarice and adorn himself with piety.

Verily the hearts of those who renounce worldly pleasures weep even when they laugh, and their sadness intensifies even when they are [apparently] happy, and their self-loathing increases even though they are [apparently] delighted with what they are given.
When the one who renounces worldly pleasures flees from the people, seek him out.
When the one who renounces worldly pleasures seeks people, flee from him.
Be one who renounces that which the ignorant ones desire.

Blessed be the ones who renounce pleasures in the world and desire the [bounties of the] Hereafter. These are the ones who have taken the earth as their carpet, its dust as their beds, its water as their perfume, the Qur’an as their inner garment and supplication as their outer garment, and have subscribed themselves to the ways of the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam (‘a).
One who neither despairs over the past nor becomes overjoyed with the future has taken asceticism from both its sides.
One who renounces [the pleasures of] this world makes light of the tribulations [he faces in it].
One who renounces [the pleasures of] this world frees himself and pleases his Lord.
One who renounces [the pleasures of] this world will be delighted by the garden of the abode [of perpetual bliss in the Hereafter].
One who does not renounces [the pleasures of] this world will not have a share in the Garden of the Abode.
Repose is in renouncing worldly pleasures.
Look at the world with the eyes of the abstinent, parting one and do not look at it with the eyes of the adoring, attached one.

Renounce the pleasures of this world and turn away from it, and be careful that death does not descend upon you (while you are a runaway from your Lord in its pursuit thereby becoming wretched or) while your heart is attached to anything of it as a result of which you are destroyed. considered to be one of the qualities of the pious people.
Visiting [one’s brothers in faith] on a regular basis is protection from lethargy.
Visit those who are obedient to Allah for His sake and take guidance from those who have been vested with His authority.
Visit each other for the sake of Allah, sit [and mingle] with each other for the sake of Allah, give for the sake of Allah and withhold for the sake of Allah.
One whose visits increase, his cheerfulness decreases.
Adornment is in righteous probity, not in elegant clothing.

Begging weakens the tongue of the speaker, breaks the heart of the courageous hero, puts the free honourable one in the position of a humbled slave, takes away the radiance of one’s face and wipes out one’s sustenance.
Begging is the collar of humiliation, it takes the honour away from the honourable and the stature away from the noble.
Humiliation [and disgrace] is in asking from people.
Begging is the key to poverty.
The bane of asking [others] is lack of success [in getting what one asks for].
If you want to be obeyed [or your request to be granted] then ask for that which is feasible.
Let your request be for a thing, the charm of which will last for you long after the negative consequences [of your asking] have ended.
One who asks properly is aided.
Whoever asks [from] other than Allah deserves to be deprived.
One who increases his requests from people is humiliated.
One who asks for that which he does not deserve is faced with deprivation.
One who repeats his request to the people, they get irritated by him.
One who asks for that which is above his rank deserves to be deprived.
When one does not protect his dignity from [the humiliation of] asking you, then preserve your honour by not turning him away.
Your countenance is like frozen water that is melted by asking; so [be careful and] consider whose presence you are melting it in.
Do not ask the one from whom you fear deprival.
Never turn away the beggar, even if he exceeds the limits.
Do not turn away the beggar and safeguard your magnanimity by not depriving him.
There is no humiliation like asking [for something from others].
There is nothing more tormenting than having to ask from the ignorant out of desperation.
Verily you are in greater need of the reward for that which you give than the asker is [in need] of that which he takes from you.
Verily you will gain more joy by [the reward of] what you have given than the one who seeks from you gains in what he has received from you.
Give the beggar before he asks, for indeed if you make it necessary for him to ask, then you will have taken from his dignity that which is greater than what you have given him.
Give your wealth generously to the one who has sacrificed his self-respect for you, for indeed the sacrificing of self-respect cannot be matched by anything.
Give generously when you are asked.
Seeking one’s need from he who is not worthy [of being asked] is harder than death.
What an evil trait importunity is!
Sacrificing one’s dignity by begging is greater [in value] than the extent of one’s need, even if it is great and even if it is granted.
Sacrificing one’s dignity in front of the wicked is the greatest death.
Make your address polite and you will hear a polite reply.
One who hastens to reply does not arrive at the right [answer].
Giving correct reply is an evidence of merit.
A discourteous reply stems from a discourteous address.
When one is asked about that which he knows not, he should never feel ashamed to say: I do not know.
Do not use harsh words [or foul language] even if you are unable to reply.
Never ask about that which has not [yet] happened, for in that which has already come about there is enough knowledge [that one can gain].
Do not be offensive in your address thereby being offended by the rudeness of the reply.
One who abandons the words “I don’t know” comes upon his [place of] destruction.
The person most prepared to [give a] reply is one who does not get angry.
Ask and you will learn.

When you ask, ask in order to learn and do not ask in order to embarrass [the one whom you are asking]. Indeed the ignorant one who learns is similar to a learned person and verily the learned one who is oppressive is similar to an ignorant person.
If you are ignorant then learn, and when you are asked about that which you do not know then say: Allah and His Prophet know better.
Too much asking leads to restlessness.
One who asks, learns.
One who asks, benefits.
One who asks properly, learns.
One who asks in his young age, answers in his old age.
The means by which an incapable person achieves his goal is the same one (means) that makes the powerful person incapable to achieving what he seeks.
The firmest rope that you can hold on to is the rope between you and Allah.
For everything there is a cause.
The strongest means [of gaining success in this world and the next] is having excellent [qualities and] merits.
The best means [to achieve closeness to Allah] is refraining from anger and keeping away from the humiliation of asking [others].
If you must be competitors, then compete with each other in establishing the ordinances of Allah and in enjoining good.

The physical prostration is putting the foreheads on the earth and placing the palms and knees on the ground along with the toes of the feet, with complete submissiveness of the heart and sincerity of intention.

The spiritual [aspect of] prostration is emptying the heart of [love for] that which perishes, proceeding with firm resolution in endeavouring towards the everlasting, removing pride and fanaticism, cutting off worldly ties and adorning oneself with the etiquettes of the Prophet.
What good forms of worship Prostration (sujūd) and bowing (rukū’) are.
The prison is one of the two [types of] graves.
One whose displeasure is much, his pleasure is not known.
One whose displeasure is much is not admonished.
How ugly is displeasure and how nice pleasure is!
Displeasure is enough of a suffering.
Whoever is displeased with what has been destined, adversity befalls him.
Do not be upset by the displeasure of the one who is pleased with falsehood.

Be wary of the displeasure of the One aside from whose obedience nothing can save you, and aside from whose disobedience nothing can destroy you, and aside from whose mercy nothing can accommodate you; and turn to Him and trust in Him.Be wary of the displeasure of the One aside from whose obedience nothing can save you, and aside from whose disobedience nothing can destroy you, and aside from whose mercy nothing can accommodate you; and turn to Him and trust in Him.
Generosity earns love [of people] and adorns one’s character.
Generosity is one of the two felicities.
Generosity clears away sins and attracts the love of the hearts.
Generosity and courage are honourable instincts which Allah, the Glorified, puts in the one whom He loves and has subjected to trials.
Generosity means being open-handed with your [own] wealth while being cautious with the wealth of others.
Generosity is that which one gives [himself], for if he gives after being asked, then it is [a result of] shame and embarrassment.
Generosity is the fruit of the intellect and contentment is the evidence of nobility.
Generosity and shame are the best characteristics.
The most courageous of people is the most generous of them.
The most honourable of qualities is generosity, and the most universal in benefit is justice.
The best [form of] generosity is for you to be open-handed with your wealth while being cautious with the wealth of others.
Verily the generosity of keeping oneself away from that which others possess is better than the generosity of giving.
The best thing by which praise is gained, is generosity; and the thing that draws forth the most abundant, lasting benefits is charity.
Generosity is a [righteous] trait; honour is a virtue.
Generosity is a [virtuous] quality.
Generosity is the adornment of a human being.
Generosity sows [the seeds of] love.
Generosity is the most honourable habit.
Generosity is a quality of the Prophets.
Generosity bears the fruit of [spiritual] purity.
Generosity covers up [one’s] faults.
Generosity earns praise.
Generosity is the symbol of magnanimity and nobility.
Through generosity, actions become beautiful.
Through generosity, faults are hidden.
Adorn yourself with generosity and piety, for these two are the embellishments of faith and the most honourable of your traits.
The best generosity is that which corresponds to the situations of need.
Generosity is the cause of adoration.
The cause of ascendancy is generosity.
The disgrace of generosity is extravagance.
He who holds back from giving has oppressed generosity.
Espouse generosity, for indeed it is the fruit of the intellect.
Espouse generosity and good etiquette for verily these two [traits] increase sustenance and bring about adoration.
One’s generosity is proportionate to one’s magnanimity.
Cover up your faults with generosity for it is indeed a covering for faults.
In generosity there is affection.
Verily the generosity of keeping oneself away from that which others possess is better than the generosity of giving.
The best thing by which praise is gained, is generosity; and the thing that draws forth the most abundant, lasting benefits is charity.
Generosity is a [righteous] trait; honour is a virtue.
Generosity is a [virtuous] quality.
Generosity is the adornment of a human being.
Generosity sows [the seeds of] love.
Generosity is the most honourable habit.
Generosity is a quality of the Prophets.
Generosity bears the fruit of [spiritual] purity.
Generosity covers up [one’s] faults.
Generosity earns praise.
Generosity is the symbol of magnanimity and nobility.
Through generosity, actions become beautiful.
Through generosity, faults are hidden.
Adorn yourself with generosity and piety, for these two are the embellishments of faith and the most honourable of your traits.
The best generosity is that which corresponds to the situations of need.
Generosity is the cause of adoration.
The cause of ascendancy is generosity.
The disgrace of generosity is extravagance.
He who holds back from giving has oppressed generosity.
Espouse generosity, for indeed it is the fruit of the intellect.
Espouse generosity and good etiquette for verily these two [traits] increase sustenance and bring about adoration.
One’s generosity is proportionate to one’s magnanimity.
Cover up your faults with generosity for it is indeed a covering for faults.
In generosity there is affection.
Abundance of generosity increases [one’s] friends and reforms [one’s] enemies.
If you were to see generosity in the form of a man, you would surely see him as a handsome person, pleasing to look at.
When there is neither generosity nor shame in a person, then death is better for him than life.
What a good trait generosity is!
There is no merit like generosity.
There can be no generosity with nothingness.1
Generosity is showing affection to the beggar and giving open-handedly.
One who acts aptly, acquires [success].
One who strives in seeking a mirage, his hardship is prolonged and his thirst increases.
One who hopes to quench his thirst from a mirage, his hope will be dashed and he will die of thirst.
One who is deceived by the mirage [of this world], the means [of attaining prosperity in the Hereafter] are cut off for him.
Dismissal with kindness is one of the two reliefs.
The goodness of inward thoughts is evidence of the soundness of insight.
Blessed is the one whose inward thoughts are good, whose outward [character] is righteous and who does not harm the people.
When the consciences are being reformed, the hidden rancour becomes evident.
When the outward gets corrupted, the inward also get corrupted.
One whose inward [feeling] is good, his outward [character] is righteous.
One whose inward [feeling] is good [and honourable] is not afraid of anyone.
Protect your affair and do not give away your secret in marriage to whoever proposes!
Keep your secret to yourself and neither entrust it to a judicious one who may err nor to an ignorant one who may betray [your trust].
The best secret discussion is that which is founded on religion and God-wariness, and is based on following the path of guidance and opposing vain desires.
Man is more protective of his secret.
Divulging [secrets] is the trait of outsiders [not that of believing Muslims].
Divulging the secret that has been entrusted to you is a [form of] betrayal.
Three people are not to be trusted with a secret: the woman, the telltale and the fool.
Your secret is a source of happiness for you if you conceal it but if you divulge it, it is your destruction.
He who divulges his secrets does not remain safe.
Your secret is your prisoner but if you divulge it, you become its prisoner.
Be stingy with your secrets and do not divulge the secret that has been entrusted to you, for indeed divulging [it] is betrayal.
Every time the keepers of secrets increase, [chances of] its divulgence becomes greater.
One who conceals the secret [that has been entrusted to him] is loyal and trustworthy.
If a person were to use his intellect, he would protect his secret from the one who has revealed [another’s secret] to him and would not inform anyone of it.
One who reveals your secret has ruined your affair.
One who conceals his secret has the choice [of doing as he wills with it] in his hand.
One who entrusts his secret to an unreliable person has forfeited his secret.
One who divulges a secret that has been entrusted to him has betrayed [a trust].
Whoever is weak in keeping his own secret, he will be even weaker in keeping the secret of others.
One who is too weak to protect his [own] secret will not be strong enough to protect the secret of others.
One who safeguards his secret from you has actually accused you [of being untrustworthy].
From the ugliest form of betrayal is divulging a secret.
I have never blamed anyone for divulging my secret when I was more unaccommodating of it than him [by revealing it to him in the first place].
The basis of a secret is its concealment.
Do not entrust your secret to one who has no trustworthiness.
Do not confide in the one who would divulge your secret.
Do not inform your wife and your servant about your secret as they will [use it to] subjugate you.
Do not confide in the ignorant one with any secret that he is unable to conceal.
One whose breast cannot accommodate his secret has no preservation (or prudence).
The speech of every gathering is [supposed to be] rolled up with its carpet.

If you gain confidence in your close friend then safeguard some of your affairs and conceal some of your secrets [from him], for it is possible that you may regret [revealing it all to him] sometime in the future.

topic: Happiness And Putting Joy In The Hearts
text: Happiness opens up the spirit and stimulates vitality.

topic: Happiness And Putting Joy In The Hearts
text: At times happiness becomes roiled.

topic: Happiness And Putting Joy In The Hearts
text: Perhaps [the joy of] happiness may turn bitter.

topic: Happiness And Putting Joy In The Hearts
text: Every joy [in this world] turns sour [eventually].

topic: Happiness And Putting Joy In The Hearts
text: No one puts joy in a [believer’s] heart except that Allah creates a grace from that joy, so whenever any calamity befalls him, it (the grace) flows over it just like the flowing of water until it expels the calamity from him just as the unfamiliar camel is expelled from the group of camels.
Extravagance is blameworthy in everything except in doing good deeds.
Verily giving this wealth where it has no right to be given is wastefulness and extravagance.
The ugliest [form of] giving is extravagance.
The refusal of the economizer is better than the granting of the extravagant.
Verily the withholding of preserver is more graceful than the giving of the squanderer.
Extravagance wipes out the plentiful.
Extravagance depletes the abundant.
Wastefulness is the symbol [and cause] of poverty.
Wastefulness is a penniless companion.
Abandon extravagance by economizing, and recall [your] tomorrow today.
Eschew extravagance, for neither is the generosity of the extravagant praised nor is his indigence sympathized [with].
The cause of poverty is extravagance.
You must abandon wastefulness and extravagance, and adopt the qualities of justice and equity.
Extravagance is censured in everything except in performance of virtuous acts and excessiveness in obedience [and worship of Allah].

Then shun extravagance by economizing, and recall today [what you will need] tomorrow; hold on to wealth [only] to the extent of your necessity and send forth the surplus for the day when you will need it.
Wastefulness is enough of an extravagance.
Too much extravagance destroys.
There is no honour in extravagance.
One who takes pride in wastefulness will be humiliated by indigence.
That which is above sufficiency is extravagance.
There is no ignorance like wastefulness.
There is no affluence with extravagance.
Woe be to the extravagant! How far he is from reforming himself and setting right his affair!
And the shunning of theft [has been prescribed] as a means of instilling virtue.
Aid your brother in every situation, and go with him wherever he goes.
Felicity is that which leads [one] to success.
The signs of felicity are sincerity [of intentions] in action.
Having a heart that is free of rancour and jealousy is from the felicity of a servant.
Felicity is gained by hastening good deeds and pure [and virtuous] actions.
The felicity of a person is [in] contentment and satisfaction.
The felicity of a man is in safeguarding his faith and working for his Hereafter.
It is enough of a felicity for a person that he be deemed trustworthy in religious and worldly affairs.
It is enough of a felicity for a person to turn away from that which perishes and become occupied with that which is everlasting.
You will never know the sweetness of felicity until you taste the bitterness of misfortune.
It is part of felicity to be granted success in performing righteous deeds.
It is from the perfection of felicity for one to strive for the betterment of the [whole] community.
Successfully attaining what is sought is part of felicity.
From the felicity of a person is his showing benevolence to those who are deserving of it.
A person does not attain felicity except through the obedience of Allah, the Glorified, and a person does not become wretched except by disobeying Allah.
No one attains felicity except by upholding the bounds of Allah and no one becomes wretched except by disregarding them.
It is from the felicity of a person that his good turns are done to one who thanks him and his benevolence is shown to one who is not ungrateful to him.
He who makes his brothers miserable does not gain felicity.
How close are felicities to misfortunes!
How far is repose in ease and inactivity from acquiring felicity!
When the presentation [of deeds] in front of Allah, the Glorified, takes place, felicity is differentiated from wretchedness.
The felicitous is one who considers that which is lost [to him] as insignificant.
Felicitous is one who fears the punishment [of Allah] so he has faith, and hopes for divine reward so he does good deeds.
Verily the most felicitous of people is one who has an exhorter in himself [that urges him] to obey Allah.
Felicitous is one who makes his obedience [and worship] sincere.
If you would like to be the most felicitous of people through what you have learnt, then act upon it.

Indeed only he is felicitous who fears divine punishment so he safeguards himself, and hopes for divine reward so he does good, and longs for Paradise so he wakes up [to worship] in the night. -Striving and Seeking
Strive to free your necks [from the shackles of this world] before the doors of ransom are shut.
Whoever hastens to the people with that which they dislike, they will speak about him that which they do not know.
Many a person strives in that which is harmful for him.
Many a person is awake so that another can sleep.
Many a person strives for one who is seated [doing nothing].
Travelling is one of the two torments.
The lies of an envoy give rise to corruption, cause the failure of the intended objective, nullify judiciousness and invalidate firm resolution.
Spilling blood without just cause invites the descending of divine wrath and the cessation of blessings.
Cut through the waves of discord by [embarking on] the ships of salvation.
Beware of dimwittedness for verily it causes one to be deserted by his friends.
Dimwittedness is idiocy.
Dimwittedness [and insolence] is an offence.
Dimwittedness is the key to ridicule.
Dimwittedness attracts evil.
Shun dimwittedness, for verily it belittles a person and dishonor’s him.
The weapon of ignorance is dimwittedness.
Dimwittedness is enough as a disgrace.
Increased dimwittedness brings about ill feelings and gives rise to hatred.
Dimwittedness is not like intelligence.
The wise person gets most fatigued when he speaks to a dimwit.
The most dim-witted of all fools is the one who boasts with foul language.
One who enters the circle of dimwits is debased.
One who censures a dimwit has exposed himself to insult.
Refraining from replying a dimwit is the best reply you can give him.
The dimwit does not know the right of the wise one.
Nothing corrects the dimwit but bitter [and harsh] speech.
Accompanying the dimwit corrupts one’s character.
It is from the [good] health of the bodies that maladies originate.1
There is no affliction greater than the unrelenting physical ailment.
There is no escape for bodies from maladies.
Solemnity is the ornament of the intellect.
Solemnity supports (or gives rise to) forbearance.
Calmness is a sign of intelligence.
Solemnity is evidence of nobility.
If you act with solemnity you will be honored.
Through solemnity, one’s reverence increases.
Espouse calmness, for indeed it is the best embellishment.
Be solemn when among the people and oft-remembering [of Allah and His bounties] when alone.
Let solemnity be your trait, for one whose silliness increases is scorned.
One who acts with solemnity is revered.
One whose solemnity increases, his exaltedness increases.
Espousing solemnity protects one from the lowliness of impetuousness.
Calmness is an excellent quality.
Solemnity is an excellent trait.
The solemnity of a man adorns him and his silliness tarnishes him.
The solemnity of an elderly person is a light and an embellishment.
The solemnity of old age is more beloved to me than the vigor of youth.
Many a thing that has been sent ahead (or has been pillaged) returns back [as it was before].
The most miserly of people is the only who is stingy with his Salām.
Offering greetings is one of the virtuous morals and traits.
Peace is the fruit of forbearance.
Peace is the cause of security and the sign of steadfastness.
Be peaceful with people and you will be safe; work for the Hereafter and you will be successful.
Whoever is peaceful with the people, his friends increase and his enemies decrease?
Whoever is peaceful with the people, his faults remain hidden.
One who is peaceful with the people gains security.
One who is pleased to live peacefully with the people will be safe from their adversities.
I found the reconciliation that does not weaken Islam to be more beneficial than war.
There is no outcome sounder than the outcomes of peace.

Islam means submission [to the will of Allah], and submission means certitude, and certitude means attestation, and attestation means confirmation, and confirmation means execution, and execution means action.
Verily Islam has a goal, so strive towards its goal and proceed towards Allah by fulfilling that which He has ordained upon you of His rights.
Islam is the most illuminated course.
And he (‘a) said about Islam: It is an instruction for the resolute, a sign for the one who examines it [carefully], a lesson for the one who takes heed and a salvation for the one who accepts it.
The embellishment of Islam is performing righteous actions.
Allah has prescribed Islam for you and has made its laws easy, and He has strengthened its pillars against those who wage war with it.
The outward side of Islam is radiant and its inward aspect is elegant.
The objective of Islam is [complete] submission [to the will of Allah].
Islam [has been prescribed] as a security form dangers.
The basis of Islam is truthfulness [in speech].
There is no fortress better fortified than Islam.
Islam is in need of faith.
Become a Muslim and you shall be safe [in the Hereafter].
The best of all Muslims in practicing Islam is he whose efforts are for his Hereafter and whose fear [of Allah’s wrath] is balanced with his hope [in His mercy].
Verily the Muslims (or the believers) are humble.
One who accepts Islam [and submits to the will of Allah] remains safe [in the Hereafter].
One who practices Islam properly is [truly] guided.

topic: Submission to the Will of Allah-
text: Submission means not blaming [Allah for what happens].

topic: Submission to the Will of Allah-
text: If you submit your soul to Allah, your soul remains safe.

topic: Submission to the Will of Allah-
text: The practice of the righteous people is complete submission [to the will of Allah].

topic: Submission to the Will of Allah-
text: Submit to Allah and your Hereafter will be saved.

topic: Submission to the Will of Allah-
text: Submit yourselves to the command of Allah and the command of His chosen servant, for verily you will never go astray with submission.

topic: Submission to the Will of Allah-
text: The end result of [complete] submission [to the will of Allah] is success in reaching the Abode of Bounties.

topic: Submission to the Will of Allah-
text: In submission there is faith.

topic: Submission to the Will of Allah-
text: Guided is the one who submits to the guidance of Allah and His Prophet and the one vested with His authority.

topic: Submission to the Will of Allah-
text: There is no faith better than surrendering to the will of Allah.

topic: Submission to the Will of Allah-
text: Verily if you submit to Allah, you will be safe and successful.

topic: Submission to the Will of Allah-
text: The root of faith is complete submission to the command of Allah.

topic: Submission to the Will of Allah-
text: One who submits to Allah remains safe.

topic: Submission to the Will of Allah-
text: Whoever surrenders to Allah will be granted security by Him and whoever wages war with Allah will be destroyed by Him.
One who seeks security remains steadfast [on the straight path].
One who desires security should adopt moderation.
One who wishes for security keeps himself steadfast on the straight path.
One who loves security must prefer poverty [over wealth] and one who loves comfort must prefer abstinence from pleasures in this world.

One who has three [qualities] in him, will remain safe both in this world and the next: He enjoins good and follows it himself, He forbids evil and keeps away from it himself, and he preserves the boundaries [and ordinances] of Allah, the Sublime and the Exalted.
There is no preservation more averting [of harm] than security [that is granted by Allah].
There is no attire more appealing than security [and well-being].
Many a person remains safe after regret.
Everyone who surrenders [to Allah] is protected.
One who surrenders [to Allah] remains safe.
One who surrenders himself to Allah is supported [by Him].
One who submits his affair to Allah is supported [by Him].
The one who surrenders [to Allah] is protected.
Forgetfulness is the reaper of longing [and desire].
One who forgets about what has been robbed from him, it is as if he has not been robbed.

He (‘a) consoled a man whose son passed away and [at the same time] was blessed with the birth of [another] son saying: May Allah make your reward great [for your patience] in that which He took away, and may His blessings be with you in that which He has bestowed [upon you].
How good a guidance having a good mien is!

Allah, the Glorified, has granted you with hearing so that it may heed [and comprehend] that which is concerns it and with sight so that what is dark for it may be brought to light [and seen clearly].
May Allah have mercy on the servant who hears a ruling so he heeds it, is invited to the right path so he approaches it, and holds on to the guide so he is saved.
Knowledge is not ruined except by the miscomprehension of the listener.
Listen and you will learn; remain silent and you will be safe.
One who listens well benefits quickly.
Do not desire for everything that you hear, for this suffices as gullibility (or foolishness).
Train your ears to listen well and do not pay attention to that which does not increase anything useful for you by listening to it, for verily this corrodes the hearts and leads to dispraise.
The listener is a partner of the speaker.
Do not discontinue the good practices that have been [previously] acted upon, and which the people have become familiar with, and which the masses have found suitable.
Beware of doing wrong [to others], for indeed it is a vile quality and verily the one who hurts others will surely be thrown into hell because of his wrongs.
Verily if you do wrong [to others] then you are only debasing and harming yourself.
Counter the wrongs [of others] by doing good [to them].
One who is thanked for doing wrong is [actually] mocked for it.
One who wrongs his subjects pleases his enviers.
One who wrongs others brings upon himself a severe reprisal.
Whoever treats people badly, they requite him with the same treatment.
One who proceeds in the course of his offences stumbles in his progress.
Do not wrong the person who does good to you, for one who wrongs the person who does him a favour will be denied favours [in the future].
Whoever wrongs his [own] family, no hope [of any goodness] can be attached to him.
How many a person has postponed doing something until death falls upon him!
The one who delays seeking repentance is in the greatest danger of the onslaught of death.
One who procrastinates in seeking repentance has no faith.
The eminent one is envied and the munificent one is loved and adored.
The eminent person is one who bears the burdens of his brothers and is neighborly to his neighbor.
The eminent person is one who neither flatters nor deceives, nor is he beguiled by greedy ambitions.
The eminent person is one who bears the responsibility of providing [for others] and is generous with his assistance.
The completion of eminence is in taking the initiative to do good to others.
The eminent among the people in this world are the generous ones and in the Hereafter, the God- wary.
The excellence of the eminent ones is in [their] devout worship [of Allah].
Righteous action, aiding the aggrieved and inviting guests [to one’s home] are instruments [and means] of eminence.
One whose brothers have to turn to other than him [for their needs] has not attained eminence.
Listening to the complaint of the aggrieved is part of eminence.
He who does not grant generously has not perfected [his] eminence.
He whose brothers need to turn to other than him [for help] has not achieved eminence.
There is no honour like eminence.
There is no eminence with vengeance.
There is no eminence in one who has a bad character.
He who does not support [and provide for] his brothers does not gain eminence.
There is no eminence in the one who lacks generosity.
Eminence is not perfected except by bearing the burdens [of others] and doing good turns.
Be wary of the sitting in the marketplaces, for indeed they are the locations of mischief and the visiting places of Satan.
The gatherings of the marketplaces are the visiting places of Satan.
Night vigil is one of the two lives.
Night vigil is the garden of those who yearn [nearness of Allah].
Night vigil is the insignia of the pious and the quality of those who yearn.
Keeping vigil at night in the remembrance [and worship] of Allah is the devotion of the Gnostics and the delight of the Near Ones.
Keeping vigil at night in the worship of Allah is the spring of the friends [of Allah] and the garden of the felicitous.
Keeping vigil at night in the remembrance [and worship] of Allah is the prize of the friends [of Allah] and the practice of the God-wary.
Keeping vigil at night in the remembrance of Allah is the opportunity of the felicitous and the promenade of the friends [of Allah].
Keep vigil at night and make your stomachs lean; and take away from your bodies so that you may be generous with it upon your souls.
The best of worship is staying awake at night in the remembrance of Allah, the Glorified.
What a good helper of worship night vigil is!
Facilitating [and making things easy for others] makes sustenance flow abundantly.
The most loathsome mode of conduct is inequity.
Through an equitable conduct, the adversary is overpowered.
Good conduct is the sign of a good conscience.
Good conduct is the beauty of power and the fortress of authority.
One whose conduct is evil, his demise makes the people happy.
One whose conduct is evil will never be safe at any time.
Woe be to the one whose conduct is evil, whose authority is oppressive, and who tyrannizes and infringes upon the rights [of those who are under him].
The most difficult of administrative policies is the removal of habits [and customs].
Tyranny is indeed an evil administrative policy.
The beauty of politics is [maintaining] justice in authority and pardoning despite having power [to punish].
Good administration is the mainstay of the citizenry.
Good administration makes leadership last.
One whose administration is good, obeying him becomes obligatory.
One whose administration is good, his leadership lasts.
One who falls short in administration [and politics] is poor in [and incapable of] leadership.
The foundation of administration is justice.
There is no leadership like [practicing] justice in administration.
Sovereignty is administration.
One who aspires to rise to power is patient in the face of the torment of politics.
Two things whose value is not understood except by the one who has lost them are youth and health.
The ignorance of a youth is excused and his knowledge is undermined.
Are those who are the prime of youth awaiting anything other than the stooping of old age?
Youthfulness and senility do not go together.
Be wary of gluttony, for whoever persists in it, his maladies increase and his dreams get corrupted.
Be wary of gluttony, for indeed it causes hardening of the heart, sluggishness in prayer and corruption of the body.
Gluttony prevents astuteness.
One who is cloyed by gluttony is obstructed by it from astuteness.
There is no astuteness with gluttony.
Gluttony and astuteness do not go together.
Overeating corrupts wisdom.
Gluttony obstructs astuteness.
Eating to one’s fill corrupts piety.
When the stomach gets filled with the permissible, the heart becomes blind to righteousness.
What an evil companion of piety overeating is!
Habitual overeating leads to a variety of ailments.
Overeating brings about insolence and corrupts piety.
One who increases his overeating is cloyed by his gluttony.
Overeating and performing one’s obligation do not go together.
How helpful to sins overeating is!
You must avoid habitual overeating, for verily it induces maladies and foments diseases.
One who informs you of your vilification has [himself] vilified you.
Courage is one of the two honours.
Courage is a ready support and an evident merit.
Courage is an embellishment, cowardice is a disgrace.
Courage is present honour, cowardice is evident dishonour.
The fruit of courage is a sense of honour.
The alms-tax of courage is struggling in the way of Allah.
The courage of a man is proportionate to his ambition, and his sense of honour is equivalent to his zeal.
It is to the extent of [one’s] zeal that courage is shown.
Fighting while dismounted [in battle] demonstrates the courage of champions.
The bane of courage is loss of resolve.
Be patient in [the face of] difficulties and dignified in [times of] turbulent upheavals.
It is for difficult times that [the friendships of important] men are preserved.
Be intent on [braving] difficulty when nothing will free you except difficulty.
Beware of surrounding yourself with evil, for you will be affected by it yourself before [harming] your enemy and you will destroy your religion by it before conveying it to others.
The greatest evil is in disparaging the painful advice of the compassionate, sincere adviser and being deceived by the sweetness of the flattery of the malicious praiser.
Verily in evil there is impudence.
Evil is impudence.
Delaying of evil is advantageous to good.
Evil is [a cause of] regret.
Evil makes its rider fall.
Evil is the ugliest of gates.
Evil is pestilent speech.
Evil is the symbol of destruction.
Evil is the carrier of misdeeds.
Evil degrades and strikes down.
Evil is punishable and brings dishonour (or is requited).
Considering evil to be loathsome impels one to refrain from it.
Delaying of evil is a benefit for good.
The consolidation of evil is in being deceived by respite [from chastisement] and reliance on [one’s own] action.
The consolidation of evil is in association with a wicked companion.
The attractiveness of evil is avarice.
The consolidators of evil are obstinacy and increased quarrelsomeness.
Many an evil may suddenly come upon you from whence you least expect it.
Increased wickedness is [a sign of] vileness and abjectness.
Counter evil with good.
Obedience to the calls of the wicked corrupts the outcome of matters.
He who embarks on evil is successful in attaining it.
The doer of evil is worse than the evil [itself].
Doing evil is a [means of] revilement.
None shall be punished for an evil act except its doer.
There is nothing worse than evil except its retribution.
There is nothing more corrupting for affairs or more destructive to the community than evil.
He who does not wear the gown of good has not disrobed from evil.
One who plunges into the depths of evil meets with danger [and adversity].
One who does evil has [actually] transgressed against his soul.
One whose evil is too much, [even] his companion is not safe from him.
Whoever abandons evil, the doors of good are opened for him.
One who lays the foundation of evil cause has [actually] instituted it against himself.
One who provokes a latent evil, in it will be his own destruction.
One who harbor’s evil feelings [and ill will] for others has actually harmed himself.
Whoever strips his heart of evil, his religion is secured and his conviction is confirmed.
One who does not know the harmfulness of evil is not capable of desisting from it.
One who repels evil with good, triumphs?
One who hates evil is safeguarded [from it].
One of the greatest deceptions is making evil appear good.
The ‘evil’ that is followed by Paradise is not [really] evil.
The foundation of evil is avarice.
One who is cautious of evil is like the one who does good.
Never count as good that by which you attain evil.
It behooves the one who recognizes the wicked to disassociate himself from them.
The evil of a man is evinced by his increased greed and his intense avarice.
How bad a provision evil action is!
The most severely punished thing is evil.
Evil is the riding mount of greed and vain desire is the riding mount of discord.
Evil is the ugliest of gates and its doer is the worst of companions.
Evil is concealed in everyone’s nature, so if its possessor overcomes it, it remains hidden and if he doesn’t overcome it, it is manifested.
Scythe the evil from the breasts of others be uprooting it from your [own] breast.
Efface evil from your heart, [and as a result] your soul will be purified and your actions will be accepted.
When you see evil then distance yourselves from it.
The one who gains victory by evil is [in actual fact] defeated.
Keep away from evil, for verily more evil than the evil [itself] is its doer.
It is the habit of the wicked to trouble [their] friends.
The habit of the wicked is harboring enmity for the righteous.
Every victor who gains victory by evil is [in actual fact] defeated.
The wicked person does not think good of anyone because he does not see them except through [the lenses of] his own nature.

Be wary of the wicked one during the coming of power [and authority], that he does not cause it to be taken away from you and during its departure [from you], that he does not gather support against you.
Be careful not to be deceived by the good act that the wicked one does by mistake.
Be careful not to be repelled by the evil act that the righteous one does by mistake.
Keep away from the wicked and sit in the company the virtuous.
The coming to power of the wicked is the tribulation of the virtuous.
The most evil of all is one who is not ashamed of [his actions in front of] the people and does not fear Allah, the Glorified.
The most evil of all people is one who boasts about his evil.
Honor is attained by earnest endeavors not by worn-out bones [of one’s ancestors].1
The greatest honour is humility.
The best honour is good etiquette.
The most honourable of honours is knowledge.
The best honour is doing good to others.
The best honour is desisting from harming others and doing good to others.
Honour is a virtue.
Honour is doing good to one’s kinsfolk.
Indeed honour is only attained by intellect and etiquette, not because of wealth and lineage.
The ladder of honour is humility and generosity.
The honour of a believer is his faith and his prestige is by his obedience [to Allah].
The honour of a man is his integrity and his beauty is his magnanimity.
One who knows the significance of his honour safeguards it from the lowliness of his base desires and falsity of his aspirations.
Holding on to comprehensive merit (or merits) is from the perfection of honour.
Honour is not perfected except through generosity and humility.
The honourable person is the one whose attributes are honourable.
The peripheries are the sitting places of the honourable.

The honourable person is not made reckless by the status he attains, even if it becomes as great as a mountain that is not shaken by strongest winds; and the lowly is made careless by the most inferior position, just as the grass that is moved by the passing breeze.
The honourable one never oppresses [others].
He (‘a) was asked about the distance between the east and the west so he replied: It is a day’s journey for the sun.
The most harmful thing is polytheism.
The smallest amount of showing off is polytheism.
Verily the slightest showing off is polytheism.
Ascribing partners [to Allah] is disbelief.
The bane of faith is ascribing partners to Allah.
The cause of destruction is polytheism.
stablish partnership with the one to whom sustenance has drawn near, for verily he is worthier of success and more befitting of prosperity.
Voraciousness tarnishes the soul, corrupts the religion and debases chivalry.
Beware of voraciousness, for verily it is a destructive quality.
Beware of voraciousness, for how many a food has prevented numerous other foods [from being consumed]!
You must refrain from voraciousness, for indeed it corrupts piety and causes one to enter the fire of hell.
Refrain from voraciousness, for verily it is the root of every vileness and the foundation of every depravity.
Beware of the vileness of voraciousness and greed, for verily it is the root of all evil, the plantation of disgrace, the debaser of the soul and the exhauster of the body.
Voraciousness is [a cause of] ignominy.
Voraciousness invites [one] towards evil.
Voraciousness is the beginning of avarice.
Voraciousness is the trait of the filthy.
Voraciousness increases anger.
Voraciousness is an accumulator of the worst faults.
Voraciousness is the foundation of every evil.
Voraciousness is from bad morals.
Through voraciousness morals are tainted.
What a bad character trait voraciousness is!
The fruit of voraciousness is rushing towards faults [and vices].
The cornerstone of [all] flaws is voraciousness.
The weapon of avarice is voraciousness.
Counter voraciousness with chastity [and moderation].
Voraciousness is enough of a destruction.
For everything there is a seed, and the seed of evil is voraciousness.
There is no chastity with voraciousness.
One whose soul is voracious becomes disgraced despite his affluence.
Everything other than voraciousness is chastity.
Every voracious one is tormented.
The voracious one will never be seen happy.
Be cautious of the enemy that enters the breast stealthily and whispers in the ears secretly.

Beware of the enemy of Allah, Iblīs, that he should not infect you with his disease [of evil] or entice you with his cavalry and his infantry, for he has aimed at you with the arrow of [false] threats and shot at you from close range.
He (Satan) has made them (the people) the target of his arrows, the ground that he steps on and the handle that he holds.

They have taken Satan as the overseer of their affairs and he has made them his partners [in crime], so he hatches [his eggs] in their breasts and creeps and crawls into their laps. He sees with their eyes and speaks with their tongues. He leads them to misdeeds and adorns for them idle talk like the action of one whom Satan has made partner in his domain and speaks falsehood through his tongue.
Your Lord, the Glorified, called you but you turned away and fled, and Satan called you so you responded and drew closer [to him].
Stand against Satan through struggle and overpower him by opposition, [by doing this] your souls will be purified and your statuses will be elevated in the sight of Allah.
The deception of Satan allures and entices.

Do not follow the claimants [of Islam] whose dirty water you drink along with your clean one, whose sicknesses you mix with your health and whose falsehood you allow to enter into your rightful matters.
Never allot a portion for Satan in your actions and do not give him access to your soul.
Occupy yourself with that which you are answerable for.
One who is occupied by the unimportant loses that which is more important.
He who puts Paradise and hell in front of him is [always] occupied.
He one whose goal is salvation and attaining the pleasure of Allah is [always] occupied.
The intercessor is the wing of the seeker [which helps him attain what he seeks].
The interceder of a criminal is his humility in seeking pardon.
The interceder of a sinner is his admission (of guilt), his repentance and his apology.
The interceder of mankind [on the Day of Reckoning] acting upon the right and adhering to the truth.
With dissension there is aversion.
Every wretchedness is [moving] towards ease.
Collecting the [wealth that is] forbidden is part of wretchedness.
Corrupting one’s Hereafter is from wretchedness.
One of the signs of wretchedness is cheating one’s friend.
One of the signs of wretchedness is offending the virtuous.
It is from the wretchedness of a person for his certitude to get corrupted by doubt.
It is from wretchedness for a person to safeguard his world at the expense of his religion.
Corruption of intention is from wretchedness.
Verily from wretchedness is corruption of one’s Hereafter.
The wretched is one who is proud of his condition and is beguiled by the deception of his hopes.
The most wretched among you are the most greedy among you.
The most wretched of [all] people is one who sells his religion for someone else’s worldly gain.1
How many a wretched person has been visited by his death while he is striving to acquire [worldly gain].
Gratitude is one of the two rewards.
Gratitude for blessings is a recompense for its past and a source of its [increase in the] future.
Gratitude has greater value than a good action because the gratitude lasts while the good action comes to an end.
Be grateful and you will increase.
Continue being grateful and the blessing upon you will continue.
Occupy yourself in being grateful for the blessing rather than being delighted by it.
Look frequently at those over whom you have been given superiority, for verily this is one of the gates [and means] of gratitude.

Be grateful to the one who favours you and favour the one who is grateful to you, for indeed there is no end to favours when they are appreciated and there is no continuation for them when they are unappreciated.
Let the recompense for the blessing which has come upon you be the showing of goodness to one who wrongs you.
Be good neighbours to the blessings of religion and this world by showing gratitude to the one who guides you to them.
Take advantage of gratitude, for the least of its benefits is increment [of blessings].
The best thing that spoken loudly [in order that others may hear] is the gratitude that is publicized.
The best gratitude for blessings is favoring others with them.
The most deserving of those to whom you do good is the one who does not disregard your good turn.
The most deserving of your gratitude is the one who does not prevent you from acquiring more.
The first thing that is incumbent upon you with regards to Allah, the Glorified, is being grateful for His blessings and seeking His pleasure.
The most effective thing that makes a blessing last longer is gratitude and the greatest thing by which tribulations are overcome is patience.
The most deserving of people for an increase in blessing is the most grateful of them for what he has been granted of it.

The most beloved of people to Allah, the Glorified, is the one who deals gratefully with the blessings that have been bestowed upon him and the most hated of them to Him is the one who deals ungratefully with His blessings.
No one acquires gratitude except by giving [generously] from his wealth.
Verily in every blessing there is a right of gratitude to Allah, the Most High, so whoever fulfils it, He increases it for him and whoever does not do so risks losing his blessing.
Verily the servant is [always] between blessing and sin, [and] nothing rectifies [or improves] them except repentance and gratitude.
Gratitude is [a means of] increment.
Gratitude is obligatory.
Gratitude is advantageous.
Gratitude causes blessings to flow forth abundantly.
Gratitude is an embellishment for blessing[s].
Gratitude is the fortress of blessings.
Showing [one’s] affluence is from [the ways of showing] gratitude.1
Gratitude is the interpreter of intention and the tongue of [one’s inner] conscience.
Gratitude is the embellishment of comfort and the fortification of blessing.
Gratitude is obligatory upon the people of blessings.
If Allah bestows you with a blessing then show gratitude.

Verily it behooves those who have been protected [from sins] and have been favored with safety [from misdeeds] to take pity on sinners and other disobedient people; and to make the gratitude for their good state prevail over them and act as a barrier for them.
When you are given, show gratitude.
When you do good to others with a blessing [that you have been bestowed with], then you have shown gratitude for it.
When the edges of blessings reach you, then do not repel their peaks by lack of gratitude.
Through gratitude, blessing lasts.
Through gratitude, more is obtained.
The fruit of gratitude is increase in blessings.
Showing gratitude leads to increment.
The best gratitude is that which warrants increase.
Constant gratitude is the symbol of obtaining increment.
Increased gratitude and keeping ties with near relative’s increases sustenance and prolongs [one’s] life.
The cause of increment is gratitude.
Showing gratitude to your Lord is [done] through prolonged praise.
The gratitude of one who is above you is through true friendship and loyalty.
The gratitude of your equal is through good brotherhood.
The gratitude of one who is under you is through generous bestowal.
Showing gratitude for blessings is a protection from adversities.
Gratitude to the Almighty brings forth abundant blessings.
Showing gratitude for blessings results in its increase and leads to its renewal.
Gratitude for blessing is a safeguard from its alteration and a guarantee of its sustentation.
The gratitude of a believer is manifested in his action.
The gratitude of a hypocrite does not surpass his tongue.
Gratitude for a past blessing results in the coming of renewed blessings.
Showing gratitude for blessings multiplies and increases them.
Showing gratitude for blessings leads to its increase and showing ingratitude for it is evidence of its reduction.
Gratitude for blessing is a safeguard from the coming of adversity.
The gratitude of a scholar for his knowledge is [in] his acting upon it and his sharing it with the one who deserves it.
Your gratitude to the one who is pleased with you increases [his] approval and loyalty (or preservation) towards you.
Your gratitude to the one who is angry with you leads to reconciliation and his having a favorable disposition towards you.

He (‘a) said to a man whom he was congratulating for the birth of his son: You have occasion to be grateful to Allah, the Giver, and be blessed in the gift that you have been bestowed with. May he come of age and may you be blessed with his devotion.
He who praises his benefactor and mentions him with goodness [and appreciation] has shown gratitude for [his] kindness.
You must give thanks [both] in ease and adversity.
You must be constantly grateful and ever patient, for these two [qualities] increase blessing and remove tribulations.
In gratitude for blessings lies their continuity.
In gratitude there is increase.
Lack of gratitude removes the desire to do good deeds.
Bind the approaching blessings with gratitude, for not everything that escapers comes back.
Gratitude is sufficient for increase.
The guarantor of increase is gratitude.
Be occupied by gratitude for your good state and [your] safety from that which has afflicted others.
None is capable of fortifying blessings the way [showing] gratitude for them does.
If Allah, the Glorified, had not made a promise [to punish those who are disobedient], it would have still been obligatory not to disobey Him out of gratitude for His blessings.
One who shows gratitude deserves more.
Whoever shows gratitude, his blessing lasts [longer].
One whose gratitude increases, his blessings multiply.
One who is inspired to show gratitude will not be deprived of increase.
One who does not show gratitude for a blessing is punished by its cessation.
One who continues showing gratitude makes the goodness [and blessing] last.
One who is bestowed with a blessing and gives thanks for it is like the one who is tried with difficulties and bears them patiently.
One who shows gratitude for [and act of] kindness has indeed fulfilled its right.
When someone thanks you without [your having done him] a good turn, then do not consider yourself safe from his censure without any breach.
Whoever thanks the one who favours him has indeed recompensed him.
One who does not show gratitude for favours should be counted [as being] from the livestock [rather than being human].
One who shows gratitude without any favor, censures without any wrongdoing?
Whoever makes the effort to show concern for you, then make the effort to show him your gratitude?
One who guards (or mixes) blessings with gratitude is surrounded by more [blessings].
One who does not begird [his] blessings by being grateful for them has indeed exposed them to cessation.
Whoever thanks Allah, He increases [the blessings] for him.
One who feels grateful for blessings in his heart deserves increase [even] before he manifests [the gratitude] on his tongue.
One whose gratitude increases, his goodness [and blessing] increases.
One whose gratitude diminishes, his goodness [and blessing] comes to an end.
One who is granted a blessing has indeed been enslaved by it until he is freed by his show of gratitude for it.
One who thanks Allah, the Glorified, has to give thanks twice as it was He who enabled him to give thanks [in the first place] and that is the gratitude for being thankful.
One who shows gratitude to you for your kindness (or the kindness of someone else) has [actually] requested you [for something].
One who does not show gratitude for blessing is deprived of more [blessings].
Nothing fortifies blessings like gratitude.
Nothing shows gratitude for favors like bestowing them on others.
Allah, the Glorified, does not open the door of gratitude for anyone and then close the door of increase [in blessings].
With gratitude blessings last [longer].
Do not forget to show your gratitude when you receive blessings.
Be a thankful servant in times of ease and a patient servant in times of adversity.
Doubt corrupts certitude and nullifies faith.
Be wary of doubt, for verily it corrupts religion and nullifies certitude.
The most destructive thing is doubt and uncertainty, and the most constructive thing is piety and keeping aloof from sin.
Doubt is misgiving.
Doubt [in the existence of God] is disbelief.
Doubt corrupts religion.
Doubt nullifies faith.
Doubt is the fruit of ignorance.
Doubt leads to polytheism.
Doubt puts out the light of the heart.

Indeed doubt was only named ‘shubha’ because it resembles the truth. As for the close friends of Allah, their illumination in it is [their] certitude and the direction of the right path is [itself] their guide; while the enemies of Allah are called towards it (doubt) by their misguidance and their guide is blindness.
The bane of certitude is doubt.
By continued doubt [in God], polytheism comes about.
The fruit of doubt is perplexity.
It is possible that conjecture may [turn out to] be correct.
The cause of perplexity is doubt.
I am amazed at the one who doubts in the power of Allah while he sees His creation!
Acting suspicious1 is a shame and having an eager desire to backbite is [a cause of entering] hellfire.
Everything that is devoid of certitude is [mere] conjecture and dubiety.
Every person has a [desire and a] need, so distance yourselves from suspicion.
A person will never go astray until his doubt overcomes his certainty.
One who falters increases his doubt.
One whose doubt increases, his religion gets corrupted.
One whose suspicion increase, his backbiting [also] increases.
The sincere one is not suspicious and the one who is certain does not doubt.
He in whose heart doubt has settled does not believe in Allah.
Keeping away from suspicion is from the best magnanimity.
Who can be more of a failure than the one who crosses [over] from certainty towards doubt and perplexity?
The smallest doubt can corrupt certitude.
Nobody more timid than the suspicious one.
Suspicion leads to mistrust.
When suspicion appears, thoughts [about others] become negative.
Abandon that which causes you to doubt for that which does not cause you to doubt.
Let your inquiry into doubtful matters be conclusive, for indeed the one who falls into them becomes confounded.
The sceptic has no religion and the backbiter has no magnanimity.
The suspicious one is never found in a sound state.
The most abased of people is the sceptic.
The suspicious person is always sick.
The sceptic has no religion.
The doubting one has no certitude.
Whoever complains of his distress to [anyone] other than a believer, it is as if he has complained against Allah, the Glorified.
Whoever complains of his distress to a believer, it is as if he has complained to Allah, the Glorified.
ne who is gleeful of the mistakes made by others, [then] others will be gleeful of his mistakes.
Participating in deliberation leads to the appropriate decision.
Consult your enemies; you will know from their opinion how much enmity they have [for you] and what their objectives are.
Consult your intelligent enemy and be wary of the opinion of your ignorant friend.
Compare some opinions with others, from this the right course of action will come to light.
Suspect your intellects, for indeed it is from trusting in them that mistakes are made.
Consultation is [a means of] ease for you and a difficulty for others.
The best person whom you can consult is the one with [abundant] experience and the worst person whom you can associate with is the one with [numerous] faults.
Consultation is [a means of] seeking [assistance and] support.
Seeking advice is the essence [and source] of guidance.
The one who seeks advice is protected from failure.
The one who seeks advice is on the side of success.
Consultation elicits for you the correct opinions of others.
Indeed consultation has only been urged because the opinion of the adviser is unbiased while the opinion of the consulter is mixed with bias.
The bane of consultation is contradiction of opinions.
When you have decided [to do something], then consult [with others].
When you proceed with an affair then proceed after deliberation and seeking advice; do not delay your action of today to tomorrow, and perform each day’s action on that same day.
Ignorance of the adviser is [a cause of] destruction of the consulter.
It behooves the intelligent one to add the opinion of the intelligent people to his opinion and to merge the knowledge of the wise with his knowledge.
It behooves the intelligent one to continuously seek the right path and abandon obstinacy.
The best among those whom you consult are the people of wisdom and knowledge, and those who possess experience and judiciousness.
Betrayal of the one who submits [to you] and the one who consults [you] is from the most atrocious acts and the gravest wickedness, and leads to punishment in hellfire.
Consult before you decide and think before you proceed.
Consult the intelligent ones and you will be safe from error and regret.
Consult in your affairs those who fear Allah and you will be rightly guided.
Being unjust to the one who seeks advice is [the worst form of] oppression and betrayal.
You must seek consultation, for indeed it is the result of judiciousness.
It is the duty of the one who is consulted to strive in giving an [appropriate] opinion but it is not for him to guarantee success.
The essence [and source] of guidance is in consultation.
Consultation suffices as a supporter.
One who acts against [good] advice gets perplexed.
One who consults an intelligent person acquires [his objective].
One whose adviser goes astray, his planning is nullified.
Whoever gives sincere advice to the one who consults him, his planning becomes good.
Whoever cheats the one who consults him, his foresight is taken away.
One who consults the people of intellect is enlightened by the lights of the intellects.
One who consults the people of intellect and wisdom attains success and rightness.
One who consults with the people shares in their [combined] intellects.
One who consults the people of intellect and wisdom, gains success through prudence and aptness?
One who persists in consultation does not lack a praiser when the right result is achieved or an apologizer when a mistake is made.
One who seeks advice does not go astray.
Nothing derives an appropriate outcome like consultation.
Consulting the judicious person who is concerned for you is a [means of attaining] triumph.
Consulting the ignorant person who is concerned for you one is dangerous.
How good a support consultation is!
What a good backing [and support] consultation is!
Do not consult with your enemy and hide your information [from him].
Never consult with the ignorant in your affairs.
Do not belittle a noteworthy opinion [even] when it is brought to you by an inferior person.
Do not include a miser in your consultation as he will turn you away from the goal and frighten you with poverty.
Never include a coward in your consultation as he will weaken your resolve in the matter and [will] make a mountain out of a mole hill.
Do not consult the liar, for indeed he is like the mirage that makes the distant seem near and the near seem distant.
Never include a greedy person in your consultation as he will facilitate evil [deeds] and glamorize avarice for you.
The intelligent one never dispenses with consultation.
There is no backing [and support that is stronger and] more reliable than consultation.
One who becomes satisfied with his own intellect (or action) has gone astray.
Longing [for Allah and the Hereafter] is from the qualities of those who have certitude.
Longing [for Allah] is the intimate companion of the Gnostics.
One who longs [for Allah] forgets [this world].
One who longs [for Allah] sets out [towards him] at nightfall.
Lust is one of the two causes of deviation.
Lustful desires are fatal illnesses, and the best cure for them is acquiring patience against them.
Lustful desires are the snares of Satan.
Overcome [your] lust, [and] your wisdom will be perfected.
Turn your back on lustful desires, for indeed they drive you to perform sinful acts and to fall upon evil deeds.
Lustful desires are fatal diseases, and the best cure for them is acquiring patience against them.
Beware of allowing lustful desires to dominate you, for indeed its immediate result is dispraised and future consequence is detrimental.
Beware of letting lustful desires overpower you hearts, for indeed its beginning is bondage and its end is destruction.
The beginning of lust is pleasure and its end is harm.
Lust entices.
Lustful desires are diseases.
Lustful desires are lethal.
Lust is spoliation [of intellect and faith].
Lust is the most harmful of enemies.
