Lustful desires are lethal poisons.
Lustful desires enslave the ignorant.
Yielding to lust is the worst disease.
Verily if you are controlled by your lustful desires, they will cause you to leap into frivolity and error.
When lust tries to overcome you then defeat it by curtailing excesses.
By controlling [one’s] lust, one becomes free of every flaw.
Abandoning lustful desires is the best worship and the most beautiful habit.
The sweetness of lust is made bitter by the shame of ignominy [and humiliation].
Repulsing lust is more effective in exterminating it while fulfilling it only makes it more intense.
Inhibiting lust and anger is the struggle of the noble ones.
Increased lust degrades magnanimity.
Being overpowered by lust is the cause of evil.
The flame of lust induces the impairment [and destruction] of the soul.
Counter lust with restraint.
Oppose lust as a rival would oppose his rival and fight it as an enemy would fight his enemy.
Obeying one’s lust corrupts the faith.
Obedience to lust is destruction and disobedience to it is dominion.
He who turns away from the lustful desires of this world attains the Garden of Repose [in the Hereafter].
The slave to lust is lowlier than the slave of a human being.
The slave to lust is a prisoner who cannot be freed from his imprisonment.
The heart that is attached to lustful desires is unable to benefit from sincere exhortations.
Being overpowered by lust is the greatest destruction, and controlling it is the most honourable dominance.
Being overpowered by lust nullifies preservation [of oneself from sin] and leads to destruction.
Overcome [your] lust before it ferocity becomes strong, for verily if it becomes strong it will possess you and use you, and you will not be able to stand up against it.
The comrade of lustful desires is the prisoner of [their] consequences.
The associate of lust has a sick soul and a troubled mind.
Resist lust by subduing it and you will be victorious.
How many a lustful desire has prevented [one from attaining] a lofty status!
How can one who is not aided by [divine] protection refrain from lust?
A servant will never be destroyed until he prefers his lust over his religion.
There is no sin that is worse than following [one’s] lust, so do not obey it as it will preoccupy you from [the remembrance of] Allah.
If you had abstained from lustful desires you would surely have been safe from tribulations.
Whoever overcomes his lust, his intellect becomes manifested.
Whoever is overcome by his lust, his soul will not be safe.
One who is patient in the face of his lust becomes complete in [his] magnanimity.
One who controls his lust is indeed pious.
One who kills his lust rejuvenates his magnanimity.
One whose lust increases, [the expense for] his provision becomes heavy.
One who overcomes his lust, protects his status.
Whoever hastens towards lustful desires, afflictions rush towards him.
One who is enticed by lustful desires permits his soul to be a target of calamities.
Whoever controls his lust, his magnanimity becomes complete and his end becomes good.
One who does not control his lust does not control his intellect.
One who has not remedied his lust by abandoning it is still sick.
Multiplication of sins stems from submission to lust.
One who is overcome by lust is more abased than one who is enslaved.
One who makes a habit of following [his] lustful desires is overwhelmed by afflictions, is associated with evils and has certainty about the permanence [of this world].
Do not exceed the limits in your lust and anger as they will degrade you.
There is no reason with lust.
Nothing corrupts God-wariness but the dominance of lust.
There is no trial [and temptation] greater than lust.
How good it would be for people not to desire that which they ought not to [crave for].

One who dies on his bed while he is cognizant of the rights of his Lord, His Prophet and the right of his household, has died a martyr and his reward rests with Allah, the Glorified. He is also eligible for the recompense of the good acts he intended to do, as his intention takes the place of drawing his sword [in battle]. Indeed, for everything there is a [limited] term that it cannot go beyond.
We ask Allah, the Glorified, for [our inclusion in] the ranks of the martyrs, the fellowship of the felicitous and the company of the Prophets and the virtuous ones.
And testimony [has been prescribed] as a means of overcoming denials.
One who gives false testimony for you will give a similar testimony against you.
There is no good in the testimony of the treacherous.
Good renown is a fortification of power.
Love of fame is the cornerstone of every affliction.
The grey hair of old age is enough of a warner.
The grey hair of old age is enough of an announcer [of impending death].
Change your grey hair [by dyeing it] and do not resemble the Jews.
When you’re black [hair] becomes white, your best [part of life] has passed away.
Grey hair [of old age] is the last of the promises of annihilation.
Verily the People of Paradise will look at the stations of our followers just as a person among you looks at the celestial bodies in the sky.

Verily Allah, the Glorified, checked the earth and chose for us followers who would help us, would be gladdened by our joy and saddened by our sadness, and would spend from their persons and their possessions in our way – these are the ones who are from us and shall rejoin us [in the Hereafter].
Our follower is like the bee. If they knew what was in its abdomen, they would surely have eaten it.
Our follower is like the citron, its smell is fragrant and [both] its outward and inward are beautiful.
Four things disgrace a man: miserliness, dishonesty, voraciousness and bad manners.
Patience is the first prerequisite of proficiency (or certitude).
Patience in times of hardship makes reward abundant.
Patience is one of the two triumphs.
Patience in the face of calamities makes one attain honourable ranks.
Patience in the obedience to Allah is easier than patience in the face of His chastisement.
Patience in affliction is better than wellbeing in [times of] comfort.
Patience is the best trait and knowledge is the most honourable embellishment and gift.
Patience is for a person to bear that which befalls him and to suppress [his anger with] that which enrages him.
Patience is of two types: enduring what you hate and abstaining from what you love.
Patience is the best vestment of faith and the most honourable of human qualities.
Refraining from lust is chastity, from anger is courage and from sin is piety.
Patience is of two types: Patience in affliction is pleasantly beautiful, but patience in refraining from the prohibited is even better.
Patience in poverty with dignity is better than wealth with indignity.
Patience in the face of agonizing distress leads to success in attaining opportunities.
Be patient [and] you will achieve.
Be patient [and] you will triumph.
Occupy yourself with patience in adversity instead of being distressed by it.
Be patient with the action which will surely bring you reward and refrain from the action the punishment for which you will not be able to bear.
Adopt patience, for indeed patience has a sweet end and an auspicious result.
Be patient with the bitterness of truth and beware of being deceived by the sweetness of falsehood.
Stick to the earth, be patient in trials, and do not move your hands and follow the fancy of your tongues [in order to start quarrels].
Espouse patience, for indeed it is the pillar of faith and the basis of affairs.
The best patience is longanimity.
The strongest resource for [facing] difficulties is patience.
The best patience is during the bitter pain of tragedy.
The best patience is abstaining from that which is loved [but prohibited].
The best asset is patience in difficulty.
The action with most praiseworthy results is patience.

Verily patience is a virtue except if it is [when others are patient] concerning you, and apprehension is bad except if it is over you; verily the affliction [we suffer] by your loss is great whereas [the hardships] before you and after you are insignificant [in comparison].1
Patience is a foundation [for other good actions].
Patience is an elevation; agitation is degradation.
Patience is a means of repelling [adversities].
Patience is a victory; haste [and impatience] is a danger.
Patience fights off mishaps.
Patience is the cornerstone of faith.
Patience is the shield against poverty.
Patience is the fruit of conviction.
Patience makes tragedy easier to bear.
Patience purges calamity.
Patience is the fruit of faith.
Patience is an asset for [facing] affliction.
Patience is the guarantor of success.
Patience is the symbol of [divine] succour.
Patience is more repelling for affliction[s].
Patience constrains the enemies.
Patience is the [best] resource for [tackling] poverty.
Patience is an aide in every affair.
Patience is the best of assets.
Patience is the strongest vestment.
Patience is a riding mount that does not stumble.
Patience is the most helpful thing in [facing the hardships of] one’s lifetime.
Patience is the best of the believer’s soldiers.
Judiciousness and excellence lie in patience.
Patience in the face of suffering leads to the gaining of opportunity.
Patience descends [in proportion to] to the extent of the hardship.
Patience in times of difficulty is from the best endowments.
Patience in hardship blunts the edge of the one who rejoices in your suffering.
Patience is more repelling for harm.
If Allah tests you with some hardship, then be patient.
If you are patient, then in [the reward of] Allah there is a restoration [and recompense] from every hardship.
If you are patient then things will transpire as ordained and you will be rewarded, and if you are agitated then things will transpire as ordained and you will bear the burden of sin.
Either be patient like the freemen or else seek distraction [and forget] like the inept.
If you are patient, you will attain the stations of the virtuous through your patience, and if you become agitated, then your agitation will cause you to enter the fire of hell.
Either be patient like the honourable ones or else seek distraction like the animals.
Verily you will never attain that which you love from your Lord except by refraining from that which you desire.
Verily if you are patient in affliction, thankful in comfort and satisfied with the [divine] decree, you will gain the pleasure of Allah, the Glorified.
When you are patient in adversity, you blunt its edge.
Through patience, adversity is made lighter.
Through patience, [one’s legitimate] desires are realized.
Through patience, the loftiness of matters is attained.
Give glad tidings of success and victory to yourself when you are patient.
Dress yourself with patience and certainty, for these two are good provisions in [both] comfort and hardship.
The reward of patience takes away the sufferings of tribulation.
The reward for patience is the loftiest reward.
Good patience is the vanguard of victory.
Good patience is the basis of every affair.
Good patience is an aide in every matter.
Persevering patience is the symbol of success and victory.
May Allah have mercy on the person who makes patience the conveyance of his life and piety the provision for his death.
The cornerstone of faith is patience.
Your patience in [times of] hardship lightens the adversity and brings abundant reward.
Your patience in bearing agonies gains you opportunities.
Bid yourselves to patiently perform acts of worship and protect yourselves from the impurity of evil deeds, [as a result] you will find the sweetness of faith.
Blessed is the one who makes patience the conveyance of his salvation and piety the provision of his death.
Per during patience is the quality of the virtuous.
Espouse patience in distress and tribulation.
Espouse patience and tolerance; for whoever espouses these two [qualities], adversities become easy for him [to bear].
Espouse patience, for indeed it is a protective fortress and the worship of those who possess certitude.
Espouse patience, for the intelligent one holds on to it and the ignorant one returns to it.
Espouse patience, for the judicious one holds on to it and the agitated one turns back to it.
It is during the first blow [of adversity] that the patience of the noble ones is seen.
During the descending of hardships and successive adversities, the excellence of patience becomes manifest.
In patience there is triumph.
In tribulation the excellence of patience is realized.
Sometimes patience becomes difficult [to come by].
It is seldom that one is patient yet he does not acquire [his objective].
It is seldom that one is patient yet he does not become powerful.
It is seldom that one is patient yet he does not gain victory.
How many a lock has been opened with patience!
One who is not patient in his toiling [for earning his livelihood] has to be patient in destitution.
The patient one is never deprived of victory, even if it takes a long time [to come].
None bears the bitterness of truth except the one who is certain of its sweet [and pleasing] aftermath.
The affair of the patient one returns to the realization of his goal and reaching his aspiration.
With patience, there is no adversity.
There is nothing that gives a more praiseworthy result, or a more delightful consequence, or is more repelling for bad etiquette, or more helpful in realizing what is sought, than patience.
One who is patient is victorious.
One who is patient attains his aspiration.
One who seeks relief from patience is relieved by it.
Have sweet patience during the bitter affair.
The guarantor of succour is patience.
For every afflicted one there is [a refuge in] patience.
Reward will never be acquired until [the bitter pill of] patience is swallowed.
One who seeks relief from patience will never be deprived of succor.
One who is patient in the obedience of Allah will be granted [something] better than what he was patient with, by Allah, the Glorified.
Whoever arms himself with the shield of patience, calamities become easy for him [to bear].
One who remains patient throughout the long harassment [of people] has demonstrated true piety.
One who is patient in the trial of Allah, the Glorified, has fulfilled the right of Allah, has feared His chastisement and has hoped for His reward.
One who is patient honours himself, attains success with reward and obeys Allah, the Glorified.
One who clothes himself with patience and contentment gains power and nobility.
Whoever is patient in the obedience of Allah and refrains from His disobedience, then he is [indeed] a patient struggler.
One whose patience is prolonged, his breast becomes straitened.
One who sets foot upon the vessel of patience gains victory?
Patience during hardships is from the treasures of faith.
Patience in [times of] calamities is from the best judiciousness.
Patience during tribulation is one of the signs of good character.
He who is patient is not afflicted.
One who adopts patience does not fail.
Nothing obtains reward like patience does.
That which you abstain from is better than that which you delight in.
How good it is for a person to refrain from that which he desires!
Afflicted one, what has made you patiently bear your disease, and [what has] made you remain steadfast in the face of your hardships, and [what has] consoled you from weeping over yourself?
There is no stumbling with patience.
Discomforts are not repelled except by patience.
There is no aide better than patience.
Patience (or virtue) is not realized except by experiencing the pain of going against what one is accustomed to [and enjoys].
With patience, judiciousness is strengthened.
The bitterness of patience bears the [sweet] fruit of victory.
The bitterness of patience is removed by the sweetness of victory.
How good a supporter patience is!
How good a succor patience is during tribulation!
The one who wears the garment of piety and certitude is [truly] guided.
Do not make haste in that which Allah has not hastened for you.
There is no faith like patience.
Whoever is patient, his hardship becomes easy [to bear].
Whoever is patient, his torment is lightened.
One who is not saved by patience, is destroyed by agitation.
One who remains patient with the bitter harassment [of people] has demonstrated true piety.
Teach your young children [how to perform the ritual] prayer and make them accountable for it when they reach puberty.
Good health is the more salubrious of the two delights.
Good health is the best blessing.
With good health, enjoyment becomes complete.
With good health, there is delight in the taste [of food].
The alms-tax of good health is striving in the obedience of Allah.
Are the people who are enjoying the vitality of good health awaiting anything other than the afflictions of illness?!
Good health and gluttony do not go together.
Good health is not attained except through a good diet.
he chest is the guard of the body.
harity is the greater of the two gains.
Charity is the better of the two reserves.
Charity brings down mercy.
Charity repels tribulation and calamity.
Verily you are more in need of spending [in charity] that which you earn than [you are of] earning that which you amass.
When you become penniless then do business with Allah through charity.
Through charity, death gets deferred.
The blessing of wealth is in charity.
Safeguard yourselves through charity.
The best charity is that which is given most secretly.
Foster your faith with charity.
Groom yourselves with piety and cure your sick with charity.
Charity given in secret expiates wrongdoings and charity given openly is a means of increasing wealth.
Charity given openly repels ill-fated death.
Give charity and you will be saved from the vileness of parsimony.
Expiate your sins and endear yourselves to your Lord through charity and keeping ties with your near relatives.
Charity is a treasure.
Charity protects one from falling into evil.
Charity is the best means of attaining closeness [to Allah].
Charity is the best of virtuous deeds.
Charity is a valuable treasure.
Charity given secretly is from the best righteous actions.
Charity protects.
Make your weights [of good deeds] heavy with charity.
Truthfulness is the strongest column of faith.
Truthfulness is the pillar of Islam and the column of faith.
Truthfulness is the cornerstone of faith and the adornment of the human being.
Truthfulness is the beauty of a human being and the column of faith.
Be truthful and you will be successful.
Adopt truthfulness and trustworthiness for indeed these are the two traits of the righteous.
Espouse truthfulness even if you fear harm may come of it, for indeed this is better for you than the lying from which benefit is expected.
Seek benefit from truthfulness in every situation and you will gain; keep away from evil and dishonesty, and you will remain safe.
Be truthful in your words, be sincere in your actions and purify yourselves with piety.
The most sublime thing is truthfulness.
The best honesty is fulfilling your promises.
The best honesty is fulfilling your promise and the best generosity is exerting yourself [in helping others].
Truthfulness is a means [of attaining success].
Truthfulness is trustworthiness; dishonesty is a betrayal.
Truthfulness saves [one from hardship].
Honesty is a merit; dishonesty is a vice.
Honesty is [a means to] success; dishonesty is a cause of disgrace.
Truthfulness is an elevation.
Honesty is the trust of the tongue.
Truthfulness is the brother of justice.
Honesty is the language of truth.
Truth is the best speech.
Truthfulness is the life of God-wariness.
Truth is the soul of speech.
Truthfulness is the garb of religion.
Truthfulness is the garb of certitude (or of the God-wary).
Truthfulness is the cornerstone of religion.
Truthfulness is a refuge and an honour.
Truthfulness is the most successful evidence.
Salvation is with the truth.
Honesty is the manifested truth.
Truth is the noblest (or the best) narration.
Honesty is the garb (or the language) of truth.
Truth is the best foundation (or the best informer).
Truthfulness is the perfection of nobility.
Truth is the uprightness of everything.
Truthfulness is the most honourable characteristic of one who has conviction.
Truthfulness is the best asset.
Truthfulness is the trust of the tongue and the ornament of faith.
Truthfulness is the correspondence of speech with divine dispensation.
Through truthfulness, salvation is attained.
Through truthfulness, magnanimity becomes complete.
By truthfulness, words become adorned.
By honesty and loyalty, magnanimity becomes complete for its possessor.
The cornerstone of faith is truthfulness.
Two things are the basis of religion: honesty and certainty.
The truthfulness of a man is to the extent of his magnanimity.
Adopt truthfulness, for it is the best foundation.
Adopt truthfulness, for whoever is truthful in his speech, his status is elevated.
The end result of truthfulness is salvation and security.
Truthfulness has diminished among the people and dishonesty has become abundant; love is been expressed by [people with their] tongue while they hate each other with their hearts.
For everything there is an adornment and the adornment of speech is truthfulness.
For [the speaker of] truth there is benefit.
Let the most trustworthy of people in your estimation be the one who is most truthful in his speech.
Let your recourse be to the truth, for indeed truth is the best companion.
If things were to be differentiated from each other, honesty would be with courage and cowardice would be with dishonesty.
A goodly mention is better for a person than the wealth that he bequeaths to the one who does not praise him.
One who speaks the truth becomes successful.
Whoever is known for his truthfulness, his lies are [also] accepted.
Whoever turns aside from truth, his path becomes narrow.
One whose speech is truthful, his loftiness is increased.

How truthful is a person’s testimony against himself and what witness is there against him better than his own deeds?! A man is not recognized except by his knowledge, just as a strange tree is not known except when it bears fruit, thus the fruits are evidence of its origins. The excellence of every person is known by his merit, and thus the honourable one is distinguished by his morals and the vile one is disgraced by his wickedness.
Do not tell the truth to one who responds to your truth by denying [and belying] it.1
There is no interpreter clearer than the truth.
There is no report better than the truth.
There is no way that is more rescuing than the truth.
He who argues with [the support of] truth is not defeated.
Truth is the best narration.
The truth saves you, even if you fear it.
The least of things [required for salvation] is truthfulness and trustworthiness.
Verily the truthful one is honoured and dignified, and indeed the liar is abased and humiliated.
The truthful one is honoured and dignified.
The truthful one is on the highest rank of salvation and honour.
Many a truthful one who informs you about [a matter of] this world may be deemed a liar by you.
Be truthful and you will become loyal.
One who is truthful improves his religiousness.
One who is always truthful will not be deprived of honour.
One whose language is truthful, his proof becomes strong.
One whose language is truthful, his proof is correct.
One who is truthful is saved.
The truthful one achieves with his honesty what the liar cannot achieve with his deception.
The truthful one earns three things with his honesty: the virtue of being considered reliable, becoming beloved and being revered.
It is during the change of circumstances that the [real] gems among the people are known.
The rigid [and difficult person or issue] may become soft.
Devote yourself to [working for] the welfare of the believers and pious ones.
How far is probity from the people of evil and impudence!
One who is dutiful with Allah, the Glorified, does not spoil [his relationship] with anyone.
If your zeal for reforming the people becomes heightened, then begin with yourself; for indeed your pursuit for the righteousness of others while you are [yourself] corrupt, is the greatest flaw.
I am amazed at the one who sets out to reform the people while his own soul is more severely corrupted yet he does not reform it and pursues the reformation of others.
How can one who does not reform himself reform others?!
Rectify when you have corrupted and complete [your good act] when you have done good.
he worst disease is vainglory.
Many a [show of ostentation and] vainglory brings about loss.

topic: Prayer and one who stands for Prayer-
text: Prayer is the better of the two means of [attaining] nearness [to Allah].

topic: Prayer and one who stands for Prayer-
text: Prayer is a fortress [that protects] from the influences of Satan.

topic: Prayer and one who stands for Prayer-
text: Prayer is the fortress of the all-Merciful and the instrument for expelling Satan.

topic: Prayer and one who stands for Prayer-
text: Prayer causes [divine] mercy to descend.

topic: Prayer and one who stands for Prayer-
text: When one of you stands to perform prayer, then let him pray the prayer of one who is bidding farewell (i.e. he should assume that it is the last prayer he will perform in his lifetime).

topic: Prayer and one who stands for Prayer-
text: And prayer [was prescribed] as a purification from arrogance.

topic: Prayer and one who stands for Prayer-
text: How many of those who stand [to perform prayer] have nothing in their prayer but [physical] effort.

topic: Prayer and one who stands for Prayer-
text: If the one who offers prayer knew how much divine mercy is descending upon him, he would surely not raise his head from prostration.

topic: Prayer and one who stands for Prayer-
text: I am not worried by a wrongdoing in which I am given time so that I can offer two units of prayer [and seek forgiveness].
Silence covers you with dignity and suffices as your provision for seeking pardon.
Be silent and you will remain safe.
Espouse silence and your thoughts will remain hidden (or will become illuminated).
Remain silent in your lifetime and your affair will become lofty.
Espouse silence, for the least of its benefits is safety.
Espouse silence and you will be accompanied by safety and security; espouse contentment and you will be accompanied by prosperity and honour.

Espouse silence and be patient with contentment for the little provision [that you have], [and as a result] you will become great (or your will overcome) in your world and will become great in your Hereafter.
The best silence is that which prevents [one] from error.
Remaining silent when speech is inappropriate is more praiseworthy than eloquence.
Silence is dignity and idle talk is disgrace.
Silence is a means of deliverance.
Silence is the garden of contemplation.
Silence is the sign of forbearance [and judiciousness].
Silence is dignity and safety.
Silence without contemplation is dumbness.
Silence is the sign of nobility and the fruit of intelligence.
Silence is the adornment of knowledge and the symbol of forbearance [and judiciousness].
If there is eloquence in speech, then in silence there is safety from blunder.
Only the one who is capable of giving a reply [but does not do so] can be called ‘silent’; otherwise ‘inarticulate’ is more appropriate a description.
When you speak a word, it controls you but when you withhold it, you control it.
Through silence, reverence increases.
Sometimes silence is more eloquent than speech.
The cause of safety is silence.
Silence that is results in your safety is better than speech that is results in your reproach.
Silence that covers you with honour is better than speech that earns you regret.
Silence that earns you reverence is better than words that drape you with disgrace.
Silence, the result of which is praised, is better than speech whose consequence is dispraised.
Your remaining silent until you are requested to speak is better than your speaking until you are requested to become silent.
The silence of the ignorant person is his covering.
Blessed is the one who remains silent except from the remembrance of Allah.
Cling to silence, for it keeps you safe and saves you from regret.
The veil of wrongdoing is silence.
Increased silence earns you reverence.
Be a person of much silence without being inarticulate, for indeed silence is the embellishment of the scholar and the cloak [that hides the ignorance] of the ignorant.
One who maintains silence is safe from reproach.
One who maintains silence is safe from aversion [and hatred of others].
Whoever restrains himself from excessive speech, the people bear witness to his intelligence.
One who remains silent is safe.
How good a companion of forbearance silence is!
There is no forbearance like silence.
There is no worship like silence.
There is no reverence like silence.
There is no guardian that is more protective than silence.
There is no treasurer [and protector of secrets] better than silence.
There is no benefit in remaining silent from wisdom just as there is no good in speaking falsehood.
There is no good in remaining silent from the truth just as there is no benefit in speech with ignorance.
One who remains safe by being silent is like the one who derives benefit by speaking.
The severest of hardships is [having] evil offspring.
Hardships are the key to reward.
Reward with Allah, the Glorified, is to the extent of the hardship undergone.
The hardship of [lacking] patience is the greatest of hardships.
Hardships are divided equally among the creatures.
Hardship in religion is the greatest of hardships.
The reward for [bearing] hardship is greater than the extent of the hardship [itself].
Indeed you are the target of calamities and the object of sicknesses.
At times, tribulation may abase [a person].
When you see that Allah, the Glorified, is continuously testing you [with hardships], then [know that] He has woken you [from your slumber of negligence].
When hardships distance themselves, solace draws near.
When you see your Lord continually testing you [with hardships] then be grateful to Him.
When you fear the difficulty of an affair then be firm against it, it will yield to you; and deceive time about its calamities, it will become easy for you.
When tribulations come to you then sit and accept them, for indeed your standing up and confronting them will only aggravate them.
When adversity takes you by surprise, then seek refuge in patience and in seeking assistance [from Allah].
Through discomforts, Paradise is attained.
Through calamities, happiness is spoiled.
The harm that one faces in calamity is to the extent of [the loftiness of] one’s rank.
It is with great difficulty that lofty ranks and perpetual bliss are attained.
The trial of a man is proportionate to his faith and religion.
The tribulation of a man is in his submission to avarice and [false] and hope.
Reward descends in proportion to the hardship [that one bears].
Three things are from the greatest tribulations: a very large family, an overwhelming loan and unrelenting sickness.
The reward for hardship is proportionate to the patience exhibited in it.
Continual strife is from the greatest tribulations.
Sometimes you may be the cause of your own misfortune.
To the extent of the hardship, there is reward.
Every time the value of a thing that is competed becomes great, the difficulty of losing it increases.
One who does not prepare himself to confront hardships [with patience and supplication], the hardships befall him [while he is unprepared for them].
One who starts complaining about the hardship that has befallen him is actually only complaining against his Lord.
One who turns his attention away from this world, hardships become easy for him [to bear].
One who hits his hand on his thigh in times of hardship has nullified his reward.
One who exaggerates small hardships, Allah tries him with great ones.
One who faces successive calamities acquires the merit of patience through them.
One of the greatest hardships for the virtuous is having to socialize with the wicked.
How great is the hardship in this world when accompanied by the severe indigence of tomorrow (i.e. the Hereafter)!
A hardship that befalls others and has reward for you is better than the hardship that befalls you while its reward and recompense is for others.
A hardship from which good is expected is better than a blessing for which gratitude is not expressed.
Be happy with tribulation and pleased with affliction [as you will gain great reward for it].
The worst of adversities are those in which there is no reckoning [and recompense].
Verily great reward accompanies great trials; so when Allah, the Glorified, loves a community, He tries them.
The one who exposes himself to affliction puts himself in danger.
Tribulation follows behind ease [and comfort].
Many a person is shown sympathy for an affliction that is [actually] his cure.
Many a person who is afflicted is made stronger by his affliction.
The distress of tribulation [one faces] is proportionate to the blessings [one receives].
Tribulation may come suddenly.
Every tribulation other than the fire [of hell] is [a means to] wellbeing.
For every heart there is anguish.
When you are tested, be patient.
How many a person is tested with blessings!
How many a person is blessed through tribulation!
Do not consider yourself secure from tribulation in your times of safety and comfort.

topic: The one who hits the mark and the one who errs-
text: The one who hits the mark, achieves and the one who errs, loses.

topic: The one who hits the mark and the one who errs-
text: Being right is [a means of] safety, erring is [a cause of] reproach and haste is [a reason for] regret.

topic: The one who hits the mark and the one who errs-
text: To everyone who shoots hits the mark.
Correctness is [performing] the most appropriate action.
Correctness is one of the branches of deliberation.
Increased correctness points to abundant intelligence.
One who strives for correctness becomes successful.
When the answer is overcomplicated, correctness is negated.
good countenance is the beginning of felicity.
A good countenance is an apparent beauty.
A beautiful countenance is the first of the two felicities.
Fasting is one of the two means to good health.
Fasting on the ‘luminous days’ (i.e. on the 13th, 14th and 15th) of every [lunar] month raises the stations and magnifies the rewards.
Fasting of the heart from thinking about sins is better than fasting of the stomach from food.
Fasting of the soul from the pleasures of this world is the most beneficial fasting.
Fasting of the body means restraining oneself from food willfully and by choice, out of fear of punishment and out of desire for reward and recompense.
Fasting of the soul means restraining the five senses from all the sins and emptying the heart of all the motives of evil.
Fasting of the heart is better than fasting of the tongue, and fasting of the tongue is better than fasting of the stomach.
And fasting [has been prescribed] as a test of the sincerity of the people.
How many of those who are fasting gain nothing from their fast but thirst!
In order to derive lessons, examples are given.
For people who take lesson, examples are given.
For people of understanding speech becomes figurative.
Metaphors are given for the people of intellect and insight.
The best [form of] laughter is a smile.
The excessive laughter of a man corrupts his dignity.
Excessive laughter alienates the companion and disgraces the leader.
One whose laughter increases, his reverence decreases.
One whose laughter increases, his heart dies.
One whose laughs excessively is regarded as being low.
Do not show your teeth [in laughter] while you have done such shameful deeds.
Never laugh too much such that your reverence is lost; and do not joke [too much] thereby [resulting in your] being taken lightly.
Sometimes suffering may last [for long].
One who discloses his suffering to the people torments himself.
The necessities of [dire] conditions lower the necks of men.1
The necessities of [dire] conditions take one towards embarking on terrible deeds.
The plight of poverty impels one towards a despicable affair.
When you become weak, then be weak in the disobedience of Allah.
Be from among those who are neither overcome by violence nor affected by weakness.
The most destructive thing is persistent deviation.
How many a deviation has been embellished by a verse from the Book of Allah just as a bronze dirham is embellished by a coat of silver.
It is enough of an error for a person to command others to do what he does not do [himself] and forbids them from that which he does not refrain from.
For every deviation there is a cause.
What is there after truth except error?
Healthy consciences are more truthful witnesses than eloquent tongues.
The soundness of consciences is from the best provisions.
When sincerity is achieved the consciences are illuminated.
onor your guest even if he is ignoble; and stand up from your sitting place for your father and your teacher, even if you are a ruler.
Hospitality is the cornerstone of magnanimity.
For every agony there is a way out.
No agony intensifies but that Allah brings its relief closer.
Many a time jubilation turns into rage.
Blessed is the one who embarks on the way of the honorable and sticks to the highway of illumination [and truth]; and [one who] is infatuated with the Hereafter and turns away from this world.
Indeed, the highway of truth has been made manifest for those who seek it.
They have indeed been given time to seek deliverance and have been guided to the clear course.
One who deviates from the clear tracks ends up following the courses of destruction.
One who slips from the highway of the course falls into the perplexity of narrowness.
One who deviates from the clear highway drowns in the depths of the sea.
Hold back from [traversing] a path when you fear its deviation.
Adopt the way of steadfastness, for indeed it will earn you honour and save you from reproach.
Take to the highway of illumination [and truth] and follow it, otherwise Allah will replace you with others.
Whoever deviates from the truth, good becomes evil for him and evil becomes good, and he gets intoxicated with the intoxication of misguidance.
Do not permit your selves to take you into the paths of the oppressors.
Food is eaten and shared with three groups [in three situations]: alongside brothers with happiness, alongside the poor with selflessness and alongside the children of this world with magnanimity.
How bad a food the forbidden [food] is!
How bad a sustenance consuming the wealth of orphans is!
Few are those who increase their consumption of food and don’t fall ill [because of it].
Seldom does one increase his consumption of excess foods without getting afflicted by sicknesses.
Eating less food is more honorable for the soul and makes good health last longer.
Eat citron before food and after it as the progeny of Muhammad (s) do this.
Whoever eats less, his aches [and ailments] are reduced.
Whoever consumes less, [the burden of] his sustenance is lightened.
One who sows in himself the love of different types of food, reaps the fruit of a variety of maladies.
Decrease your [consumption of] food and your ailments will reduce.
When you feed [someone] then satiate him.
That which you have eaten has gone, but what you have fed to others spreads [like a pleasant fragrance].
Beware of being critical of the people while going easy on yourself, thereby rendering your sin grave and being deprived of reward.
bey [Allah] and you will benefit.
Obey [Allah] and you will gain.
Obey Allah in all you affairs, for indeed obedience to Allah is superior to everything; and espouse piety.
Obey Allah, the Glorified, in every situation, and do not empty your heart of His fear and His hope even for a split second, and always seek forgiveness [from Him].
Obey the one who is above you and the one who is under you will obey you; rectify your inner self and Allah will rectify your outer state.
Obey Allah in accordance with what His Prophets have commanded you.
Respond to the calls of the Prophets of Allah and submit yourselves to their commands and be obedient to them, [as a result] you will be included in their intercession.
Beware of being missed by your Lord in His worship, or being seen by Him in His disobedience thereby making Him displeased with you.
Achievement of goodness is through maintaining obedience.
Obedience and virtuous actions are the two profitable trades.
The best [act of] obedience is turning away from [worldly] pleasures.
The best [act of] obedience is renunciation of worldly pleasures.
The one who is the most sincere well-wisher for himself is he who is most obedient to his Lord.
The best obedience is relinquishing the [worldly] pleasures.
The most beloved of servants to Allah is the most obedient of them to Him.
The most deserving of Allah’s mercy among the people are those who are most steadfast in His obedience.
The most deserving of obedience is one from whom you cannot find any escape and the one whom you cannot turn down.
The most deserving of [obedience from] those whom you obey is the one who orders you to [maintain] piety and forbids you from [following] vain desires.
Verily the true friend of Muhammad, peace be upon him and his progeny, is one who obeys Allah even if his close relatives distance themselves from him [because of it].
Verily Allah, the Glorified, has made obedience an advantage for the sagacious when the incapable ones fall short.
Obedience saves and disobedience destroys.
Obedience is compliance.
Obedience is the most protective of accoutrements.
Obedience is the prize (or endeavor) of the sagacious.
Obedience [to Allah] is a profitable trade.
Obedience is the longest lasting prestige.
Obedience is the prestige of the underprivileged.
Obedience brings forth [divine] reward.
Obedience is a mark of respect to the Imamate.
Obedience extinguishes the anger of the Lord.
He who adorns himself with obedience possesses honour.
Obedience to Allah is the strongest means [of attaining success in both worlds].
Obedience is the most protective (or most reliable) safeguard.
Verily I do not urge you to any obedience but that I practice it before you, and I do not forbid you from any disobedience except that I desist from it before you.
Verily if you obey Allah, He will save you and make your [final] abode good.
When acts of obedience diminish, wrongdoings increase.
Through obedience one draws nearer [to Allah].
Through obedience there is success.
By obedience Paradise is brought closer for the pious.
By [their] virtuous obedience, the righteous ones are known.
Seek intercession through the obedience of Allah and you will succeed.
Hold on to the obedience of Allah and He will bring your nearer [to Himself].
The fruit of obedience is Paradise.
The reward of Allah is for those who obey Him and His punishment is for those who disobey Him.
Devote yourself assiduously to obedience and rush towards performing righteous deeds, keep away from evil acts and make haste towards good acts, and keep away from doing what is forbidden.
Stop following [the path of] aggression and obduracy, and follow the path of obedience and submission [to Allah], [by this] you will be happy in the Hereafter.
Whoever embarks on [the ship of] obedience [to Allah], his port of call is Paradise.
Rush towards acts of obedience and race towards doing righteous actions, but if you fall short, then be careful not to fall short in performing that which is obligatory.
Blessed is the one who observes obedience to his Lord.
Blessed is the one who follows praiseworthy piety and opposes dispraised vain desires.
Blessed is he who follows the course of peace by the sight of the one who shows him the way and by obeying the guide who instructs him.
Blessed is the one who is successful in his obedience [to Allah], has a good character and safeguards the affair of his Hereafter.
Obedience to Allah, the Glorified, is not attained except by the one who strives [for it] and spares no effort [in attaining it].
Obedience to Allah is the key to [every] right action and the rectification of [every] corruption (or of the Hereafter).
Obedience to Allah, the Glorified, is the highest pillar and the strongest accoutrement.
The shade of Allah, the Glorified, in the Hereafter is spread out for the one who obeys Him in this world.
You must obey the One whom you cannot be excused for being ignorant about.
You must show obedience to Allah, the Glorified, for indeed obedience to Allah is superior to everything.
You must obey the one who commands you to religion [and the obedience of Allah] for verily he is guiding you and saving you [from chastisement in the Hereafter].
Obedience is proportionate to [one’s] intellect.
In obedience [to Allah] there are treasures of benefit.
The excellence of obedience makes one attain lofty stations.
And obedience [to the Imam was made obligatory] as a respect for the Imamate.
If Allah, the Glorified, had not given incentives for His worship, it would have still been obligatory to worship Him out of hope for His mercy.
One who obeys Allah, has sought [His] assistance (or has seen the truth).
Whoever seeks closeness to Allah through obedience, He grants him good gifts.
One who follows the path of obedience to Allah attains something greater [than what he would get by following other paths].
Whoever takes the obedience of Allah as his merchandise, profits come to him without any trade.
One who does not commence with sincere intention in his obedience [and worship] is not successful in gaining rewards.
One whose obedience increases, his honor increases.
From the best of deeds is acquiring [and performing] acts of obedience [and worship].
No adorner can adorn himself with anything better than obedience to Allah.
No commandment of Allah, the Glorified, that must be obeyed, comes but that it seems unpleasant [to the carnal soul].
Espousing obedience [to Allah] is the best accoutrement [for the Hereafter].
How good a means [of attainting closeness to Allah] obedience is!
He who has been granted success in obeying [and worshipping Allah] has [truly] gained success.
Guided is the one who obeys his Lord and fears his sins.
Protect yourselves from the chastisement of Allah by hastening towards obedience to Allah.
Do not apologize for an affair in which you have obeyed Allah, the Glorified, for this suffices as a [commendable] virtue.
There is no honour like obedience [to Allah].
There is no obedience to the creation in disobedience to the Creator.1
Every obedient one is honoured.

Be obedient to Allah, the Glorified, and delight in His remembrance, and when you are in a state of turning away from Him, picture Him approaching you. He is calling you to His forgiveness and covering you with His kindness.
One who obeys his Lord gains authority.
One who obeys his Lord gains success.
Whoever obeys Allah, his affair becomes lofty.
Whoever obeys Allah, his affair becomes elevated.
One who obeys Allah will never become wretched.
One who obeys Allah, the Glorified, becomes powerful and strong.
Whoever obeys Allah, the Glorified, his support becomes powerful.
One who obeys Allah, the Glorified, is not harmed by the resentful from among the people.
Whoever obeys Allah, He chooses him [to be among those who are close to Him].
One who obeys your command has exalted your status.
How quick is the downfall of a tyrant!
A seeker may fail [to achieve what he seeks].
Every seeker is [himself] sought [by death].
Every seeker other than Allah is sought.
How many a seeker is deprived while the one who does not seek is granted [sustenance].
For the seeker who achieves what he seeks, there is delight in [his] accomplishment.
Not every seeker is granted [sustenance].
Whoever seeks a thing achieves it, or part of it.
Whoever seeks that which is in the possession of people, they debase him [for it].
One who seeks that which is impossible loses his quest.
Not every seeker fails.
At times the matters that are pursued are regarded with displeasure.
Sometimes the matter that is pursued and [its] acquisition become difficult.
At times that which is sought after is attained.
Abasement, disgrace and wretchedness are in covetousness and greed.
Covetousness makes one enter [into difficulties and humiliation] but does not make him return from it; and it gives a guarantee but does not fulfil it.
The most destructive thing is covetousness.
The most harmful thing is covetousness.
The ugliest of traits is covetousness.
The worst thing is covetousness.
The root of avarice is covetousness and its fruit is reproach.
He who covers himself with covetousness has degraded himself.
The places where intellects become most deficient are under the flashes of greed.
Covetousness is harmful.
Covetousness is an affliction.
Covetousness is bondage.
Covetousness is indigence.
Covetousness humiliates while piety exalts.
Covetousness is the beginning of evil.
Covetousness is a besieging (or and evident) indigence.
Covetousness is a present humiliation.
With covetousness comes humiliation.
Coveted objects humiliate men.
Covetousness is endless bondage.
Covetousness debases the commander.
If you give in to covetousness, it will destroy you.
Through avidities the necks of men are lowered [in humiliation].
How bad a companion of religion covetousness is!
The fruit of covetousness is wretchedness.
The fruit of covetousness is humiliation in this world and the Hereafter.
Abandon covetousness and greediness and cling to chastity and piety.
The abasement of men is in the things they covet and the passing away of lifetimes is in [following] the deceptions of [false] hopes.
The cornerstone of piety is abandoning covetousness.
Sometimes there is a false ambition for an unseen (or lost) hope.
Embarking on avidities cuts off the necks of men.
The cause of corruption of certitude is covetousness.
The cause of corruption of piety is covetousness.
Oppose covetousness with piety.
The servant of the coveted is enslaved and never gains his freedom.
He who instils covetousness in his soul has deceived it.
The corruption of religion is [caused by] covetousness.
Covetousness has been paired with humiliation.
One who trades covetousness for loss of hope [and desire for what others posses], the people will not treat him with contempt.
How good an aide of hope ambition is!
The trouble for religion is covetousness and its rectitude is [in] piety.
We seek Allah’s protection from lowly coveted things and the ambitions that are disliked [by Him].
Do not covet that which you do not deserve.
Never let covetousness enslave you and be averse [to the pleasures of this world].
Never let yourself covet that which is above your needs thereby letting it overcome you with the desire for more.
Do not let covetousness enslave you while Allah has made you free.
Nothing corrupts religion like covetousness.
There is no quality more abased than covetousness.
There is no humiliation greater than covetousness.
A little covetousness corrupts a lot of piety.
Cupidity corrupts piety and licentiousness [corrupts] God-wariness.
Freedom from the captivity of covetousness is [gained] by acquiring loss of hope [in people].
Covetousness is one of the two abasements.
One who clings to covetousness is deprived of piety.
Whoever takes covetousness as his attire, it makes him swallow failure repeatedly.
One who entertains the hope of [fulfilment of] false cupidity, the grant [which he receives] belies him.
One who does not purify his soul from the lowliness of the coveted has actually abased himself and shall be even more abased and disgraced in the Hereafter.
A little cupidity corrupts a lot of piety.
Excessive covetousness is the symbol of lack of piety.
One who is possessed by covetousness is humiliated.
One who clings to covetousness is deprived of piety.
One whose covetousness increases, his downfall becomes greater.
Every coveter is a prisoner [of his desires].
How many a coveter covets pardon.
One who covets becomes abased and undergoes hardship.
There is none more abased than a coveter.
The most indigent of people is the coveter.
The most humiliated of all people is the greedy, suspicious, coveter.
The coveter is forever abased.
The coveter is forever in the shackles of disgrace.
Whoever is haughty with his brothers, nobody will be sincere with him.
Whoever is haughty with people because of his authority, his authority will get stripped away.
Haughtiness is the language of error and ignorance.
Do not be haughty with the one whom you have not enslaved.1
One of the [great] tribulations is [having] evil inner thoughts.
Frivolity [and heedlessness] makes life bitter.
Victory is [attained] by prudence, and prudence comes through experience.
The sweetness of victory effaces the bitterness of patience.
The alms-tax of victory is benevolence.
He who has been vanquished by sin has not gained victory.
The key to victory is remaining patient.
Never become vain because of [your] victory, for indeed you are not safe from the victory of time over you.
There is no victory for the one who has no patience.
Victory is the intercessor of the guilty.
In times of injustice, remember the justice of Allah with you and when you are powerful, [recall] the power of Allah over you.
Beware of oppression, for verily it brings [divine] retribution, dispels blessings and causes changes in circumstances.
Distance yourselves from injustice, for indeed it is the greatest of wrongdoings and the biggest of sins.
Keep away from injustice for whoever acts unjustly, his days are abhorred.
Keep away from injustice, for indeed it will depart from the one whom you oppress and will remain upon you.
Keep away from oppression, for verily it hastens one’s downfall and causes tears [of regret and sorrow] to flow from the one who acts upon it.1
Keep away from injustice, for it is the biggest sin; and verily the unjust will surely be chastised on the Day of Resurrection because of his injustice.
Keep away from oppression, for verily Allah hastens chastisement for the oppressor and sends down exemplary punishments upon him.
Avoid the downfalls of transgression, the disgraces of deceit and the arousal of the latent, reprehensible evil.

Know that injustice is of three kinds: the injustice that is not forgiven, the injustice that is not left [unquestioned], and the injustice that is forgiven without being questioned. As for the injustice that is not forgiven, it is the ascribing of partners to Allah as He, the Most High, says: ‘Verily Allah does not forgive that any partner should be ascribed to Him, but He forgives anything besides that to whomever He wishes’. As for the injustice that is forgiven, it is the injustice of a person to himself in committing some small sins. And as for the injustice that is not left unquestioned, it is the injustice of the people on one another. In this case the punishment is severe, not [simply] wounding with knives or striking with whips, rather it is a punishment in comparison to which all this seems small.
The most loathsome of traits is aggression.
The quickest thing is the downfall of an oppressor.
The vilest oppression is [that which is practiced] when one has power.
The vilest transgression is transgression against the intimate [friends].
The most loathsome injustice is your withholding the rights of Allah.
The most tyrannical person is he who oppresses the one who is fair to him.
The actions that are most effective in bringing chastisement are oppression and ingratitude for blessings.
Verily the evil that brings the quickest retribution is injustice.
Indeed the ugliness in injustice is equivalent to the beauty in justice.
Injustice is [the cause of divine] punishment.
Oppression takes away blessing.
Injustice brings [divine wrath and] chastisement.
Injustice has adverse consequences.
Oppression puts an end to blessings.
Injustice drives away blessings.
Oppression brings [divine wrath and] chastisements.
Injustice causes one to enter hellfire.
Oppression leads to destruction.
Injustice is the most wicked vice.
Injustice is the ruination of the populace.
Power is expunged by aggression.
Injustice has a series of destructive consequences.
Oppression is the quickest thing to be punished.
Injustice destroys homes.
Injustice destroys the one who practices it.
Oppression drives [one] towards utter destruction.
Injustice is a crime that cannot be forgotten.
Oppression causes the downfall of men and brings [their] deaths closer.

When power prompts you to be unjust to people, then remember the power of Allah, the Glorified, to punish you; and [recall the fact] that what you have brought upon them will depart from them while it will remain with you.
By injustice, blessings are removed.
By oppression, chastisement is brought down.
How bad an injustice is the injustice to one who is submissive!
How evil a provision for the Hereafter is oppressiveness to the servants [of Allah]!
Continued injustice takes away blessings and brings forth chastisement.
Remedy injustice with justice and cure poverty with alms and charity.
The cornerstone of ignorance is oppression.
One who embarks of injustice is met with ruin.
Whoever rides the mount of injustice, his mount will stumble with him.
The most evil characteristic of the souls is oppression.
Two things are such that one cannot be safe from their [evil] consequences: injustice and evil (or gluttony).
Counter oppression with justice.
Submission to tyranny causes destruction and annihilates the kingdom.
Being unjust to the weak is the most grievous injustice.
Injustice to the one who has surrendered is the greatest crime.
Being unjust to the people corrupts one’s Hereafter.
One who oppresses the people has manifested his obdurate opposition to Allah, the Glorified.
The injustice of a man in this world is the symbol of his wretchedness in the Hereafter.
Injustice to orphans and widows brings down divine wrath and takes away the blessings from those who possess them.
In tyranny there is transgression.
The destruction of the populace is in tyranny.
How many a blessing has been removed by injustice!
Injustice is enough of a dispeller of blessing and an invoker of chastisement.
Oppression is sufficient for the removal of blessing.
There is nothing that is more summoning of the removal of blessing and the hastening of chastisement than remaining steadfast upon injustice.
One who is praised for injustice is being plotted against [and deceived].
One whose injustice is excessive, his regret is abundant.
Whoever unsheathes the sword of oppression [on the people], his head becomes its sheath.
One of the most grievous injustices is the injustice of [or against] the honourable ones.
Do not make the nobles desirous of your cruelty [in their favour over those who oppose them].
Do not stretch out your hand against one who is unable to stave it off from himself.
Never oppress one who has no helper except Allah.

Consider not the injustice of the one who is unjust to you as grave, for indeed his striving only harms himself and benefits you; and it is not the reward of one who pleases you that you should offend him.
There is no evil like injustice.
There is no victory with oppression.
He who does not refrain from oppressing people does not believe in the Hereafter.
One from whose oppression people are not safe is not safe from the punishment of Allah.
A man may sleep after the loss of a child but he will not sleep under [the yoke of] oppression.
Tyranny is one of the two destroyers.
Injustice makes the foot slip, takes away blessings and destroys nations.
Injustice in this world is ruination and in the Hereafter, [it is] destruction.
Keep away from tyranny, for indeed the tyrant will not [even] smell the fragrance of Paradise.
Tyranny brings negative consequences.
Tyranny is the antithesis of justice.
One whose violations increase, his exasperation [also] increases.
Oppression is an eraser [of good deeds].
Oppression brings the quickest punishment.
he most unjust of men is one who establishes the practice of oppression and abolishes the practice of justice.
The unjust is blameworthy.
Punishment awaits the unjust.
On the Day of Judgment, the oppressor of the people will be afflicted, chastised and despoiled because of his injustice.
For every oppressor there is a reprisal.
For every oppressor there is a punishment that he cannot escape, and a downfall that will not pass him by.
For the unjust there is reprisal.
For the unjust there is a biting of his hand.1
There are three signs of the unjust among the people: being unjust to the one who is above him by disobedience, and to the one below him by overruling him, and supporting the faction of oppressors.
One who oppresses [others] gets oppressed.
One who acts unjustly corrupts his affair.
One who oppresses [others] breaks [and shortens] his lifespan.
One who is oppressive is destroyed by his oppression.
One who is unjust is annihilated by his injustice.
One who is unjust, his downfall is great.
One who oppresses, his destruction is hastened.
One who is unjust is ruined by his injustice.
One who is unjust, his life is broken [and shortened].
Whoever oppresses the servants of Allah, it is Allah who becomes his enemy instead of His servants.
Whoever oppresses the people, Allah becomes his adversary.
One who is unjust, his life gets broken and his injustice annihilates him.
The destruction of one who acts with oppression is hastened by Allah.
Whoever embarks on the clear path of injustice, his days are abhorred.
How close is chastisement to the unjust!
How great is the chastisement of the oppressor!
How great is the burden [of sin] of the one who is unjust and transgresses, and acts tyrannically and oppresses!
He who fears falling [into hellfire] does not act unjustly.
Far be it that an oppressor is saved from the punishment of Allah and the greatness of His wrath.
Even though Allah, the Exalted, gives time to the oppressor, His grasp will not spare him and He will ambush him on the passage of his way and the place where his saliva runs down.
The aggressive tyrant has many opponents and enemies.
For the oppressor there is downfall.
One who oppresses is crushed.
Woe be to the oppressors who transgress against the Fairest of all judges and the Knower of the inner thoughts of the hidden consciences.
The tyrant is hated and dispraised, even if nothing of his tyranny reaches his dispraiser, and the just one is the opposite of this.
The most oppressive of people is the one who considers his tyranny to be justice on his part.
The reign of a tyrant is from the contingent [and temporary] things.
There is no good in the rule of a tyrant.
The unjust transgressor is awaiting one of two chastisements [of this world or the Hereafter]. Apostle’s way!’
Beware of the cry of the oppressed, for verily he asks Allah for his right, and Allah, the Glorified, is more bountiful than that He should be asked for a right except that He grants it.
Verily the cry of the oppressed is answered by Allah, the Glorified, because he is asking for his right, and Allah is far greater than that He should deny a person his right.
When you see an oppressed person, then help him against the oppressor.
The oppressors of the oppressed are given respite by Allah, the Glorified, but are not overlooked.
At times the oppressed are assisted.
Be a helper for the oppressed and an enemy of the oppressor.
Whoever does not seek justice for the oppressed from the oppressor, his sins are magnified.
Whoever does not seek justice for the oppressed from the oppressor, Allah will take away his power.
How close is succour to the oppressed!
The oppressed does not prevail without a helper.
The day of the oppressed over the oppressor is [going to be] more severe than the day of the oppressor upon the oppressed.
The oppressed awaits reward [in the Hereafter].
In amassing the usurped rights [of the people] there is cessation [and loss] of power.
In [keeping] the usurped rights of the servants, there is amassing of sins.
The surmise of a believer is a divination.
The conjecture of a man is to the extent of his intellect.
The conjecture of a person is the measure of his intellect and his action is the truest witness about his origin.
The conjecture of the people of insight and intelligence is the closest thing to correctness.
One whose supposition [about others] is good, overlooks [their lapses].
One whose assumption [about others] is negative, scrutinizes.
One who thinks positively [about others], his intention becomes good.
One who thinks ill [of others], his innermost thoughts become evil.
One who thinks ill [of others], his imagination becomes evil.
When one thinks good of you, then prove his supposition to be true.
One who belies the evil assumption about his brother has a sound covenant [of brotherhood] and a relaxed heart.
One whose thoughts [about others] are negative assumes the disloyalty of the one who is not disloyal to him.
One who thinks ill of one who is not disloyal ends up thinking positively of that which is not so.
One who does not think positively of others alienates himself from everyone.
Little conjecture [and uncertainty] is [a means of falling into] doubt.
By Allah! Allah, the Glorified, will not punish a believer after he believes except because of his thinking ill [of others] and his bad character.
Do not think of a word that has been spoken by someone as evil while you find a possible positive meaning in it.
The one who thinks ill [of others] has no faith.
A servant does not think positively of Allah, the Glorified, but that Allah, the Glorified, is just as his positive thoughts are of Him.
One who thinks positively about people earns love from them.
Thinking ill of a virtuous person is the gravest sin and the ugliest injustice.
Thinking ill of one who is not disloyal stems from vileness.
Thinking ill corrupts matters and incites one to evils.
Thinking evil (of others) destroys the one who adopts it and saves the one who avoids it.
One who is overcome by negative thoughts leaves no room for reconciliation between him and his friend.
Thinking good of others lightens one’s grief and saves one from being shackled by sin.
Thinking positive of others is one of the best practices and most excellent allotments.
The positive thinking of a servant about Allah, the Glorified, is to the extent of his hope in Him.
Thinking positive is one of the best attributes and the most bountiful gifts.
Thinking positive means making your actions sincere and hoping that Allah will forgive your missteps.
One who thinks positively [about others] attains Paradise.
One who thinks positively of Allah, attains Paradise.
Be careful not to think negatively, for indeed thinking ill of others corrupts worship and increases the burden [of sin].
Conjecture is suspicion.
Correct conjecture is from the qualities of the people of understanding.
Conjecture errs, but certainty is [always] right and does err.
The bane of religion is thinking ill [of others].
In an age when righteousness prevails over a people, if a person entertains an evil suspicion about another person from whom no evil has become evident, then he has been unjust and has transgressed.
In an age when corruption prevails over a people, if a man thinks positive of another man then he has put himself in peril.
Thinking positive is a comfort for the heart and security for religion.
There is no faith with negative thinking.
Correct conjecture is one for the two [possible] views.
Cowardice, greediness and stinginess are evil characteristics that are brought together by thinking ill of Allah, the Glorified.
The best [form of] help is giving support.
How good a foresight precaution is!
The best equipage is precaution.
One who has the backing of Allah [and trusts in Him], his subjugation [by the enemy] becomes impossible.
The one who is precautious may [also at times] get afflicted.
Uprightness of the exteriors is a symbol of the soundness of the inner consciences.
For every exterior there is a hidden interior that is like it, so one who’s exterior is good his interior is also good, and whoever has a bad exterior has a bad interior.
In having a light burden there is inner peace and the safeguarding of [one’s] status.
One who fulfils the conditions of servitude deserves to be freed.
Sincere worship means that a person [puts his] hopes in none other than his Lord and fears nothing but his wrongdoing.
Reserve for yourself the best times and portions for that which is between you and Allah, the Glorified.
The best worship is contemplation.
The best worship is safeguarding the stomach and private parts [from the forbidden].
Worship is [a means to] success.
Continued worship is proof of success in attainment of prosperity.
The adornment of worship is humility [and submissiveness].
The probity of worship is [in] having trust in Allah.
The goal [and purpose] of worship is obedience.
In secluding oneself for the worship of Allah there are treasures of benefit.
He who makes his worship sincere succeeds in attaining prosperity.
Little that is practiced continually is better than [doing] a lot that makes one weary.
Little which is easy for you to act upon is better than a lot that is too heavy for you to bear.
Little that continues is better than a lot that is discontinuous.
How can one who does not abstain from lowly desires discover the delight of worship?
How can one who has not been aided by [divine granted] success derive joy in worship?
One who seeks nearness [to Allah] is not brought closer [to Him] by anything other than the worship of Allah.
The worshipper without knowledge is like the donkey that drives a mill, it moves round and round but does not depart from its place.

Verily a group worshipped Allah, the Glorified, out of desire [for reward] - that is the worship of the traders, and a group worshipped Him out of fear [of punishment] - that is the worship of the slaves, and a group worshipped Him out of gratitude - and that is the worship of the freemen.
When Allah loves a servant, he inspires him with the goodness of worship.
When Allah loves a servant, he makes trustworthiness beloved to him.
When Allah honours a servant, He occupies him with His love.
When Allah specially chooses a servant, He inspires him with [religious] devotion.
When Allah chooses a servant he covers him with His awe.
When Allah loves a servant, He adorns him with tranquillity and forbearing.
When Allah loves a servant, He inspires him with truth.
When Allah honours a servant, He helps him to establish justice.
When Allah loves a servant, He makes him hate wealth and shortens his hopes.
When Allah loves a servant, He bestows him with a good heart and an upright character.
When Allah wishes good for a servant, He grants him a sound intellect and upright action.
When Allah wishes good for a servant, He safeguards his stomach and private parts from the unlawful.
When Allah wishes good for a servant, He inspires him with contentment and sets his wife right for him.
When Allah wishes good for a servant, He makes his stomach abstain from [unlawful] food and his private parts from that which is forbidden.
When Allah, the Glorified, wishes goodness for a servant, He inspires him to talk less, eat less and sleep less.
When Allah wishes good for a servant, He makes him learned in religion and inspires him with certitude.
When Allah wishes good for a servant, He inspires him with contentment, so he becomes satisfied with the minimum and covers himself with chastity [and abstinence from the unlawful].
When Allah wishes good for a servant, He inspires him with moderation and good management and keeps him away from mismanagement and wastefulness.
When Allah loves a servant, He inspires him with right guidance and makes him successful in His obedience.
He (‘a) praised a man saying: This is one whose peacefulness benefits and injustice is not feared from him. When he says, he does and when he put in charge, he is just.
He (‘a) said about the one whom he praised: He is the unfolder [and clarifier] of the obscure, the guide in vast deserts and the repeller of complex difficulties.
The best of servants is one who is delighted when he does good and when he does evil, he repents.
People are created by [Allah’s] power, raised up with constraint and made to die through pangs of death.
If the servants were to stop when they are ignorant [about something], they would neither apostatize nor would they go astray.
When Allah humiliates (or abases) a servant, He denies him knowledge.
When Allah wants something bad for a servant, He makes wealth beloved to him and extends his [false] hopes.
When Allah, the Glorified, wishes to remove a blessing from a servant, the first thing that He alters [and takes away from him] is his intellect, and losing it is the most difficult thing for him.
Verily, one of the creatures most hated by Allah, the Exalted, is the man who has been left on his own [by Allah] and has strayed from the right path, moving on without a guide.
A servant is a servant, even if he is assisted by [divine] destiny.
The beauty of a servant is [in his] obedience. regarded as Children of God.
Take lesson and you will be deterred [from evil].
Take lesson and you will become content.
Take lessons from [the lives of] those who preceded you before those who are after you take lessons from you.
Take counsel from the examples [of others], learn lessons from the changing situations and take benefit from the Warners.
Where are the ‘Amāliqa2 and the children of the ‘Amāliqa?
Where are the tyrants and the children of the tyrants?
Where are the people of the cities of Rass who killed the Prophets and extinguished the light of the Messengers?
Where are those who rallied the troops and inhabited the cities?
Where are those who said, “Who is more powerful than us and is greater in assemblage?”
Where are those who left the best heritage, were most just in their actions and had the biggest kingdoms?
Where are those who vanquished the armies and travelled in the thousands?
Where are those who built kingdoms, paved passages, and aided the aggrieved and hosted guests?
Where is the one who strived and struggled, and prepared and mobilized [all possible resources]?
Where is the one who built and erected, paved and prepared, accumulated and counted?
Where is Khosrau3 and Caesar and Tubba’4 and Himyar5?
Where is the one who stored and amassed, and accumulated wealth upon wealth thereby multiplying it?
Where is the one who fortified and strengthened, and adorned and decorated?
Where is the one who accumulated and increased, and stored and amassed, and considered the future of his son?
Where are those who lived longer than you and left a greater heritage?
Where are the ones who were larger in numbers, had stronger armies and had greater effect?
Where are the kings and Khosraus?
Where are the children of the Yellow6 and the pharaohs?
Where are those who ruled the extremities of this world?
Where are those who used to humiliate their enemies and take possession of their forelocks [by enslaving them]?
Where are those to whom the nations were subservient?
Where are those who attained their highest ambitions in this world?
Verily for those who remain [behind] there is an example in those who have passed.
Verily for the latter there is an admonishment in the former.
Verily the passing away of those who depart is a lesson for the community that remains behind.
Taking example yields [the fruit of] inerrancy.
Time shows you examples.
Taking lesson is beneficial in [attaining] right guidance.
When Allah loves a servant, He gives him direction through examples.
You have been left with examples from the vestiges of those who passed away before you, so take lesson from them.
Continually taking lessons leads to perspicacity and bears the fruit of restraint [from evil].

I am bound by responsibility for what I say and am answerable for it. Verily, one for whom examples [of the past] have clearly shown that which was before him of exemplary punishments [given by Allah to wrongdoers] is prevented by God-wariness from falling into dubious [and questionable] actions.
Attest to the truth that has passed and take lesson from what has elapsed of this world, because indeed its one phase resembles the other and its end catches up to its beginning.
The prolonged drawing of lessons [from the past] impels one to be precautious.
In every glance there is a lesson.
In every lesson that is drawn there is discernment.
In the succession of days there is lesson for the creatures.
Successful is the one who has a habit of taking lesson [from the past] and a tendency towards being precautious.
He who has been deterred [from evil] has taken lesson [from the past].
He who takes a lesson from the past [that has gone] has taken a lesson for the remaining [future].
Every day benefits you with lessons if you accompany it with contemplation.
For the people of intelligence, what they are aware of is enough of a lesson for them.

Lessons [from events] have indeed become evident for you, and you have been deterred by what is in it of a deterrence; and after the Prophet of Allah, none have conveyed [the message] from Allah like the Warners.
If you took lessons from what has passed of your life, you would safeguard that which remains [of it].
One who takes lesson [from the past] is cautious.
One whose consideration [of past events from which he draws lessons] increases, his mistakes decrease.
One who takes a lesson from the vicissitudes of time is careful of [the evil of] others.
One who does not take lesson from others does not take precaution for himself.
One who takes admonishment from the examples [of the past] is deterred [from evil].
One who does not take a lesson from the passage of days is not deterred by reproach.
One who takes a lesson from vicissitudes does not rely on the peacefulness of time.
One who recognizes the lessons [of the past], it is as if he is living among the ancients.
One who does not take lesson from the vicissitudes of this world, advice has no effect on him.
One who considers matters arrives at their [appropriate] criteria.
One who takes lesson from the vicissitudes of this world, his desires lessen.
How many the lessons are, and how few of them are learnt!
There is no lesson to be taken for the one who has no restraint.
Taking lesson steers one towards right guidance. war to the Abyssinians, their womenfolk were ravaged and the children produced were of a yellowish skin colour.
Goodwill [and friendly admonishment] is the life of friendship [and affection].
Too much reprimand indicates [one’s] suspicion.
He who seeks forgiveness (or is indigent) is not reprimanded.
Do not reprimand the ignorant one as he will hate you, but reprimand the wise one as he will love you [for it].
Never be excessive in reprimanding, for indeed it brings about ill feelings and calls toward hatred; and seek to appease the one whom you hope to reprimand.
When you reprimand then leave some room [to make amends and do not be excessive in reprimanding].
When you become the owner [of a slave], then emancipate [him].
The slip up of impudence cannot be pardoned.
The most alienating estrangement is conceit.
Conceit is destruction.
Conceit is folly.
Conceit is the cornerstone of foolishness.
Conceit is the cornerstone of ignorance.
Conceit is the symbol of foolishness.
Self-admiration prevents growth.
Conceit is the most harmful associate.
Self-admiration is contrary to reason.
Conceit corrupts the intellect.
Conceit prevents growth.
Becoming conceited because of a good deed nullifies it.
Conceit is the bane of dignity.
Conceit manifests [one’s] shortcoming.
The admiration of a person for himself is folly.
