Self-admiration is contrary to reason and the bane of the intellects.
When you wish your merits to be glorified among the people, then do not glorify yourself.

When your self-importance is increased by the position [of authority] you are in, and this brings about arrogance or vanity in you, then look at the greatness of the authority of Allah and His power, the power which you do not even possess over yourself, for indeed this will mellow your recalcitrance, cure your vehemence and bring back to you that which had departed from you of your intellect.
By being pleased with oneself, vices and faults become manifest.
The fruit of conceit is hatred.
The evil that befalls you is better than the good that makes you conceited.
One who admires himself will be ridiculed because of it.
One who admires his [own] opinion becomes abased (or goes astray).
Whoever is proud [and pleased] with his action, his intellect gets afflicted.
One who admires his [own] speech, his intellect has departed.
One whose self-admiration increases, his correctness reduces.
One who becomes conceited by his action nullifies his reward.
One who admires his good state falls short of attaining good expediencies.
Adversity does not descend upon the one who abandons conceit and lassitude.
No one admires his own opinion except the ignorant one.
Nothing damages [one’s] merits [and good deeds] like conceit.
What has the son of Adam to do with conceit? His beginning is foul semen and his end is a rotting corpse, and in between these he is a carrier of waste products.
There is no alienation more desolating than conceit.
The self-admiration of a person is proof of his deficiency and a symbol of his weak intellect.
Keep away from self-conceit and love for praise, for these are the strongest opportunities for Satan.
Be careful not to be self-conceited, thereby making deficiency and enmity manifest upon [and against] you.

Be cautious not to consider the sin of others as great while you deem it to be small [when it comes] from yourself, or to consider your worship as abundant while you deem the same to be less when performed by others.
The self-admiring one has no intelligence.
The self-admiring one has no [valid] opinion [as he never consults with anyone else].
Inability accompanied by espousing goodness is better than power accompanied by embarking on evil.
Inability is waste.
Inability is ruin.
Inability is a cause of loss.
Inability is the worst riding mount.
Inability bears the fruit of destruction.
Inability makes enemies covetous.
The fruit of inability is losing what is sought.

Inability [and failure] is [in] occupying yourself with that which has been guaranteed for you instead of that which has been made obligatory upon you, and abandoning contentment with what you have been given.
The most powerless of people are those who consider themselves the safest from sudden events and [from] the onslaught of their deaths.
Sometimes the powerless one acquires what he needs.
The derriere is one of the two faces.
Haste is dispraised in every affair except in that which repels evil.
Beware of haste, for indeed it bears the fruit of regret.
Keep away from haste, for verily it is the symbol of loss and regret.
Keep away from haste, for surely it is associated with error.
Haste (or conceit) leads to error.
Haste prevents one from [successfully] achieving his goal.
Making haste before [having the] ability, causes distress.
The fruit of haste is error.
Being hasty before [possessing the] ability is part of foolishness.
With haste, errors abound.
The hasty one is in the wrong, even if he acquires [what he seeks].
The one who rides on [the mount of] haste is on the verge of stumbling.
In haste there is error.
In haste there is regret.
It is seldom that the view of a hasty person turns out to be correct.
It is seldom that the scheme of the hasty is successful or that the love of the one who is fed up lasts.
Few are the ones who make haste and are not ruined by it.
Everyone who is hastened asks for more time.
Too much haste makes a person slip.
A hasty person never gets praised [for his haste].
One who makes haste, errs.
One who is hasty makes mistakes.
One who makes haste, his errors increase?
One who acts hastily falls into error.
One who is hasty regrets his haste.
One who acts hastily is made to stumble by error.
One who acts hastily is bestridden by blame.
There is no achievement for the hasty.
Of all people, the one with the greatest regret and the most reproof is the hasty, rash person who is not subdued by his intellect until after his affair is lost.
Leave haste aside, for indeed the one who is hasty in matters neither attains what he seeks nor is his affair praised.
The hasty one errs or is close to [erring].
Every denumerable thing can diminish.
The best preparation is that by which one’s Hereafter is improved.
Lighten your burden, for indeed the goal is in front of you and time is behind you, driving you forward.
Lighten your burden so as to catch up [with those who are ahead you], for indeed the last among you are only being awaited by the first among you [who have preceded them].
Prepare for your journey, keep your gaze on the flash of salvation and travel on swift [and girded] mounts [of good deeds].
Return from negligence, awake from slumber, prepare yourself for the move and gather provisions for the journey.
One who has prepared for his journey is delighted upon his arrival.
Select your abode for yourself before the day of your landing and prepare your dwelling before your arrival.
Justice is the better of the two policies.
Justice is the cornerstone of faith and the accumulator of benevolence.
Justice is the mainstay of the populace and the splendour of the rulers.
Justice means that you act equitably when you are oppressed, and kindness means that when you gain authority, you forgive.
Be just and you will rule.
Be just and you will rule.
Be just and your power will last.
Have recourse to justice with good intention for the populace, reduced covetousness and increased piety.
The loftiest of endowments is justice.
The best [form of] justice is assisting the oppressed.
The most just of all people is he who is equitable to the one who has oppressed him.
Verily being fair in [your] ruling and eschewing oppression are part of justice.

Indeed justice is the scale of Allah, the Glorified, which He has placed among the creation and installed for the establishment of truth; so do not oppose Him in His scale and do not contradict Him in His authority.
Verily Allah, the Glorified, has enjoined justice and benevolence and has forbidden indecency and injustice.
Justice is brings harmony while oppression causes deviation.
Justice is the soul of testimony.
Justice is the life of decrees.
Justice is the best testimony.
Justice reforms the people.
Justice is a merit for the ruler.
Justice is the greatest of riches.
Justice is equity.
Justice is a foundation [for a healthy society]; oppression is destruction.
The just [ruler] is a custodian who awaits one of the two rewards (or the better of the two rewards).
The most just among the creation is one who judges best according to the truth.
The most just of all people is he who is equitable despite having power, and the one who has the greatest clemency is he who is clement despite having authority.
Through justice, bounties are multiplied.
Through justice, the populace is reformed.
Allah, the Glorified, made justice a mainstay for mankind, a purification from oppressions and vices, and as an opening for [the spreading of] Islam.
Virtuous justice is [the cause of] organization [and harmony] among the people.
The best of policies is justice.
How can one who is unjust to himself be just with others?!
Justice suffices as a means of governance.
Let your riding mount be justice, for one who rides on it gains mastery.
Justice can never be achieved until injustice falters [and comes to an end].
It is not from justice to judge a reliable person by conjecture [instead of accepting his testimony].1
One who is just gains [and strengthens his] power [and authority].
The ruling of one who is just gets acted upon.
The status of one who is just becomes great.
One whose justice increases, his days are praised.
Allah unfolds His mercy upon one who acts justly in the lands.
One whose deed done in private matches what he does openly and whose actions are consistent with his speech, then he is the one who has fulfilled the trust and whose justice has been established.
Whoever acts justly, Allah fortifies his kingdom.
Take with justice but give with munificence; you will possess two virtues.
The policy of justice comprises of three things: judiciousness in leniency, fairness in investigation and moderation in munificence.
Two things are such that their reward cannot be weighed: forgiveness and justice.
The uprightness [and betterment] of the populace is [achieved through] justice.
You must be just with [both] friend and foe, and moderate in [both] poverty and wealth.
The pinnacle of justice is for a person to be just with himself.
In justice there is benevolence.
In justice there is betterment of the people.
Following the way of Allah and the stability of nations lies in justice
In justice there is comfort; and one for whom justice is beleaguering, then oppression will be more beleaguering [and difficult] for him.
From the exigencies of justice is the forbidding of oppression.
Nothing brings prosperity to the lands like justice.
Do not let the weak lose hope in your justice.
There is no justice better than returning the right of the oppressed.
Justice is life.
Justice is the best judgment.
Justice is [a means of attaining]) success and dignity.
Justice is the mainstay of the populace (or of the creation).
Justice is a merit of the sultan.
Justice is the system of leadership.
Justice is the strongest foundation.
Justice is the best trait.
Justice relieves the one who acts upon it from being shackled by the rights of others.
The bane of justice is the powerful tyrant.
When your judgment is applied upon yourself [thereby showing your justice], the souls of [other] people summon each other towards your justice.
The bane of the just [ones] is lack of piety.
The coming to power of the just is from the necessities.
Many a just person is an oppressor. [mere] conjecture.
The best affair (of this ummah) is [taking] the middle course; to it return those who have gone to the extreme and with it join those who have lagged behind.
Being bound by straps is better [and more preferable] than accompanying the adversary.
The cause of enmity is lack of empathy [and consideration for others].
Enmity of near ones is more unpleasant than the sting of the scorpions.
Too much enmity is disquieting for the hearts.
Whoever stubbornly opposes the people, they hate him.
Whoever manifests his enmity, his stratagems are reduced.
One who tries to overcome his adversary has embarked on a struggle.
One who accompanies his adversary exhausts his body.
One who reforms [and reconciles with] his enemy increases in his number.
Whoever is unconcerned about you, then he is your enemy.
Whoever accompanies his adversary, he will expose his flaw and torment his heart.
One who is courteous with his adversaries is safe from battles.
One who sleeps, neglecting his enemy, is jolted awake by [his] crafty schemes.
One who finds the enmity of men sweet tastes the bitterness of the hardships of war.
One who shows enmity towards the people reaps the fruit of regret.
Whoever hides your fault from you and exposes your fault in your absence, then he is your [real] enemy, so be careful of him.
Whoever shows enmity [with the people] his paths becomes rugged, his affair becomes difficult and his way out becomes narrow.
One who reforms his adversaries attains his goal.
One who derives benefit from harming you will never be free from his enmity for you in every situation.
Never do two people [or groups] quarrel but that the more foolish of the two wins the argument.
Acting courteously with the enemies of Allah in their domains is a safeguard from the chastisement of Allah and a caution from the raging tribulations of this world.
Struggling against the enemies in their dominions and fighting against them despite their power is abandoning the command of Allah and exposing oneself to the tribulations of this world.
Do not be adversaries of the blessings of Allah upon you.1
Do not face your adversary before you are powerful enough [to defeat him].
Do not be fooled by the courteousness of the enemy for indeed he is like water, even if its heating by fire is prolonged, it is not prevented from extinguishing it.

Do not confront your enemy while he is charging towards you, for indeed his charge will aid him to overcome you and do not confront him when he is fleeing away from you, for indeed his flight is sufficient for you in dealing with him.

Do not declare your enmity to your enemy and do not rebuke your friend; and accept the excuse [you are given] even if it is a lie, and do not give [a forceful] response despite having the power to do so, even if it be your right.
When you have hatred [for someone] then do not disassociate yourself [completely – and leave some room for possible future friendship].
Let the most hated of people to you and the furthest of them from you be the one who always seeks out the faults of people.
One who hates you incites you [to wrongdoing].
The enemy has been named ‘enemy’ because he wrongs you; so one who flatters you for your faults is in actually an enemy who is wronging you.
Keep away from the enemies of Allah and maintain ties with the friends of Allah.
The worst of enemies is the one who goes to the greatest lengths and is most secretive in his plotting.
At times enemies may deceive [and pretend to be well-wishers].
One who sows enmity [and aggression] reaps loss.
Treating the enemy with kindness is one of the two victories.
Being courteous when trying to accomplish something is more effective than other means.
With regards to your enemy, be on the lookout for possibility [of defeating him] and seize opportunity, you will be [thus become] triumphant.
The weakest of enemies in plotting is the one who manifests his enmity.
One enemy is plenty.
Reforming [and reconciliation with] the enemies through good words and beautiful actions is easier than facing them and combating them with the torment of battle.
One who reforms [and reconciles with] his opponents attains his goal.
Do not consider yourself safe from an enemy, even if he is grateful.
Never underestimate an enemy, even if he is weak.
Showing enmity towards the people is a trait of the ignorant ones.
One who unsheathes the sword of aggression is killed by it.
Stances of [enmity and] hatred anger the Most Merciful, please Satan and disgrace man.
One who exceeds in [his] animosity has sinned and one who falls short [and does not show enmity when it is required] is defeated.
He who has animosity [towards others] is not capable of fearing Allah.
Quarrels [and disputes] manifest the foolishness of a person and do not increase in his right.
One whose transgression (or antagonism) increases, his enemies increase.
Power is lost through aggression [and oppression].
Being needless of offering an excuse is more honourable than truthfulness [in your excuse].1
Apologizing necessitates pardoning.
Repeating the apology is a reminder of the sin.
One who seeks pardon without having sinned has imposed the sin upon his soul.
One who admits his wrongdoing deserves forgiveness.
One who apologizes in a befitting manner deserves to be forgiven.
One who apologizes has sought pardon.
He who seeks pardon has not sinned.
How good an intercessor seeking pardon is!
Do not offer an excuse to the one who would like to find you without an excuse.
There is no intercessor more successful than apology.
Repeating the apology is a reminder of the [past] sins.
Seeking pardon (or taking lesson) is a sincere warner.2
When you do wrong, apologize.
Sometimes the admission of guilt for having committed a sin dispenses with the need for seeking pardon.
Too much apology magnifies the sins.
Keep away from that for which there is little denial, even if the excuses from you are many, for it is not such that everyone who speaks ill [of you] can be excused by you. seek pardon again.
Safeguard [your] reputations with wealth.
Nothing preserves reputations like turning away from vile traits and evil objectives.
Protect your reputations by spending your wealth generously.
Abundance of wealth [that is attained] by the derogation of reputations is ignobility.
Plenitude of religion and dignity [that is acquired] through generously spending wealth is a sublime gift.
Protect your dignity with your worldly possessions and you will be honoured, do good to others and you will be served, show clemency and you will be put forward (or you will advance).
The plenitude of dignity is [attained] through the generous spending of wealth, and the uprightness of religion is [realized] through devaluing this world.
Nothing safeguards reputations like spending generously.
Do not make your dignity a subject of the speech of every speaker [by engaging in shameful deeds].
One who sacrifices his dignity is abased.
One who sacrifices his dignity is humiliated.
One who preserves his dignity is revered.
Whoever considers his dignity to be precious, money has of little value for him.
Cognizance is perplexity and being devoid of it is dim-sightedness.
The most excellent cognizance is the human being’s cognizance of himself.
Of all the people, the most cognizant of himself is the most fearful of his Lord.
The person most cognizant of his age is the one who is not astonished by its events.
Cognizance is the light of the heart.
Cognizance is the successful attainment of [purification and] the sacred.
Cognizance is the evidence of excellence (or nobility).
The fruit of cognizance is becoming averse to the evanescent abode.
Many a cognizance leads to misguidance.
Allah is known by the revocation of resolutions, the undoing of binds and the relieving of hardship and affliction from the one whose intention is sincere.
The pinnacle of cognizance is fear [of Allah].
The pinnacle of cognizance is for a person to know himself.
It is a sufficient cognizance for a person to know himself.
The conception of cognizance is through learning knowledge.
One whose cognizance is sound, his soul and his endeavour turns away from the evanescent world.
The cognizance of a scholar is the devoutness through which Allah is worshipped, through it the human being gains obedience in his lifetime and a beautiful remembrance after his death.
The smallest amount of cognizance leads to disinclination towards worldly pleasures (or corruption of one’s actions1).
Meeting the people of cognizance is a means of strengthening the hearts and benefitting of wisdom.
One who is cognizant, refrains [from the forbidden].
It behoves the one who knows Allah, the Glorified, to desire that which is with Him.
One who is cognizant of Allah, the Glorified, will never become wretched.
One who relies on personal opinion and analogy in trying to know Allah goes astray and matters become confusing for him.
Cognizance of Allah, the Glorified, is the highest cognizance.
It behoves the one who is cognizant of Allah, the Glorified, not to make his heart devoid of hope in Him and fear of Him.
One who knows Allah believes in his oneness.2
Whoever knows Allah, his cognizance is complete.
Every cognizant one is sorrowful.
Every cognizant one is averse [to the temporary pleasures of this world].
How can one know others when he is ignorant of himself?!
The cognizant one is he who knows his soul and thus frees it and purifies it from all that distances it [from the Truth] and destroys it.
The face of the cognizant one is cheerful and smiling while his heart is fearful and sad.
One who is given honour by Allah cannot be humiliated by any king.
One who seeks honour through [anyone] other than Allah is abased.
One who seeks glory through [anyone] other than Allah is destroyed by [the] glory.
One who seeks glory without having any right to it gets humiliated.
One who seeks glory through [anything] other than truth, Allah humiliates him with [the] truth.
There is no glory except through obedience [to Allah].
The honoured is the one who becomes honoured through obedience [to Allah].
When you seek glory, then seek it through obedience [to Allah].
He whose neighbours are abased is not honoured.1
Glory is the attainment of [the power to exact] revenge.
Every glory that is not endorsed by religion is a humiliation.
In seclusion from the worldly people there is accumulation of goodness.
One who secludes [from the people] himself remains safe.
One who tests [the people who love this world] secludes himself [from them].
One who secludes himself, his indifference towards the pleasures of this world becomes strong.
Whoever secludes himself, his piety remains safeguarded?
One who secludes himself from the people is safe from their evil.
How good a worship seclusion is!
One who isolates himself from the people preserves his religion.
One who isolates himself from the people becomes intimate with Allah, the Glorified.
Safety is in solitude.
Solitude is the comfort of the worshippers.
One who isolates himself is spared from sorrows.
Continuous solitude is safer than mingling with the people.
Seclusion is the best (or the fortification of) piety.
Seclusion is the best trait of the sagacious.
Whoever reveals his decision [to others], his judiciousness gets nullified.
Whoever resolves to do evil, his arrow returns to him.
Do not resolve upon that in which you find no clear guidance.
There is no good in [making a] resolution without determination.1
Adversity degrades morals and alienates friends.
Adversity is a reproach.
Adversity corrupts morals.
ocial interaction with people of merits is enlivening for the hearts.
Let not your family or those whom you love be the most miserable of people because of you.
Do not alienate a person whose separation will harm you.
The one who mingles with people is afflicted by the evil associate and the hypocrisy of the enemy.
Preserve [the respect of others] and your respect will be preserved.
Mix sternness with gentleness, and be gentle as long as gentleness is more befitting.
Imbibe your heart with mercy for all the people and kindness towards them, and do not oppress them or be [like] a sword over them.

Remember you brother who is absent in the same way that which you would like him to remember you [in your absence] and keep away from what he dislikes; and disregard from him that which you would like him to disregard from you.
Loathe from yourself what you loathe from others and like for people what you like for yourself.
Reduced mingling preserves religion and relieves one from having to associate with wicked people.
Be equitable to people over yourself, your family, your near ones and those from whom you desire something, and be just with both enemy and friend.
Be friendly with the one who is friendly with you, accept the excuse of the one who seeks your pardon and do good to the one who wrongs you.

Guard well the sanctities [of such things that are sacrosanct] and draw near to the people of magnanimity, for indeed guarding the sanctities [and boundaries] demonstrates an honourable character and drawing near to the magnanimous indicates nobility of purpose.

Be merciful to the one who is under you and the one who is above you will be merciful to you; compare his forgetfulness with your forgetfulness and his disobedience with your disobedience to you Lord, and his need of your mercy to your need of the mercy of your Lord.

Cling to the people of virtue and piety, and request them not compliment you, for indeed excessive praise brings one close to being deceived [about his true status] and being pleased with it causes the displeasure of Allah.

Make your self a gauge between you and the other; love for him what you love for your self, and hate for him what you hate for it, and do good as you would like good to be done to you, and do not oppress just as you would like not to be oppressed.
Associate with people in the way that you would like them to associate with you, [by doing this] you will be safe from them and they will be safe from you.
Keep away from socializing with evil people for they are like fire - the one who comes in contact with it gets burnt.
Keep away from socializing with those who look for the faults (or sins) of people, for indeed even their companion is not safe from them.
Be sure to keep away from that which angers your Lord and alienates people from you, for the one who angers his Lord is faced with annihilation and one who alienates people renounces freedom.
Be careful to keep away from turning your backs on each other, cutting off ties with each other, and abandoning the enjoining of good and prohibiting of evil [with respect to one another].
The most deserving of those whom you love is the one who does not forsake you.
The most equitable conduct is for you to deal with people in the way you would like them to deal with you.
The most unjust conduct is for you to seek equity from people while not dealing with them in the same way.
The most worthy of those whom you love is he whose benefit is for you and whose harm is for other than you.
Verily the best outward appearance [and demeanour] is that which makes you mingle with people and beautifies you among them and restrains their tongues from [speaking ill of] you.
Make others incline towards you instead of distancing themselves from you.
Man is the son of his time.1
Through good social interaction, affection lasts.
Through good social interaction friendships become intimate.
By good social interaction ties (or companionship) last.
How evil an associate the spiteful person is!
Good social interaction causes affection to endure.
Interact with people through their [norms of] etiquette but separate yourself from them in [your] actions.
Interact with people in such a way that when you die, they weep over you and when you are absent, they yearn for your company.
Interact with people through your tongues and your bodies, but part from them with your hearts and your actions.
Many an associate is not a close friend.
It is in times of trial that a man is [either] honoured or disgraced.
Associate with the people of excellence and you will gain felicity and nobility.
The development of the hearts is in socializing with people of intellect.
Cutting off [ties with] the ignorant is equivalent to establishing ties with the intelligent.
The intelligent person [only] cuts off ties with you after failing to find any other way out.
Get closer to the people in their morals and you will be safe from their malice [and evil].
Having many acquaintances is a tribulation, and socializing with the people is an ordeal.
One whose social interaction increases, his piety (or reliability) decreases.
One who mingles with the people is affected by their devices.
Whoever mingles with the people, his piety decreases?
One whose social interaction is good, his brother’s increase.
One who deals leniently with people enjoys [and benefits from] their company.
One whose being alive is not beneficial to you, then count him among the dead.
Be good in your interactions, be patient in difficulties and be equitable when you have power.
Be pleased for [other] people with that which pleases you, then you will be a [true] Muslim. the commandments of Allah).
Desires have rent asunder his intellect and killed his heart while his mind is infatuated with them.
Whoever seeks protection from Allah, He saves him.
One who seeks protection from Allah is not harmed by Satan.
Whoever clings to Allah, his wish is fulfilled [and his goal is achieved].
Entrust your soul, in all your affairs, to your Lord, for indeed [by your so doing] you are turning to a secure refuge.
Seek protection with Allah in all situations, for indeed you will be clinging to One, Glorified be He, who is a powerful protector.
You must seek protection from Allah in all your affairs, for indeed this is a [means of] protection from everything.
Preserving oneself from sin is a blessing.
One who is inspired with preservation [from sin] is saved from error.
Being unable to sin is [also] a form of preservation [against sin].
Sometimes there is destruction is under what is sought.
Embarking on acts that lead to [places of] destruction is the symbol of foolishness.
Many a person is destroyed after having remained safe [and survived a disaster].
One whose empathy (or kind acts) increases, his acquaintances increases.
One who respects you because of your opulence, belittles you in your [time of] poverty.
Never regard anyone as venerable until you discover the level of his cognizance.
Chastity preserves the soul and purifies it from vile demerits.
Chastity weakens lust.
Chastity is renunciation [of worldly pleasures].
Chastity is the best (or the root of) magnanimity.
Chastity is the best trait.
Chastity is the trait of the sagacious.
Chastity is the cornerstone of goodness.
Restraining oneself from [coveting] that which people possess is chastity and high-mindedness.
The people of chastity are the most honourable of the honourables.
Through chastity actions become purified.
The crown of a man is his chastity and his adornment is his equity.
The fruit of chastity is preservation [of oneself from chastisement].
The fruit of chastity is contentment.
Virtuous chastity is from the traits of the honourable ones.
The cause of contentment is chastity.
Espouse chastity, for indeed it is a good companion.
Espouse chastity and contentment, for whoever does this, his burden of sustenance is lightened.
Espouse chastity, for indeed it is the best trait of the honourable ones.

You must espouse chastity and trustworthiness, for verily these two are the most honourable of what you can do in secret and the best of what you can practice openly, and the finest of what you can preserve.
To the extent of modesty, there is chastity.
I am amazed at the one who knows the evil consequences of [forbidden] pleasures, how can he not remain chaste?!
Just as you desire, be chaste.
One who desires that which he cannot obtain has not adorned himself with chastity.
Whoever is granted chastity and contentment, honour becomes his ally.
There is no indigence with chastity.
Whoever is chaste, his burden [of sin] is reduced and his status becomes great in the sight of Allah.
One whose flanks are chaste, his attributes become good.
The chastest among you are the most modest among you.
Verily Allah, the Glorified, loves the one who is chaste, modest, pious and satisfied [with His will].
Good health is such that when it lasts, it is disregarded and when it is lost, its value is known.
Verily well-being in religion and [in] this world is a great (or beautiful) blessing and a bountiful gift.
Well-being is the most pleasant of blessings.
There is no life more pleasant than [life] with good health.
There is no attire better than well-being.
Every well-being is [headed] towards affliction.
Well-being is the better of the two attires.
Through well-being, life becomes pleasurable.
The garment of well-being is the most pleasant of attires.
Lasting good health is the most pleasant gift and the best portion.
Ask Allah for welfare [and safety] from the lustful temptations and the trials of this world.
Hastening to forgive is from the morals of the honourable.
Forgiveness is the greater of the two virtues.
Forgive and you will be supported.
Pardon and you will be pardoned.
Do good to the one who does evil to you and forgive the one who wrongs you.
Forgive the mistake of your friend, [and] your enemy will consider you to be virtuous.
Forgive that which angers you for the sake of that which pleases you.
Pardon wrongdoings, stave off punishment and overlook that which has not become evident for you.
Accept the excuses of people and you will enjoy their brotherhood; meet them with cheerfulness and you will cause their malice [and grudges against you] to die away.
Pardon the errors of the magnanimous, for none of them slips but that the Hand of Allah lifts him [back] up.
Forgiveness is the best of favours.
Forgiveness is the charity of triumph.
Forgiveness is the evidence of intelligence.
Forgiveness is the symbol of nobility.
Forgiveness is the crown of high morals.
Many a sin is such that the [appropriate] degree of punishment for it is informing the sinner of it.
Do not persist in that [action] which is followed by sin.
Forgiveness despite [having the] power [to exact revenge] is a shield from the punishment of Allah, the Glorified.
When you have been wronged, forgive.
Through forgiveness [of others] divine mercy is invoked.
Overlook despite having power [to punish] and do good while possessing authority, [for by this] your mastery will become complete.
Overlook missteps and pardon mistakes, [for by this] your station will be elevated.
Cover up offences with forgiveness, especially for those who possess magnanimity and social standing.
Feign heedlessness [about the mistakes of others] and your affair will be praised.
Reward goodness and overlook offence, as long as it is not a breach in religion or an undermining of the authority of Islam.
Adopt [the policy of] excusing the people and do not extend your hand to that which is disagreeable to anyone of them.1
Do away with revenge, for indeed it is from the worst actions of the powerful, and he who raises himself above the evil of reprisals has taken hold of the accumulation of merits.
It is when one possesses complete authority that the virtue of forgiveness becomes manifest.
Lack of forgiveness is the ugliest of flaws and rushing to exact revenge is the gravest of sins.
Accepting the excuse of a wrongdoer is from the acts that bring honour and the [is] the most excellent of traits.
Victory is a sufficient intercessor for the sinner.
Be graciously forgiving when you become powerful and act justly when you are in authority.
Be forgiving when you are powerful, generous in your affluence and altruistic despite your poverty, then virtue will become perfected for you (or virtues will become perfected for you).
One who forgives wrongdoings has taken hold of the accumulation of merits.
One who does not favour [others] with forgiveness, wrongs [them] through vengeance.
Whoever does not accept repentance, his sin is great.
Overlooking [another’s] offence is part of religion.
How good is forgiveness while having ability [to exact revenge]!
He who scolds [someone] for a sin has not forgiven it.
Hastening in forgiving the sins [of others] is from the lofty morals of the honourable ones.
Never feel regret for forgiving and never be gladdened by punishing.
Do not hasten the punishment for a sin and leave room between the two (i.e. the sin and punishment) for forgiveness, through this you will gain recompense and reward.
There is no clemency like pardon.
There is nothing better than the forgiveness of a powerful person.
A wrongdoer can never be faced with anything better than being shown forgiveness.
It pleases me for a person to forgive the one who oppresses him, to establish ties with the one who cuts him off, to give the one who deprives him and to respond to evil with goodness.
Give people your forgiveness and pardon just as you would like Allah, the Glorified, to grant [it] to you, and never regret showing forgiveness [to others].
Honour the one who loves you and pardon your enemy, [for by this] virtue will become complete for you.
The best act of a person in power is to forgive.
Of all people, the most behoving of [granting] forgiveness is the one who has the greatest power to punish.
The most deserving of [showing] mercy is the one who [himself] is in need of it.
Better than seeking your right is to forgive [and forego] it.
The best of high morals is the forgiveness of the powerful and the generosity of the poor.
The best forgiveness is that which is shown despite having power [to exact revenge].
From the people, the one who is most cognizant of Allah is the one who is most forgiving to the people, even if he does not find them having any excuse.
Verily, confronting evil with good and the covering up wrongs with forgiveness are from the best virtues and the most praiseworthy qualities.
Verily, he who gives to the one who deprives him, establishes ties with the one who cuts him off and forgives the one who oppresses him, will find in Allah, the Glorified, a Supporter and a Helper.
Forgiveness is a virtue.
Forgiveness is the best good deed.
Forgiveness is the ornament of power.
Forgiveness brings about eminence.
Forgiveness is the alms-tax of power.
Forgiveness is the best of favours.
Forgiveness is the best revenge.
Pardoning means that a person should forgive that which is done to wrong him and show forbearance with that which angers him.
Pardoning is the best of traits.
Pardon that which you are unaware of for what you are aware of, and what you are ignorant of for what you know.2
When a wrong is done to you, then forgive.
The person most deserving of having his request granted is one who seeks forgiveness.

Be careful not to hasten towards punishment, for indeed this is detestable in the sight of Allah and brings [unwanted] changes [and removal of blessings] closer. sake of the good that he has done to you.
For every matter there is an outcome, [be it] sweet or bitter.
One who expects [and considers] the outcomes remains safe.
One who considers the outcomes remains safe.
One who considers the outcomes remains safe from calamities.
One who is careful of the outcomes is safe from peril [and destruction].
One who awaits a [positive] outcome is patient.
One who is careful of the outcomes remains safe from calamities.
When you endeavour to act upon a matter, then eschew the blameworthy outcomes in it.
Be careful of the outcomes and you will be saved from destruction.
In the outcomes [of matters] there is [either] a curer or a comforter.
The basis of [the success of] outcomes is that which results in the pleasure of Allah, the Glorified.
Disregarding the rights [of your parents] is from [the acts of] filial impiety.
The intellect is an honourable nobility that does not wear away.
The intellect is an inborn quality that increases through knowledge and experience.
The intellect and knowledge are joined together in one linkage, they neither separate nor do they differ.
The intellect is the greatest of riches and the highest honour in [both] the Hereafter and this world.
The intellect is the most beautiful adornment and knowledge is the most honourable merit.
The intellect is the root of knowledge and the herald of understanding.
Intelligence is an advantage, knowledge is an elevation and patience is a defence [and a means of repelling hardships].
The intellect is the close friend of a believer, knowledge is his vizier, patience is the commander of his army and action is his overseer.

The intellect is the leader of the army of the Most Merciful and vain desire is the chief of the army of Satan, and the soul is pulled back and forth between them, so whichever of them is victorious, it (i.e. the soul) is in its domain.

Intellect and lust are opposites; the supporter of the intellect is knowledge and the adorner of lust is vain desire, and the soul is contended for between the two, so whichever is triumphant, it is on its side.
Intelligence is for you to be moderate and not indulge in extravagance, to promise and not to break your promise, and to be forbearing when you get angry.
Intelligence is for you to speak [only] of what you know and to act upon what you say.
The intellect guides and saves whereas ignorance misleads and destroys.
The intellect is a praiseworthy friend.
Seek right guidance from the intellect and oppose vain desire, [by this] you will gain success.
Fetter your intellect, control your affair, struggle with your [lower] self, and exert your effort in working for the Hereafter.
Where are the intellects that light up (or that accompany) the lamps of guidance?
The best intellect is [that which leads one to] right guidance.
The best of blessings is the intellect.
The beginning of intelligence is being friendly [with the people].
The best intelligence is [that which leads to] good etiquette.
The best intelligence is keeping away from idle sport.
The best intelligence is for a person to know his self, for the one who knows his self becomes wise and the one who fails to know it goes astray.
The best intelligence is taking lesson [from the past], the best prudence is precaution and the biggest foolishness is being deceived [by worldly allures].
The best portion of a person is his intellect, if he gets humiliated it restores his honour, if he falls it raises him, if he goes astray it guides him and if he talks it directs him.
Verily Allah, the Glorified, loves the sound intellect and the upright action.
Verily the one who has been bestowed with a sound intellect and upright action by Allah has indeed been granted with a manifest blessing and a great bounty.
Intelligence is an adornment and foolishness is a disgrace.
Intelligence is closeness, foolishness is estrangement.
Intelligence is a remedy, foolishness is misery.
Intellects are gifts, etiquettes are earned.
The intellect is the excellence of human beings.
The intellect is the messenger of the truth.
The intellect is a friend that has been cut-off.
The intellect is a solver of every issue.
The intellect is not deceived.
The intellect is the herald of comprehension.
The intellect is the strongest foundation.
Intellect is the best thing that is hoped for.
Intelligence improves deliberation.
The intellect is the spring of goodness.
Intelligence is the preservation of [what is learnt through] experiences.
The intellect is the best ornament.
The intellect necessitates caution.
Intellect is the vehicle of knowledge.
The intellect is a sharp [cutting] sword.
Intellect is the most honourable merit.
The intellect is [like] a new attire that does not get worn out.
The intellect frees [one] from evil and enjoins [one to do] good.
The intellect is an intimate friend that is relied on in every situation.
The intellect is a tree whose fruits are generosity and modesty.
The intellect is an adornment for the one who is endowed with it.
The intellect gives one a sense of familiarity when he is away from his homeland.
The intellect elevates one to the lofty stations [in Paradise].

Verily, when I find a quality from the good qualities firmly ingrained in a person, I judge him according to it, and I forgive him for not possessing other than it; but I never exonerate him for not possessing intelligence or for lacking religion, because separation from religion is departure from security, and life is not wholesome with fear, and lack of intellect is lack of life, and the dead are not interacted with.
Verily you are gauged by your intellect, so develop it with knowledge.
Intellect is nothing but eschewing sin, considering the consequences [of one’s actions] and being [resolute and] prudent.
The bane of intellect is self-conceit.
When the intellect is complete, speech decreases.
When the intellect becomes complete, lust diminishes.
It is through the intellect that the deepest wisdom is brought out.
Through the intellect, [acts of goodness and] virtues are attained.
Through the intellect, the condition of the creatures is set right.
Through abundant intellect, forbearance becomes abundant.
Through the intellects, the pinnacle of sciences (or matters) is attained.
By leaving that which does not concern you, your intellect becomes complete.
Perfection of the soul is [attained] through the intellect.
It is through the intellect that every affair is set aright.
The completion of the intellect (or of action) is in its perfection.
The purification of a man is through his intellect.
The fruit of intellect is steadfastness [and uprightness].
The fruit of intellect is adherence to the truth.
The fruit of intellect is association with the virtuous.
The fruit of intellect is working for salvation.
The fruit of intellect is being affable with the people.
The fruit of intellect is honesty.
The fruit of intellect is aversion to this world and subdual of vain desire.
There are three things by which the intellects of people are tested: wealth, authority and adversity.
Three things show the intelligence of their lords: the messenger, the message and the gift.
A strong intellect is the beauty of the outward and inward facets [of a human being].
A good intellect is the best pathfinder.
The [highest] limit of the intellect is considering the consequences [of actions] and being pleased with what has been decreed [by Allah].
It is forbidden upon every intellect that is shacked by (or sick with) lust to benefit from wisdom.
The peak of intellect is separation from the perishing and attachment to the everlasting.
Preservation of the intellect is through opposing vain desire and turning away from this world.
The best of divine gifts [to human beings] is the intellect.
The indication of a person’s intellect is his speech.
The departure [and loss] of intellect is between vain desire and lust.
Kindle your intellect with etiquette just as you kindle fire with firewood.
The staidness of the intellect is put to the test in times of happiness and sadness.
A heightened intellect saves [one from perdition].
There are six situations in which the intellects of people are tested: association, transaction, authority, isolation, affluence and poverty.

There are six things that assay the intellects of people: forbearance when angry, patience when frightened, carefulness in obeying Allah in every situation, friendliness in dealing with others and reduced arguing [and quarrelling].
The rectitude of the intellect is [in] good etiquette.
The friend of every person is his intellect and his enemy is his ignorance.
Straying of the intellect distances one from right guidance and corrupts his Hereafter.
The straying of the intellect is the most serious deviation, and the abasement (or error) of ignorance is the greatest abasement (or error).
You must develop your intellect, for there is no wealth more profitable than it.
In times of trial (or perplexity) the [level of] intellects of the people are revealed.
In times of impromptu speech, the intellects of people are tested.
When covetousness and false hopes deceive, the minds of the ignorant are beguiled and the intellects of people are tested.
The symbol of intellect is being affable with the people.
The intellect of a person is his order, his etiquette is his foundation, his honesty is his leader and his gratitude is his perfection.
The intellects of the erudite scholars are in the points of their pens.
The highest distinction of a person is the excellence of his intellect.
The highest degree of intelligence is admitting to [one’s] ignorance.
The intrinsic nature of the intellect impels it to employ justice.
The intrinsic nature of the intellect rejects dispraised action.
The mind that is sick with anger and lust does not benefit from wisdom.
The veil of flaws is the intellect.
Lack of intellect is wretchedness.
Corruption of the intellect is [in] being deluded by deceptions.
The excellence of the intellect is [in] indifference towards [the pleasures of] this world.
At times [relying on] the intellect alone may lead [one] astray.
How many a lowly person has been made venerable by his intellect.
Many a mind has been made subservient by a commanding desire.
Intelligence is sufficient as wealth.
It is enough of intelligence for a person to be moderate in his pursuits.
It suffices for your intellect to distinguish for you right guidance from error.
Be quick to respond to your intellect and delay in responding to your vain desire.
Whenever the intellect of a person increases, his faith in divine decree becomes stronger and he takes the changing events [that bring worldly loss to him] lightly.
The gain of the intellect is refraining from harming others.
The manner of action points to the measure of intelligence, so make good choices for it and be more precautious with regards to it.
The intellect acquires consideration and precaution whereas ignorance earns negligence and deception.
The perfection of a person is his intellect and his value is his benevolence.
The perfection of a human being is his intellect.
Everything has a pinnacle, and the pinnacle of a person is his intellect.
For everything there is an alms-tax and the alms-tax of intelligence is tolerating the ignorant ones.
The intellect will never be adorned until it is complemented by forbearance.
If the intellect was sound, every person would take advantage of [every moment of] his time.
One who seeks the support of the intellect is supported by it.
Whoever seeks assistance from the intellect, it shows him the right direction.
One whose intellect is weak has bad oratory.
Do not have any expectations from one who has no intellect.
One whose intellect is complete scorns lustful desires.
One of the most affirming [and effective] means of intelligence is showing compassion to the ignorant ones.
From the most perfect of blessings is abundance of intellect.
Keeping away from wastefulness and good management [skills] are from [the fruits of] intelligence.
Adorning oneself with forbearance (or knowledge) is from the best intelligence.
The rectitude of the creation is [achieved through] the intellect.
The intellect of every person is deduced by what passes upon his tongue.
The intellect of a man is indicated by his good speech and the purity of his roots is evinced by his beautiful actions.
The intellect of a man is evinced by his increased dignity and his virtuous tolerance, and his honourable lineage is attested to by his beautiful actions.
One whose intellect overpowers his vain desire is successful.
One whose vain desire overpowers his intellect is disgraced.
One who loses his wits is not bypassed by abasement.
One who is held back by intellect is driven forward by ignorance.
Nothing is purified in the sight of Allah, the Glorified, except the cognizant mind and the disinclined soul [from the pleasures of this world].
There is nothing better than an intellect with knowledge, and knowledge with forbearance, and forbearance with power [to punish].
The intellect of a man is indicated by his adorning himself with chastity and contentment.
There is no wealth like intelligence.
There is no intelligence like feigning ignorance [when in the company of those who lack etiquette].
Intellect and vain desire do not go together.
There is no possession more beneficial than intellect.
There is no beauty more exquisite than intellect.
There is no blessing better than intellect.
The intellect does not beguile one who takes it advice.
There is no good in an intellect that is not accompanied by forbearance.
There is no ailment more debilitating than lack of intellect.
He who has no intellect has no religion.
One who loses [the friendship of] an intelligent one shows the weakness of his [own] intellect.
One who puts his intellect before his vain desire, his undertakings become good.
One who masters his intellect is indeed wise.
One who considers [and learns from the past] with his intellect, perceives.
One whose intellect becomes stronger takes more lessons [from the past].
Accumulating provisions for the Day of Return is from intelligence.
One of the signs of intelligence is speaking what is right.
Acting on the [established] practice of justice is from the signs of intelligence.
Nothing embellishes virtues like the intellect.
Allah, the Glorified, has not apportioned anything among his servants better than intellect.
Allah, the Glorified, has only entrusted man with an intellect so that it may one day deliver him.
The basis of [the rightness of] an affair is the intellect.
With intellect, forbearance [and judiciousness] becomes abundant.
The distinguishing feature of a man is his intellect and his beauty is his magnanimity.
Whoever is incapable of using his own present intellect, then he is more helpless with regards to the far-off intelligence [of others] and the one who is absent from him is more useless [to him].
The intelligent person is one who fetters his tongue.
The intelligent person is one who covers up sins with forgiveness.
The intelligent person is one who forsakes his lust and sells his world for his Hereafter.
The intelligent person does not speak except when he needs to or in order to present his case.
The intelligent person is one who abstains from sins and keeps himself free from faults.
The intelligent person is one who fetters his tongue except from the remembrance [and extolment] of Allah.
The intelligent person is one who opposes his vain desire in obedience to his Lord.
The intelligent person is one who performs acts of kindness and puts his effort in its correct place.
When the intelligent one is quiet, he reflects and when he speaks, he remembers [and extols Allah] and when he observes, he takes lesson.
The intelligent person is one who suspects his [own] opinion and does not trust everything that his self makes decorous for him.
The intelligent person is one who abstains from [the pleasures of] the lowly, perishing world and desires the sublime, everlasting, lofty Paradise.
The intelligent person is one who puts things in their right places, and the ignorant one does the opposite of this.
The intelligent person acts when he knows and when he acts, he does so sincerely, and when he becomes sincere, he secludes himself [from others].
The intelligent person is one who guards his tongue from backbiting.
The intelligent person strives in his work and shortens his hopes.
The intelligent person is one who overcomes his vain desire and does not sell his Hereafter for his [temporary life in this] world.
The intelligent one is neither pushed to the extreme by violence nor is he hampered by weakness.
The intelligent person is one who controls himself when he gets angry, when he desires and when he is frightened.
The intelligent person charges himself with performing that which is obligatory upon him and he does not charge himself with seeking that which is due to him.
The intelligent person is one who does not waste his [time and] energy in that which does not benefit him, and does not [strive to] acquire that which will not accompany him [after his death].
The intelligent person is one who overpowers his contending vain desires.
The intelligent person is one who submits to the decree [of Allah] and acts with judiciousness [and determination].
The intelligent person is one who subdues his vain desire with his intellect.
Be rational and you will discern.
Indeed, the intelligent person is one who considers the different [expressed] opinions with correct reasoning and considers the consequences [of matters].
The most intelligent of you is the most submissive of you.
The most intelligent person is one who follows the wise people.
When you make an indirect reference to an intelligent person then you have tormented him with reproof.
The most felicitous of people is the intelligent one.
The most intelligent of people is the most modest of them.
The most intelligent person is the virtuous, fearful one.
The most intelligent of people is the one who forgives [and accepts the excuses of] others the most.
The most intelligent of people is the farthest of them from all vile things.
The most intelligent of people is the most submissive of them to Allah, the Glorified.
The most intelligent of people is the closest of them to Allah.
The most intelligent of people is one who sees his own fault and is blind to the fault of others.
The most intelligent of people is the one who does not go beyond silence in punishing the ignorant.
The most intelligent of people is the best of them in estimating his livelihood and the most serious of them in endeavouring to improve his Hereafter.
The most intelligent of people is one whose seriousness overpowers his frivolity and who overcomes his vain desire with his intellect.

The most intelligent of people is one who is humbled in front of the truth so he submits himself to it, and is honoured by the truth so he does not undermine its establishment and acting upon it with goodness.
The most intelligent of people is the one who is most considering of the consequences [of actions].
Verily the intelligent one is not beguiled by covetousness.

Verily the intelligent person is one whose intellect is [employed] in right guidance and whose view is in [the process of development and] growth, that is why his view is correct and his action praiseworthy.
Indeed, the intelligent one learns through discipline while the beasts are not trained except by beating.
Verily the intelligent person is one who looks in his today for his tomorrow, and strives to unshackle his soul, and works for that which must come to pass and which cannot be escaped.
Verily it behoves the intelligent one to be cautious of death in this world, and he should make good preparations before he arrives at the abode wherein one wishes for death but does not find it.
The practice of those who possess intellect and understanding is turning towards the permanent abode, turning away from the evanescent abode and being desirous of the Garden of Paradise.
It behoves the intelligent one to make arrangements for his Hereafter and to develop [and build] the abode of his permanent residence.
The intelligent one likes the company of those who are like him.
A person is the friend of what he understands.
The intelligent one is the enemy of his delectation.
The intelligent person is one who fetters his tongue.
The intelligent one seeks perfection, the ignorant one seeks wealth.
The intelligent one puts his self down and as a result he gets elevated.
The intelligent one is grieved, sorrowful.
The intelligent person is one who safeguards his affair.
Insinuation is the severest punishment for the intelligent one.
The intelligent person is one who is admonished by experiences.
The intelligent person is one who annihilates his lust.
The intelligent person is one who spreads his generosity.
The intelligent one relies on his [hard] work, [while] the ignorant one relies on his aspiration.
The intelligent person is one who takes a lesson from [the experiences of] others.
The intelligent person is one whose words are affirmed by his actions.
The intelligent person is one who stops at what he knows.
The intelligent person is one who renounces that which the ignorant one desires.
Indeed only he is intelligent who is admonished by experiences.
Only he is intelligent who takes out the grudges [from his heart].
As the intelligent one grows older, his intellect grows younger.
Hinting at [and making indirect references to] the error of the intelligent person is one of the most agonizing punishments for him.
The wealth of an intelligent person is in his knowledge and his action.
Love of knowledge, virtuous forbearance and adhering to the right are from the merits of the people of reason and understanding.
It is a right that is due on the intelligent one to work for the Hereafter and to seek more provisions [for it].
It is a right upon the intelligent one to vanquish his vain desire before his adversary.
The reign of the intelligent one is like the relative who longs to unite [with his dear ones].
The one who possesses intellect is not known except by [his] tolerance, temperance and kindness.
The desire of an intelligent person is in wisdom and the ambition of an ignorant person is in foolishness.
The lapse of an intelligent person is dangerous.
The lapse of an intelligent person is a crushing blow.
The virtues of an intelligent ruler are spread far and wide.
The [distinguishing] quality of the people of intellect is [their] lack of lust and negligence.
The quality of those who possess intellect and understanding is [their] turning towards the Eternal Abode, turning away from the evanescent abode, and yearning for the Garden of Paradise.
The chest of an intelligent person is the strongbox of his secret.
The conjecture of an intelligent person is more correct than the certitude of an ignorant person.
The enmity of an intelligent person is better than the friendship of an ignorant one.
The sufficiency of an intelligent person is through his knowledge.
The sufficiency of an intelligent person is through his wisdom and his honour is through his contentment.
The ugly act of an intelligent person is better than the beautiful act of an ignorant person.
Every intelligent person is sorrowful (or sad).
Be intelligent in the affairs of your religion and simple in your worldly affairs.
The speech of the intelligent is a nourishment [for the soul] and the reply of the ignorant is [nothing better than] silence.
For the intelligent one, there is goodness in every action [he does].
For the intelligent one, there is nobility in every word [he speaks].
For the intelligent one, in every action there is self-discipline.
It is not for the intelligent one to move out [of his home] except for three things: to do something to improve his Hereafter, or to earn his livelihood, or to enjoy what is not forbidden.
He who is distracted by idle sport and seeks pleasure in amusement and song, has no intelligence.
One who has intelligence, comprehends.
One who has intelligence remains chaste [and abstains from the forbidden].
One who has intelligence seeks pardon [for the wrong he does].
One who has intelligence is kind [and tolerant].
One who has intelligence is content.
One who has intelligence remains silent [until there is a need to speak].
One who does not use intellect is abased, and one who is abased is not revered.
One who has intelligence takes more lessons [from the past].
One whose intellect is less, his jesting is increased.
One who has intelligence takes lesson from his past and takes precaution for his soul.
One whose intellect prevails over his lust and his forbearance [overcomes] his anger, then he is worthy of [being deemed as having] good conduct.
One who has intelligence awakens from his negligence, prepares for his journey and maintains [and develops] his abode of [permanent] residence.
One whose intellect does not have the greatest control over him does not benefit from [any] advice.
One who does not have an intellect to adorn him, does not become noble.
One whose intellect is not complete, his evils are not safeguarded against.
It is from the intelligence of a man that he not speak about all that he knows.
It is from the rights of the intelligent person to vanquish his vain desire before his adversary.
It is from the right of the intelligent person to count his evil action and his ugly conduct as being from the wretchedness of his circumstance and his misfortune.
From the perfection of your intellect is your reliance on your intellect.
One who lengthens his aspirations is not intelligent.
An intelligent person does not lie and a believer does not fornicate.
The magnanimity of an intelligent person is his religion and his distinction is his etiquette.
Half of the intelligent one is tolerance and [the other] half is feigning negligence [when encountering the bad behaviour of the ignorant].
There is no poverty for the intelligent one.
The intelligent person is never found [to be] beguiled.
There is none more courageous than the intelligent one.
He who is overcome by anger and lust should not be counted as an intelligent person.
It behoves the intelligent person not to remain aloof from the obedience of Allah and the struggle against his [lower] self, in every situation.
It behoves the intelligent person to work for the Hereafter and try to increase his provisions before he passes away and is lowered into his grave.
It behoves the intelligent one to prepare provisions for his Hereafter and to maintain [and develop] the abode of his [permanent] residence.
It behoves the intelligent person to earn praise through his wealth and to preserve himself from asking others.
It behoves an intelligent person to address an ignorant one like a doctor addresses a sick patient.
It behoves the intelligent person to increase his association with the scholars and the virtuous ones, and to keep away from the company of the evil and wicked ones.

It behoves the intelligent one to protect himself from the intoxication of wealth, the intoxication of power, the intoxication of knowledge, the intoxication of praise and the intoxication of youth, for each of these have foul odours that take away intelligence and reduces dignity.
It behoves the intelligent person not to be harsh when he teaches, and not to scorn [others] when he gains knowledge.
The intellect of every person is manifested by that which is spoken by his tongue.
The intellect of every person is indicated by his tongue, and his merit is evinced by his diction.
I am amused by a man whose intellect is seen as an extension of his tongue, while his tongue is not seen as an extension of his intellect.
Follow the intelligent one and you will benefit.
At times the intelligent person becomes blind to what is right.
The branches will surely return to their roots, and the effects to their causes, and the particulars to their universals.

He (‘a) was asked about the [beings in the] celestial realm, so he replied: [They are] forms devoid of matter, above [the need for physical] strength and ability; divine light is illuminated upon them so they shine and it rises upon them so they gleam; then He casts in their identities His likeness, thus He manifests His actions through them. He created the human being with an articulating soul, [such that] if he purifies it with knowledge and action, it resembles the essences of its primal causes, and when its demeanour is moderate and it disassociates the contraries then it becomes associated with the seven strong [heavens].
Knowledge guides [one] to the truth.
Knowledge is the lamp of the intellect and the fountain of excellence.
Knowledge is the killer of ignorance and the earner of nobility.
Knowledge without action is a plague.
Knowledge is a great treasure that does not get exhausted.
Knowledge is one of the two lives.
Knowledge is the better of the two intimate companions.
Knowledge is the better of the two beauties.
Knowledge about Allah is the better of the two types of knowledge.
Knowledge is an honourable heritage and a universal blessing.
Knowledge saves [one] from being entangled in perplexity.
Knowledge is evidence of intellect, so the one who knows has intelligence.
Knowledge is the enlivener of the soul, the illuminator of the intellect and the annihilator of ignorance.
Knowledge is the fruit of wisdom and rightness is from its branches.
Knowledge is the greatest honour for the one who has no [honourable] past.
Knowledge is greater than can be encompassed [in its totality], so take the best from every [branch of] knowledge.
Knowledge is a governor while wealth is governed.
Knowledge guides you towards that which Allah has commanded you to do and renunciation of worldly pleasures makes the path to it easier for you.
Knowledge is better than wealth; knowledge guards you while you guard wealth.
Knowledge is linked to action, so one who knows, acts.
Knowledge calls out to action, so if it responds to it [then it stays] otherwise it departs.
Knowledge guides you and action takes you to the goal.
Knowledge is the first guide and cognizance is the final end.
Knowledge is of two types: the intuitive and the learnt; the intuitive knowledge is of no benefit if there is no learnt knowledge [accompanying it].
Know, then speak.
Seek knowledge and you will increase in knowledge.
Acquire knowledge, for indeed if you are wealthy it will adorn you and if you are poor it will provide for you.
Seek knowledge and you will be rightly guided.
Acquire knowledge and it will earn you life.
Draw water from the clear spring which has been cleansed of all impurity.1
Seek knowledge and you will be known for it, act upon it and you will become from those who are worthy of [possessing] it.
Indeed, the one who does not know should never be ashamed to learn, for the value of every person is [measured by] what he knows.
Indeed, the one who is asked about that which he does not know should never consider it demeaning to say “I don’t know”.
The most useful knowledge is that which is acted upon.
The best knowledge is that which is accompanied by action.
The most honourable knowledge is that which is manifested in the organs and limbs.
The lowliest knowledge is that which stops at the tongue [and is not acted upon].
The most victorious of all people is he who overpowers his vain desire with his knowledge.
The most important knowledge for you is that without which [your good] action is not accepted.
The most obligatory knowledge for you [to acquire] is that which you are responsible for acting upon.
The most necessary knowledge for you is that which guides you to rectitude of your religion and separates you from its corruption.2
The knowledge with the most praiseworthy end is that which increases your [good] actions in this world and draws you nearer [to the mercy of Allah] in the Hereafter.
Verily the best of knowledge is [that which leads to] tranquillity and forbearance.

Indeed fire is not diminished by what is taken from it but is extinguished when it does not find firewood; similarly, knowledge is not depleted by being acquired but the miserliness of those who possess it is the cause of its absence.
Verily Allah, the Glorified, bestows wealth to the one whom He loves and the one whom He hates, but He does not grant knowledge except to the one whom He loves.
Verily knowledge guides, directs and saves while ignorance misguides, misdirects and destroys.
Knowledge rescues.
Knowledge is through understanding.
Knowledge is a treasure.
Knowledge is honour, obedience is [a] refuge.
Knowledge is a guide.
Knowledge saves you, ignorance destroys you.
Knowledge is loftiness, ignorance is misguidance.
Knowledge is life, faith is salvation.
Knowledge makes one lofty, ignorance misguides.
Knowledge is a refuge.
Knowledge is through action.
Knowledge is the annihilator of ignorance.
Knowledge is the adornment of distinction [and noble descent].
Knowledge is the leader of forbearance.
Knowledge is the most excellent honour.
Knowledge is the lamp of the intellect.
Knowledge is the best guide.
Knowledge is the most sublime provision.
Knowledge is the greatest treasure.
Knowledge is life and a cure [for the maladies of the heart].
Knowledge is a veil [that protects one] from adversities.
Knowledge is the highest success.
Knowledge is the best acquisition.
Knowledge is the riding mount of forbearance.
Knowledge is the root of every good.
Knowledge is the symbol of intellect.
Knowledge is the fecundation of cognizance.
Knowledge aids [and strengthens] reflection.
Knowledge is indeed a good guide.
Knowledge is the most excellent (or honourable) guidance.
Sciences are the recreation of the men of erudition.
Knowledge is the root of forbearance.
Knowledge is the killer of ignorance.
Knowledge is the herald of comprehension.
Knowledge does not end.
Knowledge is abundant but action is scarce.
Knowledge is a great treasure that does not get exhausted.
Knowledge is a [means of] right guidance for the one who acts upon it.
All of knowledge is a proof [against its possessor] except what is acted upon.
Knowledge is a beauty that does not remain concealed and a relation that does not abandon you (or that is not hidden).
Knowledge is the adornment of the wealthy and the wealth of the poor.
Indeed the only thing that has made people disinclined to seeking knowledge is the frequency with which they observe that only a few people act upon what they know.
The bane of knowledge is to forsake acting upon it.
When you hear knowledge then treat it seriously and do not taint it with jesting, thereby making the hearts spit it out.
When you want to benefit from knowledge then act upon it and increase in your contemplation about its meanings, [for through this] it will be retained by the hearts.
When the knowledge of a person increases, his etiquette improves and his awe for his Lord increases.
Through knowledge, wisdom is recognized.
Through knowledge, there is life.
Through knowledge, the crooked is straightened.
Sharing knowledge [with those who deserve] is the alms-tax of knowledge.
Through knowledge, the station of forbearance is attained.
The completeness of knowledge is [in] its application.
The completeness of knowledge is [in] acting according to it.
The one who forsakes acting on [his] knowledge is not certain of getting reward for his action.
The fruit of knowledge is cognizance of Allah.
The fruit of knowledge is worship.
The fruit of knowledge is acting upon it.
The fruit of knowledge is working for [a blissful] life [in the Hereafter].
The fruit of knowledge is sincerity of action.
The wealth of knowledge saves and preserves.
The beauty of knowledge is [in] its dissemination, its fruit is [in] acting upon it, and its preservation is [in] placing it with those who are worthy of it.
The best of knowledge is that which gives benefit.
The best of all knowledge is that which reforms you.
The best knowledge is that which is accompanied by action.
The best of knowledge is that by which you reform your right guidance, and the worst of it is that by which you corrupt your Hereafter.

Take from every knowledge the best of it, for indeed the bee partakes from the most beautiful of every flower, so two precious substances are produced from it: in one of them is a cure for the people (i.e. honey), and the other is a means of illumination (i.e. wax).
The cornerstone of [all] merits is knowledge.
Many a knowledge may lead to your misguidance.
The alms-tax of knowledge is its dissemination.
The alms-tax of knowledge is granting it to the one who deserves it and exerting the self to act upon it.
The adornment of knowledge is forbearance.
The cause of fear [of Allah] is knowledge.3
Ask about that which you must know and cannot be excused for being ignorant about.
The worst knowledge is that by which you corrupt your right guidance.
The worst knowledge is knowledge that is not action upon.
There are two things the ends of which can never be reached: knowledge and intellect.
The disgrace of knowledge is boasting.
You must acquire knowledge, for indeed it is an honourable heritage.
The knowledge of a hypocrite is [only] on his tongue.
The knowledge of a believer is [manifested] in his action.
Knowledge without action is like trees without fruit.
Knowledge without action is like a bow without a bowstring.
Knowledge that is not useful is like a medicine that does not cure.
Knowledge that does not reform you is misguidance and wealth that does not benefit you is a curse.
Knowledge without action is a proof of Allah against His servant.
The goal of knowledge is good action.
The utmost goal of knowledge is fear of [the displeasure of] Allah, the Glorified.
The end goal of knowledge is tranquillity and forbearance.
The excellence of knowledge is [in] acting upon it.
Saying ‘I don’t know’ is half of knowledge.
Little knowledge accompanied with action is better than a lot of it without action.
Knowledge cuts off the excuse of those who offer [many] excuses.
All knowledge that is not supported by the intellect is misguidance.
Everything diminishes when it is expended except knowledge.
Everything becomes precious when it becomes less (or scarce) except knowledge, for indeed it gains value when it abounds.
Every vessel becomes constricted by what is put in it except the vessel of knowledge, for verily it becomes wider.
Knowledge is sufficient as loftiness.
Every time the knowledge of a person increases, his concern for his soul increases, and he exerts his efforts in training and reforming it.
Just as knowledge guides a person and saves him, similarly, ignorance misguides him and destroys him.
The acquisition of knowledge is indifference towards worldly pleasures.
The perfection of knowledge is forbearance, and the perfection of forbearance is increased tolerance and suppression [of anger].
The perfection of knowledge is action.
For the seeker of knowledge, there is honour in this world and success in the Hereafter.
Knowledge will never bear fruit until it is accompanied by forbearance.
None will attain knowledge except the one who lengthens his [period of] study.
The language of knowledge is truthfulness.
The conception of knowledge is imagination and understanding.
One who seeks right guidance from knowledge, it guides him.
One who is alone with knowledge does not feel frightened by [his] loneliness.
One who is not guided by knowledge is misguided by ignorance.
One who acts with knowledge attains his goal and desire from the Hereafter.
One who is fond of knowledge has [actually] done good to his soul.
Whoever hides [his] knowledge, it is as if he is an ignorant person.
One who acts against his knowledge, his crime and sin become grave.
One whose knowledge exceeds his intellect, it becomes a burden for him.
One who learns (or lacks) the depth of knowledge proceeds (or is repelled) from the ways of wisdom.
One who quenches his thirst from the drinking-fountain of knowledge, covers himself with the gown of forbearance.
One who increases his study of knowledge [and discussion about what he has learnt] does not forget what he knows and benefits from it that which he does not know.
One who increases his reflection about what he has learnt safeguards his knowledge and understands that which he would not have [otherwise] understood.
One who does not acquire wealth through knowledge, acquires grace by it.
Whoever does not act upon his knowledge, it becomes a proof against him and a curse.
From the perfection of knowledge is acting upon what it dictates.
From the most honourable of knowledge is self-adornment with forbearance.
He who enlivens knowledge does not die.
Nothing increases knowledge like acting upon it.
Knowledge does not benefit the one who does not understand [it] and forbearance is not useful for the one who does not show clemency.
The basis of knowledge is its dissemination.
The basis of knowledge is acting upon it.
Coming together to study knowledge is the delight of the scholars.
Gatherings of knowledge are a bounty.
The adornments of a man are his knowledge and his forbearance.
How good a companion of forbearance knowledge is!
How good a companion of faith knowledge is!
How good a guide of faith knowledge is!
Do not make enmity with that which you are ignorant of, for indeed most of knowledge is in that which you don’t know.
There is no provision like knowledge.
There is no honour like knowledge.
There is no nightly conversation partner like knowledge.
There is no treasure more worthwhile than knowledge.
There is no distinction more honourable than knowledge.
There is no guide more successful than knowledge.
Knowledge is not acquired except from its masters.
Knowledge does not benefit without [divinely granted] success.
Knowledge is not attained with physical comfort.
Knowledge is not purified without piety.
Nobody obtains knowledge except the one who lengthens his study.
One who has no insight, has no knowledge.
Nobody disparages knowledge and its possessors except the foolish, ignorant one.
A little knowledge removes a lot of ignorance.
People attain superiority through knowledge and intellect, not by wealth and lineage.
Knowledge needs action.
Knowledge needs forbearance.
Knowledge needs suppression [of anger].
Obey knowledge and disobey ignorance, [for by doing this] you will be successful.
Knowledge is the most honourable guidance.
The scholar is one whose actions attest to the veracity of his words.
Scholars are strangers [in their own land] because of the large numbers of ignorant people.
