The scholar is one who is not satisfied with [his] knowledge nor does he allow himself to be satiated by it.
The scholar recognizes the ignorant one because he used to be ignorant [himself] before.
The scholar who is truly a scholar, is one who does not prevent the servants from having hope in the mercy of Allah and [at the same time] does not give them false security from the scheme of Allah.
The scholar and the student are partners in reward; there no good in anything between this.1
Scholars are the purest of people in character and the least rooted in [vain] desires.
The scholar is a living [person] among the dead.
Be careful not to disparage scholars, for indeed this will degrade you and make others think ill of you and expect evil from you.
The most learned among you are the most fearful of you.
The people who are most deserving of the [guidance of the] Prophets are those who have the most knowledge about what they came with.
The most learned person is the one who is most infatuated with knowledge.
The most learned of people about Allah, the Glorified, are the most fearful of Him.
The most learned of people about Allah, the Glorified, are the most satisfied with His decree.
The greatest of people in knowledge are the most intense in [their] fear of Allah, the Glorified.
The most learned of people about Allah are those who are most fearful of Him.
The most hated of servants in the sight of Allah is the haughty scholar.
Those with the greatest burden among the people are the scholars who exceed the limits.
The most regretful of all people at the time of death are the scholars who don’t act on their knowledge.
The most learned of people is one whose doubt does not dispel his certainty.
The person who is most learned about Allah is he who asks from Him the most.
Verily the narrators of knowledge are many, but those who are careful of [acting upon] it are few.
Verily the people who are most deserving of the [guidance of the] Prophets - peace be upon them - are those who have the most knowledge about (or act upon) their teachings.
The scholar is honoured because of his knowledge, the elderly because of his age, the doer of good because of his goodness and the king because of his kingship.
The scholars are judges over the people.
The scholar is alive even when he is dead.
The scholar is one who knows his [own] status [and worth].
The scholar sees with his heart and his mind while the ignorant one sees with his eyes and his eyesight.
The scholar is a person who does not get weary of gaining knowledge.
Scholars live on as long as the day and night remains.
The concealer of knowledge is not certain of being correct in it.
Only he is a scholar whose knowledge calls him to piety and God-wariness, to abstinence from the pleasures of the transient world and to infatuation with the heavenly abode.
The bane of scholars is love for leadership [and authority].
When you see a [true] scholar, be a servant to him.

Congratulations to the scholar who knows and thus restrains himself [from sin], and who fears the sudden coming [of death] so he prepares himself and gets ready. If he is questioned he articulates, and if he is left he remains silent; his speech is accurate and his silence is not because of his inability to give an answer.
Sit in the company of scholars and you will be felicitous.
Sit in the company of scholars and you will increase your knowledge.
The beauty of a scholar is [in] his acting upon his knowledge.
Sit with the scholars and your knowledge will increase, your etiquette will improve and your soul will become purified.
Be close to the scholars and you will perceive.
Many a scholar is killed by his knowledge.
Many a person who claims to have knowledge is not a scholar.
Many a scholar does not benefit [from his knowledge].
The rank of a scholar is the highest of ranks.
The lapse [and misguidance] of a scholar corrupts entire worlds.
The lapse of a scholar is like the breaking up of a ship, it sinks and causes others to sink along with it.
The lapse of a scholar is a serious offence.
It is upon the scholar to learn that which he does not know and to teach the people what he has learnt.
It is the duty of the scholar to act upon what he knows and then seek to learn that which he does not know.
A scholar who opposes you is better than the ignorant person who assists you.
Every scholar is fearful [of Allah].
How many a scholar is corrupt and [how many] a worshipper is ignorant, so be wary of the corrupt among the scholars and the ignorant among the worshippers.
It is enough of ignorance for a scholar that his actions contradict his knowledge.
Be either a knowledgeable speaker or a keen listener, and beware of being the third type.
Be knowledgeable about the truth and act upon it, [and through this] Allah, the Glorified, will save you.

If the people of knowledge were to carry it as it deserves to be carried, Allah and His angels would surely love them, but they bear it in order to seek worldly gain, so Allah, the Exalted, is displeased with them and they are thus abased by it.
One who has knowledge asks good [and pertinent] questions.
One who knows must act upon his knowledge.
One who gains knowledge (or acts [upon his knowledge]) is rightly guided.
One who wastes his knowledge [by not acting upon it] faces turmoil.
One who reveres a scholar has revered his Lord.
Whoever does not nurture his knowledge in solitude, it humiliates him among the people.
One who claims to have reached the end of knowledge has manifested the highest level of ignorance.
It is necessary for every scholar to secure his sides with piety and to extend his knowledge to the one who seeks it.
Considering your knowledge (or action) as little is from the excellence of your knowledge.
He who does not act upon his knowledge has not truly gained knowledge.
How many are those who gain knowledge but do not follow it!
Allah, the Glorified, did not make it incumbent upon the ignorant one to learn until He had made it incumbent upon the learned to teach.

Only two [types of] people have broken my back: the impudent scholar and the ignorant worshipper. One drives people away from the truth by his immorality and the other invites people to falsehood with his devotion.
The competition (or argumentation) of the scholars results in their gaining benefit and their earning merits.

The keepers of material treasures are annihilated while they are [still] alive while the scholars remain as long as the nights and days remain. Their bodies are lost but their examples [and teachings continue to] remain in the hearts.
Never disrespect a scholar, even if he is lowly.
There is no lapse more serious than the lapse of a scholar.

A scholar is not a true scholar until he stops being jealous of one who is above him, does not demean one who is below him and does not take in return for his knowledge anything of the vanities of this world.
The knowledge of a man should surpass his speech and his intelligence should prevail over his tongue.
The bane of the masses is a corrupt scholar.
The most helpful thing in purifying the intellect is education.
Learn and you will become knowledgeable, honour and you will be honoured.
Be humble in front of the one from whom you gain knowledge and the one whom you teach; and do not be from among the haughty scholars, lest your ignorance rises alongside you knowledge.
Acquire knowledge, for indeed if you are wealthy it will adorn you and if you are poor it will provide for you (or guard you).

Learn the knowledge of the one who knows, and teach your knowledge to the one who is ignorant, for if you do this, he will be teach you that which you are ignorant of and you will benefit [others] with what you have learnt.
He who places knowledge with one who is unworthy of it has wronged it [or him].
Through education, knowledge is gained.
Gain knowledge and you will be known by it, act upon it and you will be one of its worthy possessors.
If you are not an articulating scholar then be an attentive listener.
The student must discipline himself in his quest for knowledge and must neither become bored of his studies nor overestimate what he already knows.
One who learns becomes knowledgeable.
One who does not learn does not become knowledgeable.
One who gains knowledge so that he can act upon it is not distressed by its dullness.
One who does not learn in his young age, does not progress in his old age.
One who does not bear the hardships of gaining knowledge (or education) remains in the abject ignorance?
One who does not discipline himself (or spend his life) in acquiring knowledge cannot gain great successes.
The one who does not know must never be too proud to learn.

Do not speak to the ignorant ones about that which they do not know such that they belie you, for indeed your knowledge has a right over you and its right is that you bestow it to those who are deserving of it and deny it to those who are not deserving of it.
One who is haughty does not learn.
The age up to which Allah, the Glorified, accepts the excuse of human beings and warns them is sixty years.
The age in which a person reaches maturity is forty.
Be wary of wasting your lifetimes in that which will not remain for you, for that which has passed from it does not return.
Verily your lifetime is the dower of your prosperity if you spend it in obedience to your Lord.
Verily your breaths are portions of your life, so do not use them up except in the obedience that brings you closer [to Allah].
Verily your lifetime is the time which you find yourself in.
Verily your lifespan is the number of your breaths, and there is a watcher who counts them.
Indeed the night and day are quick in razing the lifetimes.
Indeed your life’s past is that which has come to pass and its future is hope, and the present is [time for] action.
Verily the life that is being shortened every moment and being dismantled every hour must be regarded as very short.
Indeed deceived is the one who is deluded with regards to his life and enviable is one who spends his life in the obedience of his Lord.
The lifespan [of a person] is [made up of] a specific number of breaths.
How can one be pleased with a lifetime that is diminished by [the passing of] hours?!
There is nothing more valuable than red sulphur, except that which remains from the lifetime of a believer.
One whose life is long, his tribulations become many.
One whose life is long gets afflicted by [the loss of] his dear and beloved ones.
One who spends his life in other than that which will save him [in the Hereafter] has missed his objective.
An hour of your time does not pass but that it cuts away a portion of your lifespan.
Do not waste your lifetime in useless pastimes, thereby leaving this world without any hope [in the Hereafter].
With the progression of days and nights, nothing remains of the lifetimes.
Nobody knows how much longer he has to live except a Prophet or a man of truth.
Lifetime is diminished by moments.
Guard your lifetime from being wasted in other than acts of worship and obedience [to Allah].
The bane of development and prosperity is the oppression of a tyrant.
One who delves too deep [in trying to understand the essence of Allah] does not return to the truth.
Action without knowledge is misguidance.
Righteous action is the better of the two provisions.
Action in obedience to Allah is more beneficial, and being truthful is more beautiful and [makes one more] successful.
The actions of servants in this world are [brought] before their eyes in the Hereafter.
Honour in the sight of Allah, the Glorified, is through righteous actions, not by beautiful words.
Falling short in action, for the one who is certain of its reward, is foolishness.
Busying oneself with that which will not accompany you after death is from the greatest weakness.
Acting upon [one’s] knowledge is from the perfection of blessings.
Utterances are recorded, secrets are [going to be] revealed and every soul is held hostage by what it has earned.
The [most] righteous companion is righteous action.
Act [in this world] so that you can store [provisions for the Hereafter].
Act upon [your] knowledge and you will attain [great] benefit.
Make your [righteous] action your friend your [false] aspiration your enemy.
Act like one who knows that Allah will surely recompense him for his evil and good deeds.
Strive hard in your work and do not be a storekeeper for others.
Act upon [your] knowledge and you will be felicitous.
When you know, act.
Perform good deeds while [you are in place where] deeds benefit, supplication is answered and repentance is raised [and accepted].
Eschew every action that you are in no need of and busy yourself with the affair of the Hereafter, which you must [eventually] face.
Work for the day for which the provisions have been stored and in which the secrets will be revealed.

Work while you are still alive, and while the books are [still] open, repentance is [still] accepted, the one who has strayed is [still] called [back], and the sinner is [still] given hope [of forgiveness]; before action abates, time expires, life ends and the door of repentance is closed.
Be wary of every action which, when its doer is asked about it, he feels ashamed and denies it.
Be wary of every action that is done in private and causes embarrassment in public.
Be wary of every action that the doer is pleased to perform himself but hates Muslims at large to perform.
Be wary of bad deeds, deceptive aspirations, loss of hope and the sudden coming of death.
You must keep away from evil action, for indeed it dishonours your reputation and increases your burden.
Keep away from every act that repels the freeman from you, or lowers your status, or brings harm upon you, or because of which you have to bear a burden on the Day of Judgment.
Is no one ready to work for his soul before the day of his misery [and adversity]?!

Act now, while the tongues are free, the bodies are healthy, the limbs can be flexed, there is room for change and the area of movement is vast; before all this is lost and death comes – so be certain about its coming and do not wait for it to overtake you.

Act now, O servants of Allah, while the neck is free [from the noose] and the spirit is unfettered in the period of guidance, while the bodies are at ease and the rest of your life lies ahead, while you have the free will to act, the opportunity to seek repentance and chance to rectifying your misdeeds. [So act] before you are overtaken by straitened circumstances and distress, fear and weakness, and before the approach of the anticipated hidden one (i.e. the Angel of Death) and the seizing of the Almighty, the Omnipotent.
Indeed you are in the days of hope after which is death; so whoever acts in the days of his hope before the coming of his death, his action benefits him and his death does him no harm.
Where are those who make their actions sincere for Allah and purify their hearts by the remembrance of Allah?!
The most honourable action is obedience [to Allah].
The best action is that which is done with sincerity.
The best action is that by which the pleasure of Allah is sought.
The most beneficial provision [for the hereafter] is good deeds.
The closest people to the Prophets are those who act upon their commandments [and teachings] the most.
The best of actions is restraining oneself from evil.
The most truthful of utterances is that which is spoken with the tongue of action.
The best of speech is that which is affirmed by good actions.
The best of actions is espousing the truth.
The best of actions is that which corresponds to the truth, and the best speech is that which matches with the facts.
Action is the symbol [and an indication] of one’s interior.
Good action is the mark [and distinguishing quality] of the believer.
Good action is the most perfect legacy.
Good action is the superior [form of] piety (or piety is the most preferred action).
Good action is the [close] companion of the believer.
Nothing accompanies a person [to his grave] except [his] deeds.
Actions in this world are the wares for trade in the Hereafter.
The action done in obedience to Allah is more profitable.
Beautiful action indicates strong determination [and earnest effort].
All action is [as worthless] as scattered dust except that which is done with sincerity.
If you wish to work, then work for that which will save you on the Day of Presentation [of deeds].
Verily none of your actions will be accepted except that which you did with sincerity and without vain desire or worldly motives.
Verily nothing but the good deeds that you sent forward will be of any benefit to you after your death, so gather the provision of good deeds.
Indeed you will never carry any action to the Hereafter more beneficial than patience, satisfaction, fear and hope.
Verily you are recompensed for your deeds and held hostage by them.
Verily you are judged by what you send forth and held hostage by what you leave behind.
Verily you are in greater need of acting upon what you know than of learning what you don’t know.
Surely you are in greater need of performing your actions than you are of articulating your words.
You are surely in greater need of earning good deeds than you are of earning wealth.
Verily you are in greater need of being concerned about that which will accompany you to the Hereafter than of all that accompanies you in this world.
Verily you are requited for your actions, so do not do anything except good.
Verily if you seize the opportunity to perform righteous deeds [in this world], you will attain your greatest aspirations in the Hereafter.
Verily a person is only rewarded for what he has sent in advance and meets [only] that which he sent ahead.
The bane of action is abandoning sincerity.
The bane of works is the inability of the workers.
The bane of action is idleness.
When you have considered [the consequences of an action], then do it.
Through virtuous deeds, praise becomes worthy.
Through righteous deeds, the strength of a believer’s faith is deduced.
It is by action, not laziness, that reward is gained.
It is by good action that the fruit of knowledge is reaped, not by good speech.
It is through action that Paradise is achieved, not through hope.
By righteous deeds, ranks are raised.
Delay in action is a symbol of laziness.
Keeping an action sincere is harder than performing the action itself.
Hasten towards praiseworthy actions and virtuous traits, and vie for truthful speech and generous giving.
The fruit of [good] action is the [divine] reward given for it.
The fruit of righteous action is [righteous] like its root.
The fruit of evil action is [evil] like its root.
The reward of your action is greater than your action.
The reward for an action is to the extent of the difficulty [endured] in it.
The garment of action (or knowledge) immortalizes you and does not get worn out; it preserves you and does not perish.
Persist in seizing the opportunity of performing the action whose reward does not perish.
Persist in those actions that cause you to become free from hellfire and attain Paradise.
The reward for an action is the fruit of the action.
Beautiful action declares the goodness of the source.
Allah has kept for every [good] deed a reward, for everything a reckoning and for every term a written appointment.
Virtuous action is the best provision and the greatest asset.
Good action is the substantiation of good words.
The best of your deeds are those that fulfil your duty.
The best of actions is that which earns gratitude.
The best of actions is that which rectifies the faith.
The best deed is that which is accompanied by sincerity.
The best of deeds is that which is adorned by kindness.
The best of actions is that which fulfils the requirements.
Your best action is that by which you improve your day [of reckoning] and the worst [of your actions] is that by which you corrupt your community.
The best action is maintaining a balance between hope and fear.
May Allah have mercy upon the person who anticipates death and performs good deeds for the abode of his [permanent] residence and the place of his dignity.
Many an action is corrupted by the intention.
Many a small action [that you do] is considered by you as being great.
Supplementing words with action is the best virtue and the abstraction of action from words is the ugliest vice.
Evil action is evidence of a vile origin.
The worst action is that which results in sins.
The worst action is that which destroys the good turn [that is done to others].
There is a great difference between the action whose pleasure wanes but its [ill] effects remain and the action whose hardship disappears but its reward remains.
The goodness of an action is [gauged] by the righteousness of [its] intention.
The correctness of action [and behaviour] beautifies a person.
The two qualities without which Allah, the Glorified, does not accept any deeds are: piety and sincerity.
Seeking lofty stations and ranks without any action is folly.
You must undertake righteous actions for indeed it is the provision that leads to Paradise.
You must persevere in your actions in times of activeness and laziness.
You must perform virtuous actions and hasten towards them, and let not others become more worthy of them than you.
I am amazed at the one who knows that there is reward for [good] deeds, how can he not make his actions righteous?!
The action of an ignorant person is a curse and his knowledge is misguidance.
In working for the permanent abode there is attainment of prosperity.
The merit of an action is the sincerity in it.
Everyone reaps what he sows and is rewarded for what he does.
Every person will face that which he did and is rewarded for that which he performs.
It is enough of a righteous act to have a good habit.
Whenever you perform an action with sincerity, you attain something you hope for in the Hereafter.
As you deal with others, so too will you be dealt with.
For every action there is a reward, so let your actions be for that which remains and leave aside that which perishes.
Let your most reliable provisions be [your] righteous actions.
Action will never become pure until knowledge becomes sound.
Action will never be pure unless it is accompanied by knowledge.
One who works [for the Hereafter] yearns [for it].
One who works increases in strength.
One who falls short in his action increases his lassitude.
One who works for the Hereafter attains success through the right [course].
One who does as he wishes meets that which displeases him.
One who is slowed down by his action cannot be quickened by his lineage.
One whose action is sincere will not be deprived of what he hopes for.
One who acts in obedience to Allah, he is well pleased with [by Allah].
Whoever makes his actions good, attains his hopes.
One who is sincere in his action his reward will be pure.
One whose action is action, his requital will be good.
Whoever acts upon the commandments of Allah, obtains reward.
One who acts in obedience to Allah gains [prosperity].
One who makes his actions good demonstrates the abundance of his intellect.
One who is heedless of acting in obedience to Allah has wronged himself.
One who is not pleased with his action, is forced to perform even better.
One whose action is good attains from Allah what he hopes for.
One whose action is free from sin attains his hope from the Hereafter.
One who is incapable of performing his actions falls behind in his circumstances [and does not make progress].
Whoever falls short in [his] action, Allah, the Glorified, afflicts him with distress; and Allah has no need for one who spares nothing of himself or his wealth [for attaining His pleasure].
From the perfection of [an] action is the sincerity in it.
From the best actions is that which leads to Paradise and saves from hellfire.
He who makes his actions evil has not done well.
How truthful the human being is with his [own] soul and what better evidence [is there] of his nature is than his [own] action.

That which you beget is for the dust, that which you build is for destruction, that which you amass is to perish, that which you do is recorded in a book [of deeds] and stored for the Day of Accounting.
The basis of an action [and its acceptance] is the sincerity in it.
What a good provision [for the Hereafter] good action is!
How good a preparation working for the Hereafter is!
He who works for the Eternal Abode attains his aspiration.
Never do that which would tarnish you with disgrace.
Do not do that which will lower your dignity and your reputation.
Do not shoot an arrow that you are unable to turn back.
Never undo a knot that you are unable to firmly retie.
There is no trade like good deeds.
There is no provision more beneficial than righteous deeds.
There is no good in action without knowledge.
There is no good in action except with knowledge.
There is no reward for one who has no [good] deeds.
Righteous action is not complete except with righteous intention.
Action with God-wariness is never little, and how can something that is accepted [by Allah] be [considered] little!
A person cannot dispense with his need for righteous deeds until the time when his soul leaves his body.
Nobody abandons acting upon [his] knowledge except the one who is doubtful of its reward.
Nobody acts upon [his] knowledge except the one who is certain about the greatness of its reward.
Nobody can ever dispense with his need for increasing his good deeds.
There is no good in an act except with certitude and piety.
The deeds of a person ought to be better than his words and his words should not be better than his actions.
A person is tested by his actions, not by his words.
It is shameful for a person’s deeds to fall short of his knowledge and for his actions to be incapable of matching his words.
The one who abandons [a good] action has no certainty about its reward.
One who sows something, reaps it.
The tongue of action is truer than the tongue of speech.
The one who acts with ignorance is like one who is travelling on the wrong path, so his effort in moving forward adds nothing for him but distance from his goal.
The person who gains the most felicity from [that which is] good is the one who acts upon it.
The one who acts with knowledge is like one who travels on the clear path.
One who acts upon religion for worldly gain, his recompense from Allah is [nothing but] hellfire.
Verily you are more in need of honourable deeds than you are of eloquent words.
Make your weighing scales heavy with righteous acts.
The best of deeds is that which people compel themselves to do.
The worst act is that by which you spoil your Hereafter.
The loftiest of actions is making [your] faith sincere and [having] true piety and certitude.
Verily the certitude of a believer is seen in his action, and the doubt of a hypocrite is seen in his action.
Working for the Hereafter with desire for this world has no benefit.
Actions are [carried out] through know-how.
Deeds are the fruits of intentions.
Do not make any dealings with one from whom you have no power to demand justice.

The blindest of people is one who is blind to our love and our excellence, and one who has hatred for us without any wrongdoing on our part towards him, except that we invited him to the truth while others invited him to temptation and [the pleasures of] this world, so they preferred it and displayed hatred towards us.
Sometimes the blind one arrives at his goal.
One who is blind to that which is in front of him instils doubt within himself.
Pleasing the obstinate one is a goal that cannot be attained.
ne whose lineage is wicked, his presence [in any gathering] is bad.
One whose lineage is honourable, his presence is good.
Good manners are from the [signs of] honourable descent.
The height of folly is violence.
Whoever acts violently, his goal becomes difficult [to achieve].
One who acts violently, regrets.
One who perpetrates violence, regrets.

topic: That which is of no concern-
text: Your getting involved in that which is of no concern to you is misguided ignorance.

topic: That which is of no concern-
text: Do not busy yourself with that which is of no concern to you, and do not take upon yourself more than what is enough for you, and exert all your efforts for that which will save you.

topic: That which is of no concern-
text: Leave aside that which does not concern you and busy yourself with the important work that will save you [in the Hereafter].

topic: That which is of no concern-
text: Blessed is the one who reduces his effort in that which does not concern him and exerts all his efforts for that which will save him.

topic: That which is of no concern-
text: One who discards that which is of concern to him falls into that which does not concern him.

topic: That which is of no concern-
text: One who prolongs his talk about that which he ought not to [speak of] has indeed made himself liable to dispraise.

topic: That which is of no concern-
text: The greatest inconvenience is troubling yourself with that which does not concern you.

topic: That which is of no concern-
text: One who occupies himself with that which does not concern him loses that which is important to him.

topic: That which is of no concern-
text: Whoever occupies himself with that which is unnecessary, it causes him to lose [what is more to] his benefit.
At times the crooked may become straight.
The best worship is overcoming [a bad] habit.
Habit is second nature.
Habit is an enslaving enemy.
The bane of training [of the self] is the overpowering habit.
Through overpowering [evil] habits, there is attainment of lofty stations.
Superfluity [in speech] is one of the worst habits.1
Change your habits and acts of worship will become easier for you [to perform].
One who submits to his [evil] habits does not attain lofty stations.
Habit has authority over every human being.
Whoever makes jesting his habit, his seriousness is not known.
Blessed is the one who remembers the [Day of] Resurrection and thus increases his provisions.
Blessed is the one who remembers the Resurrection and thus does good [deeds].
You must work hard and struggle to improve your Hereafter.
The Hour [of reckoning] has shown its face and the sign [of its coming] is evident for the one who recognizes it.
The Hour has drawn near with its quakes and it has settled down with its chest on the ground.
They have risen from the resting place in their graves and gone towards the site of reckoning, and evidence has been brought against them.
One who improves his Hereafter attains success through the right [course].
One who is certain about the Hereafter increases his provisions [for it].
The goodness of the Hereafter is [attained] through good deeds.
When the horrors of the Day of Reckoning will be witnessed, there will be many who will show extreme regret.
Being occupied with improving your Hereafter will save you from the chastisement of hellfire.
Separating yourself from the masses is from the best magnanimity.
Assist and you will be assisted.
Assist your bother in gaining his guidance.
Just as you assist [others], you are assisted.
Do not assist a strong person over a weak one.
One who assists [a disbeliever] against a Muslim has indeed exited from the fold of Islam.
One who seeks assistance from the weak demonstrates his [own] weakness.
Whoever seeks assistance from one who is not independent has wasted his affair.
Whoever seeks the assistance of his enemy in order to fulfil his need, increases his distance from it [instead of getting it].
One who seeks assistance from Allah is assisted by Him.
Seek assistance from your Lord, and ask Him to grant you success and the abandonment of every shortcoming (or disgraceful act) that drives you into doubt or surrenders you to misguidance.
One who seeks assistance from the people of intellect traverses the path of right guidance.
Succour descends from Allah to the extent of one’s requirement.
To the extent of the need, there is succour from Allah.
Whoever turns his request to you [and seeks his need from you], assisting him becomes incumbent upon you.
Being loyal to the treacherous is treachery in the sight of Allah, the Glorified.
Loyalty is the twin of trustworthiness and the adornment of brotherhood.
Loyalty means preserving the rights [of others] and magnanimity means caring for one’s close relatives.
Verily loyalty is the twin of truthfulness and I do not know of a shield that is more protective than it.
Loyalty is nobility.
Loyalty is the twin of truthfulness.
Loyalty is the trait of the honourable.
Loyalty is the symbol of abundant religiosity and strong trustworthiness.

If something happens between you and your enemy, which leads you to a truce and the enacting of a peace treaty, then preserve your pact with loyalty and guard your pledge with trust, and make your soul a shield between you and that which you have pledged.
The bane of covenants is lack of care [in fulfilling them].
The bane of loyalty is treachery.
When you make a promise, keep it.
When you make an agreement, fulfil it.
By their faithful loyalty, the virtuous ones are known.
The distinction of creatures is [by their] loyalty.
Guard your promise with loyalty and your reward will be good.
The abode of loyalty is never without the [presence of the] honourable, and is never occupied by the wicked.
The cause of intimacy is loyalty.
Keeping promises is the practice of the honourable ones.
You must espouse loyalty, for it is the most protective shield.
Loyalty is the ornament of the intellect and the symbol of nobility.
The most honourable characteristic is loyalty.
Loyalty is honour, friendship is compassion.
Loyalty is a symbol of purity.
Loyalty is the fortress of eminence.
A promise is an ailment and its cure is its fulfilment.

I have never slept with a promise I made to someone that had remained unfulfilled, thereby causing him to toss and turn restlessly in his bed so that he could successfully get what he needs [from me in the morning] but that my restlessness on my bed was much greater as a result of my desperation to meet him and fulfil the debt of his promise and out of fear of a hindrance that could cause its reneging, for indeed reneging on a promise is not from the characteristics of the honourable.
The basis of a promise is its fulfilment.
How good a characteristic loyalty is!
How good a companion of truthfulness loyalty is, and how good an associate of God-wariness piety is!
How good a companion of trustworthiness loyalty is!
The promise of an honourable person is immediate and swift.
The promise of a wicked person is delayed and full of excuses.
Do not promise that which you are incapable of fulfilling.
Do not guarantee that which you are incapable of fulfilling.
Never make a promise that you are not confident you will be able to keep.
He who breaks his promises is not loyal in his covenants.
Be a keeper of promises and a fulfiller of vows.
One who fulfils his promise demonstrates his nobility.
One who safeguards his covenant is considered loyal.
One who is unwaveringly loyal deserves to be chosen [as a friend].
The promise [that is made] is one of the two bondages.
Fulfilling the promise [one makes] is one of the two emancipations.
A polite refusal is better than a protracted promise.
Fulfilling promises is from the signs of distinction.
Sincere friendship and fulfilling promises are from loyalty to [one’s] pledge.
Be steadfast [and loyal] in fulfilling your pledges.
Never trust the promise of the one who has no religion.
One who has no loyalty cannot keep a promise.
The promise of one who has no intellect is not relied upon.
You will never abide by the covenant of the book until you know the one who has cast it away.

Never let the hardship that you undergo in [fulfilling] the covenant of Allah lead you to break it, for indeed your patience during the hardship from which you seek relief and a favourable outcome are better for you than the excuse [and betrayal] whose evil consequences you fear and because of which you are encompassed by chastisement from Allah.
The most honourable of endeavours is being careful of [fulfilling] one’s pledges (and the best trait is keeping ties with near relatives).
Verily fulfilling promises is part of faith.

Indeed promises are [like] metal collars around the necks [of people] until the Day of Resurrection, so whoever fulfils them is delivered by Allah, and whoever breaks them is forsaken by Allah, and whoever takes them lightly, they will take their plea to the One who has enjoined them and has ordered His creation to fulfil them.
Do not renege on your covenant and do not break your pledge; and do not double-cross your enemy, for Allah has made his covenant and his pact a safety for him.
One of the most honourable of traits is safeguarding [and fulfilling] your pledges.
One of the most honourable of traits is being faithful to your pledges.
He who does not observe his promises and agreements has no conviction in Allah.
One who enters upon the springs of loyalty is quenched by the drink of purity.
People are safe from the betrayal of one in whose heart resides loyalty.
One of the signs of faith is fulfilling promises.
Keeping promises is from the perfection of [one’s] magnanimity.
From the best [teachings] of Islam is the fulfilling of pledges.
How good is loyalty and how evil is treachery!
He who delays in fulfilling a promise has not kept it.
Fulfilling [one’s] pledges is the adornment of honour.
One who breaks his pledge earns dispraise.
For every pledge that is broken there is uncertainty.
The greatest flaw is that you fault others for what is [also] in you.
The most incompetent of all people is one who is able to remove a flaw in himself but does not do so.

Verily everyone has faults, so do not expose that which is hidden from you, for indeed Allah, the Glorified, has hidden them out of clemency; and hide the faults [of others] as much as possible, [and in return] Allah, the Glorified, will hide that which you would like to remain hidden.
The inner hearts will soon become aware of the secret faults.
Scrutinizing the faults of others is a fault [in itself].
I am surprised at the one about whom it is said: ‘Indeed in him there is evil,’ and he knows it is in him, how can he be annoyed?
I am amazed at the one who is described with a good trait that he knows is not in him, how can he be pleased?
Those with faults love to spread the faults of people so that they get a greater excuse for their own faults.
I am amazed at one who disapproves of the faults of people while he has more faults himself and does not see them.
The eyes of the lover are blind to the faults of his beloved, and his ears are deaf to the ugliness of his evils.
Covering up the faults [of others] is generosity and virtue.
A person’s own faults are enough to keep him occupied from the faults of other people.
Let what one knows of his own faults hold him back from [disclosing] what he knows of the faults of others.
Let that which you know of your own faults prevent you from mentioning the faults of others.
Let the most preferred people in your eyes be the ones who guide you to your faults and help you to reform yourself.
Let the most beloved of all people to you be one who guides you to the right and discloses your faults to you.
Not every fault is manifested.
If the deficient person came to know of his own deficiency, he would be greatly disturbed by what he learnt of his faults.
One who seeks a fault [in others] will find it.
One who shows you your fault has indeed counselled you.
One who knows what [flaw] is in himself hides the faults of his brother.
One who informs you of your faults is indeed your friend.
One who hides your faults [from you] is indeed your enemy.
One who discloses your faults to you guards you in your absence.
One who flatters you for your fault, criticizes you in your absence.
One who sees his own faults does not fault anyone.
One who is looking for the faults of people should start with himself.
Whoever disapproves of the faults of people but accepts them in himself, then that is a fool.
One who belittles others for that which he himself does, then that is an imbecile.
One of the greatest faults of a person is for his flaws to be hidden to him.

Nothing prevents any of you from meeting his brother who has a fault which he hates [and advising him to reform] except the fear that he too may meet you with a similar fault; indeed you have joined together in the love of this transitory [life] and have rejected the Hereafter.
He who mentions your faults has not guarded you in your absence.
He who points you to your faults and guards [your honour in] your absence has spared no efforts in advising you.
A person’s cognizance of his own faults is the most beneficial knowledge.
Never pursue the faults of people, for indeed if you think about it, you have of your own faults that which will keep you occupied from finding faults in others.
Do not fault others for that which you do yourself, and do not punish (or rebuke) others for the sin that you permit yourself [to indulge in].
Pursuing the faults [of others] is from the gravest evils.
Pursuing the faults [of others] is from the most detestable of faults and worst evils.
Whoever exposes his brother’s veil [and reveals his flaws], the faults of his own household (or family) get exposed.
One who pursues the faults of people, Allah exposes his own faults.
One who seeks to learn about the secrets of his neighbour, his [own] curtains [of secrets] are torn apart.
Whoever searches for the secrets of others, Allah uncovers his own secrets.
Whoever pursues the hidden flaws [of others], Allah makes the affection of the hearts forbidden to him.
Hide the flaw of your brother because of what you know is in yourself.
Hide the flaws [of others] as much as you can and Allah, the Glorified, will hide for you that which you would like to remain hidden.
The most hated of all people is the fault-finder.
Whoever taunts others for something is himself affected by it.
The most pleasant life is [a life of] contentment.
The person with the worst lifestyle of all people is the jealous one.
The most felicitous lifestyle is achieved by abandoning unnecessary constraints [and formalities].
Of all the people, the person who has the best lifestyle is one in whose grace other people live.
The person with the most blessed lifestyle is one who has been granted contentment by Allah, the Glorified, and who has been given a good wife.
Verily the person who has the happiest life of all people is one who is satisfied with what Allah has apportioned for him.
Verily the person with the best lifestyle is one through whose life the lives of others are improved.
Death is preferable to abasement.
Death is preferable to succumbing to disgrace (or giving up freedom).
Having less is preferable to humiliation.
Management [and planning] makes life good.
The mainstay of life is good estimation and its basis is good management.
One who lives, dies.
One who lives [a long life], loses his loved ones.
Early death is better than a wretched life.
Life has sweetness and bitterness.
The bane of livelihood is mismanagement.
Three things don’t let their possessor enjoy a happy life: malice, jealousy and bad character.
The beauty of life is [in] contentment.
One who stays in the company of his enemy does not enjoy a happy life.
Good estimation with sufficiency is better than striving in extravagance.
Preferring comfort [over hard work] cuts off the means of profit [and benefit].
Lowering the gaze is a sign of magnanimity.
Lowering the gaze is better than staring.
Lowering the gaze is one of the best [acts of] piety.
Lowering the gaze is from perfect gracefulness.
One who lowers his gaze relieves his heart.
One who lowers his gaze, his regret reduces and he is saved from harm.
How good an act of piety lowering the gaze is!
How good a curtailer of lustful desires lowering the gaze is!
There is no magnanimity like lowering the gaze.
One who does not feign negligence and lower his gaze in many situations, his life becomes bitter.
One who frees his gaze occasions (or brings about) his [own] destruction.
The eye is the scout of the heart (or of temptations).
The eye is the emissary of the heart.
Eyes are the informers of the heart.
Eyes are the hunting traps of Satan.
When the eye sees what is [lustfully] desired, the heart becomes blind to the consequence.
Blessed is the eye that forsakes its sleep in obedience [and worship] to Allah.
The day has dawned for those with two eyes.1
Bear annoyances patiently [in life] otherwise you will never be pleased.
The glance is the scout of temptations.
There is no part of the body that is less thankful than the eye, so do not give it what it seeks thereby letting it occupy you from the remembrance of Allah.
Seeing something [yourself] is not the same as being informed about it.
There is no good in a helper who humiliates.
The worst inarticulateness is [that which is caused by] irritation.
Muteness is better than inarticulateness (or error).
The sign of inarticulateness is repeating oneself during a debate and increased excitement during conversation.
No declaration can be made with inarticulateness.
Inarticulateness is beleaguering.
Little with a praised outcome is better than plenty with a harmful consequence.
Enviable is the one whose certitude is strong.
Many a person is envied [by others] for something which is [actually] his affliction.
How many a person is envied for the blessing he has been given [in this world] while he is among those who will be destroyed in the Hereafter.
Deceived is the one who is occupied with the world and loses his share of the Hereafter.
Deceived is the one whose faith is corrupt.
Deceived is the one who sells a lofty Paradise for a lowly sin.
Who is more deceived than one who exchanges Allah, the Glorified, for other than Him?!
Imbecility is misguidance.
Counter imbecility with astuteness.
It is enough of imbecility for a person to look at the faults of people when the same faults are hidden to him of himself.
Imbecility is from the most detestable of traits.
Treachery by everyone is evil, but by those who have power and authority it is worse.
Treachery increases the burden [of sin] and degrades one’s status.
Beware of treachery, for indeed it is the ugliest betrayal; and verily the treacherous one is humiliated in the sight of Allah.
The worst treachery is divulging the secret [that has been entrusted to you].
Treachery is the quality of the wicked.
Treachery multiplies [one’s] sins.
Eschew treachery, for indeed it takes you away from the Qur’an.
The treachery of a man is a disgrace upon him.
Be one who acts with goodness, forbids evil and shuns the trait of treachery.
One who acts treacherously is sullied by his treachery.
He who is certain about the place of [final] return does not act treacherously.
How appropriate it is for the treacherous one to be dealt with disloyally.
There is no faith in the treacherous.
With treachery, the companionship of a friend does not last.
Treachery with the treacherous is loyalty in the sight of Allah, the Glorified.
Treachery is the worst of the two betrayals.
The person who will face the quickest retribution is the man with whom you make a contract while having the intention of being loyal to it, whereas his intention is to betray you.
Be cautious of being deceived by the delusion of a small hindrance or being made to stumble by the joy of an insignificant transitory pleasure [of this world].
The consolidation of delusion is in sleeping with ease in the presence of the enemy.
Blessed be the one who has not been killed by the lethal poisons of deception.
It is enough of a delusion for a person to trust all that his soul lures him towards.
He (‘a) said about the one whom he praised: He has not been killed by the lethal poisons of delusion and has not been covered (or overcome) by the uncertainties of matters.
He who trusts in the falsehood of delusions and yearns for the false [and short-lived] joys has not thought about the consequences of matters.
One who is deluded by respite, is tormented by death.
Delusion is suffices as ignorance.
One who is deluded by his condition, reduces his efforts.
One who is deluded by the peacefulness of the time gets distressed by the impact of calamities.
When a person persists in sinning and [still] expects to be forgiven, then he is under a delusion about Allah, the Glorified.
There is no judiciousness with heedlessness.
There is no heedlessness [and delusion] like reliance on the times.
A deluded person may [sometimes] remain unharmed.
How many a person is deluded by the good that is spoken about him.
How many a person has been deluded by what is concealed from him.
Neither is every deluded person saved, nor is every seeker needy.
ne usurped stone in a house is the guaranty of its ruin.
Anger strikes down its possessor and exposes his faults.
Anger is a kindled fire, one who suppresses it extinguishes the fire and one who lets it burn freely is the first person who will be burnt by it.
Anger arouses hidden feelings of malice.
Keep away from anger, for its beginning is madness and its end is regret.
The person who is most capable of being on the right is one who does not get angry.
The best control is control over anger.
Leave some room from your anger for your satisfaction, and when you fly off [in a rage] then calm back down.
Guard yourselves from the vehemence of anger, and prepare for it the restraint and forbearance that will help you fight against it.
Beware of anger, for it is indeed a burning fire.
The best of people is one who swallows his anger and displays forbearance despite having power [to take revenge].
A person’s most bitter enemies are his anger and his lust, so whoever controls these two, his status is elevated and he attains his goal.
Anger is the conveyance of impetuosity.
Anger evokes impetuosity.
Anger is the fire of the hearts.
Anger is an evil which will destroy [you] if you obey it.
Anger is an enemy, so do not let it control you.
Anger corrupts intellects and distances one from the right (or from reward).
Verily if you obey the vehemence of anger, it will lead you to the utmost destruction.
When anger comes over you, then overcome it with forbearance and dignity.
Through excessive anger, impetuosity comes about.
How evil an associate anger is! It exposes faults, brings evil closer and distances good.
Remedy your anger with silence and your lust with reason.
Repelling anger with forbearance is the fruit of knowledge.
Repel [fits of] rage with forbearance.
Yielding to anger is the cause of destruction.
Counter anger with forbearance and you will make your results praiseworthy in every matter.
The raging fire of anger leads to the embarking of destruction.
Counter anger with forbearance.
Yielding to anger leads to regret and disobedience.
One who overcomes his anger has gained victory over Satan.
Satan is victorious over the one who has been overcome by his anger.
In anger there is destruction.
Increased anger degrades its possessor and exposes his faults.
Be slow in getting angry, quick in calming down and ready to accept excuses.
The devil has no greater lasso [to ensnare human beings with] than anger and women.
One who gets angry frequently makes others weary [of him].1
One who turns his anger loose hastens his [own] death.
One who is overpowered by his anger is not safe from destruction.
One whose anger overpowers him is susceptible to its harm.
One who opposes his anger has yielded to forbearance.
Whoever submits to his anger, his ruin is hastened.
One whose anger is much, his pleasure is not known.
He who gets angry on the one whom he cannot harm, prolongs his sadness and torments himself.
Whoever is overpowered by his anger and lust, then he is in the category of beasts.
He who gets angry upon one whom he has no power over, dies with his rage.

When shall I vent my anger if I get angry, is it when I am incapable (of taking revenge) and it is said to me “it is better for you to be patient” or when I have the power to (exact revenge) and it is said to me “it is better for you to forgive”?
Let your anger never prevail over your forbearance.
Never be quick in getting angry, thereby letting it become your uncontrollable habit.
There is no etiquette with anger.
There is no relationship move vile than anger.
The glory of anger does not match the humility of seeking pardon.
Seek forgiveness and you will be provided sustenance.
The best supplication (or means of coming closer to Allah) is seeking forgiveness.
Seeking forgiveness wipes out [one’s] sins.
Seeking forgiveness is the remedy of sins.
Seeking forgiveness has the greatest recompense and the quickest reward.
Sincere repentance purges one’s sins.
If the people were to turn in repentance [to Allah] and seek forgiveness whenever they disobeyed [or sinned], they would neither be punished nor would they be destroyed.
One who has been granted [the opportunity to seek] repentance shall not be deprived of forgiveness.
One who seeks forgiveness from Allah attains absolution.
What a good means [of gaining the pleasure of Allah] seeking forgiveness is!
There is no intercessor more successful than repentance.
No one gains forgiveness except he who reciprocates evil with good.
The wakefulness of eyes is of no benefit with the negligence of hearts.
Negligence reaps delusion and brings one closer to destruction.
Be cautious of negligence, for indeed it is from the corruption of [one’s sensory] perception.
Beware of negligence and being deluded by respite, for indeed negligence corrupts deeds, and death cut off hopes.
Negligence is misguidance and heedlessness is ignorance.
Negligence is joy.1
Negligence is the most harmful enemy.
Negligence is the trait of the foolish.
Negligence is the opposite of judiciousness.
Negligence is the misguidance of souls and the symbol of misfortunes.
Continuous negligence blinds insight.
The intoxication of negligence and delusion is harder to recover from than the intoxication of wines [and alcoholic drinks].
Counter negligence with attentiveness.
I am surprised by the negligence of the intelligent ones with regards to seeking provisions and preparing for the Hereafter.
Taking repose in negligence is delusion.
Pitiable indeed is the negligent person whose entire life will be used as proof against him and whose days will lead him to wretchedness.
Listener, awaken from your negligence, reduce your hastiness, brace yourself, be on your guard and remember your grave, for indeed you must pass through it.
Negligence is enough of a misguidance.
It is enough of negligence for a person to waste his efforts in that which does not concern [or benefit] him.
It is enough of negligence for a person to squander his life in that which will not save him [in the Hereafter].
One who is negligent becomes ignorant.
I am amazed at the one who is negligent, while death is swift in seeking him.
One whose negligence is prolonged, his destruction is hastened.
One whose negligence overcomes him, his heart dies.
One who is negligent about the events of [his] days is awakened by death.
Woe be to the one who is overcome by negligence so he forgets his [final] journey and does nor prepare for it.
No deed is accepted from the negligent one.
At times the [one who is] vanquished may gain victory.
He who tries to vanquish the one who is above him is overpowered.
Every victor other than Allah, is vanquished.
Do not pick a fight with one whom you cannot repel.
A person’s mistake about (or harshness towards) the one who is friendly towards him is one of the most forbidden things for him.
The worst thing that can come upon the hearts is betrayal.
The tongue of a perfidious person is sweet but his heart is bitter.
The vilest perfidy is the perfidy of the leaders.
Verily the most perfidious of all people is the one who is most deceitful to himself and most disobedient to his Lord.
Perfidy is the trait of the recalcitrant.
Rancour is the seed of evil.
Rancour is the malady of hearts.
Perfidy earns vituperation.
Rancour nullifies good deeds.
Perfidy is the worst craftiness.
Perfidy is from the characteristics of the wicked.
Deceiving a friend and being disloyal to one’s pledges are from [the acts of] betrayal of one’s covenant.
Whoever deceives the people in their faith, then he is an opponent of Allah and His Prophet.
When one deceives you out of his enmity [with you], then do not blame him or censure him.
Grief makes one dispirited and ends one’s joy.
Sorrow destroys the body.
Sorrows are the ailment of the hearts.
Grief is the distinguishing mark of the believers.
Grief wears away the body.
Sorrow and anxiety do not bring back what has been lost.
To the extent of pleasure, there is distress.
One who bears his distress [patiently] realizes [his] opportunities.
Grief is one of the two senilities.
Cast away the sorrows that come upon you through resolute patience and virtuous certitude.
Grief emaciates the body.
Grief is an ailment of the soul.
To the extent of endeavours, there are anxieties.
How many a sorrowful person has been driven to perpetual bliss by his sorrow.
One whose grief increases, his sorrow becomes permanent.
To the extent of [one’s material] acquisition, there are heartaches.
For every distress there is a relief.
One who continuously worries is overpowered by sorrow.
One whose grief increases, his body becomes sick.
One whose entire concern is for his Hereafter attains what he hopes for.
Dispense with your dependency on anyone and you will be like him.
One who is independent from people, Allah, the Glorified, enriches him.
One who becomes independent becomes an honour for his people and one who is needy becomes contemptible to them.
That which you have no need for is better than that through which you gain independence.
A rich person is he who becomes rich through contentment.
A [truly] rich person is one who prefers contentment.
The rich person feels at home [even when he is] in a strange land.
The ignorance of a rich person abases him whereas the knowledge of a poor person elevates him.
At times a rich person may be lowlier than an ugly sheep.
Sometimes a rich person may be needier than a poor person.
Few are the rich who [financially] support and assist others.
How many of the rich are unneeded [because of their unwillingness to help others].
It is obligatory upon the rich person not to withhold his wealth from the poor.
Never count the one from whose wealth others don’t get sustenance as a rich person.
There is no offence greater than the offence of the rich who deprives the needy.
Opulence through other than Allah is the greatest indigence and wretchedness.
Seek refuge with Allah from the intoxication of riches, for indeed it has an intoxication that takes long to recover from.
The richest of you are the most contented among you.
The greatest of all riches is the intellect.
The most honourable wealth is abandoning [false] aspirations.
The best of riches is that through with one’s honour is secured.
The richest of the rich is one who is not a prisoner to greed.
The greatest of riches is contentment and toleration of poverty.
Opulence brings about transgression.
Riches turn one who is not a master into a master.
Wealth and poverty manifest the essences of men and their qualities.
The brother of affluence is one who covers himself with contentment.
Arrogance in wealth sows the seed (or warns) of abasement in poverty.
The bane of affluence is stinginess.
The best affluence is the affluence of the soul.
Many an opulence leads to lasting poverty.
The alms-tax of affluence [and comfort] is being good with neighbours and keeping ties with near relatives.
Two things are such that their value is recognized only by one who has lost them: wealth and power.
Restraining oneself from that which is in the possession of [other] people is present affluence.
The deception of wealth leads to insolence.
Loss of wealth is an advantage for the sagacious and a [cause of] regret for the foolish.
The whole of affluence is in contentment and satisfaction.

One who would like to gain affluence without possessions, prestige without authority and abundance without kinsfolk, then let him them come out of the abjectness of disobedience to Allah into the honour of His obedience, for indeed [through this] he will find all of these.
He who has been granted hopelessness in [obtaining] what people possess, contentment with what he is given and satisfaction with the divine decree has acquired affluence.
Do not be delighted by wealth and comfort, and do not be grieved by poverty and tribulation, for verily gold is tested by fire and the believer is tested by tribulation.
Affluence through [complete reliance on] Allah is the greatest affluence.
One who does not become needless of this world through Allah has no religion.
There is no affluence except through contentment.
No affluence [can be acquired] with mismanagement.

topic: Coming to the aid of the aggrieved-
text: Through aiding the aggrieved, there is a protection for you from the chastisement of Allah.

topic: Coming to the aid of the aggrieved-
text: From the expiations of great sins is aiding the aggrieved.

topic: Coming to the aid of the aggrieved-
text: Coming to the aid of the aggrieved is one of the best benevolent acts.

topic: Coming to the aid of the aggrieved-
text: Nothing beings reward like aiding the aggrieved.
The one who listens to gossip is one of the two backbiters.
Beware of backbiting, for indeed it makes you hated by Allah and the people, and renders you rewards void.
The wicked of [all] people is the backbiter.
The most hated of creatures in the sight of Allah is the backbiter.
Verily the mentioning of slander is the worst falsehood.
Slander is the worst falsehood.
Backbiting is the sign of a hypocrite.
Backbiting is the effort of the feeble.
Backbiting is the food of the dogs of hell.
The one who listens to gossip is just like the backbiter.
One who listens to gossip is one of the two backbiters.
One who listens to gossip is the partner of the backbiter.
One who is fond of backbiting about others is reviled.
The one who listens to gossip is like its narrator.
Do not accustom yourself to backbiting, for indeed being accustomed to it is a great sin.
Even a little slander is calumny.

Servant of Allah, do not make haste in [exposing] the fault of a servant, for he may have been forgiven for it, and do not count yourself safe from [your] small sins as you might be punished for them.
In the unseen there is wonder.

Beware of being possessive in a situation where it is not required, for verily this will lead the soul that is sound to become sick and the one that is innocent [and calm] into suspicion [and uneasiness].
The proof of a man’s sense of honour is his chastity.
A man’s sense of honour is faith.
The possessiveness of a woman is transgression.
A man’s sense of honour is to the extent of his self-respect.
The believer’s possessiveness is for [the sake of] Allah, the Glorified. look at them or have any contact with them as this would hurt one’s sense of honour.
The thing with the worst outcome is deviation [from the right path].
Deviation is insolence.1
One who deals offensively [with others] is dealt with in the same way.
Woe be to the one who persists in his deviation and does not return to the right path.
There is no piety with deviation.
Whoever attains the utmost of what he loves, then let him expect the utmost of what he hates.
Be optimistic and you will become successful.
Unrest (or acquisition [of property]) is accompanied by hardship.
In times of unrest, be like an adolescent camel that has neither udders for milking nor a back strong enough for riding.
One who ignites the fire of sedition will become fuel for it.
One of the greatest tribulations is the continuation of strife.
I swear by my life that in the flames of unrest [that come after me], the believer will get destroyed while the non-Muslim shall remain safe.
Not everyone who is enthralled is reproached.
Chivalry is a gift that is granted and a harm that is restrained.
The human being has not been adorned with anything more beautiful than chivalry.
The order of chivalry is being tolerant of the mistakes of one’s brothers and fulfilling one’s obligation towards his neighbours.
Wickedness is a decrepit fortress, it does not prevent [any harm from reaching] its people, nor does it protect the one who seeks refuge in it.
Beware of immoral gatherings, for indeed they anger the Most Merciful and take you to the fire of hell.
Wickedness is from the traits of the disbelievers.
Verily the wicked comprise of all the oppressive and treacherous people.
The wicked is one who declares [his sins] openly.
There is no [sin for] backbiting for the [openly] corrupt.
The immoral person has no [sense of] caution.
The reign of the wicked is the [cause of] abasement of the virtuous.
Flee far away from the wicked, immoral one.
The cutting off ties with an immoral person is a gain.
There is no affluence with immorality.
It behoves one who knows the wicked not to act like them.
The one who publicizes an immoral act is like the one who has committed it.
Be careful of obscene language and lies, for indeed they degrade the speaker.
Using obscene language with one who is above you is destructive ignorance.
Using obscene language with one who is below you is abasing ignorance.

Using obscene language with one who is at your level is a pecking like the pecking of two cockerels, and a quarrelling like the quarrelling of two dogs, they will never separate until they are wounded or humiliated, and this is neither the act of the wise nor the practice of the intelligent; and it may be that he (your rival) shows forbearance towards you, thereby becoming greater than you and more honourable, while you remain lower than him and more contemptible.
One who uses obscene language is reviled.
One whose obscenity increases is regarded as vile.
An honourable person never uses obscene language, ever.
There is none more shameless than the one who utters obscenities.
Indeed obscene language and vulgarities are not from the morals of Islam.
One who uses obscene language cures [the envy of] his enviers [and brings them joy].
The one who is forbearing does not use obscene language.
Two people never insult each other except that the one who is wicked of the two prevails.
What reason has a human being to be proud when his beginning is a drop of semen and his end is a carcass; neither can he sustain himself nor can he repel his [own] death!

Never become proud of a state that you attained without [any] device [and hard work], and never be arrogant of a rank that you attained without merit, for indeed that which is built by circumstance is destroyed by entitlement.
There is no foolishness greater than arrogance.
Boasting ought to be about the greatest effort, keeping promises and being overly generous, not about the worn out bones [of one’s ancestors] and evil traits.
Boastfulness stems from the smallness of [one’s] status [and worth].
Beware of contesting with Allah, the Glorified, in His greatness, for Allah, the Most High, abases every tyrant and belittles every boaster.
The more restricting [and difficult] the hardship, the closer the relief.
The time when relief is closest is when the affair becomes unbearable.
When the openings [and ways] get blocked, the rays of relief begin to appear.
When the difficulties reach their peak, there is hope for relief.
The first act of worship is waiting for relief with patience.1
Expecting relief is one of the two comforts. justice to the oppressed believers.
How many a joyful [person] has been driven by his joy towards perpetual sorrow.
Do not be joyful about that which is coming [to you].
Never be joyful about the downfall of others for verily you do not know what time will do to you.
Do not be happy with the mistake of others, for indeed you will not always be correct.
Flee towards Allah, the Glorified, and do not flee away from Him, for indeed He will find you and you will not escape Him.
Not everything that has gone comes back.
One who takes advantage of [unexpected] opportunities remains safe from distress.
Whoever finds a place where sweet water enters and he can quench his thirst with it but does not take advantage of it, he will soon feel thirsty and seek it, but will not find it.
Many a lost thing is such that it cannot be regained.
It may be that he who strives and acts quickly is saved [and succeeds] while the slow seeker [only] hopes [to attain it in the future].
The return of an opportunity [that is lost] is far off and unlikely.
Seize the opportunity when it arises, for indeed you will not get it [again] after you lose it.
Breathe before the necks are strangled, and yield before being driven violently.
Take the respite of the days, protect the boundaries of Islam, and anticipate the sudden attack of death.
May Allah have mercy on the one who takes the benefit of respite [and opportunity], hastens towards good deeds and cowers out of fear [of Allah].
Opportunity is quick to pass on and slow to return.
The [passing of] hours diminishes lifetimes and bring [one] closer to annihilation.
Arrange an abode for yourself before your descent and prepare the dwelling before your arrival.
Make your time of comfort a [means of] preparation for the days of your tribulation.
Opportunities are things that are [meant to be] seized.
Loss [of opportunities] are [a cause of] distress.
Opportunity is a booty.
Loss [of opportunity leads to] burning regrets.
The lost [opportunity] does not return.
Losing an opportunity is distressful.
Times of happiness are short-lived.
Opportunities pass by like the passing of clouds.
When what you want does not happen, then want what happens [and be satisfied with it].
When the opportunity arises, then seize it, for indeed wasting an opportunity leads to distress.
Seize good opportunities, for indeed they pass by [quickly] like the passing of clouds.
The greatest distress is [caused by] loss of opportunities.
Verily that which has passed from your day has gone, and that which remains from it is not certain, so take advantage of your [present] time by performing [good] actions.
Verily opportunities pass away [quickly] like the clouds, so seize them when they arise in the gates of good, otherwise they will turn into regrets.
The fruit of loss [of opportunity] is regret.
For everything there is a passing away.
With loss there is regret.
There is no regret like loss [of an opportunity].
Preparation does not benefit when the time has elapsed.
What has passed of your day is lost, what is to come is uncertain; your time is a blessing, so make haste in it while you have the opportunity, and beware of relying on the future.
In loss [of opportunity] there is regret and (or) blame.
In every moment there is loss.
At times an opportunity may arise.1
You will never attain that which has been taken away from you so be moderate in your acquisition.
Not every opportunity can be realized.
One who lets an opportunity pass by is crippled by its loss.
Whoever delays taking an opportunity at the right time, then let him be sure that he will lose it.
One who seizes the opportunity is saved from distress.
Not everything that disappears comes back.
One who tarries lets [the opportunity] go.
The one who seeks nearness [to Allah] by performing the obligatory and the recommended [acts], doubles his gain.

Verily Allah, the Glorified, has made the obligatory [acts] incumbent upon you, so do not neglect them; and has delimited boundaries for you, so do not transgress them; and has forbidden you from certain things, so do not violate them; and has remained silent about certain things, though not out of forgetfulness, so do not undertake them.

Verily whoever busies himself with what is obligatory upon him instead of that which has been guaranteed for him, and is satisfied with what has been decreed for and against him; he will be the healthiest person in wellbeing, the most profiting from felicity and the most benefitting from happiness.

Verily if you were to occupy yourself with meritorious supererogatory acts instead of fulfilling the obligatory ones, then the merit you acquire will never make up for the religious obligation that you have neglected.
When recommended acts come in the way of obligatory actions, then abandon them.
It is upon you to preserve every matter that you cannot be excused for neglecting.
Fulfilling the obligatory is from the most noble of actions.
There is no worship like the performing of obligatory acts.
No closeness is achieved through recommended actions if they hamper the obligatory actions.
Do not perform a recommended act at the time of an obligatory one; start with the obligatory [prayer] and then pray whatever more you wish to.
Be wary of neglect for verily it causes censure.
Neglect is an affliction of the capable.
The fruit of neglect is censure.
Counter neglect with judiciousness [and resoluteness].
From idleness comes inclination towards [vain] desire.
With idleness there is inclination towards [vain] desire.
Beware of separation [from the people], for indeed the one who is isolated from the people is [a target] for Satan.
Beware of separation, for indeed the one who is isolated from the people of truth is [prey] for Satan just as the lonely sheep is [prey] for the wolf.
The worst endeavour is separating two close friends.
For every gathering there is separation.
Remain with the community and eschew separation.
Destroyed is the one who makes a [wrongful] claim, and unsuccessful is the one who fabricates [a lie].
One who is pleased by corruption is displeased by the Hereafter.
There is no rectitude with corruption.
One who corrupts [his relationship] with Allah will not be upright with anyone.
Do not corrupt the thing whose rectitude is important for you.
Indolence is deficiency.
Cure the ailment of lassitude in your heart through determination and the slumber of negligence in your eyes through alertness.
The shame of ignominy embitters the sweetness of pleasure.
Compel yourself to [acquire] virtues, for indeed you have a natural propensity for vices.
Ascending towards virtues is a hardship that saves.
Your knowledge conveys your merit and your generosity tells of your kindness.

When you keep away from the forbidden, refrain from that which you are unsure about, fulfil that which is obligatory and perform the acts that are recommended, then you have perfected the virtues of faith.
The peak of [all] merits is controlling anger and eradicating lustful desires.
During successive hardships the virtues of a person become manifest.
The symbol of a person’s merit is his intelligence and good character.
The highest of all merits is intelligence.
The highest of all merits is knowledge.
The merit of a man is known from his speech.
Merit is [acquired] by perfection [of character] and noble deeds, not through excessive wealth and eminent feats.
Virtue is overcoming [one’s bad] habit.
The pride of a man is by his merit, not because of his origin [and lineage].
The merit of a person is [lies in] doing good to others.
He who overcomes his anger and controls the impulses of his lustful desires has acquired virtue.
It suffices as a merit for a man to humble himself.
The perfection of virtues is [in] honourable qualities.
The human being has two merits: intellect and speech; he derives benefit through his intellect and benefits others by his speech.
Lineage is not defined by the fathers and mothers, rather [it is defined] by the praiseworthy merits.
One whose merits are few, his means are weak.
From the best of merits is accepting the excuse of the wrongdoer.
It is from the merit of a man not to put the one whom he has been forbearing with under obligation.
Performing good deeds and spreading goodness are from the greatest virtues.
Through the gaining of merits the enemy is subdued.
The consolidation of merits is in doing good to the freeman and being kind to the people of virtue.
Safeguarding the tongue and doing good to others are from the best merits of a human being.
Become distinguished by virtues and renounce vices.
The best of virtues is granting the wishes and fulfilling the needs of the seeker and being moderate in what one seeks.
The best of virtues is establishing ties with the one who has distanced himself, being cordial with the one who is averse, and holding the hand of the one who stumbles.
Verily only the virtuous know the merit of the people of virtue.
Your virtue is proven by your action and your munificence by your open-handedness.
The worst thing which a person occupies his time with is the superfluous.
The wastage of intellects is in seeking the superfluous.
Whoever restrains himself from the superfluous, his view is harmonized by the intellects.
Whoever occupies himself with the superfluous, the important matter that he hopes for eludes him.
Astuteness is [gained] through discernment.
Astuteness is [a means of attaining] guidance.
Loss is [a cause of] sorrows.
Poverty is beneficial for the believer, and gives him comfort from the jealousy of the neighbours, the flattery of the brothers and the domination of the ruler.
Verily poverty is disgracer for the soul, a confounder of the intellect, and a bringer of sorrows.
Poverty causes forgetfulness.
Poverty is the adornment of faith.
The grave is better than poverty.1
Poverty with debt is [like] a red death.2
Poverty disables the astute one from [presenting] his argument.
Poverty in one’s homeland is like being a stranger in it.
Extreme poverty is better than disgraceful affluence.
True poverty and wealth are [determined] after presenting [the account of] one’s deeds before Allah, the Glorified.
Love of poverty earns piety.
Many a poverty turns into with lasting affluence.
The disadvantage of poverty is more praiseworthy than the arrogant insolence of wealth.
Poverty of the soul is the worst poverty.
All [forms of] poverty can be redressed except the poverty of foolishness.
Whoever manifests his poverty, lowers his status.
The hardships of poverty are preferable to facing humiliation.
There is no poverty with good management.
The most apprising complaint is that which is enunciated by manifest affliction.
The little that one is in need of is better than the plenty that one is needless of.
There is no shame in being far away from one’s hometown; the only shame is being indigent in one’s one hometown.
One who pretends to be poor, becomes poor.
Displaying neediness gives rise to poverty.
Poverty with debt is the greatest wretchedness.
The pauper who is satisfied is saved from the traps of Satan, whereas the rich person falls into his snares.
The most hated of servants in the sight of Allah are: the pauper who is haughty, the elderly fornicator and the immoral scholar.
The most foolish of people is the arrogant pauper.
The richest people in the Hereafter are the poorest of them in this world.
The poor person is [like] a stranger (or is scorned) in his hometown.
The needy person is a stranger in his own homeland.
One who sits in the company of the poor increases in [his] gratitude.
Many a poor person is wealthier than all the rich people.
The wealth of a poor person is his contentment.
How many a poor person is needed by someone else.
How many a poor person is rich and [how many] a rich person is needy.
One who is overcome by poverty should frequently recite: There is no might and no power but by [the will of] Allah, the Most High, the Most Mighty.
It is obligatory on the poor that he should not put forward his request [to others] unless he has no other choice.
The kings of this world and the Hereafter are the poor who are satisfied [with what they have].
The poorest of people is one who is stingy with himself despite [his] wealth and affluence, and leaves it behind for others [in the end].
