Many a poor person is mightier than a lion.
The true scholar is one who neither makes people lose hope in the mercy of Allah nor cause them to despair of the comfort of Allah.
The bane of scholars is not safeguarding themselves [from error].
When the elevated one becomes learned, he shows humility.
When the vile one becomes a scholar, he considers himself to be above [others].
When you [wish to] learn, then become learned in the religion of Allah.
Think and you will perceive.
The root of wisdom is reflection, and its fruit is wellbeing.
The root of safety from error is thinking before acting, and reflecting before speaking.

Verily the one who observes with his heart and acts with foresight begins his action by first looking at [the consequence of] his action, is it his favour or against him; if it is in his favour then he goes ahead with it and if it is against him then he holds back from [doing] it.
Thinking guides, truth saves.
Contemplation is worship.
Contemplation is [a means to] right guidance, heedlessness is [a cause of] loss.
Contemplation illuminates the mind.
The benefit of thinking is finding solutions.
Thinking guides [one] towards the way of right guidance.
Thinking is the recreation of the God-fearing.
Contemplation leads to gaining wisdom.
Thought is a gleaming mirror.
Thinking is the polish of the minds.
Thinking about the bounties of Allah is the best worship.
Thinking outside [the bounds of] wisdom is folly.
Thinking about good [action] invites one to act upon it.
Thinking about the consequences saves one from places of destruction.
When you precede all your actions with thought [and deliberation], your outcomes will be good in all matters.
By thinking, deliberation is improved.
By repeated thinking [and contemplation], doubt is dispelled.
Through contemplation the darkness [and ambiguity] of matters get clarified.
By repeated thinking the outcomes become sound.
By considering the consequences, one is saved from harm.
Distinguishing the everlasting from the perishing is from the noblest discernment.
Think before you decide, consult before you proceed and ponder before you rush forward.
Your thinking leads to your gaining insight, and acquiring lessons [from the past].
The fruit of reflection is wellbeing.
Continuous reflection and caution protects from error and saves from the vicissitudes of time.
May Allah have mercy on the person who reflects and then takes lesson, and who takes lesson and hence perceives [the reality of things].
The cornerstone of insight is contemplation.
Deliberate before acting and you will be saved from error.
Deliberate before [taking] action [and] you will not be criticized for what you do.
The deliberation of the slow is better than the impulsiveness of the hasty.
Lengthy contemplation makes the end results praiseworthy and prevents the corruption of matters.
Lengthy contemplation improves the outcomes of planning.
Lengthy consideration equals [benefitting from] the opinion of the advisor.
You must reflect, as this is [means of] a guidance from error and a rectifier of deeds.
The thought of an intelligent person is guidance.
The thought of an ignorant person is misguidance.
Thinking for a short while is better than prolonged worship.
Your contemplation guides you to the right path and motivates you to improve your Hereafter.
A man’s thinking is a mirror that shows him his good actions from his bad ones.
The merit of thinking and understanding is more beneficial than the merit of revision and study.
Your thinking about worship prompts you to act upon it.
Your thinking about sin drives you to fall into it.
So think, O people, and observe; take lesson and seek advice, and acquire provisions for the Hereafter, [for by this] you will attain felicity.
Measure and then cut, think and then speak, verify and then act.
How can the thought of one who is always sated be pure?
Contemplation is sufficient for right guidance.
Not everyone who shoots hits the target.
One who ponders [about the past] learns a lesson [from it].
One whose thinking is prolonged, his observation becomes good.
One whose thinking increases, his end result becomes good.
One whose thought is prolonged, his discernment becomes good.
One who puts his mind to work arrives at the correct answer.
One who thinks before acting, his accuracy increases.
One whose thinking is weak, his inattention [and gullibility] is strong.
One who reflects on the essence of Allah apostatizes.
One who thinks about the consequences is saved from [places of] destruction.
One who thinks a lot about sins is pulled towards [committing] them.
One who thinks a lot about [worldly] pleasures is overpowered by them.
One who reflects, perceives the outcomes.
One who keeps his mind’s eye awake reaches the height of his endeavour.
One who reflects on the majesty of Allah loses hope.
One who thinks and reflects learns a lesson from everything.
He who excels in thinking never gets humiliated.
There is no worship like contemplation.
There is no [means to] right guidance like reflection.
One who does not take lessons [from the past] does not reflect.
Thinking about the consequences [of one’s action] saves one from unpleasant calamities.
Thinking is one of the two means of guidance.
Thinking about the kingdom of the heavens and earth is the worship of the sincere ones.
Thinking about a matter before undertaking it saves one from error.
Thinking leads to taking lesson, saves one from missteps and bears the fruit of precaution.
Reflect and you will awaken [and become alert].
Contemplation guides [one] to the right path.
One who is pleased by that which harms him will not be successful.
The successful one is he who [either] spreads his wings1 or remains peaceful and enjoys ease.
Whoever leaves his matter to Allah, He resolves it (for him).
Understanding is [achieved] though intelligence.
Understanding is a sign of knowledge.
One who tries to understand, understands.
One who tries to understand increases [his understanding].
One who understands learns the depth of knowledge.
One who is not granted understanding by Allah, the Glorified, does not benefit from the advice of any adviser.
One who possesses understanding does not become needy.
Stay near (or pass by) the graves and you will learn a lesson.
How excellent a son-in-law the grave is!1 in the time of Islam, this expression was used in a general sense to remind people that they will eventually die and be lowered into their graves.
One who faces [and anticipates] issues [with thought and reflection], perceives.
Verily if you turn towards Allah you have progressed, and if you turn away from Him, you have regressed.
By turning towards [Allah] misfortunes are warded off.
Making a good choice, doing good to the freemen and taking adequate precaution [or support] are from the signs of turning [to Allah].
For every advance [and progress] there is a retreat [and a regress].
One of the signs of turning [towards Allah] is doing good to the people.
From the signs of turning [to Allah] are: correctness of speech and kindness in actions.

topic: Martyrdom in the way of Allah-
text: Verily the most honourable of deaths is martyrdom. By He in whose hand my soul is, one thousand strikes with the sword are indeed easier [for me] than dying on the bed.
One who plunges into the depths of the sea, drowns.
Dominating the weak and the slave are from the exigencies (or wickedness) of power.
Power manifests the praiseworthy and blameworthy qualities [of an individual].
The bane of power is withholding favour.
The bane of might is aggression and defiance.
Power makes one forget [about] self-preservation.
When power increases, desire decreases.
When [one’s] capability is reduced, the offering of excuses increases.
The alms-tax of power is even-handedness.
One of the best actions of the powerful person is for him to show forbearance when he is angry.
One who does not know his worth, transgresses his limits.
One who remains within his rank [and does not overstep his limits] is honoured by the people.
One who oversteps his limits is humiliated by the people.
One who is ignorant about the place where he steps is made to stumble by the reasons of his regret.
One who limits himself to his [rightful] status, it will be more lasting for him.
One who is ignorant of his own worth does not know anyone’s worth.
One who knows his worth is not disparaged among the people.
He who knows his worth does not get ruined.
He who oversteps his limits has not used his intellect.
How good it is for a servant to know his status and not to overstep his limits!
Ruined is the one who does not know his status.
Do not do that which will degrade your status.
There is no ignorance greater than transgressing [beyond] one’s status.
One who transgresses his limits and his status has no intelligence.
May Allah have mercy on the one who knows his status and does not overstep his limits.
Do not rush to [occupy] the highest place in a gathering, for indeed the position that you are raised to is better than the position that you are lowered from.
Do not undertake that which you are afraid of being incapable of.
Do not close a door which you are unable to open.
When you are high, do not think of the one who is below you from the ignorant ones, rather follow [the example of] those who are above you from among the scholars.
When you are unable to understand something with your intellect then follow the opinion of the intelligent one and he will remove your ignorance about it.
The Qur’an is the better of the two forms of guidance.
Excel in your recitation of the Qur’an, for it is indeed the most beneficial (or the best) of stories, and seek cure from it, for it is the cure for [what is in] the breasts.
Follow the light that is not put out and the face that does not become old, and surrender and submit to its command, for indeed you will not go astray with submission [to it].
The best reminder is the Qur’an, through it the breasts are expanded and the souls are illuminated.

Verily the outer aspect of the Qur’an is elegant and its inner aspect is profound [in meaning]; its marvels do not end, its wonders do not cease, and the darkness [of ignorance and misguidance] is not removed except through it.
Verily this Qur’an is the adviser that does not deceive, the guide that does not lead astray and the speaker that does not lie.
Reflect upon the verses of the Qur’an and learn lessons from it, for indeed it is the best imparter of lessons.
Learn the Qur’an, for it is indeed the spring of the hearts and seek a cure from its light, for verily it is the cure of the hearts.
Hold fast to the rope of the Qur’an and take counsel from it, consider as permissible what it permits and forbidden what it forbids, and act on its injunctions and rulings.
The charm of the Qur’an are [in the surahs] al-Baqarah and Aāl ‘Imrān.
He (‘a) said about the Holy Qur’an: it is an intercessor whose intercession is accepted and it is a speaker whose speech is affirmed.
The outward aspect of the Qur’an is elegant and its inward aspect is profound.

You must take this Qur’an, accept what it has permitted, stay away from what it has forbidden, act on its definitive [and clear] verses and refer its unclear verses to the one who knows their meanings; for indeed it is a witness over you, and it is the best thing that you can petition with.
In the Qur’an is the information about what was before you, the news about what will come after you and the rulings regarding your present time.
The Qur’an is sufficient as a caller [towards the right path].
Let your nightly conversation partner be the Qur’an.
There is no poverty for anyone after the Qur’an nor is there any affluence for anyone before it.
One who feels at ease with the recitation of the Qur’an does not become lonely by the separation of his brothers.
One who takes the word of Allah as a guide is directed to that which is most upright.
One for whom the Qur’an intercedes on the Day of Judgment, its intercession for him is accepted, and one about whom it complains shall testify to [and affirm] it.
One who deems what the Qur’an has forbidden to be permissible does not believe in it.
None has sat in the company of this Qur’an but that he has risen with an increase or a decrease – an increase in guidance or a decrease in [spiritual] blindness.

He said about the Qur’an: It is a light for one who seeks illumination by it, a witness for one who disputes with it, a success for one who argues by it, knowledge for one who is attentive and a judgment for one who judges.
In describing the Qur’an [he said]: It is what prevents the desires from deviating towards the forbidden and the uncertainties and opinions from causing doubt.

In describing the Qur’an [he said]: It is the decisive word and not a jest. It is the articulator of the practice of justice and the enjoiner of virtue. It is the strong rope of Allah and the wise reminder. It is the trusted revelation of Allah and His strong rope. It is the spring of the hearts and the fountains of knowledge. It is the straight path. It is guidance for the one who follows it and an adornment for the one who beautifies himself with it. It is a protector [from sin] for the one who seeks protection by it and a firm rope for the one who holds on to it.
Do not seek a cure from other than the Qur’an, for indeed it is a cure for all ailments.
He said describing the Qur’an: Its marvels do not end and its wonders do not cease, and doubts do not get cleared save by it.
The people of the Qur’an are the people of Allah and His special servants.
The near one may [at times] become distanced.
Attaining nearness to Allah is [achieved] by asking [from] Him and [gaining closeness] to the people is [achieved] by refraining from asking [them for anything].
Address your complaints to one who is capable of sufficing you.
Seek nearness to Allah, the Glorified, for verily He brings closer those who seek nearness to Him.
Seek nearness to Allah, the Glorified, through prostration (sujūd), bowing (rukū’), submission to His majesty and reverence (or subservience).
Nothing brings one closer to Allah, the Glorified, except copious prostration (sujūd) and bowing (rukū’).

topic: Admission and confession of one’s sins-
text: How appropriate it is for one who knows his Lord to admit his sins.

topic: Admission and confession of one’s sins-
text: The best intercessor for a sinner is [his] admission [of guilt].

topic: Admission and confession of one’s sins-
text: There is no apology that wipes out sins more than admission [of one’s guilt].

topic: Admission and confession of one’s sins-
text: Pardon bears more fruit with admission [of one’s guilt] than it does with giving excuses.

topic: Admission and confession of one’s sins-
text: Confession is the intercessor of the wrongdoer.

topic: Admission and confession of one’s sins-
text: Admission [of one’s guilt] is [a means of] seeking pardon.
One who gives a loan to Allah is recompensed by Him.
Take benefit from the one who takes a loan from you in your time of prosperity so that you may take its repayment in your time of hardship.
One who continues knocking the door insistently [eventually] enters through it.
The most bountiful share is good health.
The most pleasant share is contentment and good health.
The wealthiest of people is one who is pleased with what Allah has allotted to him.
By the measured apportionment of Allah for the servants, the balance of this world has been established and this world has been made complete for its inhabitants.
One who trusts in the allotment of Allah does not blame Him with regards to sustenance.

Do not put the worry of your [entire] year on your day. That which is apportioned for you each day suffices for you in it. Then if you are to live another year, verily Allah, the Glorified, will bring to you what He has apportioned for you in each new day and if you will not live that long then why are you worried about that which is not for you?
Counter hard-heartedness with gentleness.
Hard-heartedness is from the greatest wretchedness.
There is no wickedness more ruthless than hard-heartedness.
Lost is the one who has a goal other than Allah.
One whose goal is evil, his place of arrival [in the Hereafter] will be bad.
Moderation makes [that which is] little grow [and increase].
Moderation makes the small grow [big].
Moderation [in one’s expenses] is half of livelihood.
The bane of moderation is stinginess.
Be moderate in [your] affairs, for whoever is moderate, the burden of his expenses is lightened.
Our way is moderation and our practice is right guidance.
You must be moderate in your affairs, for the one who deviates from moderation is unjust and one who takes to it is just.
Espouse moderation, for indeed it is the most helpful thing in attaining a fruitful life; and a person will never be destroyed until he prefers his lust over his faith.
Espouse moderation in food, for indeed it is farther from extravagance, healthier for the body and more assisting in the performance of worship.
The height of moderation is contentment.
Everything that exceeds moderation is extravagance.
One who is moderate will never be ruined.
There is no wastage in moderation.
One who does not practice moderation is ruined by extravagance.
Whoever is moderate, the burden of his expenses is lightened.
One who is moderate in [both] affluence and poverty has prepared himself for the calamities of time.
Whoever adopts moderation, it will make his prosperity last and will make up for his poverty and deficiency.
Being generous without extravagance and magnanimous without wastefulness is part of moderation.
There is no ruin with moderation.
Everything that one is contented with, suffices.
Let your riding mount be moderation and your goal be right guidance.

topic: One who is neglectful and falls short-
text: The tongue of the neglectful is short.

topic: One who is neglectful and falls short-
text: One who falls short is deficient.

topic: One who is neglectful and falls short-
text: One who is neglectful in his days of hope, before his death comes, has indeed made a loss in his life and is harmed by his death.
The sword rents asunder and the religion joins together; for religion commands good and the sword forbids evil. Allah, the Exalted, says: Indeed in retaliation there is life for you.
And retaliation [has been ordained] as a prevention of bloodshed and the execution of punishments [has been ordained] for realising the importance of prohibitions.
The most severely chastised of all people on the Day of Judgment will be the one who resents the decree of Allah.
Verily Allah, the Glorified, manages affairs in accordance with what He decrees, not according to what pleases you.

Verily Allah, the Exalted, does not give a servant more than what He has decreed for him in the Wise Reminder, even though his means [of seeking it] may be great, his craving for it intense and his stratagems for it strong; nor does the weakness of a person or the paucity of his means stand between him and what is ordained for him in the Wise Reminder. And indeed, the one who knows this and acts upon it will have the most comfort in benefit among all people, and verily the one who disregards it and doubts in it will have to face the most harm.
Divine decree works contrary to the estimations and planning [of the people].
Destiny overpowers the cautious.
Reliance on [divine] decree is more comforting.
Devine decree cannot be repelled by strength and struggle.
The impediments of divine decree are the bane of eminence.
When the destiny descends, caution becomes nullified.
When divine decree comes, the plans [of people] are nullified.
When destiny cannot be repelled, then cautiousness is futile.
Allah has set for everything a measure, and for every measure a [specified] term.
In the changes brought about by divine decree there is a lesson for the people of reason and intellect.
The verdict [of Allah] is precise and His knowledge is absolute.
Everything has a way out except [what has been decided by] divine decree.
How can one whose certitude is not true [and firm] be pleased with the divine decree?
One who seeks to overpower destiny is overcome by it.
One who is certain about destiny is not disturbed by what befalls him.
One who is pleased with what has been destined [for him] is not troubled by warning.
The tribulations of destiny overtake precaution.
The best expeller of distress is reliance on divine decree.
The descending of destiny overtakes precaution.
The descending of destiny blinds the sight.
Destiny comes to pass in accordance with divine decree, contrary to the choice and planning [of the people].
The worst of things is displeasure with the divine decree.

He (‘a) was asked about destiny so he said: It is a dark path, so do not traverse it, and it is a deep sea, so do not dive into it, and it is a secret of Allah, the Glorified, so do not trouble yourself with [trying to understand] it.
Destiny overpowers precaution.
The most abominable (or divisive) thing is the injustice of judges.
The bane of judges is greed.
The worst of judges is one whose judgments are oppressive.

And he (‘a) said about the one whom he dispraised1: He is a dim-sighted person who frequently embarks on obscurities, an ignorant person who frequently embarks on unintelligent arguments, an aggressor against his own soul and an embellisher of traversing the path of the impossible and vain trivialities for it.
One whose judgments are oppressive, his power comes to an end.
One who cuts himself off [from Allah and turns] towards other than Allah becomes wretched and faces hardship.
Many a person sits back from that which would delight him.
How great is the success of the one who follows in the footsteps of the Prophets!
It is forbidden upon every heart which is inclined to this world that God-wariness should reside in it.
Wage war against these hearts [and their desires], for indeed they are quick to stumble (or get obliterated).
Sadness of the hearts purges the sins.
When the heart is empty of God-wariness, it gets filled with the lures of this world.
Humble your heart with certitude, make it acknowledge the transience of this life, and make it see the calamities of this world.
The adornment of the hearts is sincerity of faith.
The worst of hearts is the one that doubts in its faith.
Blessed are those whose hearts are broken for the sake of Allah.
Blessed is the one who occupies his heart with reflection and his tongue with remembrance [of Allah].
Blessed is the one whose chest is void of rancour and whose heart is safe from deception.
Blessed is one in whose heart the coolness [and tranquillity] of certitude is made to enter.
Purify your hearts from the filth of evil deeds and your good deeds will be multiplied.
The strong muscles of the body and its height are of no benefit if the heart is empty.
Then listen attentively, O people, and open the ears of your hearts so that you may understand.
So his appearance is [in] the form of a human being but his heart is the heart of a beast.
The heart of a fool is in his mouth and the tongue of the intelligent one is in his heart.
The heart of a fool is behind his tongue, and the tongue of the intelligent one is behind his heart.
The pure hearts of the servants are places that Allah, the Glorified, looks upon [with His mercy]; so whoever purifies his heart, He will look upon it.
There are some evil thoughts that come into the hearts, but the intellects deter one from [acting upon] them.
Your heart must submit to Allah, the Glorified, for one whose heart submits, all the other parts of his body also submit.

Indeed there is a piece of flesh that has been placed inside this human being which is the most amazing thing in him, and that is his heart; it has sources of wisdom and things contrary to it. If hope enters it, covetousness humiliates it and if covetousness increases in it then greed destroys it. If despair takes control over it, grief kills it. If anger comes over it, its rage intensifies. If it is blessed with pleasure, it forgets precaution. If it is overcome by fear, it becomes preoccupied with caution. If peace prevails around it, it becomes neglectful. If a hardship befalls it, impatience disgraces it. If it gains wealth, affluence makes it oppressive. If it faces indigence, distress overtakes it. If hunger attacks it, weakness disables it. If its eating increases, the heaviness of his stomach pains it. Thus every curtailment is harmful to it and every excess is injurious to it.
One whose heart is dead enters the fire [of hell].
Whoever keeps knowledge about Allah in his heart has accommodated independence from the creation of Allah in it.
Deaf is the heart that does not have an attentive ear.
Nothing comes forth from a sound heart except the direct meaning.
There is no good in a heart that does not surrender, an eye that does not shed tears and knowledge that does not benefit.
Verily there are evil thoughts that come into the hearts but the intellects deters one from [acting upon] them.
Verily these hearts are receptacles, and the best of them are those that are most receptive to good.
Verily these hearts grow weary just like bodies become weary, so seek out wise sayings for them.
Verily hearts have desire and aversion, an advancing and a retreating, so approach them from whence they advance and desire, for indeed when the heart is forced [to do anything] it becomes blind.
The heart is a spring of wisdom and the ear is the place where it sinks [and enters] in.

Enliven your heart with exhortations and kill it with asceticism, strengthen it with certitude and humble it with the remembrance of death, make it see the transience of this life and show it the calamities of the world.
Indeed destitution is an affliction, and worse than destitution is sickness of the body, and worse than bodily ailment is the sickness of the heart.
Where are the hearts that have been presented to Allah and have been bound to the obedience of Allah?
The most rancorous heart is the heart of the spiteful.
The best of hearts is a heart that has been filled with understanding.
Verily the heart has an advancing and a retreating, so when it advances then make it bear the [performance of] supererogatory acts, but when it retreats then make it suffice with the obligatory acts.
The heart is the treasurer of the tongue.
The heart is the book of reflection.
The hearts are locks and their keys are inquiry.
Verily the heart of a youth is like an empty [cultivation] land, it accepts anything that is sown in it.
The hearts of men are wild, so whoever shows them affection [and tames them], they turn towards him.
Little that is continuous is better than a lot that is discontinuous.
Having less is all right, but being humiliated, never!
he least of things [required for salvation] is truthfulness and trustworthiness.
One who is less [in generosity and affection] is abased.
Prolonged qunūt and prostration saves one from the punishment of hellfire.
I am amazed at the one who loses hope while he has with him salvation in the form of repentance.
Despair kills its owner.
Every despairing one has lost hope.
The contented one is saved from the woes of covetousness.
Be content and you will gain honour.
Be content with what you are given and you will be made sufficient.
Be content with little from your worldly possessions for the safety of your religion, for indeed the believer is satisfied with the little that he gets of this world.
The wealthiest of all people is the contented one.
A slave is free as long as he is content and a freeman is a slave as long as he covets.
Contentment is the helper of poverty.1
Contentment is the most lasting honour.
The most at ease among the people is the contented one.
Contentment is the sign of the God-wary.
Contentment is the [path to the] most comfortable lifestyle.
Contentment is honour and prosperity.
Contentment is a sword that does not get blunt.
Contentment is the cornerstone of prosperity.
Contentment leads to honour.
Contentment and obedience bring about prosperity and honour.
Contentment is continence.
Contentment is a blessing.
Contentment is honour.
The contented one is rich, even if he is hungry and unclothed.
There is no contentment with avarice.
If you are content, you will gain honour.
Verily you are in greater need of being content with a little sustenance than being greedy of acquiring more.
Verily if you become contented you will gain independence [and affluence] and the burden of worldly provisions will become lighter for you.
When you are deprived, then be content [with what you have].
When you seek wealth, then seek it through contentment.
Through contentment there is honour.
The fruit of contentment is prosperity.
The fruit of contentment is being moderate in earning [one’s livelihood] and refraining from asking [others].
The fruit of contentment is honour.
The goodness of contentment stems from continence.
It is enough of contentment for you to suffice with what Allah, the Glorified, has apportioned for you.
Preserving that which is in your possession is better for you than seeking that which is in someone else’s possession.
Blessed is the one who covers himself with contentment and keeps away from extravagance.

Blessed is the one who fears the punishment [of the Hereafter], works for the Reckoning, espouses continence, is content with what suffices [him] and is pleased with [the decree of] Allah, the Glorified.
You must have contentment, for indeed there is nothing that wards off poverty more than it.
Contentment is proportionate to the degree of continence.
In contentment there is prosperity.
The one who is content has gained honour.
Contentment has been paired with prosperity.
Every contented one is continent.
Contentment is enough of a possession.
Be contented and you will become rich.
Contentment will never be attained until greed is lost.
One who is not satisfied with the little that he gets has not adorned himself with contentment.
One who is content becomes rich [and independent].
One who is content gets satiated.
One who makes himself content becomes contented.
One who is content does not get depressed.
Whoever is content, his worship becomes good.
Whoever is content, his greed becomes less.
One who is contented with the allotment of Allah becomes needless.
One who is not satisfied with what has been decreed for him faces hardship.
One who lacks contentment is not made affluent by riches.
One from whom contentment turns away is not enriched by wealth.
One who is content with the sustenance of Allah has no need for the creation.
One who is granted contentment is preserved by it.
One whose soul is contented remains dignified even in hard times.
One who is contented is spared from the humility of asking [others].
Whoever clings to contentment, his poverty disappears.
One who desires the blessings of the Hereafter is contented with the little [he has] of this world.
One who is contented with the allotment of Allah becomes needless of the people.
One who suffices with little becomes needless of plenty.
One of the most honourable morals is adorning oneself with contentment.
Remaining contented is from the noble endeavours.
How good it is for a person to be contented with little and generous with much!
The best fortune is contentment.
The best attribute is contentment.
One who has been granted contentment has acquired honour.
There is no treasure like contentment.
Contentment is the better of the two riches.
Contentment is the better of the two forms of continence.
Indeed contentment and overcoming lustful desires are from the greatest forms of abstinence.
The most helpful thing in reforming the self is contentment.
Verily in contentment there is prosperity.
Contentment enriches.
Every contented one is rich.
One whose contentment increases, his submissiveness [to the people] decreases.
One who is content gains honour and becomes independent.
None has more honour than the contented one.
Contentment is the symbol of satisfaction [with Allah’s decree].
The honour of contentment is better than the humiliation of subordination.
There is no wealth like contentment.
Acquisitions are [a cause of] sorrows.
Acquisitions are deprivation [from peace of mind].
Acquisitions bring about sadness.
Acquisitions are a spring of sorrows.
Acquisitions are the spoils of disasters.
The discarding of hardships [one endures for attaining worldly gain] is the best of acquisitions.
To the extent of [one’s] acquisitions, sorrow and grief is multiplied.
The fruit of acquisitions is sorrow.
Speech is between two bad qualities, namely: too much and too little; too much [of it] is babble and too little is inarticulateness and speechlessness.
Speaking too much makes the wise one stumble and makes the tolerant one weary, therefore do not talk so much that others get fed up and do not be so reticent that you are humiliated.
Speech is in your control as long as you have not uttered it, but once you utter it you become shackled by it.
Speech is like medicine, a little of it is beneficial but too much of it can be fatal.
Reduce [your] speech and you will be safe from blame.
Reduce your speech and you will remain safe from censure.
Beware of offensive speech for indeed it fills the hearts with spite [and hatred].
Beware of excessive speech for indeed it increases errors and brings about weariness.
Beware of excessive [and impertinent] speech, for indeed it manifests your hidden flaws and provokes your silent enemies.
Beware of speech which is offensive, for indeed it confines you to [the company of] vile people and repels the honourable ones from you.

Beware of speaking about something whose way you are unfamiliar with and whose reality you are unaware of, for indeed your speech indicates your intellect, and your expression informs about your level of understanding, so limit your long tongue to that which keeps you safe, and make your speech concise to [the extent of] what is deemed good, for indeed this is more beautiful for you and more indicative of your merit.
There is no benefit in speech without action.
The most veracious speech is that which conforms to the truth.
The best of utterances is that which is affirmed by action.
The people who most resemble the Prophets of Allah are those who speak the truth the most and are most patient in acting upon it.
The closest of servants to Allah, the Glorified, is one who speaks the truth even if it is against him and one who acts upon the truth even if there is something he dislikes in it.
It is worse than inarticulateness for one to speak more than [what] is necessary.
The most accurate shot is speech that is prudent.
The best speech is that which is adorned by good arrangement and understood by [both] the elite and the general public.
The most conveying eloquent speech is that which is easily passed on [and understood] correctly and which is appropriately concise.
The most honourable speech is the truth.
The best speech is that which is not dismissed by the ears and is not difficult for the minds to comprehend.
Verily polite speech and the propagation of peace are forms of worship.
Indeed the preference of speech over action is a shortcoming, and the preference of action over speech is indeed a beauty and an adornment.
The practice of the wicked is [using] vulgar speech.
The one who listens to obscene speech is a partner of the speaker.
Bad speech degrades one’s prestige and magnanimity.
Offensive speech degrades ones status and corrupts brotherhood.
The worst speech is that which contradicts itself.
The worst of narrations is one that has the most falsehood.
I am amazed at the one who speaks about that which neither benefits him in this world nor for which reward is written for him in the Hereafter.
Eschew speaking about that which you do not know, and making statements about that which you are not responsible for, and hold yourself back from a path when you fear its deviation.
Many an utterance is hurtful.
Many an utterance is like a [sharp] sword.
Many an utterance has taken away a blessing.
Many a syllable has brought death.
Many an utterance is more severe than an assault.
Many a strife has been instigated by a word.
Many a speech is such that the [appropriate] reply for it is silence.
Many an utterance is such that silence is better than it.
Many a war has been started because of a [single] word.
Many a word is more piercing than an arrow.
Think and then speak, [for by this] you will remain safe from error.
Speech may, at times, be harmful.
Speaking less hides [one’s] faults and decreases [one’s] sins.
Speaking less conceals shameful flaws and keeps one safe from missteps.
Reduce your speech and shorten your hopes.
How many a war has been started by a single word.
How many a word has taken away a blessing.
Too much talking makes the ear weary.
Excessive talking makes one’s brothers fed up.
Excessive speech is such that its marginal issues are expanded and its meanings are reduced, so no end is seen for it and nobody benefits from it.
For every statement there is a reply.
One who speaks less, his sins are less.
One whose speech is less, his fault is nullified.
One who speaks that which he ought not to, hears that which he does not like.
One who makes his speech prudent proves the abundance of his merit.
One whose speech is good, success is in front of him.
One whose speech is bad, his censure increases.
One whose speech is accompanied by modesty, corruption [and destruction] is removed from his action.
One who talks a lot increases his babble and one who jokes a lot increases his silliness.
One who does not make his speech appropriate (or is not able to bear [others’] speech) does not hear beautiful words.
One whose words are evil, his lot will be evil.

The place where speech is infixed is the heart, its repository is the mind, its strengthener is the intellect, its initiator is the tongue, its form is letters, its soul is [its] meaning, its adornment is [correct] syntax and its order is appositeness.
Never say anything the reply for which will hurt you.
Do not speak that which you fear others will consider a lie.
Do not speak of everything you know, for that is [itself] a sufficient ignorance.
Do not look at who has spoken, look at what he has said.
Do not say that which will make your burden [of sin] heavy.
Do not speak of that which you do not know, for indeed most of the truth lies in that which you do not know.
Do not relate to the people all that you hear, for this suffices as silliness (or foolishness).
Do not contest all that the people relate to you, for this suffices as foolishness.

Never say that which conforms to your vain desire, even if you say it playfully or assume it to be idle talk, for many a playful talk may alienate a freeman from you and [many] an idle talk may bring evil [consequences] upon you.
Never speak when you cannot find an appropriate situation to speak.
Never debate except with one who is fair and never guide anyone but the seeker of guidance.
Do not talk so much that you annoy others and do not speak so less that you fall [in the eyes of others].
Never say that which you do not do, for indeed you will never become free of the failure that attaches itself to you and the blame that you earn.
Do not say that which you do not know, for indeed Allah, the Glorified, has prescribed obligations upon all your body parts which He will use as proof against you.

Let not what people say about you dishearten you, for indeed if what they say is true then it is a sin whose punishment has been expedited and if it is not true then it is [as] a good deed that you have not performed [but has been recorded in your book of deeds].
Do not be, in that which you mention, like the one who collects firewood at night or like the froth over the flood.
Do not say that which you do not know, thereby making others suspicious of your statements about what you do know.
None is careful of evil in his actions but he who is careful of evil in his speech.
Good speech is not completed except by good action.
Words are the moulds of meanings.
The elocution of a man apprises of the strength of his heart.
Speak and you will be known, for indeed a man is concealed under his tongue.
Beautiful speech is proof of abundant intelligence.
Preservation of that which is in the vessel is [achieved] by fastening the cover.
Deliberation [and carefulness] in speech saves one from faltering and error.
Speaking the truth is better than inarticulateness and silence.

If you would like to remain safe and conceal your faults, then reduce your speech and increase your silence, [by this] your thinking will abound, your heart will become illuminated and people will remain safe from you.
I am more capable of turning away that which I haven’t spoken than I am of taking back that which I have said.
Verily you are accountable for your speech, so do not say anything except [that which is] good.
The bane of transmission is distortion of the narration.
The bane of speech is lying.
The bane of speech is prolongation.
When you speak, be truthful.
When you relate [something], be truthful.
When speech is reduced, accuracy is increased.
Be pleased with what you say if it is free from mistakes.
Reduce your speech and shorten your hopes, and do not say that which will earn you sin or will alienate a freeman from you.
Be cautious of every statement or action that will lead to the spoiling of your Hereafter and religion.
The best speech is that which is pertinent.
Be good in your speech, beautiful in your actions, for indeed the speech of a person is the evidence of his merit and his action is the symbol of his intellect.
The speech of a man is the measure of his intellect.
Your speech is recorded, forever to remain in your book of deeds, so make it about that which brings you closer [to Allah] and beware of uttering that which will destroy you.
When the intellects decrease, impertinent speech increases.
When you make your speech good, then make your action good also so that you can bring together excellent speech with virtuous benevolence.
When the speech corresponds to the intention of the speaker, the listener accepts it but when it is against his intention, it does not take up a good position in his heart.
Through moderate [and unbiased] speech loftiness is affirmed.
Whoever speaks too much, others get fed up with him.
When you are overcome by speech then be careful not to be overcome by silence.
I am amazed at the one who speaks about that which, if it is related from him, will harm him and if it is not related from him, will not benefit him.
For every situation there is an appropriate thing to say.
Speech has some banes.
Speech will never be beneficial unless it is joined with action.
One who increases [his talk] makes others weary.
One whose speech is polite, loving him becomes unavoidable.
One whose speech is excessive, his lapses increase.
Whoever reviews his speech, his mistakes reduce.
One whose speech is excessive is never free from lapses.
One who knows that he is accountable for his speech should shorten his speech.
The worst of speech is babble.
Excessive speech is annoying.
Deliberation in speech saves one from error.
The best speech is that which is neither boring [because of its length] nor too brief.
The best speech is truth.
Eschew speech about that which does not concern you, and in situations that are inappropriate, for many a word has taken away a blessing and [many] an utterance has brought about bloodshed.
Steadfastness is safety.
There is no path that is nobler than steadfastness.
There is no course more secure than steadfastness.
How can the heart of one whose faith is not steadfast be upright?
One who remains steadfast is not bereft of safety.
The command of Allah, the Glorified, is not established [and executed] except by one who neither corrupts nor beguiles, nor is he deceived by [that which he] desires.
A strong person is one who subdues his pleasures.
The bane of the strong person is underestimating the enemy.
When you [wish to] become strong, then be strong in the obedience of Allah, the Glorified.
Arrogance is an inviter towards plunging into sins.
Arrogance is a destructive trait, one who seeks to increase by it, diminishes.
Arrogance grips the hearts just like a fatal poison.
Suppress the manifestations of pride and restrain the flashes (or risings) of arrogance.
Beware of arrogance, for it is the cornerstone of tyranny and disobedience to the Most Merciful.
Beware of arrogance, for indeed it is the greatest of sins and the vilest of faults, and it is the ornament of the Devil.
Beware of behaving haughtily with the servants of Allah, for every haughty one is crushed by Allah.
The ugliest character is arrogance.
The lowliest of all people is one who considers himself to be great.
Arrogance humiliates.
Arrogance degrades the elevated.
Arrogance shows [one’s] depravity.
Arrogance is the worst of faults.
Arrogance is the same as foolishness.
Seeking honour [for oneself] through arrogance is [a cause of] humiliation.
Being arrogant about [one’s status in] this world is deficiency.
Arrogance is the basis of ruin.
Arrogance is the great trap of the Devil.
Verily, if you become arrogant, Allah will abase you.
The bane of nobility is arrogance.
Due to arrogance there is loathing.
Through increased arrogance, loss [and ruin] comes about.
The arrogance of a man abases him.
The arrogance of a lowly person invites his insult.
The fruit of arrogance is vituperation.
The worst of morals is arrogance.
The worst of all woes of the intellect is arrogance.
Counter arrogance with humility.

Fear Allah O servants of Allah; do not put on the garment of arrogance, for indeed arrogance is the greatest trap of the Devil which he grips the hearts just as fatal poisons [rush through the body and] overcome [it].
Arrogance is sufficient as a [cause of] loss [and destruction].
Arrogance is enough as an abasement.
If Allah were to make arrogance permissible to any one of His creation He would make it permissible to His Prophets, but He made it hateful for them to be arrogant and approved of their humility.
One who shows haughtiness is crushed.
From the ugliest forms of arrogance is a man’s arrogance towards his close relatives and members of his [own] tribe.
Nothing brings hatred like arrogance does.
Never turn your face away disdainfully and be courteous [to others]; and be humble in front Allah, who has elevated you.
There is no praise with arrogance.
There is no quality uglier than arrogance.
It does not behove one who knows Allah to become haughty.
The haughty oppressor is destroyed by his sins.
I am amazed at the arrogant one who was [nothing but] a drop of semen yesterday and will tomorrow be [just] a corpse.
At times the haughty one is humiliated.
Every arrogant one is low.
The arrogant one has no friend.
One who becomes arrogant is abased.
One who shows arrogance is loathed.
One who is arrogant towards the people gets humiliated.
One who is haughty with the one who is below him gets broken [and pulled down from his position].
One who is arrogant will not be devoid of loss [and injury].
Whoever shows haughtiness, Allah belittles him and abases him.
One who wears the attires of arrogance and extravagance takes off the attires of merit and honour.
None is arrogant except the vile.
The actions of a haughty person are not pure [and righteous].
No one shows arrogance but the vile, unknown one.
The book is one of the two interlocutors.

When you write something then take another look at it before putting a seal on it, for indeed [by putting a seal on it] you are only putting a seal on your intellect [as your intelligence will be gauged by your writing].
The writing of a man is the symbol of his intellect and the evidence of his merit.
The writing of a person is the gauge of his merit and the measure of his nobility.
How good an interlocutor a book is!
Writing is the interpreter of intention.
Books are the gardens of scholars.
Whoever takes solace [and delight] in [reading] books will never lack [any] solace.
Secrecy is the basis of confidential conversations.
Loquaciousness has been paired up with boredom.
One who is loquacious is abandoned.
One who talks too much makes others fed up.
One who speaks too much [makes] blunders.
One who speaks too much gets rebuked more.
One who does too much of something is known by it.
Amassing that which does not last for you and for which you will not remain is from the greatest ignorance.
Lying destroys the one who accompanies it and saves the one who eschews it.
Lying is [a cause of] disgrace in this world and [leads one to] hellfire in the Hereafter.
The most repulsive quality is dishonesty.
Lying is treachery.
Lying makes one fall [into destruction].
Lying is the enemy of truthfulness.
Dishonesty is a disgraceful flaw.
Lying is alien to [and incompatible with] faith.
Lying is disgrace and treachery (and regret).
Lying degrades a person.
Lying leads to slander.
Lying tarnishes one’s character.
Lying corrupts everything.
Lying destroys you even if you are [apparently made] safe by it.
The ugliest thing is falsehood.
Lying leads to hypocrisy.
Lying is the disgrace of the tongue.
Lying and treachery are not from the qualities of the honourable.
Lying is the deviation of speech from the divine order [of creation].
It is through lying that the hypocrites adorn themselves.
How evil a speech lying is!
The fruit of lying is disgrace in this world and chastisement in the Hereafter.
Eschew lying for indeed it alienates one from faith.
The sickness of dishonesty is the worst sickness and the lapse of the cautious one is the gravest lapse.
The consequence of lying is rebuke and regret.
Lying is the corruption of [one’s] prestige.
And [Allah has ordered the] abandoning of lying as a means of honouring the truth.
A person may lie about himself regarding that which he did not do when he is faced with severe tribulation.
Excessive lying leads to slander.
Excessive lying takes away a person’s prestige.
Excessive lying corrupts the religion and increases the [burden of] sin.
Telling lies is not from the moral teachings of Islam.
How repulsive is dishonesty by1 the people of virtue!
The spoiler of knowledge is dishonesty and the spoiler of seriousness is idle play.
Lying and magnanimity don’t go together.
There is no trait more repulsive than lying.
The most prevalent thing [among the people] is lying and treachery.
The [one who is known to be a] incessant liar is suspected in his speech, even if his proof is strong and his tone is truthful.

The incessant liar and the dead are similar, for indeed (or because) the merit of the living over the dead is the ability to rely on him, so if his words are not reliable then [it is as if] his life is nullified.
The furthest of all people from goodness is the incessant liar and the brazen-faced.
The liar is disgraced and humiliated.
A liar is at the brink of an abyss [of ruin] and disgrace.
Your knowing that you are a liar suffices as a rebuke for lying.
There is no trustworthiness in an incessant liar and there is no safeguarding [from sin] in the morally corrupt.
One who lies corrupts his magnanimity.
One who lies excessively is not believed.
One who is known for lying, [even] his truth will not be accepted.
One whose lying increases, his prestige decreases.
One who is known for lying, the trust [of others] in him decreases.
One who eschews lying, his words are accepted as true.
From the disgrace of the incessant liar is his readiness to swear [that he is truthful] for one who does not [even] ask him to swear.
The habitual liar has no shame.
There is no good in the words of liars.
There is no good in the knowledge of habitual liars.
There is neither any good in those who are habitual liars nor is there any good in dishonest scholars.
The liar earns three things by his lies: the wrath of Allah upon him, scorn of the people and hatred of the angels.
Being noble-minded means having a good character and eschewing lowly traits.
Munificence is [in] giving generously and fulfilling promises.
Nobleness is [in] preferring the pleasantness of praise over the love of wealth.
The best munificence is altruism.
The highest level of munificence is self-sacrifice.
The most excellent munificence is completing [one’s] favours.
Munificence is excellence and loyalty is nobility.
Nobleness is the source of goodness.
Munificence is the best eminence.
Munificence is the best of traits.
Nobleness is [being] free from jealousy.
Nobleness is bearing the wrongdoings [of others].
Nobleness is having good patience [and tolerance].
Munificence is bearing the [heavy] burdens of [other people’s] liabilities.
Nobleness is preferring dignity over wealth.
Nobleness is [being] more compassionate than close relatives.
Nobleness is control over one’s tongue and doing good to others.
Nobleness is the result of lofty endeavour [and high resolve].
Nobleness is nothing but refraining from [committing] sins (or misdeeds).
Munificence is nothing but granting the wishes and fulfilling the needs of the seeker.
The fruit of nobleness is keeping ties with near relatives.
The best munificence is being generous without seeking [any] recompense.
It is not from munificence to spoil the favours [one does to others] by [putting them under] obligation.
Completion of favours is part of munificence.
It is part of nobleness to have good [and praiseworthy] traits.
Completing [one’s] favours is from the perfection of munificence.
Fulfilling one’s obligations [and pacts] is part of nobleness.
Doing good to the one who wrongs you is from the best [forms of] nobleness.
One of the signs of nobleness is hastening in [giving] reward.
Part of nobleness is doing good to others and granting [them] support.
From the perfection of munificence is hastening [to give] reward.
It is from nobleness for you to overlook the wrong that has been done to you.
The order of nobleness entails successively doing good to others and assisting one’s brothers [financially].
The nobleness of a man is evinced by his cheerfulness and his kindness [to others].
The noble-minded person is one who keeps away from the forbidden and steers clear of [disgraceful] flaws.
The munificent person is one who brings [and gives away] whatever is available.
A noble-minded person is one who repays evil with good.
A noble-minded person is repulsed by that which the wicked take pride in.
The munificent one cuts off his favour when he is approached harshly and is soft [and kind] when he is entreated [politely]
When a noble-minded person is able [to take revenge] he forgives, and when he gains possession [of something] he grants generously, and when he is asked [for something] he accords [it].
A noble-minded person rejects disgrace and honours his neighbour.
A noble-minded person considers his virtuous actions as a debt that he has to repay.
The noble-minded person raises himself above [the expectation of] rewards in everything good that he does.
When a noble-minded person needs you he excuses you [from helping him] and when you need him he suffices you.
The noble-minded person forgives despite having the power [to exact revenge], is just in his rule, restrains his harm [from others] and bestows [favours] generously.
The noble-minded person is felicitous and worthy of reward in the sight of Allah, and is loved and venerated in the sight of the people.
A noble-minded person is one who safeguards his honour with his wealth while the wicked person is one safeguards his wealth by [sacrificing] his honour.
Be cautious of the noble-minded person when you offend him, and the forbearing one when you injure him, and the courageous one when you torment him.
Be cautious of the assault of the noble-minded person when he is hungry and the insolence of the wicked one when he is satiated.
Be cautious of the authority of the noble-minded person when he is humiliated and the vehemence of the wicked one when he is elevated [to a position of power].
The noble-minded person feigns inattention and pretends to be deceived.
Noble-minded people have the most patient souls.
The noble-minded person makes [his] ownership righteous.
A noble-minded person is one who initiates his act of kindness [before it is requested of him].
The noble-minded person shows gratitude for little whereas the wicked one is ungrateful for much.
The munificent person is one whose giving precedes his being asked.
When the noble-minded person promises [something], he keeps his promise and when he threatens [to punish], he forgives.
When the munificent person is well-to-do, he fulfils the needs [of others] and when he faces hard times, he lightens the burden of others [by not seeking their assistance].
When the core of a man is noble, [both] his absence and presence are [considered] noble.
The authority of a noble-minded person manifests his positive attributes.
The possessor of noble-mindedness has beautiful traits, grants favours [to others] and keeps ties with near relatives.
The success of a noble-minded person brings deliverance.
The success of noble-minded people is [through] forgiveness and benevolence.
The shadow of noble-minded people is vast and pleasant.
In times of [their] altruism, the excellence of the noble-minded people become manifest.
Generosity is the habit of the noble-minded people.
Doing good to others is the habit of noble-minded people.
Be cautious of the noble-minded person if you offend him, and of the wicked one if you honour him and of the forbearing one if you force him into a difficult position.
The merit of initiating good deeds and performing generous acts belongs to the noble-minded people.
The one who has honoured you has made you uncomfortable if you are noble-minded and the one who has offended you has made you comfortable if you are forbearing.
Indeed I am happier to [get to] know a noble-minded person than to acquire an expensive and precious jewel.
It is not the habit of noble-minded people to delay bounties.
Being hasty in taking revenge is not from the traits of noble-minded people.
Remaining alongside a noble-minded person in humiliation is better than accompanying the wicked in order to gain favour.
The pleasure of the noble-minded people is in feeding [others] whereas the pleasure of the wicked people is in eating [themselves].
One of the most honourable actions of the noble-minded person is feigning inattention towards that which he knows.
Giving generously is from the traits of the munificent.
The munificent person is never deserted.
The propensity of a noble-minded person is always towards the [positive] traits of his forefathers.
The happiness of noble-minded people is in giving generously [to others] while the joy of the wicked is in evil retribution.
A high-minded person is never spiteful.
None deserves to be called munificent except the one who gives before he is asked.
A person does not ennoble himself until he belittles his wealth.
The munificent person is one who bestows his favours generously [to others].
It is not from the traits of a noble-minded person to wear the cloak of disgrace.
The noble-minded one is bright whereas the wicked one is immature.
One who is not set aright by high esteem is put right by indignity.
One who is not reformed by high esteem is reformed by indignity.
It is a right upon one whose esteem has been increased by Allah that he should [in turn] be more respectful to the people.
One who is raised by disgrace is made vain by high esteem.
When you desire to acquire noble traits then keep away from the forbidden.

Rush towards noble deeds, make haste in bearing the liabilities [of others] and hurry to fulfil the needs of the one who is unaware [of your assistance], your reward will thus be good in both abodes, and you will acquire a great prize from Allah.
Work hard to acquire noble traits and bear the burden of [others’] liabilities, [as a result] you will achieve the greatest gains.
The best of noble traits is altruism.
End your day’s work with noble deeds and begin the night by fulfilling the needs of the one who is asleep [and unaware of your assistance].
Acquire noble traits and do good to the people, for indeed these two things protect one from falling into difficulties and lead to loftiness.
The pinnacle of noble traits is altruism.
From the best noble deeds is bearing the liabilities [and debts of others] and being hospitable to one’s guests.
One of the best noble deeds is spreading goodness [and virtue].
One of the best noble deeds is keeping away from the forbidden.
Noble traits [and deeds] are not complete except with chastity and self-sacrifice.
Noble traits are [attained] by [bearing] that which is disliked.
The disliked act which has a praiseworthy result is better than the action which one loves [but] whose outcome is dispraised.
The purest of earnings is lawful earning.
The worst kind of earning is the unlawful [earning].
Embarking on the terrifying [and surmounting one’s fears] brings wealth.
One who earns by unlawful means accumulates sins.
One who is always lazy, his hopes get dashed.
Do not rely on a lazy person in your affairs.
One who reveals his distress to others has accepted humiliation.
No action is more beloved to Allah, the Most High, than for a person to remove the distress [and adversity] from another person.
The suppressor of anger is one who extirpates his grudges.
Suppress [your] anger and you will increase in forbearance.
Suppression [of anger] is the fruit of forbearance.
The cornerstone of forbearance is suppression [of anger].
Blessed is the one who suppresses his anger and does not let it loose, and [who] disobeys the command of his [carnal] soul and thus is not destroyed by it.
How many a time is anger suppressed out of the fear of that which is more severe than it.
Whoever suppresses his anger, his forbearance becomes complete.
Suppress [your] rage when you are angry and overlook [the fault of others] despite having authority, [in this way] the outcome will be in your favour.
Doing good to an ingrate is from the greatest of crimes.
Being ungrateful for a blessing causes it to be taken away and being thankful for it causes it to last.
Ingratitude for blessings makes one stumble and strips away the blessings.
Ungratefulness for a blessing is vileness, and accompanying a fool is [a cause of] misfortune.
Being ungrateful for a blessing is the cause of its removal.
The one who is unthankful for blessings is ungrateful for the bounty of Allah.
Ingratitude for blessings is the thing that brings [divine] retribution.
The one who is ungrateful for blessings is dispraised in the sight of the Creator and the creation.
Ingratitude for blessings is not a success [rather it is a failure].
There is no blessing with ingratitude.
Verily ingratitude for blessings is vileness and accompanying the ignorant is [a cause of] misfortune.
Blessings are stripped away by ingratitude.
The bane of blessings is ingratitude.
The cause of alteration [and removal] of blessings is ingratitude.
In ungratefulness for blessings is [the cause of] its removal.
Whoever is ungrateful for blessings, [divine] retribution comes upon him.
The disbeliever is a vile deceiver, perfidious, deluded by his ignorance and duped.
For the disbeliever, this world is his Paradise, the transient is what he strives for, death is [the cause of] his wretchedness and hellfire is his final end.
The disbeliever is an immoral, ignorant person.
The disbeliever is ill-tempered and has an evil manner.
The disbeliever is a misguiding deceiver, hard-hearted, [and] perfidious.
The final end of the disbeliever is hellfire.
The disbeliever did not disbelieve until he became ignorant.
The concern of the disbeliever is for his [life in this] world, his efforts are for the transient [pleasures] and his goal is [fulfilling] his lust.
Disbelief is disappointment [and failure].1
Counter disbelief with faith.
Disbelief is loss.
Restraining yourself from that which others possess is one of the two generosities.
Verily restraint during the confusion of misguidance is better than embarking on terrors.
There is no piety like self-restraint.
Being pleased with what is sufficient is better than striving for lavishness.
Being pleased with what suffices leads to virtue.
Blessed is the one who adorns himself with virtue and is satisfied with what suffices.
One who is content with that which suffices is led by it towards virtue.
One who limits himself to what suffices hastens comfort and lives in an abode of ease.
No one can dispense with the need to seek his sustenance and that which he requires of provisions.
Extend your hand in recompense to the one who has done good to you, and if you are unable [to do this] then the very least you should do is thank him.
Recompense is liberation.
One who endeavours to recompense the good that is done to him has indeed recompensed it.
One who does not recompense offence with favour is not from the noble-minded ones.
Recompensing the wrongdoer with favour is from the perfection of faith.
The most severely punished of all people is one who recompenses good with evil.
When your hand is short and unable to recompense [the one who does good to you] then lengthen your speech with gratitude.
Return the stone from whence it came to you, for indeed evil is not repulsed except by evil.1
One whose competence is good is loved by his sovereign.
One who is raised [to a high rank] without competence is dropped without wrongdoing.
One whose competence is good deserves [to be given] authority.
One who imposes upon you a duty that you are unable to bear has indeed asked you to disobey him.
Affectation is from the morals of the hypocrites.

Verily Allah, the Glorified, commanded His servants by choice and forbade them by warning. He made duties easy and did not impose difficult duties. For a little He gave plenty. He is not disobeyed out of defeat nor is He obeyed by force. He did not send prophets for sport, nor did He reveal the Book to the creation for amusement. He did not create the Heavens and the earth in vain: That is a conjecture of the faithless. So woe to the faithless for the Fire.1
For every speaker there are times [and conditions where he is able to speak].
You have started flying while still a nestling and growling before coming of age.
The ideal [person] is one whose seriousness prevails over his jesting [and frivolity].
Perfection is in three things: Patience in calamities, piety in pursuits and fulfilling the needs of the seeker.
Perfection [of what is desired] is non-existent in this world.
You will never attain perfection until you rise above imperfection.
From the perfection of a human being and the abundance of his merit is his own feeling of imperfection [in himself].
One who is not cautious of [evil] plots before they occur, does not benefit from regret after their assault.
The foundation of a sagacious person is his intellect, his magnanimity is his character and his religion is his distinction.
The sagacious person is one whose today is better than his yesterday and [one who] keeps blame away from himself [by not doing anything blameworthy].
The sagacious person is one who enlivens his virtues and kills off his vices by subduing his lust and his vain desires.
The sagacious person is one who is inattentive towards others while expecting much from [and constantly judging] himself.
The sagacious person is one who controls the reins of his lustful desires.
The sagacious person is one who dons the garment of modesty and the armour of forbearance.
The most sagacious person of all is one who loathes this world, cuts off his hope and aspiration from it, and turns his desire and expectation away from it.
Verily the sagacious people are those who have loathing for this world and lower their eyes from its splendour; they turn their hearts away from it and yearn passionately for the everlasting abode.
Verily the sagacious person is one who restrains his lustful desire and subdues his outburst in times of anger by quelling it.
The sagacious person’s friend is truth and his enemy is falsehood.
Only he is sagacious who seeks forgiveness when he does wrong and regrets when he commits a sin.
For the sagacious person there is admonition in everything.
Sagacity is [in] fearing Allah, the Glorified, eschewing the forbidden and improving one’s Hereafter [through good deeds].
The most sagacious among you is the most pious among you.
The greatest sagacity is God-wariness.
The determination and effort of the sagacious one is for the improvement of his Hereafter and for acquiring more provisions [for it].
The sagacious person is one who shortens his hopes.
The sagacious person is one who knows himself and is sincere in his actions.
It is a sufficient sagacity for a person to recognize his own flaws.
It is a sufficient sagacity for a person to remain moderate in his goals and reasonable in his quests.
It is a sufficient sagacity for a person to overcome his vain desire and possess intelligence.
It is a sufficient sagacity for a person to discover his own flaws [instead of dwelling on the flaws of others] and be moderate in what he seeks.

topic: There is no God but Allah-
text: ‘There is no God but Allah’ is the declaration of faith, the first step towards good deeds and acquiring the pleasure of the Most Merciful, and a means of repelling Satan.
Vileness is preferring the love of wealth over the delight of praise and commendation.
Vileness is the opposite of all the virtues and the combination of all the vices, evils and lowly traits.
The greatest vileness is praising the blameworthy.
Vileness is the foundation of evil.
Vileness is the accumulator of dispraise.
Vileness necessitates deceit.
Vileness is preferring wealth over people.
Vileness is ugly so do not make it your attire.
Hastening punishment is one of the signs of vileness.
Betraying [one’s] agreements is one of the signs of vileness.
Being a bad neighbour is from the signs of vileness.
Slandering the righteous is one of the ugliest vile traits.
It is from vileness for a person to preserve his wealth and sacrifice his dignity [instead].
It is from the greatest vileness for a man to protect himself while surrendering his wife.
Being ill-natured is from vileness.
When the vile one attains a position above his status, his condition changes [for the worse].
The vile one is harsh when he is approached entreatingly and becomes soft when he is berated.
The vile person does not follow anyone except the one who is like him and he does not incline towards anyone but the one who is similar to him.
No good is expected from a vile person, and no one is safe from his evil and secure from his ills.
The vile one dons the attire of dishonour and harms the freemen.
The vile one considers his favours as debts that he will demand repayment for [in the future].
The vile one is such that when he needs you he puts you in difficulty, and when you need him he torments you.
Be cautious of the vile one when you honour him, and the depraved one when you bring him forward, and the lowly one when you raise him.
The vile one spares no effort in seeking evil vengeance for the wrong that has been done to him.
Beware of depending on the vile one, for indeed he forsakes the one who depends on him.
The most difficult objective is seeking that which is in the possession of the vile ones.
The vile ones are the most patient physically [but are weakest in spirit].
The vile one has no magnanimity.
The vile person is never ashamed.
The vile person is one who puts a lot of obligation [on others when he does any good to them].
The vile one is such that when he has the power, he commits atrocities and when he makes a promise, he breaks it.
The vile one is such that when he gives, he does begrudgingly and when he is given something, he is ungrateful.
When you come upon vile [and miserly] people then give the excuse of fasting [so that you may leave them without partaking of a meal].
When the vile one attains a position above his status, his condition changes [for the worse].
When the vile one increases his reverence for you then increase your scorn for him.
The authority of a vile person manifests his evil traits and flaws.
The dominion of the vile is the humiliation of the honourable.
The ascendency the vile ones is from the calamities of the times.
The one who seeks good from vile people is deprived of it.
The triumph of a vile person leads to destruction.
The triumph of vile people leads to haughtiness and defiance.
The shadow [and patronage] of the vile ones is [an] endemic adversity.
The habit of vile people is to repay good with evil.
The habit of vile people is denial [the blessings they have been given].
The habit of vile people is ugly slander [and backbiting].
Harming honourable and liberated people is the habit of the vile and ignorant ones.
The honour of a vile person is humiliation and the deviation of the intellect is the worst deviation.
Flee as far as you can from the foolish, vile one.
The poverty of the honourable one is better than the wealth of the vile one.
Absence of vile people is a [source of] comfort for the people.
Every time the rank of a vile person is raised, the people around him diminish, whereas the honourable one is the opposite of this.
One who is vile, [the occasion of] his birth is evil.
One who needs something from the vile ones has indeed been forsaken.
Hard-heartedness is from the traits of the vile ones.
The one who accompanies vileness is censured.
The withholding of the honourable one is better than the granting of the vile one.
The vile one is recognized by [his] evil action, ugly character and blameworthy miserliness.
The practice of the vile ones is denial.
There is nothing after clarification but confusion.
Milk is one of the two meats.
The stubborn one has no [valid] opinion.
The stubborn one has no planning.
Never argue with a stubborn person in a gathering.
A stubborn person has no [valid] opinion.
Stubbornness causes its rider to stumble.
Stubbornness gives rise to hostilities and kindles rancour in the hearts.
Stubbornness is the most harmful of all things in this life and the next.
Beware of blameworthy stubbornness, for indeed it provokes hostilities.
Stubbornness is ill-fated.
Stubbornness is the seed of evil.
Stubbornness tarnishes the soul.
Stubbornness is the provoker of hostilities.
Stubbornness causes its rider to fall off.
Stubbornness is the symbol of destruction [and ruin].
Stubbornness is followed by detriment.
Stubbornness corrupts opinion.
Stubbornness brings to a person that which he is not in need of.
The fruit of stubbornness is ruin.
The rider of stubbornness is exposed to affliction.
Stubbornness is the cause of turmoil [and war].
Stubbornness may bring about that which a person is not in need of.
There is no mount more insubordinate than stubbornness.
Importunity is an inviter of deprivation.
Importunity is enough as a [reason for] deprivation.
Excessive importunity leads to refusal.
The excessive importunity of a man leads to his deprivation.
One whose importunity increases gets deprived.
One who is importunate in asking irritates [people].
One who is importunate in asking gets deprived.
One who is importunate in his asking invites his own deprivation.
One who understands the times [in which he lives] does not neglect to prepare [for what is to come].
One who is crippled by the hardship of the times is raised by the assistance of the noble-minded ones.
How quick the hours pass in the day and how fast the days pass in the month and how quick the months pass in the year and how fast the years pass in the lifetime!
Days are the pages of your lifetime so eternize [or bind] them with your best deeds.
Hours are the lurking place of banes.
Hours plunder lifetimes.
The passing of days brings the benefit of experiences.
Hours diminish lifetimes.
The passing of days reveals the hidden secrets.
Verily you are only [the sum total of] a fixed number of days, and every day that passes you by takes a piece of you with it, so reduce your desires and be moderate in your earning.
Verily the previous generations were only wiped out by the alternation of movements and stillness.
The early morning hours of Saturdays and Thursdays are a blessing.
The era of the just [ruler] is the best of eras.
Verily your moments are portions of your life, so do not pass your time except in that which will save you [in the Hereafter].
In every instance there is an action [that should be performed].

There will come a time upon the people when nothing of the Qur’an will remain except its written text, and nothing of Islam [will remain] but its name; on that day their masjids will be marvellously constructed buildings, but will be empty of (or desolate with regards to) guidance.

A time will come upon the people when none will be given a high position except the slanderer, none will be deemed witty except the corrupt and none will be regarded as weak but the just. People will consider charity as a loss, keeping ties with near relatives as an obligation and worship as a means of gaining superiority over people. Vain desires will overcome them and guidance will disappear from among them.
The camel growls after its silence, and time pounces [attacking] like a rapacious beast of prey.

By the One who split the seed and created humankind, there will surely come forth amongst you a community that will strike the heads on the interpretation of the Qur’an just as Muhammad (s) began [conveying to you] its revelation, this is the decree from the Most Merciful upon you in the end of days.
Do not plunge into the surge (or fire) of sedition that comes your way, and move away from its path while opening up the middle of the road for it [to pass].
He will direct desires towards guidance when [people] will have turned guidance towards desires, and he will turn his opinion towards the Qur’an when they turn the Qur’an towards their opinions.
You have forgotten what you were reminded of and felt safe from that which you were warned about, so your opinion has gone astray and your affair has dispersed.

Do you see (or observe) anyone other than a poor man suffering poverty, or a rich man who shows ingratitude in return for the blessings that Allah has bestowed on him, or a miser who denies the right of Allah in order to increase his wealth, or an unruly person who closes his ears [as if he is deaf] to all [wise] counsel.

By the One who sent Muhammad (s) with the Truth, you will verily be mixed [and shaken] a complete mixing, and sifted a total sieving and fully mixed as by a ladle in a cooking pot, until those who are low from among you become high and the high ones become low, and those who have fallen behind will come forward and those who are in front will fall behind.
The masses are not reformed except by justice.
It was said to him (‘a): Verily nothing can reform the people of Kufa except the sword. To this he (‘a) replied: If nothing but my destruction reforms them then may Allah not reform them!
The bane of the masses is disobedience [to the rightful ruler].
How many an owner of great wealth has been turned into a lowly pauper by [the passage of] time.
How will you remain in your current state when time is [in the process of] transforming you?!
One who blames [the vicissitudes of] time, his blame will be lengthy.
People do not say about anything, “[what a great] blessing!” except that time has hidden a bad day for it.

Verily you are [living] in an age when those who speak about the truth are few, and tongues are weary of uttering the truth, and those who stick to the truth are humiliated. The people of this time are engaged in disobedience and make peace with each other upon treachery [and deceit]. Their youths are violent [and wicked] while their elders are sinful.
