Their scholars are hypocrites and their speakers are deviants. Their young do not respect the elderly and their rich do not support the poor.
Verily you will be faced with my vilification and repudiation, so revile me [if you must], but beware of repudiating me.
We have come upon an age of intransigence and an era of ingratitude. In it the good-doer is counted as an evil-doer and the unjust increases in his insolence.
The people may become brothers in wickedness and desert one another in religion, and [they may] love each other over falsehood and hate each other over the truth.

So fear Allah with the fearing of one whose body has become fatigued by fright, and who has been kept awake from his little sleep by his night worship, and who has been made thirsty in the heat of his days by hope [of attaining nearness to Allah].

How amazing it is; and why would I not be amazed by the mistake of this community (or these groups) with their different arguments with regards to their religion. They neither follow the footsteps of the Prophet nor do they emulate the actions of the vicegerent. They do not believe in the unseen and do not restrain themselves from [sins and] shortcomings. They act on uncertainties and tread in [the way of] their passions. For them good is whatever they [like and] consider good and evil is whatever they [dislike and] consider evil. Their reliance for resolving problems is on themselves and their confidence in regard to dubious matters is on their own opinions, as if each one of them is his own leader, even though he has formed his opinion without turning to reliable sources and strong proofs.
Indeed, you have again reverted to the position of the Bedouin Arabs after migration [to Islam] and have become [divided into] different parties after once being closely united.
Indeed those who [would] remember and remind [the people about Allah] have left you and only those who forget [Allah and the Day of Resurrection] and cause others to forget have remained behind.
Indeed the reins of destruction are dragging you and locks of darkness [and malice] lay fixed on your hearts.
Indeed you have become devoted to one another in the love of this transient world and the rejection of the Hereafter.
Indeed the religion of one among you has become like the licking of his tongue, [or like] the hobby that is pursued by one who is free from his work and has gained the approval of his master.
They have plunged into the seas of temptations and have taken to innovation rather than following the practices of the Prophet, and they have gone deep into ignorance while abandoning knowledge.
Do not lose hope in time when it withholds, and do not rely upon it when it gives, and always be extremely cautious of it.

Verily time will pass for those who remain [in this world] just as it passed for those gone by. That which has gone shall not return and that which is in it will not remain forever. Its later deeds are the same as the former ones. Its affairs try to excel each another and its banners follow each other. Its companion is never separated from hardship, annihilation, pillage and war.
Verily time has its bow stretched [and ready], and its arrow does not miss, and its wound does not heal. It afflicts the healthy with sickness and the [one who is] safe with destruction.
Time is responsible for the separation of loved ones.
An hour of humiliation is not compensated for by a lifetime of honour.
Be flexible with time when it submits itself to you and do not put anything in danger out of hope for gaining more [than it].
Time has indeed made its gratitude incumbent on the one who attains what he seeks.
Time wears out the bodies, renews hopes, brings death closer and takes aspirations further away.
Time consists of two days: a day for you and a day against you, so when it is for you then do not become vain and ungrateful, and when it is against you then have patience.
Time has two states: destruction and bestowal; that which it destroys does not return and that which it bestows does not last.
Verily time is an enemy who is not shown enmity, a [chosen] judge who is not unjust and a fighter who has not [and cannot be] fought.
One who resists time is compelled by it and one who submits to it is not safe [from it].
The age of the tyrant [ruler] is the worst of ages.
Every day is driving towards its morrow.
Calamities are born from the passage of time.
There is no guarantee on time.
One is neither safe from the passage of time nor secure from the calamities of the days.
It behoves the one who knows about time not to feel secure from its adversities and vicissitudes.
Obedience is the shield of the masses and justice is the shield of the [rulers of] nations.

So the hearts are heedless of right guidance, too hard to accept their [good] fortune, traversing on the wrong paths as though the one being addressed is someone else, and as though the fortune lies in amassing worldly gains.
How effective these admonitions [would be] if only they were received by pure hearts, attentive ears and unwavering minds.

From them mischief will spring up and all wrong will turn towards them. They will fling anyone who isolates himself from it (i.e. the mischief) back into it and they will drive anyone who stays back from it towards it.
If falsehood dominates, it has [always] been so in the past, and if truth diminishes, that too has often occurred and may [again] happen. It is seldom that a thing lags behind and remains behind.
Indeed the evil people have emerged and the righteous people have hidden; and falsehood has become abundant while truth has diminished.
Time has indeed come full circle to its [initial] state, as it was when the heavens and earth were first created.
The abominable has become so rampant that the shame one feels from it has reduced.
Dishonesty has increased so much that there are only few who can [now] be trusted.
Why is it that I see you as bodies without souls, and souls without prosperity, and devotees without righteousness, and traders without profits?!
Time betrays its companion and does not please the one who blames it.
When the epoch becomes corrupt, the wicked gain mastery [over the people].
In time there are vicissitudes (or lessons [to be learnt]).
One who busies himself with [the worldly activities of his] lifetime becomes occupied by it [and pays no heed to the Hereafter].
Whoever feels safe from time is betrayed by it and whoever regards it as great is humiliated by it.
Whoever insults [and disputes with] the people, his enemies increase.
Pleasure distracts.
Pleasures are corrupters.
Pleasures are woes.
The root of [all] woes is being distracted by [worldly] pleasures.
Many a pleasure has death [hidden] in it.
Few are those who are enticed by pleasures but that their destruction is caused by it.
How many a vile pleasure has prevented one from [attaining] lofty stations.
Nobody delights in any of the pleasures of this world but that it will be a distress for him on the Day of Resurrection.
There is no good in a pleasure that does not last.
There is no pleasure in transient desires.
The pleasure of disobedience is not worth the chastisement of hellfire.
The sweetness of [worldly] pleasure does not compensate for the bitterness of adversities.
The pleasure of disobedience does not equate to the disgrace in the Hereafter and its painful chastisements.
There is no good in the pleasure that brings about regret and the desire that is followed by pain.

With every pleasure remember its [eventual] end, and with every blessing [recall] its removal, and with every hardship its [ultimate] relief; for indeed this makes the blessings last longer, subdues lustful desires more, takes vanity further away, brings relief closer, and is more conducive for the relieving of distress and attainment of aspirations.
The tongue is a gauge that is given weight by the intellect and made light by ignorance.
Safeguard your tongue just as you treasure your gold and your money.
Protect your head from the slips of your tongue, and constrain it with reason, judiciousness, God- wariness and intellect.

Restrain your tongue before it prolongs your incarceration and destroys your soul, for there is nothing more worthy of long imprisonment than a tongue that has strayed from the right and is hasty in responding.
Be cautious of the tongue for indeed it is an arrow that can miss its mark.
Beware of making your tongue a medium for slandering your brothers, or of saying that which will become proof against you and a reason for harming you.
Know that the tongue is a part of a person’s body, so when he desists, speech will not assist him and when he opens up [and is ready to speak], speech will not give him time to pause.
Now surely the good repute of a man that is preserved for him by Allah among the people is better than the wealth that is inherited by those who do not praise him.
Verily your tongue demands from you that which you have made it accustomed to.
The tongue is the interpreter of the heart.
The tongue is recalcitrant to its owner.
The tongue is the interpreter of the intellect.
A person is hidden under his tongue.1
The tongue is a beast of prey, if you let it free it will injure [you].
The tongue is the gauge of a human being.
The tongues reveal that which is concealed by the inner consciences.
The affliction of a human being is in his tongue.
The edge of a spearhead severs the appendages [of the body] whereas the edge of the tongue cuts short lifetimes.
The edge of the tongue is sharper than the edge of a spearhead.
Many a tongue destroys a person.
The slip of the tongue is more harmful than the thrust of the spearhead.
The slip of the tongue is more severe than the injury caused by a spearhead.
The slip of the tongue causes the greatest destruction.
Restraining the tongue is [a means of attaining] fortune and authority while setting it free is [a cause of] destruction.
The piercing of the tongue is more injurious than the piercing of the spear.
Accustom your tongue to polite speech and you will remain safe from reproach.
It is very rare for the tongue to remain fair in spreading [news about] the ugly and the good acts [of others].
Set your tongue aright and you will be secure.
Every person is held accountable for the offence committed by his tongue and his hand.
How much blood has been spilt by the mouth!2
How many a person has been destroyed by the tongue!
The tongue of the intelligent person is behind his heart.3
The tongue of the ignorant person is the key to his destruction.
Your tongue demands from you that which you have made it accustomed to.
He (‘a) said about the one whom he reproached: His tongue is like honey but his heart is a prison for rancour.
The tongue of a virtuous person is enthralled by the continued remembrance of Allah.
If you restrain your tongue, it will save you and if you set it free, it will ruin you.
Your tongue demands from you that which you have accustomed it to and your soul requires from you that which you have familiarized it with.
One whose tongue is sweet [and polite], his friends increase.
One who protects his tongue honours himself.
One who does not control his tongue regrets.
One who imprisons his tongue remains safe from regret.
One who sets his tongue aright adorns his intellect.
One who makes his tongue his master has decreed his own death.
One who restrains his tongue is safe from regret.
One who sets his tongue free demonstrates his own foolishness.
Guarding the tongue is part of faith.
One who does not guard his tongue has not completed his faith.
Without a tongue, the human being would be nothing more than lifeless statue or a wild beast.
Nothing attracts the heart of a human being more than a [sweet and eloquent] tongue, and none beguiles the soul more than Satan.
Do not move your tongue except to say that which will earn you reward and that which behoves you to speak [of] openly.
Never use the sharpness of your tongue against the one who has made you speak or the eloquence of your speech against the one who guides you [to the right path].
The slips of the tongue cannot be controlled.
Nothing is more beneficial for a human being than guarding the tongue and doing good to others.
This tongue is recalcitrant to its owner.
When you are the cause of someone’s affliction, it is obligatory upon you to show courtesy [and kindness] in trying to remedy his affliction.
Many a vain talk results in evil [action].
Good meetings strengthen the bond of brotherhood.
Good encounters (or meetings) are one of the two successes.
One who loves to meet Allah, the Glorified, forgets this world.
One who settles for hinting [and indirect reference] becomes needless of declaration.
Excessiveness in reproach ignites the fire of obstinacy.
The easiest thing is censuring the ignorant ones.1
When you [have to] censure [someone], make it short.
Many a person who is reproached has done nothing wrong.
When slips and errors increase, reproach increases.
Blame may at times be beneficial.
Reproof is one of the two punishments.
Repetition of [the] reprimand is more severe than the pain of a beating.
Too much reproof instils hatred in the hearts and alienates the companions.
One whose reproach increases, his disgrace increases.
The blamer should not blame anyone but himself.
Amusement corrupts serious resolutions.
Keep away from amusements for indeed you have not been created aimlessly so that you may be amused, and you have not been left without purpose so that you may indulge in vanities.
The furthest of all people from righteousness is one who is [excessively] fond of amusement.
The beginning of amusement is play and its end is war.
The furthest of all people from prosperity is one who is fond of amusement and jest.
Amusement is from the fruits of ignorance.
Amusement is the provision of foolishness.
Many an amusement alienates a freeman.
The worst thing that one’s lifetime can be wasted on is idle sport.
One whose amusement increases is considered a fool.
One whose amusement increases, his intelligence decreases.
Whoever is overpowered by amusement, his seriousness is nullified.
Gatherings of amusement corrupt the faith.
Intellect [and wisdom] and idle play do not go together.
One who takes pleasure in idle sport and is fond of amusement and entertainment does not become successful.
The night and day are pursuing their courses in covering those who remain and wiping out the traces of those who have passed away.
Verily your night and day are not enough to meet all your needs, so divide them between your work and your relaxation.
Verily the night and day are working in you [by making you older] so work in them, and they are taking from you so take from them.
The succession of the night and day is the hiding place of calamities and the herald of separation [from loved ones].
The succession of days are [like] dreams, their pleasures are [causes of] agonies and their gifts are [fraught with] evanescence and maladies.
One whose nights and days pass him by is made old by them.
One whose nights and days pass him by is chastised and afflicted, and brought closer to his death by them.
Verily one whose riding mount is the night and day is carried [forward] by it even when he is stationary, and he traverses the distance even if he is settled in one place.
Through gentleness, the souls feel at ease.
Be soft without being weak and stern without using force.
One whose nature is gentle, loving him is unavoidable.
One whose wood is soft, his branches become thick.1
One who has a gentle demeanour makes his community’s love [for him] last.
One who is not lenient with the one who is under him will not obtain what he requires.
Make your demeanour gentle and humble yourself in front of Allah, He will elevate you.
Make your demeanour gentle for indeed whoever has a gentle demeanour, his community’s love [for him] will last.
erily distinction is nothing but your giving that which you owe [of the rights of others] and forgiving the offences [of others].
He who has been forgone by praise does not attain distinction.
He who has been forgone by praise will not acquire distinction.
One who lacks diligence does not attain distinction.
Verily tribulations have certain extents that have to be passed so remain in slumber until they pass, for indeed trying to find a solution before this only increases [and prolongs] it.

Verily tribulations have certain extents, and the extents have limits, so remain patient until you reach their limits, for trying to find a solution for them before they have passed only increases [and prolongs] them.
Tribulation is linked with love of this world.
Tribulation has been linked to love of this world.
Be on your guard against excessive flattery and praise for indeed these two have a foul odour in the heart.
Beware of praising anyone for something that is not in him, for indeed his action affirms his attribute and belies you.
The ugliest truth is a person’s praise for himself.

Verily the person who praises you is surely a deceiver of your intellect, [and] a cheater who cheats you about yourself with false compliments and spurious praise; so if you deprive him of your grant or withhold from him your favour, he will label you with every scandal and will attribute every ugly act to you.
Commendation causes vainglory and brings one closer to heedlessness.
When you praise, be brief.

When one of the pious believers is extolled [for his virtues], he fears what is said about him, so he says: I know myself better than others, and my Lord knows me better than myself. O Allah! Do not hold me accountable for what they say and make me better than what they think of me.
Recommendation of the evil ones is one of the greatest sins.
Love for compliments and praise is from the surest opportunities of Satan.
The best praise is that which flows from the tongues of the righteous.
The worst praise is that which flows from the tongues of the wicked.
Seeking praise without deserving it is foolishness.
How many a person is thrilled by the praise showered upon him.
Excessive praise is flattery; it causes vainglory and brings one closer to heedlessness.
Every praiser has the right to a good reward or a handsome gift from whom he praises.
One who praises you has [actually] slaughtered you.
One who praises you for what is not in you is indeed likely to blame you for that which you have not done.
One who is praised for that which is not in him is ridiculed by it.
Whoever praises you for that which is not in you, then it is actually a criticism of you if you think about it.
One of the ugliest blameworthy acts [of a person] is praising the wicked.
The one who praises a person for that which is not in him is mocking him.
The one who praises you for that which is not in you is [actually] mocking you, and if you do not give him that which fulfils his wants, he will be excessive in his blame and defamation of you.
A person is in the position where he places his soul through his devotion and obedience, so if he purifies it, it becomes pure and if he sullies it, it becomes sullied.
A person is in the position that he chooses for his soul. If he preserves it, it becomes elevated and if he does not preserve it, it becomes abased.
A person is [gauged] by his two small parts: his heart and his tongue. If he battles, he fights with his heart and if he speaks, he speaks by his articulation.

The human being changes in three instances: when he is close to kings, when he gains positions of authority and when he becomes wealthy. So whoever does not change in these conditions, then he is one who possesses a strong intellect and an upright character.
A man is [to be gauged] by his astuteness not by his appearance.
A person is [valued] by his endeavour [and effort], not by his [material] acquisition.
A man is [gauged] by his endeavour.
A person is [judged] by [what is in] his heart.
A person is [gauged] by his faith.
The distinction of a man is [by] his wealth but his honour is [by] his religion.
The distinction of a man is his intellect and his magnanimity is [by] his [good] character.
The distinction of a person is [by] his knowledge and his beauty is his intellect.
The evidence of a person’s roots is his action.
The value of every person [gauged by] is what he knows.
The value of every person is his intellect.
A person’s worth is based on the extent of his merit.
The worth of every person is [measured by] that which he does well.
Every person has a need (or for every affair there is [a proper] etiquette).
The good and evil of every person, and the purity or impurity of his origin is evinced by what he manifests of his actions.

When the virtues of a man are more than his vices, then that [person] is ideal, and when his virtues and vices are equal then he has protected himself [from destruction], but if his vices are more than his virtues then he is doomed.
The evil man does not think positively about anyone because he does not see anyone but through the depiction of his own soul.
The worst person is he who sells his religion for the worldly life of others.
At times people are deceived.
A person is weighed by his speech and valued by his action, so say that which is weighty and do that which has great value.
A person’s value is indicated by his knowledge and intellect.
Every person is answerable for what is in his possession and his family.
Magnanimity is a person’s eschewal of that which dishonours him and his earning that which embellishes him.

Magnanimity is [displaying] equity when in authority, showing forgiveness despite having the power [to take revenge] and being financially supportive [to those in need] in one’s society (or in times of hardship).
Magnanimity is spreading goodness and being hospitable to guests.
Magnanimity is a title that encompasses all the [other] merits and virtues.
The most honourable magnanimity is loyal brotherhood.
The best magnanimity is preserving goodwill [and affection].
The root of magnanimity is modesty and its fruit is chastity.
The most honourable magnanimity is controlling one’s anger and killing one’s lustful desires.
The most excellent magnanimity is tolerating the offenses of one’s brothers.
The most excellent magnanimity is for a man to preserve his dignity.
The beginning of magnanimity is obedience to Allah and its end is keeping away from vile traits.
The beginning of magnanimity is [having] a cheerful mien and its end is being affectionate towards the people.
The beginning of magnanimity is cheerfulness and its end is persistence in righteousness.
The most excellent magnanimity is modesty, and its fruit is chastity.
The most excellent magnanimity is financially supporting your brothers with [your] wealth, and treating them as your equals in status.
Magnanimity is fulfilling one’s promise.
Magnanimity is eschewing vile traits.
Concealing [one’s] poverty and sickness is part of magnanimity.
Magnanimity is bereft and devoid of every [form of] vulgarity.
Magnanimity impels [one] towards noble traits.
There is no magnanimity like remaining free from sins.
Magnanimity is contentment and tolerance (or patience).
Magnanimity prevents every vileness.
Magnanimity is being free from every [form of] wickedness.
Magnanimity is being free from vulgarity and disloyalty.
There is magnanimity in three things: lowering one’s gaze, lowering one’s voice and walking with modesty.
Three things are the consolidators of magnanimity: Giving without being asked, being faithful without having made a promise and being generous despite having less.
Three things amount to magnanimity: generosity despite poverty [and hardship], tolerance of everything other than humiliation and refraining from asking others.
The completeness of magnanimity is for you not to do in private what you would feel ashamed of doing in front of others.
Two qualities have in them the consolidation of magnanimity: a person’s eschewing that which disgraces him and his acquiring that which embellishes him.
One’s magnanimity is to the extent of the nobility of his soul.
He who is not careful of his obligation towards his friends and does not treat his enemies justly cannot be attributed with magnanimity.

If magnanimity was not difficult to acquire and heavy to bear, the wicked and ignorant ones would not have left from it anything even for a single night, but its acquisition is difficult and its burden is heavy, so the wicked and ignorant turned away from it and the honourable and virtuous ones adopted it.
Part of magnanimity is going beyond one’s [normal] capacity in working for [the pleasure of] Allah.
Lowering the gaze and walking with modesty are part of magnanimity.
Obedience to Allah and good estimation are part of magnanimity.
Keeping away from the forbidden is one of the conditions of magnanimity.
From the completeness of magnanimity is for one to feel ashamed of himself.
Magnanimity is one of the most excellent religious teachings and there is no good in a religion which has no magnanimity in it.
Staying clear of vile traits is from the completeness of magnanimity.
Keeping ties with near relatives is from the most excellent magnanimity.
Maintaining resoluteness [and judiciousness] is from the most excellent magnanimity.
It is from the completeness of magnanimity for you to forget your right upon others while recalling their right upon you.
It is from magnanimity for you to go out of your way when you are asked [for something] and to lighten [your requests] when you ask [someone for anything].
It is part of magnanimity for you to be moderate and not extravagant, and to keep the promises you make.
Bearing the offences of one’s brothers is from magnanimity.
Nobody has carried a burden heavier than magnanimity.
With affluence, magnanimity becomes manifested.
The magnanimity of a person is to the extent of his intellect.
The magnanimity of a person is [gauged by] the truthfulness of his speech.
A person’s magnanimity is in his tolerance of his brothers’ mistakes.
The basis of magnanimity is truthful speech and doing good to others.
The establishment of magnanimity is in struggling with your brother to make him obey Allah, the Glorified, and restraining him from disobeying Him, and increasing your censure [of him] for it.
Magnanimity is not perfected except for the intelligent one.
There is no magnanimity like keeping clear of sins.
There is no magnanimity in one who has no determination.
Magnanimity is not completed except by bearing the hardships of good acts.
Magnanimity is evinced by increased modesty, generous giving and refraining from harming others.
The magnanimity of a person is evinced by [his] spreading goodness, granting favours and abandoning [putting others under] obligation.
Sickness is [a form of] confinement of the body.
There are two things that should not be scorned: sickness and the poor relative.
One who hides his sickness from the physicians has betrayed his body.
Whoever conceals his hidden ailment, his physician becomes incapable of curing him.
Sickness in one of the two confinements.
Disputation is the seed of evil.
Argument in religion corrupts certitude.
The fruit of disputation is hatred.
Too much disputation is the cause of hatred [and enmity].
One should not dispute with six types of people: the jurist, the leader, the low, the lewd, the woman and the child.
One whose disputation increases does not remain safe from error.
Whoever accustoms himself to disputation, it becomes his habit.
One who makes disputation his habit will not turn his night into day [and will remain in the darkness of ignorance].
One whose false disputations increase, his blindness from the truth persists.
One who disputes with a fool has no intelligence.
With excessive disputation, there can be no affection.
Joking is a [cause of] separation that is followed by rancour.
Beware of recalling that which was funny in the speech [of others], even if you narrate it from someone else.
Excessiveness in joking is foolishness.
Abandon [excessive] joking for indeed it is the conception of rancour.
In impudence and excessive joking there is foolishness.
Too much joking diminishes one’s reverence [and dignity].
Too much joking takes away prestige and brings about enmity [and rancour].
Everything has a seed, and the seed of enmity is joking.
One who jokes [excessively] is taken lightly.
One whose joking increases is deemed ignorant.
One whose joking is excessive is considered a fool.
One whose joking increases, his reverence [and dignity] decreases.
One whose joking increases, his dignity diminishes.
Whoever jokes excessively will never be without one who bears a grudge against him and one who takes him lightly.
Any time a person makes a joke, he parts with a portion of his intellect.
Do not make fun of a noble person such that he ends up bearing a grudge against you.
Never make fun of a friend thereby turning him into an enemy, or of an enemy thereby making him [want to] destroy you.
Keep walking in your customary way (or with your ailment1) as long as you can.
Delay and obligation are the spoilers of [the] favour [one does to others].
Delay [in giving] is one of the two refusals.
Delay [and procrastination] is a chastisement of the soul.
Scheming and malice are things that keep faith away.
Beware of scheming, for indeed scheming [and plotting] is a blameworthy quality.
Scheming is wickedness, deception is evil.
Scheming is the practice of the mutinous.
Scheming is the trait of the wicked.
Scheming against one who trusts in you is ingratitude [and betrayal].
The bane of cleverness is scheming.
The cornerstone of wisdom is eschewing deceptions.
Many a plotter has been struck down by his own stratagem.
One who feels secure from the devising of Allah is destroyed.
One who feels secure from the devising [of Allah] meets with harm.
The one who always hatches plots [against others] is a devil.
The one who is always scheming [against others] is a devil in the form of a human being.
One who schemes is afflicted by his own scheming.
Whoever schemes against people, Allah, the Glorified, turns his scheme back on him.
There is no trustworthiness in the schemer.
Evil scheming does not beset anyone but those who practice it.
Beware of flattery, for indeed flattery is not from the characteristics of faith [and the faithful].
Flattery is not part of the character of Prophets.
One whose flattery increases, his [sincere] joyfulness is not recognized.
Verily only the one who does not flatter you [truly] adores you, and [only] one who does not make you hear his praise for you [truly] praises you.
A tyrant ruler and an immoral scholar are the most harmful of all people.
Accompany the ruler with caution, the friend with humility and cheerfulness, and the enemy with that which you can [use to] establish your proof over him.
Verily the ruler is a trustee of Allah on earth, the establisher of justice in the lands and among the people, and the one who deters people from misdeeds in the land.
The tyrant king frightens the innocent.
An evil commander commissions the vulgar one [to work for him].
The bane of kings is evil intentions.
The bane of viziers is wicked inner thoughts.
The bane of leaders is weakness in politics.
The bane of a kingdom is [having] weak defences.
When you become the ruler then be kind [to your subjects].
When a king builds his kingdom on the foundations of justice and sustains it on the pillars of reason, Allah helps his friends and forsakes his enemies.
When the ruler makes you come closer to him, then increase your exaltation of him.
Kings have no affection.
Transient and fleeting kingship is wretched and insignificant.
Being independent of [and not seeking anything from] kings is the best kingship.
Boldness [and defiance] in front of the king is the quickest [means of] destruction.
The adornment of kingship is justice.
The wrath of kings is the messenger of death.
The merit of a king is in building prosperous cities.
It is seldom that the affection of kings and traitors lasts.
The friendship of kings seldom lasts.
The hearts of the people are the treasuries of their leader, so whatever he deposits in them, be it justice or oppression, he will find it there.
There is no reward with Allah, the Glorified, greater than the reward of a just ruler and a benevolent man.
One who gains authority [usually] adopts partiality.
One who becomes haughty in his kingship has belittled it.
One whose aggression is prolonged, his rule [soon] comes to an end.
One whose kingship is tyrannical, his destruction becomes great.
Whoever is betrayed by his vizier, his administration gets corrupted.
One who fears your whip wishes for your death.
One who relies upon your goodness is concerned about [the end of] your rule.
One who boldly [and defiantly] faces the ruler becomes vulnerable to disgrace.
Whoever betrays his king, his security is nullified.
One who is just in his kingship becomes needless of his aides.
One who is concerned about his kingship curtails his aggression.
Whoever treats the people unjustly, Allah causes his reign to end and hastens his ruin and destruction.
One who is tyrannical in his kingdom, the people wish for his annihilation.
One who unsheathes the sword of aggression is stripped of the grandeur of kingship.
One who seeks the favour of a king without [the proper] etiquette moves out from safety into harm.
Whoever is tyrannical in his reign and increases his aggression, Allah will demolish his foundation and tear down his pillars [of kingship].
Whoever is just in his rule and shows kindness [to the people], Allah will elevate his stature and will strengthen [and grant victory to] his helpers.
One who makes his kingship subservient to his religion, every king will submit to him.
When one makes his religion subservient to his kingship, every person will covet it.
One who is occupied with [serving] the king will not [have time to] attend to his brothers.
It is a right upon the king to govern himself before his soldiers.
Disputing with kings takes away blessings.
Evil viziers are the helpers of tyrants and the brothers of wrongdoers.
Oppressive governors are the worst of the ummah and opponents of the [true] leaders.
Do not separate from your [rightful] ruler, thereby making the consequence of your affair blameworthy.
Never visit kings frequently, for they are such that if you accompany them they will become weary of you and if you advise them sincerely they will debase you.
Do not desire to mingle with kings, for indeed they consider replying salutations to be too much speech and striking the necks to be insignificant punishment.

Do not associate with the king in times of disturbance and upheaval, for indeed the sea is such that even when it is calm, the seafarer barely manages to remain safe in it, so how would he fare with its turbulent winds and the tumultuous waves?!
Never desire to gain the affection of kings, for indeed they will forsake you when you are most intimate with them and they will cut you off when you are closest to them.
There is no prosperity [in the place] where the king passes (or is oppressive).
When the intention of the king changes, the times change (or get corrupted).
When the king becomes enraged, Satan takes control [over him].
Seeking power [and sovereignty] is from the deceptions of Satan.
The justice of a king is the life of the populace and the prosperity of the creatures.
The worst of all rulers is one who is ruled by his vain desire.
The worst of rulers is one whose subjects are oppressed.
The king’s courtier is like a person who is riding on a lion, people are envious of his status while he is more aware of his own [dangerous] position.
Partnership in sovereignty leads to turmoil.
Holding a post with kings is a key of tribulation and the seed of affliction.
The best king is the just one.
The best king is the one who has the most continent soul.
The best of all kings in character is one whose justice prevails over all the people.
The most exalted of rulers is one who is not ruled by his vain desires.
The most exalted of kings is one who has control over himself and spreads justice.
The best of kings is one whose action and intention are good, and who is just with his army and his people.
The king who is in the best condition is one whose subjects become prosperous in his prosperity and whose justice prevails over all his people.
The people whom one should be cautious of the most are the tyrannical king, the powerful enemy and the disloyal friend.
The most intelligent of kings is he who governs himself for the people in a way that will remove any proof against him and governs the people in a way that affirms his proof against them.
The kings are [supposed to be] defenders of the religion.
The king’s crown is his justice.
It is a right upon the king that he should govern himself [first] before his troops.
The best of commanders is one who has command over himself.
The best king is one who annihilates oppression and enlivens justice.
The lassitude of a king is more harmful for the people than the oppression of a king.
The alms-tax of the king is assisting the aggrieved.
The worst of kings is one who opposes justice.
The worst of viziers is one who is a vizier to the vicious.
Guard your position near your king, and be cautious of not being lowered from it by negligence towards that which raised you to it.
Works are [only] accomplished by the [right] workers.

He (‘a) said about al-Ashtar al-Nakha‘ī when he was informed about his death (may Allah have mercy upon him): If he was a mountain, he would have been a great one, no hoofed animal would have reached its peak and no bird would have been able to fly over it.

He (‘a) said about al-Ashtar al-Nakha‘ī: He is the sword of Allah that does not fail to strike and is not blunt in its edge; he is not impressed by any innovations nor is he led astray by misguidance [and temptation].

Verily with every person there are two angels who protect him, and when his time is up they leave him alone with his impending death, and verily the [decreed] lifetime [of a person] is a strong protective shield.
He (‘a) said about angels: They are captives of faith; neither divergence nor deviation breaks them from its hold.
Many a slave is such that one cannot bear his separation.
One whose disposition is good [with those who are under him] remains safe from annihilation.
One who is fed-up has no [sense of] brotherhood.
One who is fed-up has no magnanimity.
Never feel secure from the one who is fed-up [with you] even if he is endowed with gifts for indeed there is no enjoyment in lightening for the one who is plunged into darkness.
There is no brotherhood for the one who is fed-up.
There is no friendship for the one who is fed-up.
Irritation (or kingship) corrupts brotherhood.
Every inaccessible thing is difficult to obtain and seek.
Putting someone under obligation blackens the favour.
Obligation is the corruptor of good actions.
Obligation spoils the favour.
Obligation corrupts the good act.
Obligation corrupts the favour.
There is wickedness with obligation.
Doing acts of kindness along with obligation is vileness.
The bane of generosity is obligation.
Through obligation the favour is spoilt.
By putting a lot of obligation, the good action is spoilt.
Prolonged obligation spoils the pureness of a good turn.
One who puts an obligation [on others] by his good action has oppressed magnanimity.
The oppression of favours is [through] the repulsiveness of [putting others under] obligation.
Too much obligation spoils the good action.
One who puts an obligation [on others] with his kind act drops [and forgoes] his gratitude.
One who puts obligation with his goodness has spoilt the good act that he has done.
Whoever puts an obligation with his favour, it is as if he has not done a favour.
One who puts obligation with his good action corrupts it.
Nothing spoils good actions like putting [others under] obligation.
He who puts an obligation [on others] has not made his grant pleasing.
One who puts [others under] obligation with his good act has not perfected it.
He who puts [others under] a lot of obligation has not made his good turn felicitous.
The sin of the charity given by the one who puts obligation is greater than its reward.
One who puts [others under] obligation does no good to others.
There is no good deed with obligation.
There is no pleasure in the good turn of the obliger.
There is no evil quality more repulsive than [putting others under] obligation.
people of goodness and beneficence, do not put [others under] obligation with your favours for indeed favours and good turns are nullified by the repulsiveness of [putting others under] obligations.
Beware of putting obligations with your good acts for indeed [putting others under] obligation spoils favours.
Death clings to you more closely than your own shadows and has greater authority over you than [you have over] yourselves.
Continuously remember death and remember what you will face after death; and never wish for death except after being sure that you have fulfilled the condition for security [in the Hereafter].

Increase your remembrance of death and of the place you have to go suddenly and return to after death, until it comes to you while you are on your guard against it and have prepared yourself for it, and let it not come over you suddenly thereby taking you by surprise.
Prepare yourselves for death for indeed it overshadows you.
Let your ears hear the call of death before it calls you.
Remember the destroyer of pleasures and the spoiler of lustful desires and the caller towards separation.
Beware of death and be adequately prepared for it, [for by this] you will be happy in your place of [final] return.
Beware of insufficient provisions and increase your preparations for your departure.
Is there nobody who is ready to meet his Lord before his soul leaves [his body]?
The best gift for a believer is death.
More severe than death is that which one seeks to be freed from through death.
Verily one who walks on the face of the earth will surely end up inside it.
Verily it behoves you to prepare for the matter about the timing of whose sudden occurrence you have no knowledge of before it overcomes you.

Verily this matter has not started with you nor will it end with you, for this companion of yours travels, so consider him to have gone on one of his travels, and if he comes back to you [then so be it], otherwise you are [all] going towards him [and will meet him].
Verily the one who approaches, bringing with him [either everlasting] felicity or wretchedness, is deserving of the best preparation.
Indeed the absent one who is driven forward by the [succession of the] new night and day, is indeed worthy of a quick return.
Verily in front of you there is a path that covers a long distance, and severe hardships, and you cannot do without good exploration and acquiring the necessary amount of provisions.

Verily our statement: “Indeed we belong to Allah” is an affirmation we make to ourselves that we are owned and our statement: “Indeed we will return to Him” is an affirmation to ourselves that we will die.

Verily before you is an arduous mountain-pass [that is difficult to traverse] where the one with a light burden will be in a better condition than the one with a heavy burden and the one who has to go through it slowly will be worse off than the one who can pass through swiftly. Indeed its place of descent for you inevitably leads either to Paradise or hellfire.
Verily this death is a swift seeker - neither does the steadfast escape it nor does the fleer frustrate it.

Verily death is a relief for the one who was a slave to his lust and a prisoner of his vain desire, because the more his life lengthened the more his sins would increase and his offenses against his soul would become worse.
Verily death has agonies that are more terrible than can ever be described or comprehended by the intellects of the people of this world.
Verily death has been tied to your forelocks whilst this world coils behind you.
Verily death is a visitor who is not loved, a killer who is not held accountable and an invincible adversary.
Departure [from this world] is imminent.
Death is soothing.
The matter is near.
Death is expiration [and loss of opportunity].
Death is a heedless watchman (or friend).
Death is the gate of the Hereafter.
White hair [of old age] is a messenger of death.
Death is the first justice of the Hereafter.
Death is preferable to vileness.
Death is separation from the transient abode and a journey to the everlasting abode.
Verily you are on the run from the death whose fleer is not saved and must eventually meet it.
Verily behind you is a swift seeker in the form of death, so do not be negligent.
Verily you are all running away from the death which will take you if you remain steadfast [to resist it] and will catch up with you if you [try to] flee.
When death arrives, hopes are exposed.
When one cannot remain secure from the onslaught of death, then not being prepared for it is incompetence.
Deaths cut off hopes.
When you are moving away [from this world] and death is moving towards you, then how quickly you will meet each other!
When the bringer of the news of death comes frequently to you, he will [soon also] announce your death to others.
The one who does not prepare for death and take benefit of respite is negligent of the onslaught of death.
Begin your journey for you have been pushed forward and prepare for death for it has overshadowed you.
Remembrance of death makes the means [and comforts] of this world seem trivial.
Sometimes the choker (or drinker) is choked by water [and dies] before quenching his thirst.
Death is the cause of loss.
Fill yourselves with desire for the bounties of Paradise, [and] you will love death and loathe [this worldly] life.
I am amazed at the one who forgets death while he sees others dying [around him].
I am amazed at the person who sees his body and his lifespan decreasing every day and still does not make preparations for death.
I am amazed at the one who fears the ambush [of death] and still does not desist.
The end of death is loss.
The absent death is more deserving of being awaited and is closer in its approach [than any other traveller whose return is expected].
In death there is [either] delight or regret.
In every soul there is death.1
In death there is comfort for the felicitous.
Death may [at times] be hastened.
Every expected thing [eventually] arrives.
Every comer is near.2
Every near one is close by.
Every person will meet his death.
How can one who is sought by death remain safe?
How can you forget death while its signs are [constantly] reminding you [of it]?
For every rising one there is a setting.
For every [being with a] soul there is death.
For every living thing there is death.
For all [beings with] souls there is death.
The affluent person will never be saved from death because of his abundant wealth.
The poor person will never be saved from death because of his poverty.
If death could be bought, the affluent would have surely bought it.
One who dies, passes away.
One who is certain of the [eventual] departure [from this world] prepares for the journey.
One who sees death with the eyes of his certitude, sees it nearby.
One who sees death with the eyes of his hope, sees it far away.
One who remembers death forgets his aspirations.
One who recalls the distance of his journey, prepares [for it].
One who frequently remembers death is saved from the deceptions of this world.
One who is missed by the arrow of death is fettered by old age.
One who anticipates death hastens towards good deeds.
One who visualizes death before his very own eyes, the affairs of this world become easy [and trivial] for him.
One who frequently remembers death is pleased with whatever suffices him of this world.
Whoever frequently remembers death, his desire in [the pleasures of] this world is reduced.
Whoever frequently remembers death is satisfied with the little he possesses of this world.
Whoever has [the angel of] death given charge over him, is overrun and annihilated by it.
One who is sought by death cannot be saved from it.
One who counts tomorrow as part of his lifetime has not recognized the reality of death.
How beneficial death is for the one who has filled his heart with faith and God-wariness!
The deaths of this world are easier to bear than the deaths [and chastisements] of the Hereafter.

We are the helpers of death and our lives are targets of mortality, so how can we expect to live forever while the night and day do not elevate anything in status but that they quickly destroyed that which they have built and separated that which they have brought together.
Are the people who have been given time to live [in this world] awaiting anything but the time of death, while the hour is close and the journey is at hand?
Can the near ones repel [death] from you, or can the wailing [of the women and children] be of any benefit to you?
Far be it for death to lose the one whom it seeks or for the one who flees it to get saved [from it].
The arrival of death cuts off action and exposes [false] hopes.
The arrival of death expunges respite, brings the appointed time closer and dashes [one’s] hope.
There is no soother like death.
Death does not desist from extermination [and will annihilate all].
There is none whose arrival is nearer than death.
There is no absent one that approaches quicker than death.
There is no blame on the one who flees from his death.
Destiny holds sway over the expectations [and plans of man] until death occurs in the [execution of his own] plans.
It behoves the one who knows about the quickness of his departure to be well prepared for the move.
Death is preferable to the shame of disgrace.
Death comes to every living thing.
Do not remember the dead negatively [by recalling their bad actions] for this suffices as a sin.
Wealth honours its possessor in this world and abases him in front of Allah, the Glorified.
Wealth honours its possessor as long as he spends it and abases him when he is miserly with it.
Wealth and children are the ornaments of this worldly life while good action is the tillage of the Hereafter.
Wealth elevates its possessor in this world but lowers him in the Hereafter.
Wealth is a burden for its possessor except that which he sends ahead from it [for the Hereafter].
Wealth is the tribulation of the soul and the plunder of calamities.
Wealth is reduced by spending [it] whereas knowledge grows when it is given away [and shared with others].
Hold on to wealth according to the extent of your need, and forward the rest for the day of your indigence.

Beware of reserving for yourself (or concealing) that which all the people have an equal right to and turning a blind eye to what is manifest for the onlookers otherwise it will surely be taken from you and given to someone else.
The best wealth is that by which the freemen become enthralled.1
The best of all wealth is that by which men become enthralled.
The purest wealth is that which has been earned by its lawful means.
The most beneficial wealth is that by which the obligatory is fulfilled.
The purest wealth is that with which the Hereafter is bought.
The best wealth is that which has been earned by its lawful means.
The best wealth is that which has the best effect upon you.
The best wealth is that by which the rights [of others] are fulfilled.
Verily your wealth is for the one who praises you in your lifetime and the one who vilifies you after your death.
Verily a person comes to that which he has sent forward [of his good deeds] and regrets [about] that which he has left behind.

Verily Allah, the Glorified, has ordained the provisions of the poor in the wealth of the rich, so no poor person goes hungry but because of the withholding of the rich, and Allah will question them about this.

Surely the person with the greatest regret on the Day of Resurrection will be the man who earns wealth without obeying [the commandments of] Allah, then a man inherits his wealth and spends it in obedience to Allah and through it enters Paradise whereas the first one enters Hell because of it.

Verily when a man dies people say: ‘What has he left behind?’ while the angels say: ‘What has he sent forward?’ Your forefathers are for Allah!2 Send some of your wealth forward, so that it may be a provision for you [in the Hereafter], and do not leave all of it behind such that it becomes a [heavy] burden on you.
Verily the best wealth is that which earns praise and gratitude and brings about reward and recompense.
Verily the best wealth is that which bequeaths to you a provision [for the Hereafter] and a legacy, and earns you praise and reward.
Indeed the best wealth is that by which the freeman is enthralled and [by which] reward is earned.
Verily your wealth cannot fulfil the needs of all the people, so reserve it specifically for the followers of the truth.
Wealth is reckoning [in the Hereafter].
Wealth is a borrowed loan [and will not remain with you forever].

Verily that which is in your possession has had an owner before you and will go to someone after you. You are only amassing [wealth] for one of two kinds of people: either the one who will use what you amassed in obedience to Allah, thereby becoming felicitous by that which made you wretched, or the one who will use what you amassed in disobedience to Allah, thereby becoming wretched by what you amassed, and neither of these two deserve to be preferred by you over yourself or of being carried by you on your back.
Wealth is the plunder of calamities.
Wealth is a solace [and comfort] for the heir (or heirs).
Wealth strengthens one who [is weak and] lacks support.
People serve wealth, wealth does not serve people.3
Wealth is the leader of the wicked.
Wealth is the object of desires.
Wealth strengthens one’s hopes.
Wealth manifests the intrinsic natures of the people and their characters.
Wealth corrupts the outcomes and extends the [false] hopes.
Wealth is the cause of trials and the plunder of calamities.
Wealth is the inviter of difficulty and the riding mount of hardship.
Wealth does not benefit you until it parts from you.
Verily only the wealth which you send ahead for your Hereafter is yours, while that which you leave behind belongs to your heirs.
When you accumulate wealth, then you are [actually] a representative for another person who will rejoice with it while you become miserable.

When you send forth your wealth for your Hereafter and leave [the affair of] your heirs in the hands of Allah, you will be felicitous by that which you have forwarded and Allah will take good care of those whom you leave behind.
It is by overcoming [one’s] fears that wealth is acquired.
The affluence of this world is the poverty of the Hereafter.
Abundance of wealth causes destruction, makes one rebellious and perishes.
Love of wealth is the cause of tribulations and love of leadership is the root of tribulations.
Love of wealth corrupts the [final] outcome.
Love of wealth strengthens [false] hopes and corrupts actions.
Love of wealth weakens faith and corrupts certitude.
The best of your wealth is that which safeguards your dignity.
The best wealth is that which enthrals a freeman.
The best wealth is that which helps one perform noble deeds.
The best of your wealth is that which suffices you.
Take from the most precious of your possessions and spend it on that for which your Lord will elevate your lofty deeds.
Many a person accumulates [wealth] for one who is not grateful to him.
The alms-tax of wealth is benefitting others [with it].
The worst [type of] wealth is that which earns censure.
The worst wealth is that which does not benefit [and fulfil the need of] its owner.
The worst wealth is that from which nothing is spent in the way of Allah and the [obligatory] zakāt of which is not paid.
The worst wealth is that from which the right of Allah, the Glorified, is not given.
The owner of wealth is faces difficulty and one who gains victory through evil [means] has [actually] been defeated.
Little [wealth] that suffices is better than a lot which makes one insolent.
The little that saves [one from hellfire] is better than plenty that destroys.
Send forth some [of your wealth] as it will be [beneficial] for you [in the Hereafter], and do not leave all of it behind as this will become a burden for you.
How many a person accumulates that which he will leave behind.
How often it is that one who gets less, benefits while one who gets more, loses.
Increased wealth corrupts the hearts and gives rise to sins.
Be a [generous] donor with your [own] wealth while being cautious with the wealth of others.
That portion of your wealth which teaches you a lesson and earns you gratitude will never go [to waste].
He who does not reform his [means of earning or spending] wealth has not earned it.
One who does not spend [his] wealth [in the way of Allah] has not been blessed with wealth.
That portion of your wealth which is used to safeguard your dignity has not gone [to waste].
That part of your wealth which is used to fulfil your obligations has not been lost.

A person does not give his wealth to the one who has no right to it, or his favour to one who is not deserving of it, but that Allah deprives him of their gratefulness and their love, too, would be for others.
One who gives [generously from] his wealth makes [others] subservient [to him].
One who earns his wealth from unlawful sources damages his Hereafter.
One who accumulates wealth so that he can benefit people [with it] is obeyed by them and one who accumulates [it] for himself is disregarded by them.
One who considers wealth to be precious, regards people as insignificant.
Whoever spends his wealth in the way of Allah, He quickly replaces it [for him].
Whoever withholds wealth from the one who praises him bequeaths it to one who does not praise him.
One who earns wealth from sources that are unlawful, spends it in the places that are unworthy [and inappropriate].
One who does not let go [of his wealth] while he is praised will have to leave [it] while he is vilified.
One who does not forward his wealth for his Hereafter while he is [sure to be] rewarded [for it], leaves it behind while he is sinful.
One whose wealth is stripped away by disasters, gains from it the benefit of caution.
Never waste your wealth in other than what is good [and right].
Do not spend your wealth in sinful acts thereby coming before your Lord without any [good] deed.

Never leave behind anything from this world, for indeed you will [only] be leaving it for one of two types of people: either the man who uses it in obedience to Allah, so he becomes felicitous by that which made you wretched, or the man who uses it in disobeying Allah, in which case you will have been a helper for him in his disobedience, and neither of these two deserves to be preferred by you over yourself.
Love of wealth and praise do not go together.
There is no pride in wealth except when accompanied with generosity.
Little that suffices is better than a lot which makes one insolent.
Worldly wealth and power turns the mistake of its owner into a proper act and the proper act of his opponent into a mistake.
Everything inclines towards its [own] kind.
Every person inclines towards one who is like him.
Every bird stays close to its [own] kind.
Nobility is [attained] by adorning [oneself] with generosity and fulfilling [one’s] promises.
Verily nobility is nothing but the shunning of disgraceful actions.
The habits of the noble ones are: generosity, suppressing anger, forgiveness and forbearance.
The symbol of nobility is doing good to people.
It is from nobility for a man to spend his wealth and safeguard his dignity.
Acting on the principle of justice is from the signs of nobility.
The nobility of a man is evinced by the paucity of his speech and his merit is deduced from his abundant tolerance.
Be a community that is cried out to so they wake up.
Alertness of the eyes does not benefit while the hearts are negligent.
Is there no one who will wake from his slumber before the time of his death?!
Listen to your godly leader, keep your hearts open for him and listen [to him] if he calls out to you.
Listen to (or accept) advice from the one who gifts it to you and preserve it in your minds.
Messengers of Allah, the Glorified, are interpreters of the truth and intermediaries between the Creator and the creation.
The Messengers of Allah have a clear elucidation for every [divine] command.
The most successful of you are the most truthful among you.
The person who attains his objective the most is one who has intelligence and is mild-mannered.
If you seek of prosperity, then reject negligence and diversion, and espouse diligence and effort.
The bane of success is laziness.
At times success may be attained.
The healing of a wound may at times lead to disability.
How close is success to one who is quick to release [and send forth his provisions for the Hereafter].
The basis of salvation is espousing faith and [having] true certitude.
None is successful in attaining salvation but the one who fulfils the requirements of faith.
There is no salvation for one who has no faith.
He from whose evil people are not safe, is not saved from [the punishment of] Allah, the Glorified.
There is salvation in three things: espousing truth, shunning falsehood and working hard.
How can one who flees from Allah be saved?!
One who seeks help from the lowly is abased.
One who does not help [others] is not helped.
There is no good in secret conversation except for two people: the articulating scholar or the cautious listener [who can keep secrets].
Remorse is one of the two [forms of] repentance.
Be remorseful about the evil that you have done and do not regret the good act that you have performed.
Remorse is [a form of] repentance.
Being remorseful for a misdeed causes it to be wiped off.
Being remorseful for a misdeed is [a form of] repentance.
Being remorseful for [committing] a sin prevents one from returning to it.
Remorsefulness of the heart covers up the sin and purges the wrongdoing.
Blessed is every remorseful one who regrets his mistake and makes up for his past error.
One who is remorseful has repented.
Warning is vindication.
Do not argue with a vile person for he will be bold [and disrespectful] with you.
Do not dispute with the fools and do not be infatuated with women, for indeed this degrades the intelligent ones.
Disputing with the ignoble ones disgraces the [status of the] eminent ones.
A beautiful home is one of the two Paradises.
One whose space is restricted, his comfort is less.
Avoid [building homes in] places of negligence and wickedness and [places where] there is a paucity of supporters for the obedience of Allah.
How many a builder has built that which he does not reside in.

topic: Remaining pure and free from sin-
text: Remaining free from sins is the worship of the penitents.

topic: Remaining pure and free from sin-
text: Keeping away from sin is the essence of astuteness.

topic: Remaining pure and free from sin-
text: Remaining free from sin is the beginning of nobility.

topic: Remaining pure and free from sin-
text: Keeping away from sin is the sign of chastity.

topic: Remaining pure and free from sin-
text: Keeping away from sin is one of the traits of the immaculate souls.

topic: Remaining pure and free from sin-
text: Be free from sin and you will be pious.
Sometimes an outing may turn into a bitter experience.
An outing may turn into an agony.
A person may be a devotee while he [actually] has no religion.
Women are the greater of the two temptations.
Women are [like] meat on the butcher’s block, except that which is protected [and defended].
Beware of evil women, and be on your guard [even] from the good among them.

Beware of excessive infatuation with women and being tempted (or deceived) by the pleasures of this world, for indeed the one who is infatuated with women faces trials and the one who is tempted by the pleasures [of this world] is abased.

Beware of consulting with women, for indeed their opinions are inclined towards immaturity and their decisions are infirm; and restrain their gazes [by keeping them behind the veil], for your veiling them is better than being suspicions about them, and their coming out [in public] is not worse than your letting one who cannot be trusted enter their abode; and if you are able to ensure that they do not get acquainted with anybody other than you then do it.
Verily women are [only] concerned about the ornaments of this world and [creating] mischief herein.
Being infatuated with women is the trait of the foolish.

If you see something suspicious from your women, then assign to them a guard who will watch over the old and young [among the family, and not for the women in particular as this will cause them unease], and beware not to continuously scold them for this will incite them to commit sins and make it easy for them to bear the scolding [as they will become accustomed to it].
The best of traits for women is the worst of traits for men.
Obedience to women is the height of ignorance.
Obedience to women degrades the noble ones and destroys the intelligent ones.
Obedience to women is the trait of the foolish.
Whoever [constantly] delights in women, his mind gets corrupted.

People! Verily women are deficient in faith, lacking in intellect and deficient in shares. As for their deficiency in faith, it is their abstention from prayers and fasting during their menstrual periods, and as for their deficiency in shares, it is due to their inheritance being half of what is inherited by men, and as for their lacking in intellect, it is because the testimony of two women equals the testimony of one man; so beware of the evil women and be on your guard [even] from those of them who are good.
Do not obey women in good [actions] such that they expect [your obedience] in evil.
Never be frequently alone with women, for they will become weary of you and you will also become weary of them, and leave a part of yourself and your mind to tarry [away] from them.
Let women not bear your burden and [try to] be independent from them as much as possible, for indeed they put many obligations [on you] and are ungrateful for [many of your] favours.
The woman is wholly evil, and more evil than her is the fact that man cannot do without her.
A woman is a scorpion whose sting is sweet.
Verily a woman is only [considered] a plaything, so whoever takes her should cover her.
Guarding the woman [from people and places that would harm her chastity] is better for her condition and more lasting for her beauty.
Do not give a woman the responsibility that she cannot bear for indeed a woman is [like] a sweet basil and not a strong ruler [who can govern the people].
Whoever forgets Allah, He makes him forget himself.
Forgetting [Allah] is darkness and loss.
One who forgets [Allah,] the Glorified, Allah makes him forget himself and blinds his heart.
Sincere advice reaps affection.
Giving sincere advice is a characteristic of the noble ones.
Sometimes advice is given by one who is not sincere.
At times one from whom sincere advice is sought, deceives.
Blessed is the one who follows the adviser who guides him and keeps away from the misguided person who leads him to destruction.
He who seeks advice from his enemies is indeed ignorant.
You have been advised so take the advice, you have been shown [the truth] so see [it], and you have been guided aright so accept the guidance.
You have been guided if you seek guidance and have been admonished if you seek admonishment and have been advised if you seek advice.
How can one who takes pleasure in [acts that bring] disgrace benefit from sincere advice?!
One who trades with you by [giving you] advice has indeed made your profit abound.
One who trades with you in advice is your partner in profit.
One of the best forms of advice is disclosing the ugly traits [of a person to him so that he may change].
Being sincere [in giving advice] is from the best [teachings] of religion.
Pointing [people] towards reconciliation is the best advice.
The bitterness of sincere advice is more beneficial than the sweetness of deceit.

Your sincere adviser is concerned about you, shows kindness to you, considers your outcomes and rectifies of your shortcomings; so in obedience to him lies your development and in opposition to him, your corruption.
Your advice [when given] in front of other people is [considered] a rebuke.
Never reject the [advice of a] sincere adviser and never assume the one who counsels you to be a deceiver.

Do not take advice from one who has lost his senses and do not trust one who has an ignoble background, for indeed the one who has lost his senses deceives while he thinks he is offering good advice, and one who has an ignoble background corrupts while he thinks he is rectifying.
There is no sincerity like [giving] sincere advice.
There is no admonisher more effective than sincere advice.
There is no good in a community that does not sincerely advise [each other] and does not love sincere advisers.
The wicked one does not sincerely advise anyone except out of desire or fear, so when the desire or fear disappears, he returns to his true nature.

People, accept advice from the one who advises you and receive it from the one who carries it to you with obedience, and know that Allah, the Glorified, has not praised but the most attentive of hearts to wise counsel and only those people who are quickest in responding to the truth; and know that the greater struggle is the struggle against one’s self, so occupy yourself with struggling against your selves and you will be felicitous, reject idle talk and you will be safe, increase in your remembrance of Allah and you will gain, [and] be brothers to each other, O servants of Allah, and you will be prosperous with the everlasting bounty [of Allah].
There is no advice like warning [against evil].
One who disobeys his sincere adviser has assisted his adversary.
One who turns towards the sincere adviser turns away from evil.
One who considers the sincere adviser to be a deceiver is engulfed by evil.
One who shuns the advice of a sincere adviser is burnt by the evil schemes of the one who harbours enmity against him.
Whoever opposes [good] advice, perishes.
At times the [only] benefit a sincere adviser gains [for his advice] is suspicion [about his motives].
The one from whom [good] advice is sought may at times deceive.
At times one who is not a sincere adviser may give good advice.
How can one who deceives himself give sincere advice to others?
Sometimes the reliable advisor may betray [you] and the one who is [deemed] disloyal may give good advice.
Whoever gives you sincere advice has indeed helped you.
Do not deceive the one who seeks advice from you.
One who gives you sincere advice has shown concern for you.
He who deems the sincere adviser to be a deceiver, considers evil to be good.
One who accepts [good] advice remains safe from disgrace.
Sincere advice reaps affection.
If you must be fanatical, then be fanatical in assisting the truth and aiding the aggrieved.
If you had not turned away from assisting the truth, you would not have felt weakness in overpowering falsehood.
One who assists the truth shall be successful.
Assist Allah with your heart, your tongue and your hand, for indeed Allah, the Glorified, has guaranteed assistance to one who assists Him.
One who neglects to assist his friend is awoken by the footsteps of his [advancing] enemy.
He who sharpens the spearhead of anger for the sake of Allah acquires the strength to defeat the stalwarts of falsehood.
One who seeks assistance through patience will not be deprived of victory.
One who assists falsehood faces loss.
Whoever seeks support from the enemies of Allah deserves to be forsaken.
Whoever seeks support from Allah attains a glorious victory.
One whose helper is Allah gains victory over his enemy and gains [in Him] the support [like that] of a [large] group.
The virtuous one does not seek justice from the vicious.
A scholar does not seek justice from an ignorant person.
The noble person does not seek justice from the wicked.
Justice can never be sought from the foolish one except by being forbearing with him.
Equity is [a source of] comfort, evil is [a sign of] impudence.
Equity is a symbol of nobility.
Equity is a trait of the honourable ones.
Equity is the most superior of merits.
Equity removes differences and brings about harmony.
Being equitable with others is like being just [while] in authority.
Indeed the greatest reward is the reward of [justice and] equity.
Equity is the best of traits.
Equity causes love to last.
Equity unites the hearts.
Verily if you show fairness to others, Allah will bring you closer [to Him].
Through fairness relationships last.
Three types of people never seek justice from three other types: the intelligent person from the fool, the virtuous from the vicious, and the noble one from the wicked.
It is on equity that affection is established.
Treat all the [other] people with equity but treat the believers with altruism [and prefer them over yourself].
The height of equity is for a person to be equitable with himself.
Whoever is equitable [to others] will be shown fairness.
One who is not equitable is not associated with [by others].
Whoever does not show fairness, Allah takes away [his power and] ability from him.
One whose equity increases, [all the] people bear witness to his justice.
Whoever adorns himself with equity attains the [lofty] ranks of honour.
One who does not show fairness to you out of his [sense of] shame will not be fair with you because of his religion.
With equity brotherhood lasts.
Equity is the ornament of [power and] authority.
The equitable person has many friends and intimates.
The most equitable of people is one who shows fairness himself, without being compelled to do so by any authority.
Indeed it is from the merit of a man to be fair with others, and to do good to the one who does him evil.
The equitable person is noble whereas the oppressor is wicked.
There is no good in that which is viewed except when accompanied with a good source of information [or good elocution].1
Assign for each one of your servants work that you hold him responsible for, as indeed this is more appropriate to ensure that they do not depend upon one another in your service.

Blessing is linked to gratitude and gratitude is linked to increase [in blessings], and these two are linked together in one chain, for increase [in blessings] from Allah, the Glorified, will never cease until the gratitude of the thankful one ceases.
Seek good out of every blessing that Allah has bestowed upon you and do not waste any favour of Allah over you.
Let the effect of that which Allah, the Glorified, has blessed you with be seen on you.
Seek the perfection of Allah’s blessing upon you through patience in obedience to Him and preserving that which He has commanded you to preserve [and act upon] of His book.
Beware of the slipping away of blessings, for not everything that runs away comes back.
Indeed, one of the blessings is affluence, but good health is better than affluence, and the God- wariness of the heart is [even] better than good health.
The best things that Allah, the Glorified, has blessed his servants with are: knowledge, intelligence, power and justice.
The person who is in the best condition of all people is he who makes present blessings last by being grateful for them and gets those that are lost restored through patience.
The least that you must do for Allah, the Most High, is ensure that you do not use His blessings as a means of disobeying [and sinning against] Him.

Verily Allah, the Glorified, has certain selected servants upon whom He bestows blessings for the benefit of the people, causing these [blessings] to remain in their possession as long as they grant them [to the people], but if they withhold them [from the people], He takes away these blessings from them and transfers them to others.
Verily Allah, the Most High, bestows the blessing of benevolence in [times of] ease and the blessing of purification [in times] of hardship.
Blessings last through gratitude.
If you are able to ensure that there is no [other] benefactor between you and Allah then do so.
The only way that the value of blessings can be known is by suffering their contraries.
When you see Allah continuously sending blessings upon you despite your sins, then [know that] it is a means of driving you [towards greater punishment].
When a blessing comes down to you then receive it with gratitude.
When you see your Lord sending continuous blessings upon you, then be careful.
By the befalling of calamities blessings become roiled.
Many a blessed person is gradually being driven [towards punishment] by those blessings.
The alms-tax of blessings is doing good to others.
The adornment of blessings is keeping ties with [one’s] near relatives.
The cessation of blessings is [caused] by withholding the rights of Allah from them and falling short in showing gratitude for them.
The cause of cessation of a blessing is ingratitude.
In every blessing there is a reward.
Every bounty of this world is [headed towards] destruction.
Every blessing from which good is done [to others] is indeed safe from being taken away and is protected from vicissitudes.
Whenever the blessing of an ignorant person becomes good, his ugliness in it increases.
Let the effect of what Allah has blessed you with be visible on you.
Nothing has the ability to make blessings last like showing gratitude for them and nothing beautifies them like granting them [to others].
Whoever enumerates his favours [on others] effaces his munificence.
One who takes the help of a blessing [in order] to sin is indeed an ingrate.

The one upon whom the blessings of Allah are abundant, the people’s needs towards him also abound (so if he fulfils with it what Allah, the Glorified, has made obligatory for him, then he makes it last, and if he refuses what Allah, the Glorified, has made obligatory from it, then he has exposed it to cessation).
Whoever extends his hand to bestow favours [to others] has protected his [own] blessing from cessation.
It is incumbent upon the one whom Allah has munificently blessed to be generous in granting favours to the people.
A truthful friend is one of the blessings [of Allah].
Being adorned with generosity and chastity is one of the most perfect blessings.
Nothing safeguards blessings like granting them to others.
Nothing guards blessings like gratitude.
How great are the blessings of Allah, the Glorified, in this world, yet how small they are in comparison to the blessings of the Hereafter.
How close bounty is to woe!
Allah has not bestowed any blessing on a servant who then does injustice with it but that he becomes deserving of it being taken away from him by Allah.
The blessings of the ignorant are like a garden on a cesspit.
The blessing that is not appreciated is like the evil that is not forgiven.

The blessings of Allah, the Most High, are greater than can be appreciated, except with the help of Allah, and the sins of mankind are greater than can be forgiven, except what Allah pardons [out of His mercy].
We ask Allah, the Glorified, for the completion of His favours [upon us] and for the ability to hold on to His rope.
Do not waste any of the blessings that Allah, the Glorified, has blessed you with, and let the effect of what He has blessed you with be visible on you.
Blessings are not guarded but by gratitude.
Son of Adam, when you see Allah, the Glorified, continuously sending you His blessings then beware of Him, and secure the blessings by being grateful for them.
