The least that is owed to the one who bestows blessings is that no sin should be committed with his blessing.
Verily the inability to commit sins is a blessing.
To the extent of happiness there is trouble.
There is no pleasure with trouble.
Everything is averse to its opposite.
Turn away from the path of mutual aversion and abandon the crowns of boastfulness.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The noble soul is not affected by misfortunes.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The honourable soul does not find it difficult to [spend wealth in order to] acquire provisions.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The ignoble soul does not separate from [its] vile attributes.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: A person’s upbraiding of his own soul is evidence of the gravity of his intellect and the symbol of his abundant merit.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Souls are free but the hands of the intellects hold their reins and protect them from [wretchedness and] misfortune.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who is pleased with himself is cheated and one who is overconfident is faced with affliction.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The one who is pleased with himself cannot see his own faults but if he were to know the merits of others, he would cover up (and feel ashamed of) the faults and flaws that are in him.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The refractory, alluring soul flatters as the hypocrite flatters and feigns the attribute of an assenting friend, until such a time when it deceives and gains mastery, then it dominates as an enemy would dominate and dictates as the tyrant would dictate, thereby taking one into the places of evil.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Honour your soul as long as it aids you in the obedience of Allah.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Humiliate your soul as long as it makes you recalcitrant in the disobedience of Allah.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Have fear of Allah in your soul, wrest away the control that Satan has over you, turn your attention towards the Hereafter and make [the pleasure of] Allah the object of your striving.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Ennoble your soul from every vile quality, even if it drives you to your desires, for indeed you will never be able to compensate for what you have lost of your soul.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Make yourself a guardian over your soul and reserve a portion of this world for your Hereafter.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Move closer to your soul by retracting from it (I mean that you should move towards your loftier and higher self which has been adapted from the light of your intellect and acts as a barrier between you and the inclinations of your base nature; and by retracting I mean you should retract from the soul that commands to evil and shakes hands with defiance).

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Restrain your soul from lustful desires and you will remain safe from calamities.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Be equitable yourself before equity is sought from you, for indeed that is loftier for your status and more deserving of the pleasure of your Lord.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Gain control over your souls by your continuous struggle against it.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Occupy yourselves with [acts of] obedience [to Allah], and your tongues with the remembrance [of Allah], and your hearts with acceptance [of His will] in what you love and hate.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Restrain these souls for indeed they are very desirous, and if you follow them, they will lead you towards the worst evil.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Knowledge about oneself is the more beneficial of the two types of knowledge.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Beware of being pleased with yourself thereby increasing the number of those who are displeased with you.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Beware of overconfidence for this is one of the biggest traps of Satan.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Indeed there is no price for your souls other than Paradise, so do not sell them except [in return] for it.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The greatest affliction is poverty of the soul.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: He who is controlled by lustful desires and enslaved by (worldly) aspirations has degraded his soul.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The strongest of people is one who has the greatest command over his soul.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The weakest of people is one who is unable to reform his soul.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The person with the greatest control over his soul is the one who subdues his anger and kills off his lustful desire.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Verily when souls are in harmony they become close [with one another].

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Verily your souls have [great] value, so do not sell them except for Paradise.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Indeed the one who sells his soul for anything other than Paradise suffers great tribulation.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Verily these souls are very desirous, if you obey them they will lead you to the depths of evil.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Verily obeying the self and following its vain desires is the root of every tribulation and the cornerstone of every aberrance.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Verily the soul has far-reaching desires and continues to be inclined towards disobedience in its desires.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Verily this soul commands towards evil so one who neglects it [and does not discipline it] is indomitably driven by it towards sins.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Verily your soul is a deceiver; if you trust it, Satan will lead you to commit forbidden acts.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Verily the soul commands towards evil and indecency, so whoever trusts it, it deceives him and whoever has confidence in it, it destroys him and whoever is pleased with it, it makes him enter the worst of places.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Verily the true believer does not enter his evening and morning but that he distrusts his soul, so he continues to belittle [and find fault with] it and seeks more [good] for it.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Verily the soul is a valuable gem, whoever guards it elevates it and whoever does not preserve it abases it.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Verily the soul that seeks short-lived desires will surely perish in its quest and will be wretched in its place of return [in the Hereafter].

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Verily the soul that struggles to acquire the everlasting desires will surely achieve its goal and will be felicitous in its place of return [in the Hereafter].

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Verily the soul is like the camel that likes to eat bitter grass, and the ear does not retain much of what it hears, so do not cut off your understanding by being importunate with your soul because for each part of the body there is [need for] repose.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Verily your soul is your riding mount, if you make it carry more than it can bear, you will kill it and if you treat it with kindness, you will save it.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Verily if you contravene this division [and allotment of specific times for specific deeds] then the supererogatory acts you perform do not take the place of the obligatory that you have neglected.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Being preoccupied with disciplining the soul is better [for you].

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Overconfidence [in oneself] is one of the strongest opportunities for Satan.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Redressing the corruption of one’s soul is the most beneficial accomplishment.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Your preoccupation with your own flaws is sufficient to keep [the] shame [of searching for others faults] away from you.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: If you do not restrain your soul from many of the things that you love out of fear of its displeasure, then vain desires will drive you towards a lot of harm.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Verily if you give your [carnal] soul control over yourself, you will corrupt your Hereafter and put you into unending affliction and incessant wretchedness.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Verily if you obey your [carnal] souls, they will lead you towards the worst end.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Indeed you are just like the one who stabs himself in order to kill the one who is sitting behind him.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: When you make your soul obey Allah you have honoured it, and if you allow it to disobey Him you have humiliated it.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: When your soul becomes obstinate with you then be obstinate with it and it will be humble to you, and deceive your soul with regards to yourself, it will yield to you.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: When you desire the uprightness of your soul then you should adopt moderation, contentment and the reduction of [your] wants.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Uprightness of the soul is [attained] through struggle.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Take it upon yourselves to discipline your souls and turn them away from their harmful habits.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Demand from your soul [the performance of] that which it obligatory upon it and you will be safe from the demands of others, scrutinize it and you will have no need for the scrutiny of others.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: He (a) said about the one whom he was censuring: His [lower] self dominates him by means of that which he assumes, and he cannot overpower it with what he is certain of. He has made his vain desire his master and he obeys it in all his affairs.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Try yourself in the obedience of Allah through patience in performing obligatory acts and perseverance in performing supererogatory acts and duties.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Hold yourselves to account [for your deeds] and you will be safe from the fear of Allah and will attain what you desire [from that which is] with Him.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Hold yourself to account for your [own] soul for indeed other souls have someone else who will hold them to account.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Hold your souls to account before they are held to account and weigh them before they are weighed.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Hold your souls to account for their deeds and seek from them the fulfilment of what is obligatory on them and their taking from the evanescent for the eternal; and gather provisions and make preparations before you are resurrected [on the Day of Reckoning].

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Beautify your souls with chastity and keep away from wastefulness and extravagance.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The best souls are the purest among them.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Take [good deeds] from yourself for your soul [in the Hereafter], gather provisions today for your tomorrow, benefit from the slumber (or respite) of time and seize the opportunity [to do good while you can].

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Deceive your heart into worshipping and be gentle with it (or do not compel it), and engage it [in worship] when it is free and lively, except for what has been prescribed as obligatory, for indeed that must be fulfilled [in any case].

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Take from your bodies and bestow them generously to your souls, and strive to free yourselves before your ransoms are blocked.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Oppose your [carnal] soul and you will become upright, mingle with scholars and you will learn.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Serving the soul means protecting it from [unlawful] pleasures and acquisitions, training it with knowledge and wisdom and making it strive in performing acts of worship and obedience, for in this lies the salvation for the soul.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The cure of the soul is abstaining from vain desires and abstinence from the pleasures of this world.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The highest peaks [of success] are not attained but by those who espouse discipline and hard work.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Have humility in your soul and honour in your faith; preserve your Hereafter and be open-handed with your worldly possessions.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Humble your souls by abandoning [bad] habits, lead them towards performing acts of obedience [and worship], make them bear the burdens of [others’] liabilities, beautify them through noble deeds, and protect them from the filth of sins.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Humble your soul through obedience and adorn it with contentment; reduce your wants and be moderate in your earning.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: May Allah have mercy on the person who holds back the reins of his soul from acts of disobedience to Allah and steers it towards the obedience of Allah by its reins.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: May Allah have mercy on the person who subdues the inclinations of his soul towards vain desires thereby protecting it, and steers it towards the obedience of Allah by its reins.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Deterring the soul from vain desire is the greater Jihad.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Deterring the soul from vain desire is the Jihad that is beneficial.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Deterring the soul from the vanities of this world is the fruit of reason.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Deterring the soul from the temptation of vain desire is the fruit of nobility.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Turn your soul away when faced with lustful desires and make it steadfast on the book of Allah when faced with doubts.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Restraining the soul and struggling against its vain desires raises one’s ranks and multiplies the good deeds.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Your satisfaction with yourself is an indication of the corruption of your mind.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The person’s satisfaction with himself is [always] accompanied by the displeasure of his Lord.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: A man’s satisfaction with himself is evidence of his feeble-mindedness.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Turning away from [the pleasures of] this world is the means of reforming the soul.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Governing one’s soul is the best [form of] administration and the eminency of knowledge is the most honourable pre-eminence.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The worst indigence is poverty of the soul.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The worst thing is being pleased with oneself.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The uprightness of the soul is [in] reduced greed.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Reformation of the soul is [achieved by] struggling against vain desires.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The misguidance of souls is between the impulses of lust and anger.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The fruit of self-appraisal is reformation of the soul.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Weigh your souls before they are weighed and hold them to account before they are held to account, and breathe before the throat is constricted, and follow submissively before you are driven by force.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Restrict your souls by holding them accountable and control them by opposition [to their whims].

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who holds himself to account, gains.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who holds himself to account becomes felicitous.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who undertakes to hold his soul to account is safe from flattery [and deceit].

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who holds himself to account becomes aware of his faults and realizes his sins so he seeks forgiveness for his sins and tries to correct his faults.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Blessed is the one who has in his soul that which keeps him preoccupied from the [faults of other] people.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Blessed is the one who strives to free his soul before the shortness of breath and the severity of despair [at the time of death].

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Blessed is he who considers himself as low, gains honour through his obedience [to Allah] and becomes free from want through his contentment.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Blessed is the one who has in his soul that which keeps him preoccupied [from others] and the people are at ease from him, and who acts in obedience to Allah, the Glorified.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Blessed be the soul that fulfils its duty to its Lord.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Purify your souls from the filth of lustful desires and you will attain lofty stations.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever disobeys Allah and obeys Satan has oppressed his soul.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever is satisfied with the temporary abode in place of the everlasting abode has oppressed himself.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Accustom your soul to virtue, for indeed it will make that which is spoken about you good and will make your reward great.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Accustom yourself to being engrossed in remembrance [of Allah] and repentance, for indeed this will wipe out your sin and make your reward great.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Habituate yourself to [performing] noble deeds and bearing the burden of [others’] liabilities, [for through this] your soul will become honourable, your Hereafter will thrive and those who praise you will increase.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Habituate yourself to good intention and virtuous purpose, you will attain success in your aspirations (or endeavours).

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Habituate yourself to forbearance and eschewing importunity, [and as a result] righteousness will adhere to you.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: I am amazed at the one who knows himself, how can he feel at ease in the temporary abode [of this world]?!

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: I am amazed at the one who searches for the thing he has lost while he has lost his own soul and does not seek it!

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: I am amazed at the one who oppresses his own soul, how can he be fair to others?!

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: I am amazed at the one who is ignorant about himself, how can he know his Lord?!

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Compel your souls to abandon acts of disobedience and it will become easier for you to lead them towards acts of obedience [and worship].

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Compel your souls to abandon bad habits and you will overcome them; fight against your vain desires and you will gain control over them.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Perfection of righteousness is in struggling against the [carnal] soul.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The guidance of the soul is in opposing it.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The misguidance of the soul is in obedience to it.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The corruption of the soul is [caused by] vain desire.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Your power over your soul is the best power and your authority over it is the best authority.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: How can one who is not content with little have the ability to reform himself?!

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Being preoccupied with one’s soul is enough to keep a person distracted from the people.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: At the time when you are most confident in your soul be equally cautious (or fearful) of its deception.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Be the guardian of your soul, and do with your possessions that which you would like others to do with it.1

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Hold yourself to account and struggle against your evil nature, and beware of blaming your sins on your Lord.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Be a preventer and a forbidder for yourself [from evil], and a suppressor and a subjugator for your wealth (or outburst) during zeal (or anger).

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The souls have certain evil natures [and characteristics] and wisdom forbids [one from] them.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: There is no price for your souls except Paradise, so do not sell them for anything but it.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: There is no expectation [of goodness] from the one who wrongs his own soul.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: There is none on the face of this earth more honoured in the sight of Allah, the Glorified, than the soul that is obedient to His commands.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who considers himself to be more [important or powerful than others] becomes less.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who humbles himself is honoured.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who reforms his soul gains mastery over it.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who neglects his soul destroys it.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who honours his [carnal] soul is abased by it.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever trusts his [carnal] soul is betrayed by it.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever neglects his soul incurs loss.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who knows himself divests himself [of all worldly desires].

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever obeys his soul kills it.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever disobeys his soul has awarded it.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who is ignorant of his soul neglects it.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever considers himself to be great is humiliated.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever protects his soul [from evil] is revered.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever controls his [carnal] soul, his affair [and status] is elevated.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever is controlled by his [carnal] soul, his status is lowered.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever loathes his [carnal] soul is loved by Allah.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever abases his [carnal] soul is honoured by Allah.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever knows himself knows his Lord.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever knows himself, his matter becomes sublime.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who deceives himself cannot [sincerely] advise others.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who governs [and trains] his soul has [truly] comprehended [the art of] administration.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever takes care of his soul with vigilance, remains safe.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who fears for his soul does not oppress others.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever wrongs his [own] soul, no goodness is expected from him.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever protects himself from asking others becomes exalted.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One whose soul is noble, his affection [and compassion] increases.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who does not govern [and train] his own soul, destroys it.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever is displeased with himself pleases his Lord.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever is pleased with himself angers his Lord.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever is able to gain control over his [carnal] self has attained the highest degree of strength.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever struggles with his soul in order to reform it, becomes felicitous.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever neglects his soul [as it indulges] in its pleasures becomes wretched and distanced [from the mercy of Allah].

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who does not struggle against his [carnal] soul in his young age does not become noble in is old age.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever continually disciplines his soul derives [great] benefit.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever is pleased with himself, many are angry with him.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever indulges his soul in that which it loves, its wretchedness in that which it does not love gets prolonged.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever preoccupies himself with that which is not necessary, lets the matters that are obligatory slip by.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever holds himself accountable preserves his standing and the outcomes of his affair are praised.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever neglects his soul corrupts his affair.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever commands you to reform yourself is most deserving of your obedience.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever scrutinizes himself remains safe from the scrutiny of others.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever oppresses himself is more oppressive to others.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever is great in his own eyes is low in the sight of Allah.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who is ignorant about himself is more ignorant about others.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever is miserly with himself is more miserly with others.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One whose soul is honourable endeavours to purify it from the lowliness of worldly pursuits.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who knows the value of his soul does not abase it with transient things.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever troubles himself with that which does not benefit him gets caught in that which harms him.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One whose soul is content is assisted by it to become pure and remain chaste.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One whose soul is noble finds it easy to give generously and help others.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who considers his soul to be honourable does not abase it by sinning.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One whose soul is vigilant and careful has protectors from Allah watching over him.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who knows himself understands others better.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who considers his soul to be honourable, his [lustful] desires become insignificant to him.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who is lenient with his soul in that which he loves is troubled by it in that which he hates.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever accuses himself has indeed overpowered Satan.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever opposes his [carnal] soul has indeed defeated Satan.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever obeys his soul in its lustful desires has indeed helped to destroy it.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever is pleased with himself, his flaws become known.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever reprimands his soul for [its] faults, it is deterred from many of the sins.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who has in his soul a restrainer [from evil], has a protector over him from Allah.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever knows himself has indeed attained the highest goal of every cognizance and knowledge.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who does not discipline [and purify] his soul, will not benefit from the intellect.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever does not benefit from his [own] soul, people do not benefit from him.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who does not humble himself in his own eyes will not be elevated in the sight of others.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who does not reform himself cannot reform others.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One whom Allah does not help [to fight] against his [carnal] soul will not benefit from the advice of the adviser.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who leaves his [carnal] soul free [to do as it wills] will be taken by it to the paths of darkness [and evil].

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever deals leniently with [and flatters] his soul, it makes him rush towards forbidden sins.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever does not set right his soul by reforming it, his malady becomes worse and curing it becomes impossible, and he will not find any physician [who can treat it].

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One whose grief over his soul is prolonged in this world, Allah will give him delight on the Day of Resurrection and put him in the Eternal Abode [in Paradise].

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever preoccupies himself with other than his [own] soul falters in the darkness and becomes entangled in [a web of] destruction.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who does not know himself is distanced from the path of salvation and stumbles in misguidance and ignorance.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who advises [and admonishes] himself is worthy of giving advice to others.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who deceives himself is more deceitful with others.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One whose soul is honourable, his dissension and disagreement [with the people] is reduced.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever blames his soul, reforms it.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever praises his soul, slays it.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One whose soul is honourable, this world becomes insignificant in his eyes.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever sells his soul for other than the bliss of Paradise has indeed oppressed it.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who does not discipline his soul is disgraced by [its] bad habits.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who thinks good of his [own] soul has indeed done more harm to it.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Being obedient [to Allah] is from the nobility of the soul.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Being obedient [to Allah] is from the God-wariness of the soul.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Hastening towards obedience [of Allah] is a merit of the soul.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Being satisfied at all times is a sign of an honourable soul.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: None abases his [carnal] soul but the intelligent one.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: None considers himself to be imperfect [and disparages his carnal soul] but the perfect one.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who sincerely advises others does not deceive himself.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: How blind is the covetous soul to the terrible [and painful] end [it will face]!

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: mankind, what has made you pleased with the destruction of your soul? Is there no cure from your ailment and no awakening from your slumber?! Do you not feel compassion for yourself as you have mercy on others?

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: No servant considers his soul to be honourable but that the world becomes lowly [and insignificant] in his eyes.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Cognizance of the self is the most beneficial of all [types of] knowledge.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Your [carnal] soul is the closest of all your enemies.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Purify your soul of every lowly trait even if it drives you towards the things that you desire.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Introspection turns one’s attention to self-reformation.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who is successful in knowing himself has achieved the greatest success.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Purify your souls from the filth of [forbidden] pleasures and the evil consequences of lustful desires.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Your [carnal] soul is a hostile enemy and an aggressive adversary, if you are unmindful of it, it will kill you.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Lower yourself from your [rightful] position and people will raise you higher than your rightful position.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The souls of the virtuous are averse to the souls of the wicked.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Purify your soul from every vileness and make an effort to perform every noble deed, you will become free from sins and will achieve noble qualities.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The souls of the virtuous are repulsed by the actions of the wicked.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The one who is pleased with himself and relies on that which his soul has made decorous for him, is destroyed.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The ardent desire of the soul for [forbidden] pleasures misguides and destroys.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Maintain your self-respect by keeping away from jokes, funny narrations and useless speech.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Safeguard yourself from the fire whose fuel is men and stones by advancing towards obedience to Allah, eschewing His disobedience and seeking His pleasure.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Do not sanction for yourself that [action] which you would disapprove of from others.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Do not permit yourself to engage in any evil speech or action.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Do not have fear of injustice from your Lord but fear the injustice of yourselves.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Do not be lenient with your [carnal] soul when it entices you.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Do not defy your soul when it guides you to the right path.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Do not let your soul be devoid of a thought that increases your wisdom and a lesson that safeguards you [from sin].

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Never seek the obedience of others while your [own] soul refuses to obey you.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Do not be ignorant of yourself for indeed the one who is ignorant about himself is ignorant about everything.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Do not abandon struggle in reforming yourself, for indeed nothing but diligence will assist you [to achieve this].

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Never declare war against Allah for there is no power that can protect you from His wrath and you can never be free from need for His mercy.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Do not permit yourself to submit to vain desires or to prefer the pleasures of this world such that your faith gets corrupted and cannot be reformed and your soul loses and does not gain.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Do not surrender yourself to the deception of covetousness and do not respond to the call of greed, for indeed these two [traits] reap wretchedness and disgrace.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: One who cannot control his [carnal] soul is not safe from [the wrath and punishment of] Allah.2

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: A person has no enemy worse than his [own carnal] soul.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The soul does not become devoid of hope until it comes upon death.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: There is none stronger than he who overpowers his soul thereby gaining mastery over it.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: There is no one more powerless than he who neglects his soul thereby destroying it.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: It behoves the one who knows himself to espouse contentment and chastity.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: It behoves the one who knows the honour [and value] of his soul to purify it from the lowliness of this world.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: It behoves the one who knows himself not to separate [himself] from sadness and caution.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: It behoves a man to guard his soul, watch over his heart and protect his tongue.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: It behoves the one who wants to reform himself and protect his religion to avoid mingling with people who seek [the wealth and pleasures of] this world.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: It behoves the one who knows himself not to be separated from caution and regret out of fear of falling into error.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: How befitting it is for a person to have a fixed time, when he is not distracted by anything, in which he holds his soul to account and looks at what he has earned for and against it in its night-time and daytime.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: None is enviable except the one whose endeavour is [to purify] his soul and who does not neglect to regularly hold it to account, demand answers from it and struggle against it.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: A person’s rebuking [and finding fault with] his own soul is evidence of the soundness of his intellect and the symbol of his abundant merit.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The greatest mastery is mastery over the soul.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Control the passion of your soul, the intensity of your rage, the power of your hand and the sharpness of your tongue, and guard against all these by delaying the initiation of any action and refraining from using force until your rage subsides and you recover your senses.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Take control over your vain desires and the distress of your soul, for indeed the distress of the soul lies in acting equitably in [both] the things which it loves and [in those which it] hates.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: The one who keeps his soul steadfast against the temptations of worldly pleasures is a master [over it] and the one who neglects it is destroyed.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Self-restraint during times of anger saves one from situations that lead to harm.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Self-restraint during desire and fear is from the most excellent etiquette.

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Every person who relies on himself [instead of Allah] is thrown [into destruction].

topic: The soul and holding it to account-
text: Whoever is deceived by his soul is delivered by it to places of destruction.
Beware of withholding [charity], for indeed you are [only] a treasurer for someone else in that which you withhold from what is in excess of your daily requirement.
If you spend your wealth for the sake of Allah, then [know that] indeed Allah is quick in recompense.
When you are blessed with sustenance then give charity.
When you are blessed with sustenance then give generously.
Your garments are more lasting for you when worn by others rather than yourself.
A dirham that benefits [others] is better than a dinar1 that throws one into ruin.
The dirham of a poor man is purer in the sight of Allah than the dinar of the rich.
Many a thing that is little grows and develops much more than that which is plenty.
Little that belongs to you is better than plenty that belongs to others.
Nobody gains anything from his worldly life except that which he spends on others.
One who gives with a short arm is given with a long arm.2

Verily you are more in need of giving charity from what you have earned than acquiring what you accumulate. little charity that he gives. For the entire explanation refer to the commentary of Nahj al-Balāgha, Hikma no. 232
Beware of hypocrisy, for indeed the two-faced person is not eminent in the sight of Allah.
Hypocrisy is the brother of polytheism.
Hypocrisy is a disgraceful character.
Hypocrisy is the twin of disbelief.
Hypocrisy corrupts [one’s] faith.
Hypocrisy is from the andirons of ignominy.
Hypocrisy is founded on falsehood.
How reprehensible it is for a human being to have a sick interior and a beautiful exterior.
A hypocrite’s tongue pleases but his heart causes harm.
A hypocrite’s words are beautiful but his actions are a painful malady.
The hypocrite is a shameless, foolish, wretched sycophant.
The hypocrite flatters himself but maligns others.
The most obvious of hypocrite among the people is one who enjoins obedience [to Allah] but does not act upon it himself, and forbids sin but does not refrain from it himself.
Be cautious of the hypocrites for indeed they are misguided and misguide others, they have erred and make others err, their hearts are diseased while their outward appearance looks pure.
The hypocrite is sceptical [and puts others in doubt].
The hypocrite is sly, harmful and suspicious.
I fear for you from every eloquent speaker who is a hypocrite at heart, he says what you know [to be good] but does what you dislike [and know to be bad].

He (‘a) described the hypocrites thus: they are jealous of [those in] comfort, intensify [the] distress [of the distressed] and destroy hopes [of the hopeful]. Their fallen victims are lying on every path, they have means to approach every heart and they have false tears for every [occasion of] grief.
It is the habit of hypocrites to change their character [depending on their circumstances].

He (‘a) said about the hypocrites: They have indeed prepared for every truth a falsehood, and for every straight thing something crooked, and for every living thing a killer, and for every [closed] door a key, and for every night a lamp.
Every hypocrite is a sceptic [who puts doubts in the minds of the people].
One whose hypocrisy abounds, his sincerity will not be recognized.
How repulsive is it for a human being to agree externally while being hypocritical internally.
How repulsive it is for a human being to be two-faced.
The example of the hypocrite is that of a colocynth, its leaves are green but its taste is bitter.
The hypocrisy of a person stems from the inferiority [and humiliation] he finds within himself.
About the hypocrites [he (’a) said]: They are the congregation of Satan and the dwellers of hellfire. These are the party of Satan, and indeed it is the party of Satan who are the losers.

They walk stealthily and tread slowly, hiding behind trees. Their words are [like] a cure but their actions are incurable diseases. They exchange praise [with each other] and come near each other through (or are careful of) reward. They obtain what they covet by means of despair. When they talk they create doubts, they dissemble in their speech and when they speak they delude (or distort).
The [person who is] most severe in his hypocrisy is one who enjoins obedience but does not act upon it himself, and forbids sin but does not refrain from it himself.
It suffices as a deficiency for a man to consider himself as great.
The deficient one is he whose faults are hidden from him.
Rushing to take revenge is from the traits of the wicked.
The most revolting act of a powerful person is revenge.
Evil retribution [and revenge] is from the vileness of victory.
One who punishes the guilty [instead of forgiving him], his merit [and kindness] gets corrupted.
Whoever takes revenge on the wrongdoer nullifies his merit in this world and loses the reward of the Hereafter.
Being hasty in taking revenge is from the traits of the wicked.
How is it that you are not kept awake by the [fear of] Allah’s punishments that befall you by night while you lie in the way of Allah’s wrath because of your disobedience to Him?!
How close is the punishment of Allah to the oppressors (or the unjust) and wrongdoers!

topic: The Defaulters, The Iniquitous And The Transgressors -
text: Indeed Allah has commanded me to fight against those who revolt and break pledges and create strife on the earth. As for the defaulters, I have fought them and as for the iniquitous, I have struggled against them and as for the transgressors, I have vanquished them. As for the Satan of the pit, I have dealt with him with an overpowering scream, until I heard the restless beating of his heart and the trembling of his chest.
One who marries many women is engulfed by embarrassments.
Beware of talebearing, for indeed it plants [the seed of] rancour and distances one from Allah and the people.
The worst [type of] truthful speech is gossip.
Talebearing is the characteristic of a traitor.
Talebearing is an offense [and a sin] that cannot be forgotten.
The worst trait is talebearing.
One who seeks to slander [others] by talebearing is fought by the near one and hated by the one who is far [from him].
One who narrates to you [about others] narrates [to others] about you.

Do not be quick in accepting the words of a talebearer, even if he resembles the good advisers, for indeed the slanderer oppresses the one whom he slanders [about] and deceives the one whom he slanders to.
Be neither scandalmongers nor revealers of others’ secrets.
Trustworthiness and talebearing do not go together.
Belie slander and talebearing, whether it is false or true.
The slanderer is a liar to the one whom he spreads his slander and an oppressor to the one whom he slanders about.
People are like writings on a scroll [of parchment], whenever part of it is rolled up, another part of it is unrolled.
People are children of this world, and a child is naturally inclined to love its mother.

People are divided into two types of seekers, and each seeker is also sought after; so whoever seeks this world is sought after by death until it takes him out from it, and whoever seeks the Hereafter is sought after by this world, until he gets his sustenance from it in full.

People are of three types: the godly scholar, the student who is on the path of salvation and the uncultivated rabble who run after every caller, neither seeking light from the effulgence of knowledge nor taking recourse to any strong support.
People are like trees, their drink is one but their fruits are different.

People are made deficient and flawed, except those whom Allah, the Glorified, protects. The questioner among them aims to embarrass and confuse while the answerer creates trouble. It is not long until the one who has the best views among them is turned away from his good opinion by pleasure or displeasure, and at any moment the most strong-willed among them will get affected by a single glance or transformed by a single expression.

The people who work in this world are of two types: one works in this world for this world; his world has indeed distracted him from his Hereafter. He fears poverty for those whom he will leave behind but feels safe from it himself; so he spends his entire life for the benefit of others. The other one works in this world for that which is to come after it, so that which is [allotted] for him comes to him without [extra] work. Thus he acquires both the shares together and gains possession of both the abodes collectively.
Out of fear of humiliation, people are hastening [towards] humiliation.
The best of people are those who benefit others the most.
The most felicitous person is the intelligent believer.
The most excellent person is the generous one who possesses certitude.
The best people in fulfilling the rights of others are the best in their [following of] Islam.
The loftiest of people is the one who humbles himself.
The strongest person is one who gains an upper hand over his [carnal] soul.
The strongest person is one who overpowers his vain desires.
The most sagacious person is one who rejects [the pleasures of] his worldly life.
The person who makes the most profit is one who buys the Hereafter with this world.
The person who suffers the greatest loss is one who settles for this world in exchange for the Hereafter.
The best person is one whose own faults distract him from the faults of others.
The people who are most felicitous are those who are least interested this world.
The best person is one whose soul is pure and who is indifferent towards this world despite being wealthy.
The most enviable person is the one who rushes to perform good deeds.

Of all the people, the most deserving of compassion are: the scholar upon whom an ignorant person passes judgment, the noble person who is dominated by a vile person and the virtuous person who is under the command of a vicious person.
The best people in this world are the generous ones, and in the Hereafter, the God-wary.
The person in the worst condition is one whose material wealth is cut off but his habit [of spending] remains.
The person who has the weariest heart is one whose endeavour is great and whose magnanimity is abundant, yet his [financial ability and] resources are minimal.
The person living in the most straitened circumstances is one whose desire is much, whose endeavour is great and whose provisions are plenty but his support is less.
The best person is one who resists his vain desires and better than him is he who rejects [the pleasures of] his worldly life.
The most wretched person is one who is overcome by his vain desire so his worldly life gains mastery over him and he corrupts his Hereafter.
Verily people are only either scholars or seekers of knowledge, all others are rabble.
Indeed the elite among the people are only those who have admirable intellects, honourable ambitions and are possessors of nobility.
Let the person who enjoys your favour the most be he who is most protective of the weak and acts most in accordance with the truth.
The best person is he who shows forbearance if he is angered, forgives if he is oppressed, and does good [in return] if is wronged.
The best person is one who benefits the people.
The best person is he who bears the responsibility of providing for the people.
The best of people are the most pious amongst them and the worst of them are most immoral amongst them.
The best person is one who shows gratitude when he is given, remains patient when he is tested [with tribulations], and forgives when he is wronged.
The best person is one who removes greed from his heart and resists his vain desires in obedience to his Lord.
The best person is one who purifies his soul from lustful desires, quells his anger and pleases his Lord.
The best person is one who is generous and thankful in times of prosperity.
The best person is one who is altruistic and patient in times of hardship.
The best person is one whose soul is uninterested in worldly pleasures, whose desire is less, whose lust is dead, whose faith is pure and whose certitude is true.
The entry of people into [discussion about] a thing is the prelude to its [coming into] existence.
The worst person is one who deceives others.
The worst person is one who oppresses others.
The worst person is one who neither accepts excuses nor pardons offences.
The worst person is one who considers himself to be the best of them.
The worst person is one who does not care if people see him doing evil.
The worst person is one who does not give thanks for blessings and does not respect the inviolable boundaries [of others].
The worst person is one who slanders his brothers and forgets the favours [done to him by others].
The worst person is one from whom good is not expected and from whose evil people do not feel secure.
The worst person is one who neither keeps the trust [that has been placed in his care] nor does he avoid treachery.
The worst person is one who neither forgives mistakes nor covers up the faults [of others].
The worst person is one who assists [the oppressor] against the oppressed.
The worst person is he who puts on the armour of vileness and helps the unjust.
The worst person is one who looks for the faults of others while turning a blind eye to his own faults.
The worst person is one who fears the people with regards to [fulfilling the commandments of] his Lord but does not fear his Lord with regards to the people.
The worst person is one who hopes for calamities to befall on others.
The worst person is one who does not trust anyone because of his suspicion and who is not trusted by anyone because of his evil actions.
The worst person is one whom people are cautious about out of fear of his evil.
The worst person is one who repays good with evil while the best of people is one who repays evil with good.
The worst person is he who has lengthy aspirations and does evil deeds.
One who knows [the true nature of] the people, isolates himself.
One who wishes ill for the people will not remain safe from affliction.
Whoever knows the [true nature of the] people does not rely on them.
Whoever is ignorant about people has confidence in them.
Whoever deals with the people in a beautiful manner, they respond to him in a similar fashion.
The best person is one who deals most gently with others and the most sagacious of them is one who is most persevering on the truth.
The person who has the most hope of reformation is one who hastens to change himself when he learns of his faults.
The person who is most concerned about you is the one who is most helpful to you in improving [and reforming] yourself and is most sincere in advising you with regards to your religion.
Verily the best person in the sight of Allah is one who enlivens his mind, kills off his lust and exerts himself for the betterment of his Hereafter.
People are of two types: the seeker who does not find [what he is looking for] and the finder who is not satisfied [with what he has found].
People are of two types: the generous one who does not possess [anything to bestow] and the one who possesses [plenty] but does not help others [with it].
People are only [one of] of two types: the follower of [divine] law or the innovator of an innovation.
It behoves the one who knows the [true nature of] people to be uninterested in that which they possess.
People are fine as long as they are dissimilar from one another.
The best-off people in the Hereafter are the poorest of them in this world.
The most eminent person is one who is humble despite his high standing and who shows humility despite his might.
Sleep is a relief from pain and its counterpart is death.
What a bad rival sleep is! It wastes the short life [a person has] and causes one to lose a lot of reward.
One who sleeps a lot at night loses the [opportunity to perform the] deeds that he cannot make up for during the daytime.
What a rescinder sleep is for the resolutions of the day!
One who is deep in sleep is belied by his dreams.
Woe to the sleeper, how great is his loss! His actions fall short and his reward is little.
When you are appointed as a deputy, then be resolute [in fulfilling your obligation].
Whoever obtains [great wealth or power] becomes overbearing.
Righteous intention is one of the two actions.1
The best of provisions is having good inner consciences.
The closest intentions to success are those that are nearest to righteousness.
The most effective thing in making mercy flow forth [and surround you] is having mercy in your heart for all the people.
Verily Allah, the Glorified, knows the hidden intention of every concealer, the speech of every speaker and the action of every doer.
Verily making intentions sincere and free from corruption is more difficult for the doers [of good deeds] than a prolonged, difficult struggle.
Verily Allah, the Glorified, likes a person’s intention towards the people to be good just as He likes his intention in His obedience to be strong, not shaky.
Actions are the fruits of intentions.
Intention is the basis of action.
Having a good intention brings about reward.
When the intention gets corrupted, affliction befalls.
Through good intentions, what is sought is attained.
The servant attains nearness to Allah through the sincerity of his intention.
Making intentions sincere and free from corruption is more difficult for the doers [of good deeds] than a long, hard struggle.
Having good aims [and intentions] is an indication of legitimate birth.
Having a good intention is a means of attaining one’s aspiration.
Good intention is the beauty of the innermost consciences.
Good intention is from the soundness of [one’s] conscience.
Many an intention is more beneficial than action.
Evil intention is a hidden malady.
The sincerity of [one’s] intention is to the extent of the strength of [his] faith.
When the intention becomes corrupt, blessings are taken away.
In sincerity of intentions lies the success of [all] matters.
If the intentions became sincere, the actions would become pure.
Whoever has an evil intention is deprived of his aspiration.
Whoever makes his intention sincere is purified from vileness.
One whose intention is good, his reward is increased, his life becomes good and affection for him becomes inevitable.
One whose intention is good is assisted with God-given success.
A person’s attainment of all that he wishes for, such as a good life, the security of his flock and an increase in wealth, is through the goodness of his intention and excellence of his character.
He who has no intention has no action.
He who has no knowledge has no intention.
One whose resolve [and intention] is evil, his death is a cause of happiness.
hoever relies upon Allah becomes free from need.
Whoever relies upon Allah puts his trust in Him.
Whoever relies upon Allah has preserved his certitude.
Whoever is certain that what Allah has decreed for him will never escape him, his heart becomes relaxed.
Many a person who relies on something [or someone] gets ashamed.
Attainment [of one’s goal] is solace.
Whoever hides a pain that has afflicted him for three days and complains of it [only] to Allah, the Glorified, then Allah will be the one who restores his good health.
Honour your friendship and keep your promise.
Affection is an auspicious blessing.
When you love [something or someone] then do not be excessive [in your love].
When friendship gets established then [mutual] co-operation and support becomes necessary.
Through affection comes love.
The best person in granting favours is the one who begins by [showing] friendship.
The quickest friendships to get cut off are the friendships of wicked people.
Verily friendship is expressed by the tongue whereas love is expressed by the gaze (or the eyes).
Friendship is kinship.
Friendship is affinity.
Friendship is the closest relationship.
Friendship is the closest kinship.
Friendship is an acquired affinity.
Being friendly with people is the cornerstone of intelligence.
Friendship for the sake of Allah is the best relationship.
Friendship for the sake of Allah is stronger than the bond of blood-relationship.
By [showing] affection love is strengthened.
Three things bring about love: religion, humility and generosity.
Three things bring about love: good character, good companionship and humility.
The best choice is making friends with the virtuous.
The cornerstone of intelligence is being friendly with the people.
Many a [seemingly] friendly person is only feigning [friendship].
Ask the hearts about [your] affections, for indeed they are witnesses that do not accept bribes.
Soundness of friendship is part of honouring one’s promise.
In times of hardship and adversity, the value of [one’s] friendship becomes apparent.
Every friendship [and affection] that is based on [anything] other than seeking proximity to Allah is misguidance, and relying on it is impossible.
Be an upholder of friendship even if you do not find any custodian [for it].
One whose friendship is sincere, his audacity is tolerated.
Whoever befriends a silly person proclaims his own silliness.
One who befriends you for a [specific] objective, turns his back [on you] once it is accomplished.
Nothing brings about love like generosity, companionship and good character.
One who does not give good advice is not sincere in his friendship.
The friendship of the religious ones does not get severed quickly and is ever firm and lasting.
The friendship of a fool is like a tree of fire, part of it consumes [its] other parts.
The friendship of a fool vanishes the way a mirage vanishes and is dispersed the way mist gets dispersed.
The friendship of ignorant people constantly changes [with changes in circumstances] and quickly transforms [into enmity].
The friendship of lay people parts like the parting of clouds, and disappears like the mirage disappears.
The friendship of worldly people is cut off when its [worldly] motives are severed.
The friendship of the people who care for the Hereafter lasts as long as its motive [of pleasing Allah] lasts.
Have affection for those whom you befriend [only] for the sake of Allah and hate those whom you dislike [only] for the sake of Allah, the Glorified.
Do not grant your friendship to one who has no loyalty.
Do not be keen in befriending a person whose true nature you have not known.
Do not befriend the disbeliever and do not accompany the ignorant.
Do not rely on the friendship of the one who does not fulfil his promise.
Never extend your friendship when you do not find a [suitable] place for it.
No one shows compassion like the sincere friend.
No one befriends the wicked except those who are like them.1
The friendship of one who has no faith is not something to be envious about.
The loyal friend does not turn away from his friendship even if he is far away.
Friendship that lacks equity does not last.
It is befitting for the person who values the friendship of a fool to be humiliated.
The most beneficial of treasures is the love of the hearts.
Friendship is one of two [close] relationships.
Friendship for the sake of Allah is the more perfect of the two kinships.
Friendship is the [mutual] empathy of the hearts and the harmony of the souls.
The closest proximity is the affection of the hearts.
The farthest remoteness is the aloofness of the hearts.
Beware of loving the enemies of Allah or having sincere affection for other than the friends of Allah, for indeed whoever loves a group of people is resurrected with them.
Seek the love of Allah, the Glorified, by desiring that which is with Him.
Endear yourself to the people by being uninterested in their possessions and you will be successful in gaining their love.
How can one in whose heart love for this world resides, claim to love Allah?!
Friendship does not become pure [and sincere] with one who is not well-mannered.
Piety reforms the faith, protects the soul and adorns magnanimity.
Restraining oneself from the forbidden [actions] is from the traits of the intelligent and is the quality of the honourable.
Abandoning sins is better than seeking repentance [after sinning].
The most authoritative thing is piety.
The most beneficial thing is piety.
Piety is the best attire.
The pious person is one whose soul is pure and whose attributes are noble.
Piety is stopping when faced with doubt.
Be cautious of [your duty towards] Him just as He has warned you of Himself and fear Him with a fear that would prevent you from [doing] that which causes His wrath.
Beware of falling into doubts and being inclined towards lustful desires, for indeed these two lead you towards falling into the forbidden and committing many sins.
The best [and most virtuous] thing is piety.
The best piety is thinking positively [about others].
Keeping away from evil deeds is better than earning [reward through] good deeds.
The root of piety is keeping away from sins and refraining from the forbidden.
The best [form of] piety is keeping away from lustful desires.
He who divests himself of piety has corrupted his faith.
The most excellent attire is piety and the best provision is God-wariness.
The most pious of people is one who is most free from wants.
Verily the most beautiful characteristics are piety and chastity.
Piety is eschewal [of the forbidden].
Piety is a shield.
Piety is the most excellent attire.
Piety is the best companion.
Piety is nothing but the purification of oneself from sins.
Piety is nothing but scrutinizing one’s earnings [to ensure lawfulness] and abstaining from worldly pursuits.
Lack of contentment is the bane of piety.
Through piety there is purification from lowly traits.
Through true piety, religion is protected.
It is through piety that a believer is purified.
The fruit of piety is the uprightness of one’s soul and faith.
The fruit of being pious is purity [from sins].
The indication of a man’s piety is his purity [from sins].
The proof of good piety is the soul’s refrainment from the disgrace of avarice.
May Allah have mercy upon the person who refrains from the forbidden, bears the liabilities [of others] and vies in hastening towards the abundant prizes [of the Hereafter].
The cornerstone of piety is lowering one’s gaze.
The cause of integrity of faith is piety.
The cause of righteousness of the soul is piety.
Two things cannot be matched in weight by any [other] action: virtuous piety and kindness towards the believers.
Espouse piety, for it is indeed the best protection.
You must espouse piety, for indeed it is a helper of the faith and a trait of the sincere ones.
Espouse piety and beware of the deception of avarice, for indeed it is a pasture without herbage.
During the presence of lustful desires and pleasures, the piety of the God-wary becomes evident.
Piety has been paired with God-wariness.
How can one who is possessed by avarice possess piety?
Let your piety be true, your striving for the right be intense and your intention be sincere in the trust [you take] and the vow [you make].
One who is not reformed by piety is corrupted by avarice.
One who is truly pious keeps away from the forbidden actions.
Whoever shuns lustful desires has safeguarded his soul.
One who lacks piety, his heart is dead.
One whose piety increases, his sins decrease.
One who adopts piety, his worship becomes good.
Whoever divests himself of piety puts on the attire of disgrace.
One of the prerequisites of piety is refraining from sins.
It is from the most excellent piety that you not do in private what you would be embarrassed to do in public.
Eschewing forbidden actions is from the most excellent piety.
Nothing reforms the faith like piety.
The basis of piety is refraining from the forbidden [actions].
With piety, actions bear fruit.
Piety is indeed a good companion and avarice is certainly an evil associate.
The piety of a man is to the extent of his religiosity.
Be pious and you will become pure.
The piety that saves is better than the avarice that ruins.
The piety that dignifies is better than the avarice that humiliates.
The piety of a person frees him from every vileness.
The piety of a believer is manifested in his action.
The piety of a hypocrite is not manifested but on his tongue.
There is no piety like overcoming [one’s] lust.
There is no purity like piety.
There is no piety like eschewing sins.
Nothing reforms faith like piety.
Piety and avarice do not go together.
There is no stronghold more protective than piety.
There is no safeguard for the one who has no piety.
There is no piety more beneficial than eschewing the forbidden.
There is no piety more beneficial than abandoning the forbidden and eschewing sins.
There is no action better than [practicing] piety.
It pleases me for a person to be righteously pious, free from avarice, abundant in kindness and lacking in [making others feel a sense of] obligation.
One of the prerequisites of piety is refraining from sins.
Piety is the distinguishing mark of the God-wary.
Piety is a shield against evil deeds.
Piety is the lamp of success.
Piety is an exalter.
Piety is the fruit of chastity.
Piety is a trait of the learned scholar.
Piety is the basis of God-wariness.
Piety restrains one from committing acts that are forbidden.
Piety is better than the disgrace of avarice.
Verily if you adopt piety, you will become free from the filth of evil deeds.
Verily supporting [one’s] companions financially is a sign of noble descent.
Giving financial support [to a believer] is the best of actions.
Nothing preserves brotherhood like financial support [in times of need].
Whoever believes [the words of] a tattletale spoils his friendship.
You will never get connected to the Creator until you sever your ties with the creation.
Connecting to Allah is in severing ties with the people.
Establish ties [with each other] and come to agreements, and beware of severing ties and forsaking one another.
Establish ties with the one who cuts you off, give the one who asks you, and initiate in giving to the one who does not ask from you.
The one who establishes ties with you while he has nothing is better than the one who shuns you while he has plenty.
Whoever establishes ties with you through the sanctity of Islam has associated [with you] through the firmest means.
Being connected [and keeping ties] with the people of excellence leads to loftiness.
Establish ties with the one whom you keep relations with for the sake of Allah, and sever ties with the one whom you disassociate with for the sake of Allah, the Glorified.
The ties established [with you] by a pauper is better than the shunning of the affluent.
The one who consociates with the people is he who establishes ties with the one who cuts him off.
Never let your brother be stronger in severing ties with you than you are in establishing ties with him.
umility is the more superior of the two honours.
Humility in spite of [having a] high rank is like forgiveness in spite of [possessing the] power [to punish].
Humility is the cornerstone of intelligence and pride is the cornerstone of ignorance.
Be humble and you with be elevated.
The greatest of people in loftiness is one who humbles himself.
The most honourable of attributes is humility, forbearance and affability.
Humility elevates, pride abases.
Humility is the fruit of knowledge.
Humility elevates the abased.
Humility is the symbol of nobility.
Humility spreads [one’s] virtue.
Humility is the alms-tax of honour.
Humility is the most honourable eminence.
Humility is the ladder of honour.
Humility is one of the snares [for capturing] of honour.
Verily if you become humble, Allah will elevate you.
It is through humility that one gets elevated.
Through humility the loftiness [of a person] is measured.1
Through increased humility, honour is perfected.
Humble yourself before Allah and He will elevate you.
The humility of a person elevates him.
The completeness of honour is [in] humility.
The humility of a noble person is the cause of his honour.
The fruit of humility is love.
The result of humility is honour.
Humility suffices as an honour.
Humility suffices as loftiness.
As you become humble, you become great.
One who has humility is elevated.
One who is humble is never bereft of honour.
Whoever has humility, Allah honours and elevates him.
None is humble except the lofty.
Nothing earns honour like humility.
Nobody shows humility but that Allah, the Exalted, increases his loftiness.

How good is the humility shown by the wealthy towards the poor in order to attain that which is with Allah, the Glorified, and how good is the pride of the poor in front of the wealthy out of [their] trust in Allah, the Glorified!
There is no honour like humility.
By being humble, matters are put in order.
It is from the restriction of means to remain in one’s homeland [and not travel].
Separation from one’s homeland is one of the two separations.
Take light from the flame of the preacher who practices what he preaches, accept advice from the adviser who is vigilant, and act upon what he teaches you.
Indeed the most hearing ear is one that listens to admonition and heeds it.
The most beneficial of admonitions is that which deters [someone from sin].
The most effective admonition is taking a lesson from the place where the dead lay.
The most effective admonition is looking at the places where the dead lay, and taking a lesson from the outcome of one’s forefathers and foremothers.
The most effective adviser for you is this world, if only you took a lesson from what it shows you of the changing circumstances and what it informs you of disunion and separation.
Verily there is a lesson and an admonition in everything for the people of wisdom and understanding.
Verily the most sincere of people is one who admonishes himself and is most submissive to his Lord.
Verily the admonition that is neither discarded by the ears nor matched in benefit is that which is not expressed by the speaking tongue, rather it is exhibited by the tongue of action.
Accepting admonition means taking a lesson [and putting into action].
Admonitions are the means of enlivening the hearts.
Sincere advice bears the fruit of affection.
Admonition is a curative advice.
Admonitions are a sanctuary for one who heeds them.
Admonitions are a remedy for the one who acts upon them.
The beneficial admonition is that which deters [from sin].
Admonitions are the sheen of the souls and the polish of the hearts.
Through admonitions heedlessness is dispelled.
Between you and the admonition there is a veil of heedlessness and negligence.
The fruit of admonition is awareness.
The best of admonitions is that which deters [from sin].
May Allah have mercy on the person who accepts admonition, is deterred [from sin] and benefits from the lessons [he has] learnt.
Many a commander [towards good] does not follow [his own] commands.
Many a preventer [of evil] does not prevent himself [from it].
Many an admonisher does not [follow his admonishment and] deter himself [from sin].
Hearing with the ear does not benefit when the heart is heedless.
In admonitions there is polishing of the hearts.

Comprehension [and acceptance] of admonitions invites one to caution, so take admonition from the examples [of the past], and take lesson from the [sudden] changes in circumstances, and take benefit from the Warners.
For the people who possess intellect, what they experience is sufficient as an admonition.
One who finds tranquillity in thinking positively about the [passing] days has not understood the admonitions of time.
Do not shun the one who admonishes you [to good].
Whoever admonishes you [to act righteously] has done you a favour.
Whoever does not take lesson from [what happens to] the people, Allah makes an example out of him for the people.
Whoever understands the admonitions of time will not be at ease with positive thoughts about his days.
Admonition is an excellent gift.

He (‘a) said about the one whom he was rebuking: He is bold in his words but falls short in his actions. He rebukes others but flatters himself. He has been given respite by Allah along with the heedless ones. He leaves in the morning in the company of sinners without a [straight] path to follow or a leader to [act as a] guide, without any clear knowledge or strong faith. He fears death but does not fear loss [of opportunity to do good deeds for his Hereafter].

Never be one of those who do not benefit from admonition unless you give him a painful punishment, for indeed the intelligent one takes admonishment from discipline whereas beasts are not deterred except by beating.

people, how much admonition will you be given yet you decline it? How much have the preachers preached to you, the warners warned you, the preventers prevented you and the scholars conveyed [the message] you! The Prophets and Messengers have guided you to the path of salvation, presented their proof and shown you the clear way. So hasten towards good deeds and take advantage of the time [you have in this world], for indeed today there is action without accounting and tomorrow there will be accounting without action, and the wrongdoers will soon know to what final place they will return.

He loves to be obeyed while he disobeys and to be given his full share while he does not give others their dues. He loves to be described as generous while he does not give [anything to the needy] and to seek from others what is due to him while not letting others ask for their rights from him.
He speaks of the world with the words of the abstemious yet acts in it with the actions of the desirous.

He manifests the traits of the virtuous yet secretly performs the actions of the wicked. He hates death because of his numerous sins yet does not abandon them in his lifetime. He expedites sins but delays repentance. He loves the righteous ones but does not follow their actions. He hates the sinful yet he is one of them. He says: ‘Why should I act and become weary, instead I will sit and aspire.’ He always hastens towards what perishes and leaves aside that which remains.
