He is incapable of being thankful for what he is given yet always seeks more in what remains. He guides others to the right but deceives himself. He forbids the people from that which he does not forbid himself from and enjoins them to perform that which he does not perform. He takes upon himself more responsibility from people than what is required yet he neglects from his own soul what is more important [and necessary]. He commands the people but does not follow the commandments [himself] and he warns them but does not heed the warnings. He hopes for the reward of an act which he has not performed and feels secure from the punishment of an act which is undoubtedly a sin. He attracts the attention of people through his religiousness yet he conceals within himself the opposite of what he displays. He knows the right that he has on others but does not recognize the right that others have on him. He fears for others more than [he fears about] his sins and hopes for himself more than [he deserves by] his actions. For big things he puts his hope in Allah but for small things he puts his hope in the people, so he gives the servant that which he does not give the Lord. He fears the servants with regards to [the commandments of] his Lord yet does not fear his Lord with regards to the servants.
The one who accepts admonition has indeed awoken.
God-given success is the more honourable of the two shares.
God-given success and God’s abandonment1 each pulls the soul towards itself, so whichever [of the two] prevails, it enters its fold.

Verily when Allah, the Glorified, wishes good for a servant, He grants him success in spending his lifetime doing the best deeds and blesses him with the ability to quickly use his available time to perform acts of worship, before [the coming of] his death.
God-given success is [God’s special attention and] favour.
God-given success is a mercy.
God-given success is [a means of] advancement [towards Allah].
God-given success (or kindness) is the key to sustenance.
God-given success is the leader towards righteousness.
God-given success is from the attractions [that pulls one] towards the Lord.
God-given success is the beginning of [many] blessings.
God-given success is a supporter of the intellect.
God-given success is the cornerstone of felicity.
God-given success is the fountainhead of prosperity.
God-given success is the favour [and special attention] of the Most Merciful.
God-given success is the best virtue.
Through God-given success felicity is achieved.
God-given success is the best leader.
God-given success is the best helper and good action is the best associate.
There is no succour like God-given success.
There is no blessing greater than God-given success.
One who considers evil to be good and turns away from the words of the sincere adviser does not become successful.
Whoever is granted success does good [work].
One who is assisted by God-given success does good work.
One who is not assisted by God-given success does not turn towards the truth.
Taking [and acting upon] good advice is from the biggest success.
Part of the success of a freeman (or a person) is his earning wealth through legitimate means.
From the success of a man is putting his secret in the hands of one who conceals it and [placing] his goodness with one who spreads it [and makes it known to others].
We praise Allah, the Glorified, for the ability He has granted us to carrying out [acts of] obedience and to keep away from disobedience.
One who is supported [by Allah] in his affairs is successful in achieving his goals.
Whoever takes Allah to be His adviser attains success.
Excessive agreement is hypocrisy.
The worst countenance is [that of] the shameless.
How shameless the ignorant one is!
The shamelessness of a man disgraces him.
Beware of impudence, for indeed it drives you to embark on ugly acts and to rush towards evil deeds.
Impudence is the symbol of evil.
The cornerstone of every evil is impudence.
Revere Allah the Glorified, keep away from what He has forbidden and love those whom He loves.
Revere your elders and your youngsters will revere you.
Espouse precautionary dissimulation for indeed it is a trait of the praiseworthy.
He who has no precautionary dissimulation has no religion.
Precautionary dissimulation is religiosity.
God-wariness is a fortified stronghold for the one who takes refuge in it.
God-wariness is the accumulator of [all] purity and chastity.
God-wariness is the fruit of faith and the sign of certitude.
The exterior of God-wariness is honour in this world while its interior is honour in the Hereafter.
God-wariness is the strongest connection between yourself and Allah if you hold on to it, and it is a shield against the painful chastisement [of the Hereafter].
God-wariness is such that there is no alternative or substitute for it.
God-wariness is for a person to be cautious of all [the things] that could lead him towards sin.
Be God-wary and you will succeed [in this world and the next].
Fill your heart with God-wariness and oppose your vain desires, [by this] you will overcome Satan.
Fear Allah with some God-wariness, even if it be little, and place between yourself and Him a veil [of shame], even if it be thin.
Fear Allah by obeying Him, and obey Allah by fearing Him.
Be wary of your duty towards Allah, whom you must eventually meet, and with other than whom you have no ultimate end.
Be wary of your duty towards Allah with regards to that which He has created you for.
Be wary of your duty towards Allah, [the Lord] who hears when you speak and knows when you conceal something in your heart.
Be wary of your duty towards Allah with the wariness that is due to Him, and strive to attain His pleasure, and be cautious of what He has warned you about from His painful chastisement.

Be wary of your duty towards Allah with the wariness of one who hears [the message of guidance] hence humbly submits, commits a misdeed hence confesses [and repents], learns [the truth] hence trembles in fear, is cautious [about the Hereafter] hence takes the initiative [to do good] and performs an action and does it well.
Turn to God-wariness, for indeed it is an impenetrable shield. Whoever turns to it, it protects him and whoever holds on to it, it preserves him.
Hold on to God-wariness, for indeed it has a rope with a firm handle and a stronghold with an insurmountable peak.
Indeed God-wariness is like trained [and docile] riding mounts with their riders on them and their reins given to them, so they take them into Paradise.
The most protective shield is God-wariness.
The most impenetrable fortress of religion is God-wariness.
Verily God-wariness is a protection for you in your life and a means of gaining nearness [to Allah] after your death.

Verily Allah the Most High has enjoined God-wariness upon you and has made it the means by which His pleasure is attained by His creation. So fear Allah, [the Lord] who is closely watching you and in whose grip are your forelocks.

Verily the wariness of their duty towards Allah has shielded His friends from what He has forbidden and has made their hearts bound by His fear, so much so that their nights pass in wakefulness and their midday’s in thirst; thus they take comfort in hardship and are quenched by thirst.

Verily the fear of Allah is a provision and a place of return. It is a provision that takes one to his destination and a prosperous place of return. The best inviter has called towards it and the most heedful [of people] have heeded to it. So the inviter has told the people about it and those who have given heed to it are successful.
Verily God-wariness is the right of Allah, the Glorified, upon you and it necessitates your right over Allah, so seek Allah’s help to achieve it and use it as a means of attaining proximity to Allah.

Verily the fear of Allah [and God-wariness] has continually presented itself to the people of the past and those who came after them, because they will [all] need it tomorrow when Allah resurrects what He has created and takes back what He has given; but how few are those who undertake it the way it deserves to be undertaken!
Verily the fear of Allah has a rope with a firm handle and a stronghold with an insurmountable peak.

Indeed God-wariness makes Allah most pleased with His servants and it is what He demands from His creation. So be wary of your duty towards Allah who knows what you do in secret and records what you do openly.

Verily God-wariness is a strong fortress [of protection] for the one who takes refuge in it, and impiety is the dilapidated fortress [of humiliation] which does not protect its people and does not offer security to the one who takes refuge in it.
Verily God-wariness is today a safeguard and a shield, and tomorrow [it is] a pathway to Paradise; its path is clear and the one who travels on it, gains.
Indeed the fear of Allah is the maintainer of faith and the pillar of certitude, and it is surely the key to righteousness and the lamp of success.
Verily the one who has been shown what is in front of him by the examples of the exemplary punishments of the past is prevented by God-wariness from falling into doubts.
Verily the one who abandons God-wariness is lured by pleasures and lustful desires, and falls into the wilderness of sins and is constantly plagued by grave (or many) [evil] consequences.

Indeed the fear of Allah is a key to rightness, a store for the Hereafter, emancipation from every [form of] bondage and safety from every destruction. Through it the runaway is rescued, what is sought is attained and what is desired [of the Hereafter] is acquired.
God-wariness dignifies, immorality disgraces.
God-wariness is eschewal [of the forbidden].
God-wariness is the best provision.
God-wariness is the most fruitful cultivation
God-wariness is the cornerstone [all] of good deeds.
God-wariness is the leader of moral virtues.
God-wariness is a fortified stronghold.
God-wariness is the reserve for the place of return [in the Hereafter].
God-wariness is the strongest foundation.
God-wariness is the key to uprightness.
God-wariness is the fortress of the believer.
God-wariness is a safeguard for the one who adopts it.
God-wariness is the strongest fortress and the most protective sanctuary.
If you fear Allah, He will protect you.
Indeed you are in greater need of the provisions of God-wariness than you are of the provisions of this world.
When you [wish to] guard yourself, then be wary of the things that Allah has forbidden.
The sting (or blackness) of sins is cut off by God-wariness.
It is with God-wariness that preservation from sin has been paired.
Through God-wariness, actions become pure.
The garment of God-wariness is the most honourable of attires.

Treat your [spiritual] ailments with God-wariness and anticipate [and prepare for] your death by it; take a lesson from those who have neglected it and ensure that those who heed to it do not take a lesson from you [for having neglected it].
The cornerstone of God-wariness is abandoning lustful desires.
The cause of the probity of [one’s] faith is God-wariness.
The probity of God-wariness is [in] eschewing doubt.
Blessed is the one who fills his heart with God-wariness.
Espouse God-wariness, for indeed it is the character of the Prophets.
Espouse God-wariness, for indeed it is the most honourable distinction.
Espouse God-wariness in hiding and in the open, and adhere to the truth in anger and pleasure.
Espouse God-wariness, for it is indeed the best provision and the most protective accoutrement.

So be wary of [your duty towards] Allah with the God-wariness of one who listens hence humbles himself, who commits [a sin] hence he confesses, who becomes afraid hence he performs virtuous acts and is cautious hence he hastens [towards good deeds].

So be wary of [your duty towards] Allah with the God-wariness of one who attains certitude hence he does good, who is given lesson [from the happenings of this world] so he takes it, who is warned so he desists, who is shown [the right path] so he sees [it], and who fears the chastisement [of the Hereafter] and works for the Day of Reckoning.

So be wary of [your duty towards] Allah, O servants of Allah, with the God-wariness of one who has preoccupied his heart with reflection, who [always] has the remembrance [of Allah] on his tongue and who advances [good deeds out of] fear for his safety [in the Hereafter].

So fear Allah in relation to the purpose for which He has created you, and be cautious of [your duty towards] Him just as He has warned you of Himself. Make yourself deserving of what He has promised you by having confidence in the truth of His promise and being afraid of the terror of Day of Resurrection.

So be wary of [your duty towards] Allah, O servants of Allah, with the God-wariness of one who tucks up his clothes in preparation [for fulfilling the commandments of Allah] and makes great effort, who acts quickly during the short period [he has] and hurries out of fear [of losing the opportunity].

So be wary of [your duty towards] Allah with the God-wariness of one who thinks about returning towards the Hereafter, the end [and consequence] of his life’s journey and the place of his [final] return, so he remedies his past errors and increases his righteous actions.
Increased God-wariness is a symbol of abundant piety.
Whoever would like success in the Hereafter should espouse God-wariness.
Whoever takes off the attire of God-wariness will not be able to cover himself with anything from the devices (and means) of this world.
Whoever puts on the attires of God-wariness, his garments will not get worn out.
Nothing reforms faith like God-wariness.
The basis of God-wariness is rejection of this world.
Guided is the one who fills his heart with God-wariness.

And fear Allah, who is justified [in punishing you for disobedience] by the warning He has issued, and has a strong argument because He has made the [right] path clear and has warned you of the enemy who enters into the hearts stealthily and whispers secrets in the ears.
Neither [should you] advance nor retreat except with the fear of Allah and in obedience to Him, [in this way] you will become victorious by attaining success and [finding] the right way.
There is no honour like God-wariness.
There is no provision like God-wariness.
There is no God-wariness like desisting from the forbidden.
There is no fortress more impenetrable than God-wariness.
The thing that is rooted in God-wariness is never destroyed and the plant that grows on it never remains thirsty.
There is no dignity loftier than God-wariness.
The most virtuous of you is the most God-wary among you.
Do not dishonour the one who has been elevated by God-wariness.

Be wary of [your duty towards] Allah with the God-wariness of one who was called so he answered, who was penitent so he returned back, who was warned so he became cautious, who passed by [a place] so he took lessons [from it] and who feared so he remained safe.

topic: The God-wary and God fearing people-
text: The God-wary is one who guards against sins, and the purified is one who purifies himself of faults.

topic: The God-wary and God fearing people-
text: The God-wary are those whose souls are chaste and whose needs are few; people hope for good from them and feel secure from their evil.

topic: The God-wary and God fearing people-
text: The God-wary are those whose souls are content, whose lustful desires are dead and whose faces are cheerful while their hearts are sad.

topic: The God-wary and God fearing people-
text: The God-wary are those whose actions are pure, whose eyes are tearful and whose hearts are fearful.

topic: The God-wary and God fearing people-
text: The God-wary person is one whose lustful desire is dead, whose anger is suppressed, and who is thankful in times of comfort and patient in times of hardships.

topic: The God-wary and God fearing people-
text: Verily the God-wary are all those [believers] who are generous, chaste and benevolent.

topic: The God-wary and God fearing people-
text: Verily the God-wary have taken [and gained in both] the evanescent world and the Hereafter. They have shared with the people of this world in their worldly benefits, while the people of this world shall not share with them in their Hereafter.

topic: The God-wary and God fearing people-
text: The God-wary are those whose hearts are sad and from whose evil people are safe.

topic: The God-wary and God fearing people-
text: The God-wary person is content, free from sin and chaste.

topic: The God-wary and God fearing people-
text: The practice of the God-wary is taking advantage of respite and preparing provisions for the [final] journey.

topic: The God-wary and God fearing people-
text: Indeed successful is the God-wary person who [always] remains silent.

topic: The God-wary and God fearing people-
text: For the God-wary person there is guidance towards the right path, restraint from corruption and [a strong] desire for reforming the Hereafter.

topic: The God-wary and God fearing people-
text: There are three signs of a God-wary person: [his] sincerity in action, [his] shortening of hopes [and aspirations] and [his] taking advantage of respite.

topic: The God-wary and God fearing people-
text: If the heavens and earth were closed upon a servant and then he became God-wary, Allah would surely make for him a way out from them and provide for him from whence he does not reckon.

topic: The God-wary and God fearing people-
text: One who is on his guard remains safe.

topic: The God-wary and God fearing people-
text: One who is God-wary reforms [his Hereafter].

topic: The God-wary and God fearing people-
text: Whoever fears Allah, He protects him.

topic: The God-wary and God fearing people-
text: One whose heart is God-wary, jealousy does not enter into it.

topic: The God-wary and God fearing people-
text: Whoever fears his Lord is [indeed] honourable.

topic: The God-wary and God fearing people-
text: Whoever fears Allah gains success and becomes prosperous.

topic: The God-wary and God fearing people-
text: Whoever fills his heart with God-wariness, his endeavour becomes successful.

topic: The God-wary and God fearing people-
text: Whoever fears Allah, the Glorified, He dispels all worries and gives him a way out of every distress.

topic: The God-wary and God fearing people-
text: Whoever fears Allah, He protects him.

topic: The God-wary and God fearing people-
text: Nobody becomes God-wary but that Allah makes his way out [of difficulties] easy.

topic: The God-wary and God fearing people-
text: One who guards himself from sins is like the one who does good deeds.

topic: The God-wary and God fearing people-
text: The kings of Paradise are the God-wary and the sincere.

topic: The God-wary and God fearing people-
text: Those who are wary of [their duty towards] their Lord are driven to Paradise in throngs, having being saved from the chastisement, cut off from the punishment and delivered from the fire [of Hell] into the Abode of tranquillity, and they will pleased with their dwelling and residence.
Trusting in Allah is an honourable sufficiency for the one who relies upon it.
Trusting in Allah means distancing oneself from [reliance upon one’s] strength and power, and waiting for what is brought by divine decree.
Beware of choosing [a path] for yourself [instead of putting your trust in Allah], for indeed most of the success lies in that which is not reckoned.
The root of the heart’s strength is in putting [one’s] trust in Allah.
Verily the perfection of trust in Allah stems from the verity of certitude.
Trusting in Allah is [a means of] sufficiency.
Trusting in Allah is an asset.
Trusting in Allah is the best pillar [of support].
Trusting in Allah is the fortress of wisdom.
Trusting in Allah is the best action.
Trusting in Allah stems from strength of certitude.
It is through the strength of one’s trust in Allah that the level of one’s faith is evinced.
Trust in Allah the Glorified, for indeed He has guaranteed the sufficiency of those who put their trust in Him.
The strength of a servant’s trust in Allah is to the extent of his reliance on Him.
It is sufficient for your trust [in Allah] that you consider no one else as a channel for acquiring your sustenance other than Allah, the Glorified.
It is in trusting Allah that the true essence of conviction lies.
Whoever puts his trust [in Allah] is catered for.
One who trusts in Allah does not get worried.
One who trusts in Allah is catered for.
Whoever trusts in Allah, He suffices him.
Never allow yourself to trust in anyone but Allah, and you should have no hope in anyone but Allah.
Everyone who puts his trust in Allah is catered for [and provided for by Him].
Have trust in Allah and you will be catered for [by Him].
There is no trouble [and distress] for the one who trusts in Allah.
One who puts his trust in Allah will never lose His support.
One who trusts in Allah has no need for [seeking help from] His servants.
Whoever trusts in Allah is catered for and becomes needless [of others].
Whoever trusts in Allah, difficulties become easy for him.
Whoever trusts in Allah, doubts get cleared for him, his sustenance is catered for and he is saved from tribulations.
Whoever trusts in Allah, difficulties become tolerable for him, means become easy for him and he enters into [a place of] comfort and honour.
A righteous child is the more beautiful of the two recollections.
A child is one of the two enemies.1
The worst of all children is the undutiful one.
The loss of a child burns the heart.
The death of a child is [like a] tear in the heart.
An evil child destroys one’s honour and disgraces one’s ancestors.
An evil child dishonours one’s ancestors and corrupts one’s descendants.
The undutiful child is a tribulation and a misfortune.

topic: The close friends and lover of Allah-
text: Verily the friends of Allah, the Most High, include all those who consider their death to be near, belie their [false] hopes, and have many good deeds and only a few mistakes.

topic: The close friends and lover of Allah-
text: Verily the friends of Allah are those who remember Him the most, are constantly grateful to Him and have greater patience in the face of His trials.

topic: The close friends and lover of Allah-
text: Verily the most beloved of servants in the sight of Allah is the servant whom He helps to reform his soul such that he feels sadness [on the inside] and dons the attire of fear [on the outside]; so the lamp of guidance is illuminated in his heart, and he has prepared [for himself] a hospitable reception for the day which he will come upon.
Lethargy causes loss in this world and regret in the Hereafter.
Lethargy is wastage [of one’s lifetime].
Lethargy is [a cause of] loss.
Lethargy is the trait of the foolish.
Loss comes about through lethargy.
Counter lethargy with resolve.
One who submits to lethargy forfeits his rights.
One who submits to lethargy is encompassed by regret.
It is from lethargy that laziness originates.
any a grant is such that misfortune is better than it.
Delusion is not the same as comprehension.
hoever exposes himself to suspicion should not blame those who suspect him.
The best reserve is true guidance.
Through true guidance discernment increases.
He who takes guidance from other than the guidance of Allah has gone astray.
Blessed is the one who hastens towards true guidance before its doors are closed.
Following true guidance leads to salvation.

Successful is the one who gets illumination from the lamp of guidance, opposes the calls of [his] vain desire, makes faith the equipage for his Hereafter and [makes] God-wariness his reserve and provision.
How can the one who is astray be guided aright when the guide [he follows] is heedless?!1
How can one who is himself astray guide others to the right?!
How is the one who is overcome by [his] vain desire able to get true guidance?!
Let your garment be true guidance.
One who is guided attains salvation.
Whoever seeks true guidance through the guidance of Allah is guided to the right path by Him.
He who takes guidance from other than the guidance of Allah, the Glorified, has gone astray.
He who seeks true guidance through the guidance of Allah disassociates [himself] from the opponents [who oppose His command].
One who seeks guidance from those who do not possess it is led astray.
One who seeks guidance from the misguided becomes blinded to the course of true guidance.
The guidance of Allah is the best guidance.
There is no deviation with true guidance.
There is no guide better than true guidance.
There is no guidance for one who has no knowledge.
Gifts bring about affection.

Nothing gains the favour of the ruler, quells the rancour of an enraged person, attracts the deserter [to come back], makes difficult matters easy and keeps wickedness [and evil] at bay like the [giving of a] gift.
Keep away from idle talk, for the least of its damage is blame.
Beware of idle talk, for the one whose talk increases, his sins [also] increase.
Idle talk takes one closer to [unpleasant] changes [in circumstances].
Idle talk harms the soul.
Excessive idle talk earns disgrace.
Too much joking is a sign of ignorance.
Whoever jokes too much is considered ignorant.
Whoever jokes a lot, his seriousness becomes ineffective [and is considered just another of his jokes].
Whoever is overcome by jest, his intellect becomes corrupt.

topic: The causes of downfall and ruin-
text: Three things cause [one’s] ruin: obedience to women, yielding to rage and submitting to lustful desires.

topic: The causes of downfall and ruin-
text: Three things cause ruin: boldness in front of the ruler, trusting a disloyal person and tasting poison as an experiment [to see how effective it is!].

topic: The causes of downfall and ruin-
text: Three things break one’s spirit and cause downfall: poverty after wealth, humiliation after dignity and loss of loved ones.

topic: The causes of downfall and ruin-
text: Three things weaken one’s spirit: loss of loved ones, poverty in a strange land and unending hardship.
The scandal-monger is dispraised and reviled.
The farthest endeavours are those that are closest to nobleness.
Worries [and concerns] are [proportionate] to the extent of [one’s] endeavours.
The best endeavours are the loftiest of them.
Be lofty in your endeavours when you seek something and honourable in victory when you overpower [your enemy].
One whose endeavour is great, his care [and attention towards it] becomes great.
One whose endeavour is insignificant, his merit is nullified.
One whose endeavour is honourable, his value becomes great.
One whose endeavour is great, his cause is worthy.
Confine your endeavour to that which is necessary for you and do not enter into that which does not concern you.
One who rises to the [higher] levels of endeavour [and determination] is glorified [and considered as great] by the nations.
One whose concern is not for [attaining] that which is with Allah, the Glorified, does not realize his aspiration.
Never concern yourself with anything except that which will earn you recompense and do not strive except in gaining reward.
One’s zeal is [proportionate] to the extent of one’s endeavour.
The value of a man is proportionate to his endeavour and [the value of] his action is to the extent of his intention.
Nothing raises a person like his [earnest] endeavour and nothing lowers him like his lustful desire.
The worries of a man are to the extent of his endeavour and his sense of honour is to the extent of his zeal.

Do not make your family and children your greatest concern, for indeed if they are friends of Allah, the Glorified, then Allah does not forsake His friend, and if they are the enemies of Allah then what is your concern for the enemies of Allah?
Do not allow yourself to feel sorrow for what you have lost such that it preoccupies you from what is [yet] to come.
One who acts irresponsibly regrets.
Whoever embarks on the frightful [and risky] earns wealth.
Whoever treats people with disdain, [his status] diminishes.
Overcome your vain desires and flee from them, for indeed if they capture you they will take you into the farthest depths of destruction.
Beware of allowing vain desire to gain control over you for indeed its beginning is temptation and its end is tribulation.
Indeed, the thing I fear most for you is [the result of your] following vain desires and having lengthy aspirations.
Vain desire destroys.
Vain desires are passions of youth.
Vain desire is the enemy of reason.
Vain desire is the bane of the intellects.
Vain desire is an obeyed enemy.
Verily if you follow your vain desire, it will make you deaf and blind, ruin your place of [final] return and destroy you.
Verily if you allow vain desire rule over you, it will deafen you, blind you and destroy you.
The bane of the intellect is vain desire.
When your vain desires overcome you, they drag you into places of destruction.
Oppose vain desire and you will be safe; turn away from this world and you will benefit.
May Allah have mercy upon the person who fights his vain desire and breaks loose from the entanglements of this world.
The cornerstone of religion is opposing vain desire.
The cornerstone of reason is struggling against vain desire.
Deterring [the self from] vain desire is a trait of the intelligent ones.
The cause of corruption of the intellect is vain desire.
The cause of corruption of faith is vain desire.
Counter vain desire with the reason.
Blessed is the one who endures [the temptations of] his vain desire, rejects his [false] aspiration, hits the target and acquires recompense.
Yielding to vain desire corrupts the intellect.
Submitting to vain desire causes ruin.
Vain desire is victorious over the one who is led by his lust.
He who overcomes his vain desire is victorious in attaining the Paradise of the [everlasting] Abode.
The delusions of vain desire beguile.
Being overcome by vain desire corrupts [one’s] faith and reason.
Combat vain desire just as an adversary would combat his adversary, and battle it the way an enemy would battle his enemy, [if successful] you may gain mastery over it.
In succumbing to vain desire there is every [form of] deviation.
He who overcomes his vain desire and controls the urges of his [carnal] soul is successful.
Indeed the one who is deceived by the temptations of [his] vain desire has gone astray.
Combat your vain desire with your intellect and you will acquire right guidance.
Combat your vain desire with your knowledge and your anger with your forbearance.
Be a conqueror of your vain desire and a seeker of your salvation.
If vain desire were to be lifted, the insincere person would despise [and feel ashamed of] his [own] action.
One who is controlled by his vain desire goes astray.
Whoever yields to his vain desire is destroyed.
Whoever overcomes his vain desire is honoured.
Whoever controls his vain desire acquires intelligence [and wisdom].
Whoever agrees with his vain desire opposes his rectitude [and reason].
One whose vain desire is strong, his resolve becomes weak.
Whoever embarks on his vain desire slips.
Whoever follows his vain desire destroys himself.
Whoever opposes his vain desire has followed [the path of] knowledge.
One who proceeds with vain desire falls into destruction.
With vain desire there is no [reason and] intellect.
Whoever embarks on vain desire is afflicted by blindness.
There is no faith with vain desire.
Whoever yields to his vain desire has sold his Hereafter for his worldly life.
One whose vain desire overpowers his intellect is overcome by disgrace.
Whoever wishes to attain lofty stations should overcome his vain desire.
One who is controlled by vain desire does not accept the advice of any sincere adviser.
One whose actions are free from vain desire, his effect [and result] is good in every matter.
Whoever follows his vain desire, it blinds him, deafens him, humiliates him and misguides him.
Whoever is led by his vain desire, Satan prevails upon him.
Whoever looks with the eye of his vain desire falls into temptation and wrongdoing, and deviates and turns away from the clear open path.
Nothing opposes reason like vain desire.
Nothing destroys religion like vain desire.
Vain desire is a riding mount that throws down its rider.
Opposing vain desire is a cure for the intellect.
The one who is overpowered by vain desire is always wretched and forever enslaved.
He is drawing in large buckets [from the well] of his vain desire and exerting a lot of efforts for his worldly life.1
Following vain desire is indeed a good aide to Satan.
Ruined is the one who is led astray by vain desire and pulled by Satan towards the path of blindness.
Your vain desire is a greater enemy towards you than all [other] enemies, so overpower it otherwise it will destroy you.
Never let your vain desire relegate your knowledge.
Do not follow [your] vain desire, for whoever follows his vain desire becomes disconcerted.
Do not incline towards your ignorant people (or your ignorance) and do not follow your vain desires, for indeed the one who alights at this stop is on the brink of a collapsing bank.
Vain desire is the greater of the two enemies.
Vain desire is a worshipped deity.
Because of succumbing to vain desire and misguidance, [only a] few will be saved from hellfire.
Control your vain desire and be stingy with yourself [by keeping away] from those things that are forbidden for you, for indeed being stingy with oneself is the essence of honour.
Be cautious of the vain desire that pulls the souls down, dropping them [to the lowest levels], and causes them to become more distanced from [the place of] success [and prosperity].
The smallest vain desire can corrupt the intellect.
There is no damage [and loss] greater than [what is brought about by] vain desire.
The most destructive thing is vain desire.
Beware of yielding to vain desire, for indeed it leads [one] towards every [form of] tribulation.
The best of people is one who struggles against his vain desire.
The beginning of vain desire is temptation and its end is tribulation.
Vain desire is the partner of blindness.
Vain desire is a hidden ailment.
Vain desire is a bane of the intellects.
Vain desire is a pernicious associate.
Vain desire is the opposite of reason.
Vain desire is the foundation of tribulations.
Vain desire is the riding mount of temptations.
Vain desire is a [cause of one’s] fall to the lowest of the low.
Do not be a slave to vain desires and coveted objects.
There is no enemy like vain desire.
Vain desire is a riding mount of temptation.
Dread is [a cause of] failure.
Dread is accompanied by failure.
The bane of awe is jest.
Dread has been paired with failure.
Loss of hope [in others] is one of the two successes.
The root of sincerity is losing hope [and desire] in that which others possess.

Verily the most honourable of all people is one who loses hope [in others], espouses contentment and piety and is devoid of greed and covetousness, for indeed covetousness and greed are a ready indigence and verily loss of hope [in others] and contentment are a manifest affluence.
Loss of hope [in others] is freedom.
Loss of hope [in others] is liberty.
Loss of hope [in this world] is a solace.
Loss of hope [in this world] is a ready affluence.
With loss of hope [in others] comes honour.
Loss of hope [in others] comforts the soul.
Loss of hope [in others] is a renewed liberty.
Loss of hope [in others] is a comforting liberty.
Loss of hope [in others] exalts the prisoner.
Loss of hope [in others] is better than entreating the people [for what you need].
Through loss of hope [in others] there is [attainment of] self-sufficiency.
Adorn yourself with loss of hope in that which people possess and you will become safe from their malice and you will acquire their affection.
Hastening the loss of hope [in others] is one of the two triumphs.
The virtue of loss of hope [in others] is better than the humiliation of asking [for their help].
Loss of hope may [indeed] be an achievement [in times] when covetousness is destructive.
One who loses hope in a thing forgets about it.
The bitterness of despair is better than turning entreatingly towards the people.
The beginning of sincerity is losing hope in that which people possess. places his hope only in Allah.
Be good to your orphans, help your poor folk and be kind to the weak amongst you.
Whoever oppresses an orphan has severed his ties with his children.
Whoever takes care of the orphans, his children will be cared for.
The one who takes charge of caring for the orphans and the needy is considered [to be] among the honourable ones in the sight of Allah.
One who takes charge of caring for the orphans is favoured in the sight of Allah.
Vigilance in religion is a blessing for the one whom it is bestowed upon.
Alertness is illumination, negligence is delusion.
Alertness is perspicacity.
Indeed you have been alerted so become vigilant, and you have been guided so follow the guidance.
One who does not take support through vigilance will not benefit from [the presence of] guards.
Alertness is [a cause of] grief.
Recover, O listener, from your stupor, and wake up from your heedlessness, and curb (or cut short) your haste [towards sins].
Is there nobody who will wake up from his [slumber of] negligence before his time [on this earth] ends?
Attain certitude (or proficiency) and you will be successful.
The best faith is certitude.
The root of patience is [having] definite certainty about Allah.
The root of indifference towards worldly pleasures is certitude, and its fruit is felicity.
Certitude is worship.
Certitude is light.
Certitude is the symbol of faith.
Certitude is the best [means of] indifference towards [the pleasures of] this world.
Certitude is the pillar of faith.
Certitude is the gown of the sagacious.
Certitude eliminates doubt.
Certitude bears the fruit of indifference towards worldly pleasures.
Certitude is the cornerstone of religion.
Certitude is the best worship.
Verily I am upon complete certitude from my Lord and do not have any doubt about my religion.
Through certitude worship becomes complete.
The fruit of certitude is asceticism [and indifference towards worldly pleasures].
The cornerstone of religion is true certitude.
The cause of sincerity is certitude.
Cling to certitude and eschew doubt, for there is nothing more destructive for a person with regards to his religion than the prevailing of doubt over his certitude.
Cling to certitude and God-wariness, for indeed these two will deliver you to the Garden of [everlasting] Refuge.
The strength of one’s certitude is [proportionate] to the extent of one’s faith.
The highest form of certitude is sincerity.
Certitude is sufficient as worship.
The certitude of one who is extravagant in his wants and exerts himself in acquisition [of wealth] it is not true.
If your certitude was sound, you would not have exchanged the everlasting for the evanescent, nor would you have traded the lofty for the lowly.
One who has certitude is successful.
One who has certitude is saved.
One whose certitude is firm, has hope.
One who has certitude works diligently.
One who is certain about [divine] reward does good [deeds].
One whose certitude is strong does not [have any] doubt.
One who is certain about the Hereafter does not covet this world.
One whose conviction is firm, his worship becomes good.
One whose certitude is true does not [have any] doubt.
One whose certitude is sound abstains from dispute.
One whose heart does not have certitude, his actions do not submit to it.
One who has certitude is hopeful.
How great is the felicity of one whose heart is filled with the coolness of certitude.
Certitude is an excellent dispeller of doubt.
Sleeping with certitude is better than praying while in doubt.
One who sells certitude for doubt, truth for falsehood, and the Hereafter for this world is destroyed.
Do not turn your certitude into doubt and your knowledge into ignorance.
He who has no certitude has no faith.
Certitude is evinced by the shortening of hopes, sincerity in action and indifference towards the pleasures of this world.
Certitude is corrupted by doubt and the onslaught of vain desire.
The weapon of the possessor of certitude is patience in [times of] hardship and thankfulness in well- being.
Have certitude and you will become strong.
Whoever possesses certitude does good [deeds].
Those who possess certitude, the dedicated [and sincere] ones and the altruistic ones are from the people of the Elevations.1
The possessor of certitude is the most sorrowful of all people about [the condition of] his soul.
